GTA without GTA. Instead of GTA you play L.A. WWII detective.
Wonderfuly rendered atmosphere of L.A's atmosphere in 40's.
Amazing face motion capture, imagine every possible human emotion displayed in game. It is all there and it looks so real.
Slowly evolving story with no big suprises, almost everything is predictable. Nice game mechanics. Game could be maybe a bit repetitive after while as every case looks very similar (go to crime scene, investigate place and interrogate people, put bits together, get a new location or arrest someone and interrogate him at police station and so on and on) - but i never felt it like so as it comes very natural. You play detective in one of five LAPD departments and what detective does? Picking up a bits of evidence, talking with people and visiting different places to get case clearer.
During interrogations you really have to watch interrogated person's mimic as it corresponds with what they are talking. You have to say if interrogated person talks truth or lies, even in doubt option is here. Correct answer branches interrogation more with possible leading you to get another evedinces in case or even arrest interrogated person (if needed in case story).
If you feel bored by playing cases one can clear his head by just driving around LA watching traffic and people, everything seems very natural. Or you can just reply to dispatch and go for some street crime as an "open world" gameplay.
I putted open world in quotation marks because on one hand game is open world by its design. Big open city with pulsating life in it. On the other hand game has nothing to offer, beside of main story. Only those dispatch street missions which are for about 5 minutes or less each. And they are really repetitive. Robbery, shooting, crazy person, again and again. I can imagine more in a such nice world or city. Those you can play during main story or after finishing it you can just patrol streets of LA by just answering dispatch on your radio.
Pros:
- nice graphics, city with people and traffic feels really alive
- absolutely amazing facial motion capture, this should be in every game
- as police detective you can take over any car on street
- loved radio comedy shows during nights
- at every department you got a partner which can help you during investigations or you can ask him for advice
- overall nice atmosphere (for someone who is fan of that era this game must be like being in haven i suppose :))
- no bugs or glitches which could be rare very soon in large gaming industry }indie segment is ok as indie developers care about their customers)
- LAFD car, communal waste car, towing car, ambulance car ... any car! ;)
Cons:
- unskippable cutscenes which could get really annoying very soon when you try to do something better from certain savepoint
- partner could be more helpful sometimes
- you ride over someone, no matter if just gentle push or rolloed over a dozen of times, that person just walks away
- long display time of subtitles when reading documents, books etc. - i can imagine having some reading speed option in game as i was running game with subtitles and it took really loooooong time to read some document with more than few rows of text (it was like i can read each subtitle about 5 times again and again before it changed, i think 10 years old can read faster than those subtitled showed)
Conclusion:
If you are into atmospheric adventures, noir, detective and 40's in America, go for it, i am sure you will like it.

LA Noire is an Immersive game with a good blend of action and deductive reasoning. The games tone and atmosphere are a great homage to all those great black and white film noir movies from the 40s and 50s. All the usual suspects are here, from gun-toting gangsters in pin stipe suits to dangerous "dames" in evening dresses to tough talking cops ready to put suspects under the hot lights till they sing like a canary!
This game bathes you in the period of post war America ... everything from billboards and radio ads to the traffic lights and of course the cars; if you like old cars this game is for you! Even the crowds and traffic patterns help to really immerse you in late 1940's Los Angeles. You work your way up the ladder of the LAPD from beat cop to detective working a number of departments such as Traffic and Vice Squad.
TIP: READ THE NEWSPAPERS you find scattered around town, because they detail the overall storyline that you will become involved with later on.
One of the most unique aspects of this game was that a vast majority of the dialog was actually filmed with real actors (sharp eyed movie buffs will recognize some of the faces and voices from various cop shows and movies) and then rendered into computer graphics. The end results are some of the most realistic facial animations ever done for a game to date. This technique however locks the game at about 30 frames a minute. Some people have said that 30 FPS is too slow, however I had no issues with it at all. Individual experiences may vary.
LA Noire's combat mechanics can be a bit "wonky" at times and take some getting used to. In fact I reccommend replaying action scenes more than once just to get used to how it all works. However I never felt like the game was too unforgiving. I could usually get through an action scene, even if I didn't do everything perfectly.
I like the "Intuition" system they use for interrogations and interviews. It gives us hints without cheating. However, I sometimes wished we could use intuition more than once an interview, since there are often at least 4 or 5 questions per person.
All in all I find LA Noire to be a great game that runs well even on older hardware since the game its self is now a few years old (but still gorgeous!) and the differnt mechanics and play style make for a unique game worthy of Rockstar Games!

Really, really good and improving at dizzying speed.
Plays similarly to the original, with new complexities (neutral Factions, political system, laws).  Available quests are a welcome addition to the 4X genre (implemented in previous Amplitude titles).
Ship design is fun and involved, tech "wheel" is deep and seemingly getting deeper update to update.  Combat is 3-stage automated combat with cards, but more visually appealing and with a larger selection of cards than the original.  Tactics are no longer straightforward approach-from-long-range, rather ships can execute flight paths which attempt to take advantage of strengths and minimize weaknesses.
Where this game crushes the competition is the ultra-slick interface.   The Endless series have been improving and interating on their formula for awhile, and this one is a masterpiece.  It combines all the best parts of the Sins of a Solar Empire, Stellaris and previous Endless games for a seriously satisfying waltz through your empire.   Right-click out, seamless scrolling as far in or out as you'd like, rather than not getting in the way, as is about the best most games UIs can hope for, this interface seems to plug you in at a cerebral level.   Navigating through the menus tickles the back of your skull like a low-grade dopamine rush.   The One-More-Turn effect often morphs into the One-More-Menu effect instead.
Add to this the extremely diverse factions with very unique playstyles,  a plethora of customization, an interesting, yet not distracting political and legislative system, anomalies, unique discovery/travel systems and a host of others, and it's shaping up to be a real winner.
I picked up early access in February, and at the time there were some limitations.  Only two months on and most of these seem solved.  Universe sizes are limited to "large", custom races are not yet available as of April 3, 2017, and there are a couple of bugs, mostly with windows, highlights and a hanging combat window issue, but it's mostly a polished game.  I expect we'll see it released this year.
I'm trying to avoid too much play before full release, to give it a fair shake as the finished product, and I really should be trying to get some hours in on Mass Effect Andromeda, but it's so hard to stay away.

As for the gameplay, its terribly easy to point your aim and take a shot, but the difficulty comes from choosing the right power and path to the hole. If you play in a big enough lobby there is bound to be someone who is great at the game, who will be more than willing to teach you a trick or two!

When I first wrote this review, I already loved the game, and since then the Devs introduced a lot of interesting new features for free and fixed bugs. There might still be some minor bugs left, but I cannot tell, since I don t encounter them any more.
So basically the game gets bigger and better every time another big update is introduced. In my opinion this game is one of the most rewarding titles you can buy atm.
All in all it is a great game for those who like 4x4 games that include the story approach of Endless Legend and combine it with the scifi charm of Endless Space + the game introduces some interesting new approaches towards population and politics.

I haven't had a chance to play this at length yet (obviously, I only have 1.7 hours) BUT...
-edit Now 12 hours in, and loving it even more :)
It has been a really long time since I liked a space 4x this much. My issue with most of them, is the races are all the same. They're just templates with different music, a different JPG for your leader, and maybe some slightly varied stats. In ES2, for the first time they actually feel different. Not just JPGs, but the presented personality, the atmospheric "feel", and more importantly, the gameplay. The Vohdyani (or however you spell it) are shipbound and have a very specific method for even expanding are one very obvious example.
Then there is the aspect of storyline "quests" for each race, which really surprised (in a good way). Back to the "every race is a generic template" most of these games it doesn't really matter what race you are or are interacting with, they're all the same, and the "game" revolves entirely around the empire management (often lacking) and combat (often lacking) which leaves you with not a whole hell of a lot to occupy yourself with. The storylines do a LOT just to enhance the feel of the specific races as well as giving you something "higher" to do besides merely subduing your neighbor. Again, I haven't got into it too much, but the obvious intent is highly commendable, even if it doesn't play out as I imagine.
In all, I would say that ES2 is a massive leap forward over ES1 (which I've only dabbled with a bit) and has some very good aspects that other developers would be wise to learn from (I'm looking at the rather sterile Stellaris here, the abysmal MoO, and the well intentioned but somewhat clumsy GCIII)
No game is perfect, but there is a lot to like here already and I'm looking forward to seeing what they expand upon as ES2 moves out of EA into release. Good job, devs!

In Endless Legend, you are able to decisively move your units, and turn order matters greatly. The outfit you give your units MATTERS GREATLY. If you take the time to think about your moves, you'll find yourself playing a much more lively version of chess.
That being said, Endless Space 2's combat is based solely on who has the bigger army and better guns, with monor die rolls that tip the scale in even matchups. No skill or critical thinking goes into combat at all. It's only a matter of "Who came to this fight with more ships and bigger guns."
And don't even get me started on the ground combat. This revolves around something referred to as Manpower. Let me explain to you how ♥♥♥♥ing pointless this is: I had two ships SPECIFICALLY designed for invading planets. Each had 1900 manpower. The rest of my fleet had between 100-300 each, for a total of ~5000 manpower.
I invade some offshoot colony of the eggheads. I massacre their fleet (without losing a single ship) and then begin squatting on their system to decrease their manpower. Finally, it's around 260 and I decide "there's no reason I should not win this" and I invade it. But guess what? The game has no sense of equal ratios, it seems. My 5000 manpower to their 260 would put me at a huge advantage, dontcha think? NOPE.
I had 125 Sophon infantry V 200 egghead infantry. And I lost the battle. WHAT. THE ACTUAL. ♥♥♥♥.
And to make matters worse, ALL OF MY MANPOWER WAS DEPLETED FROM MY SHIPS. So I had to trek ALL the way back to a friendly system and refill my usless military gas tank, which took about 10 turns. Then, I go back, and guess what? Their system has FULLY RECUPERATED from any and ALL damage I had done.
TL;DR Welcome to the game where everything's made up and the points don't matter.

Super happy with this so far in early access.
This is how you do early access - FINISH the parts of the game available to people, and categorically block off parts of the game with clear messaging when they arent done.
There are a few bugs (I had a save corrupted when I turned off econonmy victory and bought the end game wonder for 200k, LOL) and lots of missing tooltips, but overall a very smooth experience.
As for the game, I don't have many complaints. I'm excited for the strategic combat view, and would like a bit more control, but overall it's pretty satisfying. The balance between macro and micro is pretty good, the only thing I dont think they've really worked out yet is population management. You can really get in there and tweak your population to live on different planets, or mix with other species to get bonuses, but in practice it's frustrating to manage... for example to exchange some population on two planets to get a bonus you have to drag them to this civilian transport thing then set the destination in both systems. The next turn they set off for the destination system. But meanwhile, the population grows to backfill the slots you just opened, so by the time the transport arrives, the system is already full again and I have no clue what happens to the transport when it gets there, it just kinda disappears.
Anyway I've already ran through five or six games and am having a lot of fun, this is one of the few EA titles that I'll be revisiting as its patched and will have lots of playtime on when it goes out of EA.

The game is interesting
When I saw it, my friends were playing it. To me, it looked like a game I'd never enjoy at all, but my friends were playing it and I installed it. I looked at the design of the characters and enemies, and I thought it was unique. I then started the tutorial, and I instantly fell in love with the game. It has everything that Destiny doesn't. It has special abilities, and more diverse weapons. Sure, you might have to spend money to get better items that look better than your original, but you can get them in the game. You just have to play it for a while. This game also has a great combat system, that you can learn real quick. It's different than other games, which makes Destiny feel like a copy cat. It also has a great price of it being free. I love the fact that each weapon and Warframe is unique. The story is interesting, the combat is great, and the items and weapons are interesting. The graphics are amazing for a free game. It sucks that people say it's a Destiny rip-off that is terrible and a trashcan of a game. I see why people believe that, but It's nothing like destiny. Don't play Warframe just for the PvP, not many people play it. It also isn't that good in my opinion. Play the missions with your friends, there is different type of missions. Such as Spy, Defensive, Survival, and more. You can also change your character, and you may say "I want to look unique, I'll look like everyone else". Well, this game lets you change almost EVERY color of your guy, weapons, and even your ship. That's right, you have your own ship. No else is allowed on your ship, but you. Which means you have total control of what your ship looks like. This is one of the most suprising games I've played, and you should try it out.

Overall, it CAN be a fun game. You run around yelling and swinging weapons at other people while occasionally trying to complete an objective. However, this game should only be played lightheartedly with friends, as trying to take it seriously brings up issues such as a mechanic that keeps you from having full control over your swings, a combat system that becomes increasingly frustrating as you play the game more, a soul-suckingly boring competetive scene, a toxic meme-spouting "git gud" community worse than the one Dark Souls II ushered in (an example can be seen in this review's comment section), friendly fire being a thing in a game where people swing 6 ft long swords, polearms, and spears around with reckless abandon and no regard for their teammates on battlefields accomodating over 32 players.. the list goes on.
"Good players" use extremely unnatural bugs-turned-features to their advantage to stomp new players in 1v1 fights. One of these 'features' is the ability to speed up an attack by placing your sword inside of the enemy before the tracer starts via turning away from them, crouching, and looking down before performing a vertical downward slash. Then there's the ballerina swordfights where people will jump and swing and bumblef*ck their way around each other until they either run out of stamina or someone finally gets hit. Any server with more than 20 people becomes a chaotic clusterf*ck of friendly fire, bug abuse, trolling, and sheer stupidity (but hey, if that's your type of thing then by all means try it out).
On the bright side, the game has a few ways to keep you interested. There are many weapons to use, and most of these are unlocked by killing people with default versions of that weapon type. For example, you kill 25 people with a mace to unlock a longer, slower, more damaging morning star. Kill 75 more people with either the star or the mace and you get a stick with a bunch of nails in it that has no business being as effective as it is. Unlock all the primary weapons for one of the 4 classes and you get a neat-looking veteran helmet for that class, which indicates you sort of know what you're doing. There's a bit of customization; you can change colors and patterns and heraldry for free and buy different class skins and weapon skins if you really want to (even if they're overpriced as hell). Nothing really too exciting though.
The novelty wears off after a while and what was once stupid fun will be replaced by a disgustingly complete lack of any emotion the more you play; a zombification of your "fun receptor", if you will.
You will probably have a blast in the beginning, but as with anything in life it won't stay that way forever. The game seems to give people about 40-100 hours of gameplay on average, so for under $10 on a sale it might be worth it.

First of all: what I wanted from this game was a good detective story, not a GTA-like game nor a shooter.
The only real positive I can think of is the facial animation, which is really something to behold. As for the negatives:
- The noire atmosphere is terribly hamfisted. It feels like they just watched a bunch of noire movies and took note of all the tropes they could use. The narration is really jarring and uninspired too.
- This game is poinltessly open world, and as a result everything looks ugly.
- Too many shootouts. You're a detective, not a goddamn SWAT.
- The logic in the interrogations is all over the place. It constantly switches between demanding you to spot absolute truths (what the witness said is what happened) and relative truths (what the witness said is wrong, but he/she couldn't know), so you never know if the contradictions you just spotted are something you should point out or just irrelevant mistakes. At some points the game forces you to choose between two alternatives that you know are both wrong, and then you are even treated like an idiot because of the "mistake" you had to make.
- Despite all of this the game still finds ways to push you forward even when you made blatant mistakes instead of having you fail and repeat. This makes the whole game feel completely pointless.
Overall I can't find redeeming qualities in this game; I'd rather play most other adventure games.

I played Warframe some years ago, and I have recently returned to it. It has changed consideraby over the intervening period.
The Good: -
1) Great graphics.
2) Incredibly fun gameplay.
3) Generally stable, with a decent ping and few connection or lag issues.
4) Easy grouping and quick access to quests.
5) A moderately interesting story mode.
6) Many weapons and suits to collect, which come in normal and prime (prime is a higher qaulity version).
The Bad: -
1) Becomes repetitieve quickly, such that the grind for the prime warframes will probably extend beyond your forebearance for repeating the same content over and over.
2) The cash shop items (particularly warframes and weapons) seem to be there to entice new players. In most instances you will be able to buy the elements required to make a Prime version of a suit more cheaply from other players than the inferior version of a suit from the cash shop.
3) Most player-player trades are for platinum (real-world money surrogate), and there is no auction house, meaning new or inexperienced players may get ripped off, and finding equipment to buy can take time.
4) Many of the missions are designed in such a way that players rush through them. This can become annoying if you want to collect resources, or just play at a more relaxed pace, and you may find yourself soloing often.
5) Many of the menus and game systems are counter-intuitive and could be designed to be more user friendly.
Conclusion: -
A fun game well worth playing, but with limited longevity.

I was a late arrival to LA Noire, and even later doing this review. I meant to do it at the time I played it but there ya go... I have played the game extensively though and was prompted to write this following an overhaul of some of my game video capturing, when I was testing it out with L.A.N. and realised again how enraptured I was with it.
Lets get this out of the way. There's a forced frame cap of 30fps but for me the game runs fluidly and so this didn't  bother or irritate me. There's a supposed hack/fix around this if it does bother you though.
The game's setting is Post War L.A. and you play the role of Cole Phelps an Ex-Marine, now turned Police Officer. You do climb the ranks fairly quickly and actually I feel the developers could have gone much deeper into Phelps's role in each of the departments he finds himself in, without the need for DLC. That said, its a small criticism.
Bearing in mind this game first released in early 2011, we are probably talking about 2010 or even 09 tech. The reason I raise this specifically, is that Rockstar introduced a
at this time for this game. Now one of my major gripes - including that of major AAA game releases – is that studios spend inordinate sums on performance capture, only to end up with character performances appearing rather wooden to say the least. Especially in regard to facial animations, which is a real shame since we're supposed to be getting better at this and generally we're not! I focus on this for a very good reason because, what Rockstar attempted to do, was pin down characters facial expressions and subtle nuances that may be exhibited when a person is lying or telling the truth and this is used as a major game mechanic while investigating crimes. What they delivered was more than  just simple fake results, what they captured was a real sense of individuals characters too. I think this remains pretty unique and I cant think of another game that has employed this method in gameplay before or since. Certainly no studio have created tech for this purpose and for the most part this has worked extremely well but that isn't the only thing I have been most impressed with. When as Phelps you’re interacting with all the other characters within the game - not just plotline peeps – I also mean everyone you might have incidental interactions with and extends to anyone you see speaking in the game. No, the most impressive  introduction of this tech is how natural and real everything then feels. This really draws you into the game much more than I have ever witnessed.
and as I understand it quite accurately represented in a depicted mid-to-late forties LA setting. Just as the setting is in the Hollywood area, so too is the feeling - as the player - that you're in a role in the movies but not in a bad way either. This isn't just about portraying or delivering an artistic theme, it seems more than that to me and it works very well in an immersive sense. The use of the facial tech becomes really important as it affects your relationships with your colleagues and superiors, because as you evaluate you're judged also and scored on your detective skills. This overall affects the points you score on the relative success or not of the individual cases. Anywho, Cole progresses through the game from a simple beat/patrolman to murder, arson and vice investigator. As you play through there's an underlying current about Phelps progression through the ranks and if you’re pretty savvy about this sort of stuff, you'll definitely sense this and will reveal itself later on in the game.
When you get to the murder cases, you really begin to feel like you're investigating real crime scenes and some of them are pretty brutal as you might expect but this element is very well executed as you'll discover. I do wish that there had been more freedom to explore hunches and go against the flow of some outcomes but to say more would reveal spoilers so I wont. Anyway its a minor gripe and you would have to have a similar structure to force the endgame scenarios.
Aside from the intrigue and storyline, its simply a joy just to drive around LA and Hollywood streets and engross yourself in that age and era. There is some wonderfully created classic cars of the period and I did root out and drive every single vehicle in the game, all 95 of them and a pleasure it was too ;)
If you haven't got the sense that I really loved this game then you missed the point. Its a great game and one which
as it turned out I bought it very cheaply in the Steam Sales and that was indeed a real bonus! I have no idea whether we will ever see LA Noire 2 but if we do I will definitely be one of the first in the queue to pre-order.

Super happy with this so far in early access.
This is how you do early access - FINISH the parts of the game available to people, and categorically block off parts of the game with clear messaging when they arent done.
There are a few bugs (I had a save corrupted when I turned off econonmy victory and bought the end game wonder for 200k, LOL) and lots of missing tooltips, but overall a very smooth experience.
As for the game, I don't have many complaints. I'm excited for the strategic combat view, and would like a bit more control, but overall it's pretty satisfying. The balance between macro and micro is pretty good, the only thing I dont think they've really worked out yet is population management. You can really get in there and tweak your population to live on different planets, or mix with other species to get bonuses, but in practice it's frustrating to manage... for example to exchange some population on two planets to get a bonus you have to drag them to this civilian transport thing then set the destination in both systems. The next turn they set off for the destination system. But meanwhile, the population grows to backfill the slots you just opened, so by the time the transport arrives, the system is already full again and I have no clue what happens to the transport when it gets there, it just kinda disappears.
Anyway I've already ran through five or six games and am having a lot of fun, this is one of the few EA titles that I'll be revisiting as its patched and will have lots of playtime on when it goes out of EA.

Stop. Stop reading, GET THIS GAME!
This is a fantastic story worthy of being slapped with 10/10, kudos and praise. Why? Because this game is like "Guardians of the Galaxy", it has personality, action and narrative.
You are Detective Cole Phelps, and are a badass at solving cases. You will run through numerous cases investigating clues and interrogating suspects, unraveling a conspiracy and a kickass story, and half the time your partners will "pull rank" or flat out refuse to do a foot chase and leave it all to you :P
Pros:
OMG GRAPHICS. Did I mention graphics? This game has the most amazing facial graphics ever. It should be, because they use motion capturing on people's faces and you can actually see emotion in their faces!!! Once you play this game you will be disapointed with every game out there that doesn't come up to snuff. It is simply gorgeous, and groundbreaking to tell if someone is lying via actual cues in their behavior and their faces! The interactivity of the game, with player and character are grade A.
The gameplayer borrows alot from GTA, with cars behaving similarly but to me feel alot better. The gun play is clunky but intuitive, it doesn't kick you out of cover akwardly or just unwieldy to do sometimes. *cough* Mass Effect *cough*.
Overall, it just feels nice and awe-inspiring to see the period perfect LA, based on real cars, on real settings and with distinct personalities. From villains to partners, you will loathe, love and grumble at people who feel real and you could have sworn probably exist in real life.
Con:
IT IS TOO SHORT. The usual benefits of getting a game on PC are the mods. Well, it doesn't have great mod capabilities and therefore the modding community can't mod new stories and there's so little DLC. I would reccomend buying this on console unless you can find it cheaper on PC.
Overall, buy it on console unless the PC version is cheaper. It's simply easier to control and feels more native on console.

Buy this game on sale only. I have been looking for a new 4x game and I figured I would give this a try, but as an Early Release it still has a lot of problems.
Edit - This edit was done just after the main release. The game is still not very combat based, if you start in a big galaxy you wont have to worry about the AI attacking you. In my current game I am at turn 150 and I started my first war just because I was bored. My industrial power allows my to build a fleet per turn, so I dont think the AI will have a chance (I still like the combat system though). One thing that does not make me happy since the release is that because of feature creap the UI does not respond as fast as it used to. This makes me sad because the fast UI is a sign that the game is well programed, and well, now the UI is slow, so ...
Cons-
- Game breaking bugs. As my game progresses in turns (I only at turn 141 now) I am unable to load a save game without errors popping up. If I revert to an earlier save (with no errors) eventually I get to a point where I cant load a save. This sucks all of the fun right out of the gaming experience.
- Pirate spam. Yes I know I can turn off pirates, but I wanted to try playing the game as intented. I have a few problems with the pirates. First, they come out of nowhere. There are no pirate bases despite the game having many possible mechanisms that could be used : minor factions, "curiosities", heck even something could be added to asteroid belts. Secondly, late in the game pirates serve no purpose. By turn 100 or so I could afford to put 2 medium sized ships in almost every one of my systems and blast pirates all day long. By turn 100 the pirates launch suicide attacks against my systems to the point where every turn a lot of time is spent auto-resolving battles (basically wasting the players time). Thirdly, the pirates (and other AI fleets in general) tend to group together into fleets very poorly. As the pirate attacks scale to the size of your empire, it is not uncommon to find 10 or 12 pirate ships in one of my systems, but due to technology limits (I am assuming) the pirates are not able to to form into a 12 ship fleet, so I end up fighting 3 fleets of 4 ships. I am not sure if some of these pirates might be part of the "privateer" mechanism, but I still think the pirates/privateers should flow from some spawn point/base.
- Non aggressive AI. Like I mentioned, I have only played to turn 141 or so, but I do not think that I have ever been attacked by the other factions. I am always at a state of "cold war" with all of the major factions, but the player does not have to worry about the other factions. You can destory other factions ships that enter your systems, but that doesnt seem to anger them enough to start anything. The AI lets you sit an build up in your little kingdom with very little interaction.
-Government type is changed with no imput from player. After a while your citizens get a little angry. There is a meter in the planet screen which shows how many turns they are from revolting, but at the 5 turn until revolt mark, your governemt type is changed to "Anarchy", then to a "Dictatorship". A dictatorship makes no one happy, but the game doesnt allow you to change to another governemt type once you have been forced to a dictatorship. In the screen where you would be able to change the goverment type (which you can only do every 10 turns I think) you can watch the count down of turns, but the governent will force a new change 1 turn before you could manually do it, so you are stuck in a never ending dictatorship. Bug may be ?
Pros -
-I love the battle system. So many games waste their time with RTS type battles. ES 2 actually has a battle system that feels different. The battle system need to have some stuff added, but I like the general idea. For those who have never played, the battles are played by giving your units general orders before the battle then you start the battle and watch it being played out with no interaction of the player. The battles are setup like sailing ships shooting broadsides at each other (dont worry its not just broadsides).
- I like the UI. The UI is pretty friendly, an functions well. There is a lot to take in, but I like a game with some complexity. It responds smoothly too. I would attribute the smooth UI to good programing (my computer is NOT a top of the line system).
Wishlist of improvements -
- Get pirates under control. Make pirate bases. Do not just have pirates spawn out of nowhere. I wouldnt mind if pirates traveled across voids and avoided jump route sometimes.
- Add other objects to solar systems. As of now there are blackholes and asteroid belts, but they are by themselves, in systems without planets, and dont really play a function in the game. I would like to see improvements (buildings) on the solar system level. Developing asteroid belts, space stations (military, research, housing).
- More random events. The game has a mission mechanic, but there needs to be a lot more missions and random events. I think some disasters would be interesting.
- Ship battles need some improvement. The routes the ships take in a battle are too ridgid. There are sometimes that a more experienced commander should change the plan to counter the enemy's moves. I would also like to see the maneuvers in battles have a bigger impact in battles, not just arbitrary bonus given at the start of battles.
- Ship battle could use some graphical improvements. I think some smoke, debris, and ship hulls would make the battles more interesting. As of now, a ship gets shot up then it explodes and disappears.
-Action cam for the ship battles needs to be zoomed out some.

I felt the need to beat the game before I wrote a review on it just so I could get a full-scale view on it. I think I've put about 27 hours into the game before I finally did beat it (and that's without any DLC), so if you're looking for a long game that is worth your money, then L.A. Noire should definitely be considered.
You play as Cole Phelps, a war veteran that has returned to the States to enlist as a police officer in Los Angeles. Throughout the game, you will solve cases by collecting evidence around crimescenes, conducting interviews on suspects or witnesses, and driving around the city. Lots and LOTS of driving (Since driving will take up a large chunk of time, the game allows you to "fast Travel" to the selected area by holding "E" next to the car). Every so often, you'll get promoted and moved to a different set of cases (Such as Arson, Homicide, and *Motor Crime*). *I'm not familiar with what Motor Crime is known under*
Phelps' life in the war is shown through flashbacks between each case, slowly placing the parts to make a giant picture.
The gameplay is pretty simple:  You are assigned a case and you must piece together the clues to solve it.
L.A. Noire offers many features that aren't availible in other detective/mystery games. First, the map. L.A. Noire is a gigantic free-roam map (you'll mainly be driving) that takes a LONG time to drive from one side to the other, even going 80 mph. The city is filled, and I mean FILLED with AI life that walks or drives along through the city, making it feel like an actual city. Many of the places on the map are real places or based on real places that were/are in Los Angeles as well.
Another feature that I must mention is the interrogation. When you interrogate a person, you will ask them a question, to which they will respond with an answer. You then must decide if they are telling the truth, if you doubt them, or if they are lying (and you can prove that they are lying). You can decide these based on evidence you had found at a crime scene and by looking at the amazing facial expressions the character emits. For example, if a character is staring straight at you while talking, they're probably telling the truth, while if a character keeps avoiding eye contact, you might want to push for more information.
The facial expressions in the game are spectacular and the mouth-to-voice dialog is spot-on. Yes, they deserved their own little two-sentence paragraph right here, that's how good they are.
I got 27 hours out of the campaign and bought it while it was on sale for $10. After playing, I know that I would have bought it for the full price, due to the well-planned and just delicate features that the game highlights.
I must mention one bug that I had with the game...at times, the game would run slow. Most of the time, it ran smoothly and I had no problem with it, but at times, (when Rockstar was busy perhaps) the game would be slightly laggy. Not enough to make the game unplayable, but enough to be quite annoying. Fortunately, if I left and came back a few hours later, I would experience no lag.
Finally, I want to promote the different action there is. Often while working a case, you'll be driving and get a call over the radio to respond to a street crime, essentially a side mission. There are many different types of action you will face in the game. There are car chases, police shootouts, tracking missions (missions where you follow the suspect without being seen), running-for-your-life-missions, and many more.
Overall, I give the game a 9/10.

L.A. Noire is a detective game, simple as that. If you're looking for another shoot everything rampage game like GTA just because this game is made by Rockstar then this is not the game for you. Sure there is shooting, but you won't be allowed to kill everyone in sight, running people over will affect your case rating etc.
Personally, I love the setting of the game, the late 40s jazz theme mixed with golden age Hollywood as well as a classic noir feel makes for a great mix, but while the storytelling is good, it's not all there. The story feels a bit like it's jumping around without finishing everything off, Rockstar gathered enough story for a movie, but not a 20 hour game. Because of this you will be left with extra things that feel like they are just there to fill up an hour of your time and parts of the story that are never properly concluded. This being said, the story has some great parts towards the second half of the game and does a great job 80% of the time, however the ending will feel incomplete.
It's fun to drive around and using your siren to move people out of the way is great. The car chases are exciting at first but end up being repetitive, as with all the chases. Shootouts feel this way too and there are one or two that will feel boring. The combat tends to feel stiff from time to time. For an open world game it is very linear and the free roam mode itself actually takes some working out to access. Street crimes are fun to attend to and interrogations are challeging. The clue finding in the game is brilliant and walking around the crime scenes never gets old although you will quickly work out the set structure to finding all the clues.
The sound in the game makes for great immersion, no complaints here really. The hint sounds at crime sounds can be turned off if they make the game too easy and the whole feel of the sirens and the radio really sells the 40s atmosphere.
The facial expressions are the best part about the graphics, I didn't notice too many hiccups in the graphics and if I did they didn't distract from the game. The faces of people look incredibly lifelike and all the other graphics are good too. The sunny setting of Los Angeles adds a bright feeling to the game.
While you do have the option to replay your cases to get all clues and perfect your interrogation this game is likely to be one you will only play the story of once, it's still fun to drive around and do street crimes but the cases tend to be something that's best as a one time thing.
Overall this game is great fun and a nice step away from GTA while still keeping to the Rockstart format. It feels fresh but also familiar. The graphics look very good for a game that came out in 2011. You will feel very immersed in the time period through use of sound and surroundings. The open world side has something to be desired and Los Angeles doesn't exactly feel as alive as GTA 4's Liberty City or Watch Dog's Chicago, it doesn't have much of a personality, the characters do. If you're looking for a good open world game, this isn't it, if you're looking for a good story with a mix of puzzle and regular shoot/drive gameplay and well designed characters then this is it.

UPDATE : So I thought I should give a second chance to understand it in more detail; nevermind that ..... money resources poping to negative values (bug > causing bankruptcy) suddenly when the upkeep of fleets is no where near the current deposit. Pirates teaming into 6 ship fleets and attacking my system blockading ship while there is a turn race going on with another AI faction (about colonizing the system first)..... this is cheap ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t gameplay. I would really love to get a refund if it hadn't taken 8 hours to see all the problems with the game...... AVOID THIS.... its not going to get better even after EA.......
Original Review:  A lot of balance issues, the system has pitfalls about construction times and population management (which effect your military and thus your effective strategy)... Some stratetegic minerals needed for constructing high tier weapons can only be found on enemy territory thus forcing you to use low tier weapons (even though you have researched higher tiers).
The upgrades to military ships are not updated to existing fleets or ships; you need to either build your own ship blueprints with the new upgrades (pay huge amount of money again??) and then re-build a fleet (more time and money ??). There is not even an "update fleet for this amount of resource" option.
Hero's level up very slowly. Political influence is basically worthless against war / cold war enemy AI; you can "praise talk" your way into peace but relations dwindle far too fast to make it effective. Also influential things like bribe, assasinations, sanctions and uprisings are not implemented (at least to my knowledge). Scientific research is only for colonization; it does not effect other things like economy / trade, political / empire or military trees.
Ability to build strong fleets by smart ship construction strategy is negated due to "commander points" which limit your ability to merge fleets together. There is an unnecessary artificial difficulty here which makes space ship combat dull and unbalanced... Battle cards are limited to a few options which doesnt make a huge difference.
There are also artificial things which in my opinion makes the AI look cheap.... for example pirate faction creates multiple blockades to your high resource producing systems when you go to war with another faction. There is no option to hire those pirates to go and attack a system (a trading or influential strategy) but since the AI knows there is a huge upkeep when using military fleets....so to drain money and man power  the AI builds blockades using "Neutral  Factions" like pirates instead of using the resources available to the war declared factions.
There are also performance problems; sometimes waiting a turn to end takes forever. And UI screens like tech trees and planetary close ups cause stutters and laggy screen movements (creating instances causes issues probably or they stream it from a server which causes the lag, I didnt check).
TL, DR; Beutiful graphics and clean Ui; poor performance and unbalanced design with some cheap difficulty tricks. I would wait for it to exit EA before thinking of buying.

I severely dislike this game so far, but it may be too early to tell.
The biggest problem with Endless Space 2 (ES2) as a sequel to Endless Space 1 (ES1), that it's a totally different game.
It's kind of FUBAR, in my opinion.
A lot of features that were present in ES1 that made the game spectacular are not present in ES2 and 'never' will be according to chats with developers on their forums.
What ES1 had (to name a view):
- Intuitive design: menu was easy to click through, easy happiness/finance slider.
- 'Free' ship design: you could load up your ships however you want it to a certain degree.
- 'Free' faction design: you had a lot of freedom to customize your faction traits.
- Combat choices: you had combat choices for your fleet, either auto-resolve or in 'real-time'.
- 'Free' research tree choices: research whatever you want and when.
Right now, none of that stuff above is in the current ES2 game, instead:
- We have a convoluted interface, totally different from ES1 and not intuitive at all.
- Ship design freedom is nerfed. You have fixed slots now for fixed components.
- Faction design isn't implemented yet, but I predict they will nerf this as well. With for example a maximum of traits you can pick.
- Hardly any combat choices now, severely nerfed. Also the option to insert commands in 'real-time' is removed. In other words, there is only auto-resolve, no choice anymore.
- Restrictions in the research tree wherever you go.
So, big thumbs down. They added a lot of new stuff, like politics. Great.
Forced Truce. Great.
But the game is still in alpha. Too early to tell whether things will change and whether ES2 is still enjoyable without my favourite key features as I mentioned above.

Anything you publish from now on is a NO BUY for me.
2017/05/31 - The latest patch was a proof that Ampliture listens to the community. The "Lesson Learned" blog post is a good description of what we (supporters of the Endless series from the start) felt with this botched release. This patch solves several of the most pressing concerns, most of those I brought up in my previous reviews, and is a clear declaration of intent from Amplitude in the right direction. I unfortunately cannot *quite* switch back to recommended. Fool me twice and all that... Some notable performance issues and major balance issues remain, and I cannot (anymore) give a goodwill rating. I will update my rating when those are fixed.
2017/05/28 - The game has now been released, and I have to flip my review YET AGAIN to NOT RECOMMENDED. The game was released with major bugs, that render the game unplayable (stop responding to commands, an issue already widely reported during early access) around turn 100. This is about halway through a play on a large map, and when things start getting interesting. Since this bug _came back_ after being seemingly fixed (or was it?) this is starting to make me lose confidence in the dev's ability to right this boat.
2017/04/10 - The game has now matured into a playable and enjoyable RTS. There are still issues with the faction balance, and while the recent redesign of the military research and combat balance have made that aspect of the game more intruiguing, it also comes with an increased difficulty to anticipate and read the results. In other words, combat is less boring, and more of a crapshoot. The stability issues that initially had led me to recommend not buying the game have been for the most part cleared up, expect for large maps, where playing beyond 100 turns is still an exercise in dodging random freezes.
2017/02/04 - RIGHT NOW, I cannot recommend purchasing this game. I loved Endless Space 1, I love the mechanics of Endless Space 2. But the stability is abysmal. Going past 50 turns without an unrecoverable crash is a challenge.

This game is another example of the infamous "one more turn" syndrome we knew and love from 4X games. Even in its Early Access stage, the game has delivered much, and already feels like a complete game in its own right (minus the obvious occasional bugs and sometimes incomplete texts or upcoming features)
With a simple yet deep gameplay, interesting smattering of lores there and there, numerous options to customise and manage your empire, and many more features, the game has many to offer for 4X players out there.
Pros
+ Many features to explore
+ Lots of lores and interesting stories to accompany the events and build up the world
+ Beautiful artwork, and graphic, especially the event artworks and the ship designs
+ Equally beautiful soundtrack to help you sink to the game
+ Ship and hero customization, with each hero type different from one another in skillset and bonus and each faction having different slots for each ship class. For example, the United Empire's explorer has more weapons slot but less support module slot than the Horatio's.
+ Senate system with political parties and ideologies behind them affected by recent events and the type of population(s) living in your empire
+ Each faction has unique quirks and playing styles, especially the Vodyani
+ Unpredictability, such as the damned space slugs stabbing you in the back after turns of lucrative trade and peace
Cons
- Still in Early Access, so it's obvious that there are still upcoming features not implemented
- (some) Bugs there and there cos' it's still in Early Access
- Some mechanics can be confusing for the first time, for example the Manpower system used to invade star systems
- Be prepared to lose much of your time, cos' the game'll absorb you like many other 4X games
- If you don't like sci-fi, the setting obviously might not appeal to you (Not for me of course lol)

Alot more hours than I thought were put into finishing this game.  I'll have to say first that it is one of the best examples of storytelling in gaming that I've seen in awhile.  There are certainly one-dimensional characters that pepper the landscape throughout, but a decent attempt is made to delve into the primary characters.  Graphics were superb, the lifelikeness of people was really well done.  1940s LA is a sprawling landscape, however not as...interactive as a GTA type game might be.
The interface was easy to use, whether walking, driving or investigating.
I was somewhat put off with the resolution of the game initially, but then realized how much it fit with the whole theme.
Interrogation was not my strong suit and I found myself repeating parts several times to really figure out clues to their full extent.
Game length was not an issue....the story kept it from becoming too repetitive over time, but then again, I guess the job of being a detective can get to a point where it feels like that.  Solve one crime, another pops up.

This is my 2nd review for ES2. The first one was from before the first update, Now we are on update 2.  Much has changed since my previous review.
This game is good, really good.  There are a couple weak points to the game but it is still early access.  The overall game has so much depth, but the current battle system is just OK kind of just bleh.  I don't hate it, but just doesn't feel like there is much depth to it unlike the rest of the game.  Ground battles are cool, but I will probably skip over them more often than not.
Pros for the current game
- Improved tech tree, I really really like the new system. It is harder for newer players and can feel overwhelming because there is so much on the screen. However, once you get used to it, I definitely prefer the new tech tree.  It is more complex and also more interesting visually.
- The differences between the races is stunning.  All of them feel totally different than the rest.  The Sophons and the Horatio are probably the best races to start with because they are fairly straight forward.
- Interesting minor races and leaders(though I feel they are slightly too common mid to late game)
- The idea that managing systems is better than managing planets.. I cant stress how smart a move this is.. my biggest complaint about 4X games is the late game tedium.. having to micro manage 50 planets is NOT fun. Having to micro manage 13 systems is much simpler.
Cons
- The battles. This isn't a huge con, most of the rest of the game is great. This is probably the only major part of them game that is just OK.
- I suspect the cinematic approach to the space battles is permanent at this point.  So, since it is here to stay, I would like a smoother cinematic battle, the screens jumps around to much IMO.
- The descriptions for the different techs are kind of lacking. Sometimes hard to figure out what it actually does. Especially for a new person to the game.  I assume this will get better as the game advances and things become more permanent.
Overall this game in its current state (factoring In its early access) is a solid 9/10.  I believe this game will revolutionize the 4X genre.  Just please make the space battles more interesting!! Cant wait for the next 2 updates.
PS> the game is worth buying now I am having a blast in EA.

The game is fun, but it has a few issues.  As a console port the game is fixed at 30fps.  This is due in part to the special technology used to graphically capture actors’ face expressions.  The biggest problem that I have with the system is it sometimes sticks me at 25 FPS despite having a GTX 980 and plenty of headroom.  Overall, the graphics look pretty good and are satisfactory as long as it keeps running at 30fps.
The gameplay is good too.  The cars drive well; the gunplay is fun, I wish there was more of it.  The detective questioning can be aggravating.  If you challenge a witness’ statement as a lie you must present some evidence to prove it, sometimes there are multiple pieces of evidence that indicate they are lying but choosing the wrong one results in a failed question. When interrogating two suspects you may be forced to charge someone who you don’t think is guilty just because you failed one interrogation.  The last issue is that if you suspect someone of being the criminal you cannot actually go after them unless it is scripted in the story.
I have mixed feelings about the plot, they make Phelps do some very uncharacteristic things to progress the story and bring everything together.  However, the scams that the local government and business owners put together is interesting and clever.
Overall, I am not much of a fan of detective stories, shows, etc; but this game is fun and if they come out with a second one I will pick it up.

This was my first space themed 4X game and it seems to be awesome. Other grand scale 4X games I've played have been EU4 and HoI4, and I just gave up on them as they felt like working and extremely time-consuming. However, in Endless Space 2 the UI is so handy (and pretty) that it is possible to get a grip of the game very fast while there is still a lot of depth to the game. The atmosphere of the game is attractive and I got addicted to pushing the next turn button to see what cool things happens next. Quests, heros, events, science and the variety in factions all create immersive experience of the game.
The UI seems to be improving (e.g. new tech tree) but some kind of better tutorial is still needed to introduce us newcommers to the game. I got the hang of it pretty well by looking at some tutorial video but there is still so much variables and parameters I have no clue about.
There is still some wonky stuff going on in the Alpha version and some that I'm not sure if it's working the way it should be. For example engaging enemy ships seems to be somehow off limits if they are not sitting still in a solar system on your turn, and this makes dealing with the pirate ships extremely difficult as they roam all over the place but do not stay still to be available for engaging with a proper fleet.
I like that the space battle system is a cinematic video instead of some kind of RTS battle. On the other hand the ground battle cinematics are very unimpressive with awkward holograms. Not a very big deal though as the core of the game is in managing your empire.

Tried it again for a few more hours. If you are looking for reasons why you may not like this game (even though many more do), here is a list of problems I encountered.
1. The objectives on the map can be confusing, especially in multiplayer - everything just moves so fast that there isn't time to get your bearings. Rushing to one objective after another is the norm and most of the time, I find myself getting carried to the end of the mission before I know what actually happened.
2. It's hard to tell apart the enemies and allies. I find myself shooting at allies as often as I do enemies. I know, the experts of the game will probably just say "git gud", but I am coming here with little background of the game and it was really hard to tell apart what's what.
3. Mods are unintuitive. Stacks of them. I upgraded some. Sold off duplicate mods only to find out I sold off everything. That UI system here is really messy. How stuff works, how it interacts - not explained at all.
4. You need to watch a lot of YouTube videos just to understand each component of the game.
TLDR: I wanted to like this game. But the UI doesn't explain anything and trying to understand the game in-game is impossible. I tried watching youtube tutorials, but in the end, it just felt like too much work to just get into the game.
It's a good game. Just not for everyone.

Sword swingin', shield bashin', axe throwin' fun. Let's get down to business though.
The Pros
This game will satisfyingly fulfill your FPS medieval blood lusts. Battle is very, VERY weighty. If you land that blade into his shoulder, you'll feel it, he's gonna feel it.

The Cons
The game is very much based on your skill level, there is no great equalizer here. I list it as a con to tell new players to prepare to practice, and to expect to be slaughtered for the first couple games.
The game changes after rank 15. Before that you have access to beginner servers, which is always fun to fight equally skilled players. After that you'll begin to run into people who's skill levels are golfs between you and them. I always see it as a nice practice. Its always satisfying blocking one of their camera twisting moves, having them look at you like a monster for a second, and then killing you. I see that as some sort of reward, at least.
Its a fun game, play it with a friend and you'll have a good time.

The control scheme is utter trash (In fairness, nothing can compare with the system developed by Taleworlds for Mount & Blade, but nothing should. Just copy that scheme. There's no shame in admitting that their system is perfect. Your game should have merits of its own that draw me to it). This is my main quarrel with the game, and normally it would only be a minor inconvenience, but in a fast-paced combat game it really matters more than anything else.
All blocks are omnidirectional, even if performed using nothing but a melee weapon instead of a shield. Not only does it make it look bizarre when you block an incoming stab by raising your sword above your head, or parry a slash by proudly displaying your poleaxe, but it makes for a less interesting combat experience. It means that blocks are simply a matter of timing and looking vaguely in the direction of your opponent's weapon. This is not a hard task to master, and you will quickly be able to block proficiently and extend duels by a considerable amount of time. I've also never seen a game with the "Press Q to Feint attack mechanic," that was genius. Here's an idea: can't I just press right control to have the AI play the infernal game for me? Could you really not work out a way of stopping the player character from completing an attack? Every single time I click attack, I have to completely follow through with the strike. There's no possible way I could manually feint?
Everything feels sluggish and warped. Like I'm experiencing the world through the defective imagination of a Down's Syndrome sufferer. It seems petty, but holy christ, Torn Banner. If you cannot make arms move in a realistic fashion in front of the camera, why are you even bothering to make a full game? This is normally the kind of thing that doesn't bother me much, but if you look at how your hands move as you're carrying a one-handed weapon, it's very clear that both of them are tracing out a sine wave at intervals 90 degrees apart from eachother, and at just the right frequency that it's so unrealistic I want to tear out my own eyes.
The graphics themselves (barring animations) look decent. HOWEVER, you won't be able to see them. I think I have a decent enough graphics card, I've certainly run more taxing games than this should be for hours on end without issue. However, if I put my graphics preset on anything higher than minimum settings, this game crashes every 10 minutes. The graphics are not that intense. Chalk this one up to simple developer laziness.
"Yeah, the latest build runs fine on my NVIDIA Titan test machine. I'm sure it'll work fine for everyone with a middle-tier AMD card, just commit the patch."
And that segways nicely into my more general criticism of this game: it seems half-finished. Everything about it screams that it's a prototype. Everything looks so rough and handles so bulkily. Going back to my point about the feint mechanic, it just seems like laziness. Everything looks and feels rushed. This could pass as an alpha, close to being a beta. Not as a finished product, and certainly not a product to be purchased for $25. Do like I did and wait for it to be on sale for $5 or less.

L.A. Noire has an excellent setting, Los Angeles in the 1940's, and everything the game has to offer feels very true to this setting.
The story of the game is very well written, offering insight to life in the 1940's overall as well as focusing even more on the lives of cops, crooks, and war veterans.
L.A. Noire's graphics are excellent. Even though the game's a few years old by now, it still looks spectacular, and nothing in the game is boring to look at.
All the animations look great and it's worth to note that there haven't been better facial animations in video games after this game.
From the sound effects to the songs and shows on the car radio as well as the music that's been carefully selected to feel right in different situations, everything in this game sounds just right.
There are gameplay elements that will instantly feel very familiar to those who've played any of Rockstar's games before. But there are also many unique features that this game has to offer.
The game is divided into different cases during which the players are also able to focus on different side quests like dealing with street crimes and finding different cars and landmarks.
Questioning the suspects and other people of the world is done very well. Although, I have to say that on a few occasions, I felt that the right choices were a bit surprising to say the least.
My playtime of 38 or so hours includes just one playthrough with all the DLC cases included. I also did over half of the street crime missions and unlocked more that a third of the vehicles the game had to offer.
I did come across a few bugs during my playthrough, but they were mostly graphical stuff that disappeared fairly quickly. I also experienced some stuttering every now and again, and the game did freeze two or three times during the almost 40-hour long playthrough. However, I feel that these had little impact to how much I enjoyed the game itself.
The game does require for the player to log in to a Rockstar Social Club account, but it is possible to choose a "Default" account for which the player doesn't have to provide any personal information and which requires no email verification or the like.

This was my first space themed 4X game and it seems to be awesome. Other grand scale 4X games I've played have been EU4 and HoI4, and I just gave up on them as they felt like working and extremely time-consuming. However, in Endless Space 2 the UI is so handy (and pretty) that it is possible to get a grip of the game very fast while there is still a lot of depth to the game. The atmosphere of the game is attractive and I got addicted to pushing the next turn button to see what cool things happens next. Quests, heros, events, science and the variety in factions all create immersive experience of the game.
The UI seems to be improving (e.g. new tech tree) but some kind of better tutorial is still needed to introduce us newcommers to the game. I got the hang of it pretty well by looking at some tutorial video but there is still so much variables and parameters I have no clue about.
There is still some wonky stuff going on in the Alpha version and some that I'm not sure if it's working the way it should be. For example engaging enemy ships seems to be somehow off limits if they are not sitting still in a solar system on your turn, and this makes dealing with the pirate ships extremely difficult as they roam all over the place but do not stay still to be available for engaging with a proper fleet.
I like that the space battle system is a cinematic video instead of some kind of RTS battle. On the other hand the ground battle cinematics are very unimpressive with awkward holograms. Not a very big deal though as the core of the game is in managing your empire.
The Games2gether is a brilliant idea and some of the great ideas from the community are implemented to the game. The game is really developing into the right direction. It will be quite the achievement if in launch the game will already be well-balanced across the board (i.e. factions, science, diplomacy, battle strength).
I haven't played enough to give an opinion on the AI or how well the diplomacy works. If those work well then those add to the immersion and this would be just a stunning game.

Paradox lures its customers with promise of grand strategy (which it delivers!!), only to then reveal to its users that its grand strategy was incomplete.  There is more behind the curtain.  A DLC is released at a price that is well beyond what a DLC should cost. Year by year, DLC by DLC, the grand strategist spends money he should have spent for education, clothes, heating, electricity, a family... just to chase the perfect version of the grand strategy game.  Tease by tease, piece by piece, never complete, always with a hint of something more to come, Paradox's soul crushing DLC savages the general public.  Never mind novel torts relating to emotional distress, the lawyers of today are unearthing new causes of action altogether caused by the societal and social ill that is Paradox DLC.
First the grand strategist was told his grand strategy was incomplete because he had only played as Christians.  Then as Muslims.  Then Jews were playable.  Then Mongols, Indians, Africans. The recent interface change was a good move, much easier on the eyes.
Plenty of combat styles to choose from, 4 different classes with different weapons within it. People will tell you that a certain class is the way to go, but I've seen an equal amount of ownage from each of them.
The game is very much based on your skill level.
The Cons
The game is very much based on your skill level, there is no great equalizer here. I list it as a con to tell new players to prepare to practice, and to expect to be slaughtered for the first couple games.
The game changes after rank 15. Before that you have access to beginner servers, which is always fun to fight equally skilled players. After that you'll begin to run into people who's skill levels are golfs between you and them. I always see it as a nice practice. Its always satisfying blocking one of their camera twisting moves, having them look at you like a monster for a second, and then killing you. I see that as some sort of reward, at least.
Its a fun game, play it with a friend and you'll have a good time.

The control scheme is utter trash (In fairness, nothing can compare with the system developed by Taleworlds for Mount & Blade, but nothing should. Just copy that scheme. There's no shame in admitting that their system is perfect. Your game should have merits of its own that draw me to it). This is my main quarrel with the game, and normally it would only be a minor inconvenience, but in a fast-paced combat game it really matters more than anything else.
All blocks are omnidirectional, even if performed using nothing but a melee weapon instead of a shield. Not only does it make it look bizarre when you block an incoming stab by raising your sword above your head, or parry a slash by proudly displaying your poleaxe, but it makes for a less interesting combat experience. It means that blocks are simply a matter of timing and looking vaguely in the direction of your opponent's weapon. This is not a hard task to master, and you will quickly be able to block proficiently and extend duels by a considerable amount of time. I've also never seen a game with the "Press Q to Feint attack mechanic," that was genius. Here's an idea: can't I just press right control to have the AI play the infernal game for me? Could you really not work out a way of stopping the player character from completing an attack? Every single time I click attack, I have to completely follow through with the strike. There's no possible way I could manually feint?
Everything feels sluggish and warped. Like I'm experiencing the world through the defective imagination of a Down's Syndrome sufferer. It seems petty, but holy christ, Torn Banner. If you cannot make arms move in a realistic fashion in front of the camera, why are you even bothering to make a full game? This is normally the kind of thing that doesn't bother me much, but if you look at how your hands move as you're carrying a one-handed weapon, it's very clear that both of them are tracing out a sine wave at intervals 90 degrees apart from eachother, and at just the right frequency that it's so unrealistic I want to tear out my own eyes.
The graphics themselves (barring animations) look decent. HOWEVER, you won't be able to see them. I think I have a decent enough graphics card, I've certainly run more taxing games than this should be for hours on end without issue. However, if I put my graphics preset on anything higher than minimum settings, this game crashes every 10 minutes. The graphics are not that intense. Chalk this one up to simple developer laziness.
"Yeah, the latest build runs fine on my NVIDIA Titan test machine. I'm sure it'll work fine for everyone with a middle-tier AMD card, just commit the patch."
And that segways nicely into my more general criticism of this game: it seems half-finished. Everything about it screams that it's a prototype. Everything looks so rough and handles so bulkily. Going back to my point about the feint mechanic, it just seems like laziness. Everything looks and feels rushed. This could pass as an alpha, close to being a beta. Not as a finished product, and certainly not a product to be purchased for $25. Do like I did and wait for it to be on sale for $5 or less.

Being a regular gamer (any genre) since the era of Pong, I really don't want to know just how many hours of my life I spent gaming.  But these last few years, I was kinda getting bored of modern day computer games.  Lots of FPS with great graphics but zero originality.  RPG's started too look dull (do quest, acquire experience, gain skills, ...).  Some nice indie games with a great art style, but these typically didn''t have much replay value.  And strategy games with all their micromanagement started to feel like a task, rather than a form of entertainment.
What I was really looking for was a great immersive game of diplomacy and intrigue.  A game that made you forget it was a game.  A game where your actions would have an impact on the outcome, but where you never had full control (either by skilfully smashing buttons, or by thorougly understanding the mechanics/numbers behind the game).
And now I finally found it : Crusader Kings II.  Brilliant, and an all-time favourite already.
Update 26/03/2014 : Nearly 2 years later and I'm still pretty much enjoying this game.  Regular expansion packs, combined with a free major patch, manage to keep things interesting.  Although not entirely bug-free, especially shortly after the major expansions come out, I applaud Paradox for continueing to support and update this title.

Paradox lures its customers with promise of grand strategy (which it delivers!!), only to then reveal to its users that its grand strategy was incomplete.  There is more behind the curtain.  A DLC is released at a price that is well beyond what a DLC should cost.  But the grand strategist's save games are no longer compatible and he realises his game is incomplete without the new DLC areas, skins, music, mechanics, etc.
Year by year, DLC by DLC, the grand strategist spends money he should have spent for education, clothes, heating, electricity, a family... just to chase the perfect version of the grand strategy game.  Tease by tease, piece by piece, never complete, always with a hint of something more to come, Paradox's soul crushing DLC savages the general public.  Never mind novel torts relating to emotional distress, the lawyers of today are unearthing new causes of action altogether caused by the societal and social ill that is Paradox DLC.
First the grand strategist was told his grand strategy was incomplete because he had only played as Christians.  Then as Muslims.  Then Jews were playable.  Then Mongols, Indians, Africans.  Now Asians.  As the world grows the grand strategist gets closer to his dreams, and as the opium addict chasing the dragon, finds his wallet empty, his ambitions unrealised, his habit all consuming.

Ok I think it's about time I gave a review for this. I've been playing for about 3 months and I've got to say DE has put quite a bit of care into their game. It may not be up to par with some AAA titles but, I'd personally say it gives some a run for their money. I'm not going to compare this to Destiny or Destiny to this. They're unique and similar in many ways but this is about Warframe. When this game was first released I shunned it. I played it once around the time it was released and never picked it back up. A couple years went by and decided to download it again. When I launched it back up I immediately noticed the difference in the game from when it was first released. You now got a daily login reward for playing it each day. Amongst these packs came platinum discounts (in-game currency), boosters for resource in-game, free credits (other money), etc. One day upon login I received a platinum discount of 50% off. So I decided to spend a bit of cash and it helped with my progress in the game. When the game was first released it was so much of a grind I gave it no chance at all to change my mind about it. Now the game is easier for solo players, players who have families or other things to do besides play games all day. They added new enemy types, a heap of new weapons and frames to use. I really enjoyed the fact the everything in the game can be earned rather then bought, with plenty of hours to grind out that precious loot.
The combat seemed a bit more fluent/fluid. One thing I immediately noticed was the movement of the character, it was different than other games. Acrobatically flying through the air; get a running start, crouch slide, jump high into the air, do a second jump, latch onto a wall, shoot a couple enemies, jump off that wall onto another, wall run, jump off that wall, crouch slide again, melee strike an enemy and walk away like it was too easy.
Not all players are against paying and helping out developers. The ones who decide not to spend any money still enjoy the game because they like the game for what it is. The one problem I have with DE's F2P model is there is basically an incentive to spend real money on fake money, hidden behind "platinum" currency walls (in-game currency that is bought). I personally have spent money of the game as I don't like really grindy games and I also have a full time job. This has helped me tremendously progress in the game and not have to invest 100's of hours leveling up. Unfortunately these packs of currency aren't cheap and I usually wait til I get a daily login for 50% off or more. There are 24 ranks in the game as of right now. I am currently rank 17 almost 18 and have 320 hrs in the game. If I chose not to spend any money, that time would probably be doubled.
At first it seemed the game had no point besides going from planet to planet and clearing out missions. Sadly only 2 missions show the full capabilities of Digital Extremes love for their game. Those missions are The Second Dream and The War Within. Those two mission will say more about the game then anything else will. I hope they go more in depth or add more story later as it would be appreciate by myself and all fans of the game. With Warframe being F2P, DE has to focus on content rather than story. Have to keep players occupied or the game would die rather quickly. By the end of the year Digital Extremes will be releasing a brand new update and a whole new open world mmo style area called the Plains of Eidolon and it will add a whole lot more to the game. If you think you found your perfect weapon now, just wait til you can craft your own!
Overall I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys RNG or 3rd Person Shooting
