Original review:
Recommended for people who have already played Amplitude's other 4X titles (Endless Space, Endless Legend). If you're new to the franchise I would recommend buying the Amplitude bundle when it goes on sale instead, as you can get all the games plus DLC for about the price of this game. The reason I say this is because the game is currently in Early Access and as of this writing has no tutorial for those that are completely new to Amplitude's games, instead only explanations for stuff that's new in Endless Space 2. Important game mechanics such as FIDSI and Heroes are not explained and are crucial to victory of any type in any Amplitude 4X.
For those who are familiar with Endless Space/Legend, this is a good game that improves the mechanics of the previous two while adding new ones. As expected with an Early Access title it's a little rough around the edges and incomplete in some parts (no Era V science tree, for example) but still manages to be an enjoyable experience. I look forward to seeing what Amplitude has planned for the future and hope that the Vaulters return as a major faction.

Crusader Kings 2 is a grand strategy game set in the middle ages, that focuses more on diplomacy management rather than being a straight economy sim. In the game you play as a specific person in charge of maintaining your families line of succession, as opposed to playing as a specific nation. You have to create, maintain, and exploit relationships with other lords in order to ensure that when you die, and begin playing as your heir, you will inherit all of your previous lands and carry on your families legacy. While the UI is very intuitive and the tutorials detailed, it was still necessary for me (as someone not familiar with grand strategy games) to watch a few hours of various Let's Play videos in order to have a grasp on how to approach the game. With that said, CK2 is tremendously fun and very engaging to anyone looking to play a strategy game with more of a diplomatic focus, rather than a economy/spreadsheet focus.

L. A. Noire is one of the best police games out there. I'd love to see a modern game use some of the same ideas that were used for making this game a great "detective" game.
The cases in L. A. Noire can be solved in slightly different ways, resulting in slightly different consequences through out the game, and the mechanics of the game function almost flawlessly. Combat, chases, interrogations, looking for evidence and just driving around in classic GTA 4 style (the game uses the same engine) is all entertaining enough on it's own to warrant a 5/10 rating.
The game also has a great story, albeit very tragic (hence the title), and can at times feel like it's almost mocking how crazy Los Angeles is/was (no offense, it's just a very different city) in best GTA style, but it feels very serious.
The characters in the game, and especially the motion capture that was used to get their facial expressions just right makes dialogues truly amazing.
One of the few tap based games I would truly recommend.

This is an excellent, unconventional strategy game. Unlike other strategy games, your goal in Crusader Kings 2 isn't so much to conquer anything- though that can be a goal- as it is to ensure your dynasty's survival against complex intrigue, Muslim invaders, and other countries who have claims to your land. Powering this game is a complex dynasty simulator that simulates the actions of every single dynasty and the Middle East, creating an alternate history that you are just another part of. The complex interface will put people off, but the most rewarding part of the game is digging through the masssive amount of information the game provides to discover the motives and stories of your rivals and allies. This game naturally creates intriguing stories of ambition, assasination and sister-♥♥♥♥ing that rivals A Song of Ice and Fire. In fact, there's even a great mod that lets your play in the world of A Game of Thrones!

I played this game at launch and it was amazing. The melee combat was unique (to my knowledge) and the game was beautiful and fun... but most of all, the *community* was phenomenal! In nearly every game of Last Team Standing, when a single opponent remained on one team, the opponents would line up and honorably duel him one by one. People lined up in a phalanx formation and fought as a single combat unit. Archers kept pressure on the front line fighters and crossbowmen kept pressure on enemy archers.
Fast-forward to today. The game is prettier - nothing wrong with that. The gameplay is *different* after numerous "balance" patches - that could be good or bad. But the greatest thing about this game, the community, has turned into an absolute cesspool of bottom-feeding, Call of Duty playing, trolling, idiotic brats.
After returning to the game for some several months away, it is painfully difficult to find even a single player in a game that will fight alongside you and play tactfully - that's assuming they aren't intentionally teamkilling you, or intentionally teamkilling you then blaming *you* for teamkilling *them* even though you didn't touch them then immediately initiating a votekick and getting the rest of the players to votekick you because they cried foul first.
The Verdict: This perfectly fine game has been utterly ruined to the point of unplayability by its terrible community. The League of Legends community is less toxic than this filth.

So this game is an interesting one, being known for being the first game to use facial motion capture from actors and also being a game that got really hyped up before release only to end up bankrupting it's creator Team Bondi. This game was ambitious and to be honest it's a shame it didn't do better. It didn't quite live up to the hype but it's still a good game.
You play Cole Phelps, a LAPD detective and decorated WWII vet with the game set in LA in 1947. The basic premise of the game is that you investigate various crimes and interrogate and question witnesses and suspects. So you'll show up to a crime scene and have to explore it looking for clues as to what happened and clues that might link to a suspect. Once you have your evidence you can question suspects.
And this is where the facial capture comes into play. When your questioning a suspect they'll give you an answer to your question and then you can choose to believe they're telling the truth, doubt them or prove they're lying using evidence. You have to watch their facial expressions to figure it out as when they're lying they'll look visibly nervous or irritated. Guess correctly and they might spill some more useful info like a new suspect or evidence.
It is a really interesting feature although it can be a bit difficult especially when choosing between doubt and lie. Also get it wrong and Cole just starts shouting at them for no reason, like he's some bipolar idiot.
As for the rest of the game, well firstly the recreation of 1940's LA is brilliant. The look and feel of the city is amazing but   the big open world of LA is never fully utilized in the game and having this big beautiful city, most of which you'll never explore nor have reason to, feels a bit wasteful.
You also have street crimes which come up as your driving between locations which are useful for getting experience points to rank up but get repetitive as they are all some combination of either pursuing a criminal or shooting them.
The big feature of the game,the facial motion capture, is great and this game has probably the most detailed faces in any game. It also features a lot of familar actors from various tv shows, although sometimes the acting is a bit over the top but still good for the most part.
The Good:
- investigating crime scenes and questioning people is really enjoyable
- the 1940's LA in the game looks and feels amazing and authentic
- facial motion capture looks great
- Most of the cases are enjoyable and interesting
- Pretty good story
The Bad:
- a big open city that feels like a waste as there's little reason to explore most of it
- street crime missions can be repetitive (although not compulsory)
-combat sections aren't very impressive
Overall this game is a victim of it's own hype but don't let that put you off. It's still a great game and worth getting particularly if your the type that likes crime thrillers. I'd also recommend by the complete edition so you get the all the DLC cases as well. All the DLC cases are good, particularly Nicholsons Electroplating so it's worth paying a little extra for them. This game gets a 8/10 from me.

The complex interface will put people off, but the most rewarding part of the game is digging through the masssive amount of information the game provides to discover the motives and stories of your rivals and allies. Warframe is a fast-paced free to play third person co-op action game.
In this game you operate so-called warframes, basically space ninjas with special abilities. You parkour all over the place, completing your objectives while killing bad guys in a multitude of ways. It's fun.
The first thing you'll realize when you get the hang of Warframe is that there's a lot of content available. Mainly because the game has been getting frequent hotfixes and an impressive amount of major content updates since its release date. Secondly because the game doesn't shy away from complexity. Warframe is surprisingly in-depth.
It's difficult to give an unambiguous description of the core gameplay. You generally go from planet to planet completing levels and quests while collecting resources to craft your arsenal and mods that make your character, weapons and companions stronger. A big part of the game is crafting equipment and leveling it up. The first time you level a piece of equipment up to the level cap, you'll gain Mastery Points. These level up your Mastery Rank. The Mastery Rank is an indicator of one's experience with the game. In essence, it's your account level. A higher MR means you'll be regarded as a more seasoned player. This incentivizes switching up your loadout as you progress through the game, leveling everything to the level cap at least once. This keeps things fresh. However, you don't have to switch up your equipment, if you don't want to. You could also stick with a certain setup and increase its effectiveness in certain areas through resetting its level, which indirectly increases the amount of mods you can install. What separates Warframe from others in the same genre is the choices it gives you when it comes to your playstyle and progression.
You can blindly progress through the game if you want to, or you can invest time into knowing how the damage system works and mod your equipment to take advantage of it. The way damage and modding works heavily rewards the player for taking the time to understand the ins and outs of its mechanics.
Once you have a certain build in mind, or you just want a specific weapon, warframe or companion, you'll have to start farming to get the stuff you need for it. This can be quite a grindfest, but fortunately this is something Warframe really nailed. The grind never feels unfair. It doesn't take a stupid amount of time to get what you want in this game. Sometimes you'll even end up with more things than you need, which you can sell or use later. Admittedly, from an outsider's perspective, this game just looks like a boring grind. However, the fast-paced action-focused gameplay, combined with the satisfaction of building your arsenal, more than makes up for it. This doesn't mean everyone will like it. If you hate grinding, you'll hate this game, regardless of the gameplay.
Of course, because Warframe is a free to play title, you also have the option to immediately acquire items in the game with real money. The game's premium currency, called Platinum, can be used to outright buy the items you want from the in-game store. Fortunately, the business model is another thing Warframe really nailed. If you have the time to grind, you're much better off doing that. As mentioned earlier: the grind never feels unfair. You never feel like you're being forced to spend real money on the game. If you don't have a lot of free time, you can just buy Platinum or Prime Access and get true value for your money. Furthermore, Platinum can be traded. This means the players can just trade items for the premium currency to buy stuff from the in-game store without spending a penny.
In short: If you like action games and don't mind grinding, you should definitely try this one out.

This is an excellent, unconventional strategy game. Unlike other strategy games, your goal in Crusader Kings 2 isn't so much to conquer anything- though that can be a goal- as it is to ensure your dynasty's survival against complex intrigue, Muslim invaders, and other countries who have claims to your land. Powering this game is a complex dynasty simulator that simulates the actions of every single dynasty and the Middle East, creating an alternate history that you are just another part of. The complex interface will put people off, but the most rewarding part of the game is digging through the masssive amount of information the game provides to discover the motives and stories of your rivals and allies. This game naturally creates intriguing stories of ambition, assasination and sister-♥♥♥♥ing that rivals A Song of Ice and Fire. In fact, there's even a great mod that lets your play in the world of A Game of Thrones!

I've persoanlly owned this game since late 2015. I was around before Kangaroos, Bolas, and TEK Tier. Ark and I have had our ups and downs. From crashes, bugs, server rollbacks, lost tames, hackers and lack of dev support. BUT, I also had the oppurtunity to see everything as it was released. We learned to tame things before the info was available on the wiki, outsmarted people that meant us harm and made some really cool friends.
Now, if youre looking for a PvP experience, the first thing that you need to understand is that there is a meta, just like every other game. The second thing you need to understand is that this game can be difficult when you first start and 90% of the community does not take well to whining or requests from people asking others to play the game for them. You will be chased and shot and hunted. However, this is a survival game and you should expect that.
PvE? It's a little safe for my taste, but it's fun nonetheless. Observing dinos and weather patterns and learning to adapt is survival at the core.
Personally, I played on official servers and private servers. I've been at the top and at the bottom. What I found the most fun of all, was joining a server with nothing, and creating something that was mine in my own way. Sure we could follow the meta game, but all already know how it plays out. It's who has more resources than who. I could go tame a max level rex and breed it until the damn thing is a perfect killing machine. But for me, I found the most fun hopping around the server on my frog, dodging dangers and taking advantage of what was available to me at the time.
If you're looking for something you can "win" this is not the game for you. If you're going to quit because Wildcard won't give you your stuff back after it was eaten by a wild dino or raided by another tribe, this game is not for you. If you expect an immediate response from the devs, this game is not for you. You WILL lose things, you WILL die, and you WILL get upset.

You start off when colonizing, to send a million people from Planet A to Planet B, over time that million people will become a billion turning an outpost into a full fledge colony and will take on aspects of an city-wide planet when you reach a trillion, although that could happen earlier or later depending on size. So technically on size of the planet, there is a point where it becomes a colony and a point where it becomes a city-wide planet, earlier the smaller it is and later the bigger it is.
* Moons - What is so problematic with moons in this series of games? Moons can come in the same flavors as planets, therefore you should have moons around gas giants or large ocean planets that could be colonized before the larger entity is colonized.
* Solar Systems - Too simplistic. I don't think these developers know how a solar system should be designed. Solar systems come in regions. Lets look at our solar system as an example. We have Inner Planets Regions which contains Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, then we have the Asteroid Belt which contains the Dwarf Planet Ceres (the Asteroid Belt is a transition between the habital region of the solar system where water can be found in its liquid form and where it is found primarily as ice), then we have the outer planets regions (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune), and then we have the Kuiper Belt (which contains many dwarf planets, but we can narrow it down to just four, the most recognized is Pluto).
* Sectors - Now if anyone has ever played Mass Effect, you would know it is not really systems are united together throughout the galaxy, it is sectors with a particular solar system that harbors a device that allows one to travel from sector to sector. And this makes sense the galaxy is so insanely big with billions of stars. if a Sector has 500 stars and there were 200 sectors, then you have 10,000 stars (but at least that likely to be a galaxy, a very small galaxy, but the best you could probably do with our primitive technology).
* Stars - there is not that much diversity in stars. No Pulsars, Blackholes or anything else in that regard.
So here is how I would improve Endless Space 2, so that is fits what every space strategist would want. If you want to beat Paradox and compete with Stellaris, here is what you gotta do. You have to think of a build up one world to a solar system to many solar systems to a complete sectors, to many sectors until you get to the galactic stage. That is how civilizations in this universe or in any (actually tangible) universe progress. So have a world (planet or moon), you are in what is called the interplanetary phase of developments, so technologies would fit in this category, although it would come to reason that would transition out of the planetary level in which you just fully colonized or control your homeworld and are now seeking to colonize other worlds. You could go before that but it would start to feel like modern paradox strategy games or axis and allies and further back feel more historically inclined. So we have to start somewhere, so we should start at the planetary level and you transitioning to the interplanetary level until you reach the complete planetary level.
Now Endless Space 2's technology is done correctly to fit this paradigm of gameplay evolution. So I would have to disagree with the critics of this game as this progress does fit to a point with what you should have in a true space conquest/development game. It would nice to have pre-requisites incline with a particular technology dwelling off another technology. However, phases of development do progress in this regard that the developers had envisioned.
Now the interplanetary level is colonizing multiple worlds within the same solar system. In this regard, you would have different regions in the same solar system and your progress in the interstellar stage will lead you to colonizing an entire solar system, although it is possible to start colonizing multiple neighbor solar systems as well. Colonizing some worlds would or might require colonizing the moon before or after. The moon should be both an extension of its host planet as well as a separate entity. At a certain point your technology will incorporate the entirety of your moons' aspects to its host world world which will improve your planets' functionality with its host world and its standing in your empire.
Technology makes your colonies become more intertwined as your technology progress from stage to stage until it unites your entirety within the host galaxy and automation and hiring of heroes to lead automation is critical in keeping your empire's hold on the Galaxy. Nevertheless when you manage your empire. You have the galaxy, sectors, systems, system regions, and individual planets or dwarf planets including their moons. You could go further, but this is a planetary and post-planetary development minded strategy game.
This is how I would envision this game and yes it is a bit extensive, but it would cement a value as a game that would be difficult to beat without copying it and its entirety.

A Crusader Kings II/Medieval II: Total War hybrid would be one of the best strategy games in my opinion. CKII is more focused on the dynasty of noble families rather than the actual factions themselves like in M2TW. In essence it's a RPG focused on your faction's family. And with a video game set during the Medieval Ages, this makes perfect  sense considering bloodlines were so important in distinguishing nobility from peasants. Thus the family tree is the most important thing in this game. Who your family members marry determines what you can have a title/land claim on and what land you could possibly inherit or disinherit down the road. Throughout the game you get event prompts--which acts as the primary role-playing element--and the decisions you make influence your campaign's outcome; providing a sense of connection with you and the game. Overall an engaging game and one for those who desire more from the grand strategy genre.

A brief mention of a technical detail is necessary however.  The game is capped at 30 FPS and this can result in some performance degradation.  You'll read numerous complaints about it being a console port and that it's unplayable.  True it is a port, but unplayable?  That is completely unfounded.
Now that we've gotten that out of the way...
If you're a fan of film noir and the crime thrillers of yore, you will enjoy this game.  It is not even necessary for you to be particularly good at gaming to complete a play through.  While there is action woven into the cases, most of the time you're putting the pieces together or interviewing suspects.  Some cases had me stumped at times, but I found that all the more encouraging to examine the evidence, make connections and solve it.
My recommendation to anyone considering playing this game, don't be tempted to find a walkthrough to breeze through the cases on auto-pilot.  Give them an honest try and use what's given to you. Games have boundaries so use that to your advantage to make your deductions.  You won't regret it and when you get that 5 star rating at the close of the case, you'll start believing you're ready to join local law enforcement (I jest).
I have to emphasize the MotionScan technology used to capture facial expressions.  This was a necessary and very impressive component to the game.  While interviewing suspects you have to examine their facial expressions and behavior to determine if they are lying or telling the truth.  It is impressive...I don't think enough people give the studio credit for this achievement.
Story wise, I was intrigued by the fact that the story emphasized the impact of WW2.  I don't want to talk about the story too much as to give anything away. The actors casted for the characters were believable and well played.  I started looking them up on IMDB to see where I recognized them from.  In some ways it made me long for the days of FMV in the late 90's but I really loved the style and animation as it stood.  I read that in a potential sequel (not a direct sequel) to LA Noire, they may be working on doing full body motion capture with the MotionScan technology rather than just facial expressions.
To further highlight how much I enjoyed this game, I even embarked upon completing the achievements and gophering around collecting all of the cars and film reels.
Do yourself a favor, give this one a run.

Written for Update (0.2.5)
Let me preface this review by saying that it is indeed an “Early Access” title. As one would probably know already, this means that the game is a work in progress, and is still within testing stages. That would mean that there will likely be sweeping balance changes, plethora of bugs, and will likely not have a smooth framerate. This is indeed the case, but as clearly visible I recommend this game. It’s already enchanted with me with alluring gameplay, and some of the finest visuals in the industry. However, if one cannot get past the issues the game currently faces, I would advise to stay away. I respect these opinions, and will simply leave you with a request: add this game to your wishlist and revisit it after it has launched. It is a fantastic game, and if the issues present get ironed out, it could perhaps be the best “Space 4X of 2017”.
The gameplay itself feels quite familiar to the other Endless games, with those familiar, FIDSI and a similar planetary style making a return. As of this update, factions such as the Horatio, United Empire, Sophons and Cravers have returned, with new factions such as the Vodyani and Lumeris coming into the fray as well. Two more factions are yet to come. For newcomers, one important part to note about the factions is that they all play extremely uniquely. While some other 4X games merely change the ship designs and tiny changes like +5% whatever speed, this series typically has game-changing mechanics tied into every race. The United Empire can wield influence to complete a plethora of tasks, while the Vodyani never settle on planets. The Lumeris can buy and sell planets, and the Cravers are extremely proficient at conflict. That being said, there’s an additional uniqueness to each faction through faction quests, events and a political system. One minor issue to note in the gameplay department however, is the currently subpar AI, lack of multiplayer and the small maps. Multiplayer and bigger maps are supposedly coming in the next update, so look for that at that time.
In terms of visuals and sounds, the game is far beyond that of the current minimalistic industry standard. The soundtrack is already brilliant, and is immersive to a degree that I keep it on no matter what. The graphics are great too, with detailed space battles and emotive portraits adding further immersion. It’s hard to express this using text, but it’s just pure brilliance.
Overall the game’s currently quite fantastic, but yet again, be wary of issues such as bugs and poor performance.

A Crusader Kings II/Medieval II: Total War hybrid would be one of the best strategy games in my opinion. CKII is more focused on the dynasty of noble families rather than the actual factions themselves like in M2TW. In essence it's a RPG focused on your faction's family. And with a video game set during the Medieval Ages, this makes perfect  sense considering bloodlines were so important in distinguishing nobility from peasants. Thus the family tree is the most important thing in this game. Who your family members marry determines what you can have a title/land claim on and what land you could possibly inherit or disinherit down the road. Throughout the game you get event prompts--which acts as the primary role-playing element--and the decisions you make influence your campaign's outcome; providing a sense of connection with you and the game. Overall an engaging game and one for those who desire more from the grand strategy genre.

Having loved Endless Space, I did go into this game rather biased, so I will try and leave that behind.  I've always loved space themed strategy games, and the Original Endless Space was the first I played in a long time since Galactic Civilisation 2 that really got me hooked. Myself and my partner used to play the original for week on end, slowly trying to wrestle galactic control from one another, and honest, I'm looking forward to this from the sequel.
Honestly, I really am enjoying what there is so far from this game. And I am really looking forward to all the future updates we know about and see what that adds to the game as a whole. The feature of combat on the planet surface, though limited in what occurs, offers more of a outcome than the original which always seemed a bit random. Admittedly I was hoping for something akin to Endless Legend in being able to command your invading ground forces, but considering the main focus of this game is about fleet battles in the depths of space, it was asking for a little too much. It really has taken the bare bones of the first game and added to it, the detail of the ships, and functionality of the weapons they employ, not to mention incorporating the resources from Endless Legend, really is a great leap for this game. It will make gaining certain solar systems more important for their resources now. I personally am really looking forward to seeing what the final product will become. I know there are a number of issues currently with the game, but that is what Early Access is for, and you just have to accept this and take them with a pinch of salt. And understand the pace of the game is not for everyone, but that's just one of those things.
Honestly, if you want a taste of what the game will have to offer, buy this and just wait out the ride for the pull version. Failing that if your impatient then I'd recommend purchasing the original.

The game is a bit strange, to be honest. Not just because it’s not the classic “runny gunny” variant of Rockstar games, but mostly because I have solved 4 or 5 cases and it feels like I haven’t really done much. I’ve unlocked outfits that look like repaints of the same basic thing (Watch_Dogs would later come to have the same exact problem), and I seem to be unlocking intuition points I don’t really need since I can just Shift+Tab to a guide that tells me when people are lieing.
I don’t want to sound like a mouthbreather who can’t handle not having violence in my face every ten minutes. But after 3 hours and two gunfights, I feel there should be a /little/ more peppered around.
My very first case I failed immediately when the perp ran away. I went to fire at him, just once, and actually managed to hit him in the leg. Instant “You failed” screen, “Man got injured” it said. No kidding? He was fleeing.
So I find a street crime a little later, THINKING I shouldn’t be shooting the masked perp with a firing gun. Since I couldn’t figure out how to melee with my gun drawn, I just tried rushing him. Mission failed. “Officer down” it says.
Christ, make up your mind.
Another street crime was a more clearcut gunfight, which was enjoyable but the game CLEARLY didn’t emphasize the gunplay. The controls were a bit sluggish as my dude slowly gets out of cover and slowly figures out that I’m holding the shift button to sprint to a different piece of cover. I haven’t died yet, but I have taken a few shots because Cole won’t move his friggn’♥♥♥♥♥
I will admit, first impressions were pretty decent. They’ve taken a slight (but only slight) dip due to the clunky movement. I also don’t feel like an “open ended” game is the right platform for the investigative style it’s going for. Indeed, it’s hardly open ended at all. I can’t really “stop” any investigation and wander. Sometimes my police car gets a call that I can generally divert and deal with, but there’s no ‘wandering’ available. I’m wondering why the world is this large when all I can do is “Investigation” and “shoot some Mexicans over here”. Even clothing is changed via the menu, no shopping to be done.
Is a more open world “unlocked” later? Rockstar is sometimes fond of that. If so, that’s fair. I’ll keep playing it (though mostly in one-hour chunks so my computer doesn’t explode).

Endless space 2 is a space themed 4x strategy game developed by Amplitude studios and published by SEGA. At the moment of writing this review it is still in early access. I will be giving an overview of the pros and cons and my final thoughts on ES2.
Pros
- The presentation is phenimenal and everything feels great.
- There are a wide variety of options to rule your empire, from the basic construction options to selecting empire wide improvements in the form of policies.
- Periodic elections reflect open new policies based on what your people want and close others that might not be relevant. as an example if you wage a lot of wars the militarist faction gets a lot of votes resulting in them getting a  majority in the elections and giving you the option to enact certain policies that help in waging war.
- The cinematic battles look great and give a sense of the scale as you see your ship shooting at some dots in the far distance.
- Every race is distinct with very different pros and cons resulting in different experiences when playing them.
- The music is beautiful, keep in mind music is subject to personal preference.
- Science is placed in eras rather than a tech tree, this results in you having different techs then your enemy.
cons
- It's still in early access, so not all the features are in and the game is very limited as a result.
- No combat controls, although the cinematic battles look great there is no way to control your fleets once they are in battle, all you can do is set the engagement range for your ships.
- The game is slow even on a small map with 3 empires, the game takes ages to process a turn.
- The game can crash, it doesn't do it very often, but is can crash.
- no multiplayer yet (there is an unclickable option in the screen so I assume it will be there when the full can releases).
Final thoughts
I enjoyed my time with ES2 although when you get further into the game the problems become worse. It looks, feels and plays great but always has an undertone of early access. I will recommend this game, but do ask yourself if you really need it now or if you can wait for the full game. As always be way of early access, amplitude studios have proven themselves before with endless legend, but the past is no guarantee for the future.

Warframe is easily the best Free to Play (FTP) game on Steam, almost everything* can be gotten in game just by playing it. This is a primarily a Player vs Environment (PvE), with a Player vs Player mode (PvP). Below is for the PvE portion of the game.
Warframe is an easy to learn, difficult to master, kind of game. Its main progression is story based quests with a steep learning curve for the basics of the game, but once you master the game it becomes a true gem.
The player is a super solider from an ancient war that was re-awaken by an enemy force seeking to control them, once you are free from the tutorial the game opens to be a mission based game taking place in our solar system with Earth as to beginning node. Each mission is randomly generated tile based map with 4 factions in the game to fight, each faction has multiple units with strengths and weaknesses to battle against as well as named Bosses to fight.
The basic gameplay is third person shooter, but it differs for all other shooters. The movement system is one of a kind, the Parkour system allows the player to traverse ground quickly via “Bullet Jumping” the player literally can shoot themselves up 30 meters in the air and then aim glide or aerial roll the gain momentum and hurl themselves across the map.
Each Warframe has unique powers that range from offensive to defense or supportive. Some are purely elemental in nature, others are theme based, while some are just too unique to describe. While they do have powers, they also bring a large and varied arsenal with them, such as Primary’s, Secondary’s, and Melee weapons. There are hundreds of weapons currently ranging from Rifles, Shotguns, Launchers, Beam weapons, Pistols, Swords, Glaives, Hammers, Whips, and the list goes on.
With the Arsenal, there is also the Mod system, modding allows the player to enhance their weapons and frame with more power. the Mod system is the most challenging aspect to the game, because you must collect certain types of mods to be able to enter high level content with ease, otherwise it will be very challenging for players.
Since this is a FTP there are some annoyances, most of all the bugs, since this game is always evolving it will have bugs, but they are fixed quickly due to the community that helps by reporting bugs.
Other things such as build timers, cosmetics, and limited slots (weapon, frame, and riven) are there to ensure that the game can be profitable, which is fine the build timers are a set amount the maximum is 3 days for building a new frame. Cosmetics are generally platinum only, the only cosmetics that are not are alternate helmets for frames. Slots are only platinum, but platinum is easy to get by trading with other players.
Which there lies the beauty of Warframe, by trading with other players you can acquire anything in the game, it does take time for a player to become profitable, but it is doable. I’ve made at least over a 1000 plat by just playing and selling off copies of mods, prime parts, or weapons.
I have purchased plat and Prime Access, but I feel as though it ruins the game for me when I do, I found myself sitting with a mountain of plat and prime goodies that I didn’t earn, and it burnt me out. Because I took the easier path I lost the what made the game fun, the simple enjoyment of grinding for a part to finally get it and the satisfaction of finally building that weapon or frame.

Endless space 2 is a space themed 4x strategy game developed by Amplitude studios and published by SEGA. At the moment of writing this review it is still in early access. I will be giving an overview of the pros and cons and my final thoughts on ES2.
Pros
- The presentation is phenimenal and everything feels great.
- There are a wide variety of options to rule your empire, from the basic construction options to selecting empire wide improvements in the form of policies.
- Periodic elections reflect open new policies based on what your people want and close others that might not be relevant. as an example if you wage a lot of wars the militarist faction gets a lot of votes resulting in them getting a  majority in the elections and giving you the option to enact certain policies that help in waging war.
- The cinematic battles look great and give a sense of the scale as you see your ship shooting at some dots in the far distance.
- Every race is distinct with very different pros and cons resulting in different experiences when playing them.
- The music is beautiful, keep in mind music is subject to personal preference.
- Science is placed in eras rather than a tech tree, this results in you having different techs then your enemy.
cons
- It's still in early access, so not all the features are in and the game is very limited as a result.
- No combat controls, although the cinematic battles look great there is no way to control your fleets once they are in battle, all you can do is set the engagement range for your ships.
- The game is slow even on a small map with 3 empires, the game takes ages to process a turn.
- The game can crash, it doesn't do it very often, but is can crash.
- no multiplayer yet (there is an unclickable option in the screen so I assume it will be there when the full can releases).
Final thoughts
I enjoyed my time with ES2 although when you get further into the game the problems become worse. It looks, feels and plays great but always has an undertone of early access. I will recommend this game, but do ask yourself if you really need it now or if you can wait for the full game. As always be way of early access, amplitude studios have proven themselves before with endless legend, but the past is no guarantee for the future.

Fantastic game.  Always enjoyed detective movies/shows, so getting this is a no-brainier.
Worth playing; Recommend getting the "complete" edition if if gets on sale (usually only a few bucks more than base) and it comes with a few more missions and such.
Music: It has some good '40's music playing on radios, but when you drive it's just soundtrack (shame i know) But the OST is still good regardless. Would like to hear some music while I just drive around. - 8.5/10
Graphics: Facial animation is stunning. The lengths they've gone to; amazing. 30fps cap. 9/10
Story: The more you play, the better it gets. You get flashbacks of Detective Cole back in the war after every few cases, and reading newspapers will give you back-story on "current events" (or something)  9-ish/10  Plot twists on your plot twists.
Driving: I don't like it. Too sensitive for me. Tap directional key and the car moves across the street. No mouse steering. No in-car radio. When driving it's always the background music. (shame). No drive-and-shoot (Your a detective with common sense. That's why.)  5/10 - Average, could be better.   -- Reckless driving will give you a lower end-case rating. so don't cause city/personal damage - This isn't GTA. You're a traffic cop gone detective. A man of the law.  -- You can always hold "E" to let your partner drive to the location selected (if there are case-related dialogue; that will be said, then loading screen then you'll be at the location; with you behind the wheel.  - If there are car chases, you'd have to drive no matter what.
World and level designs: the city is giant. Streets seem well done with placement of names, ads, and such that is realistic.
The main map has almost every street on it, so when dispatch says "on the corner of this and that" you check the map and see what streets to take (there's no on-road line to see where to go) 9/10
- The buildings are well made, with loads of clutter of personal items like photos that make it seem like there's someone living in there.
- Only enter buildings with a Golden doorknob. So don't know what floor the perp is on? look for the golden doorknob.
- The cars, buildings, clothes, even some speech is something from the '40/'50s - Devs captured it perfectly.
Overall: 9/10 - Play now.
TL;DR: Buy this game. Sale or full, get it. Worth every cent.  Good luck detective.

It's a pretty game but the mechanics as a 4x title needs work. The tech tree is my issue with the game right now as it is gating progression and preventing early tactics like blitz and exterminating weaker factions or minor races.
With a two hour window to "demo" the game I pushed my colonies well beyond what is normally possible (100000 starting currency (dust) and influence) which should make me god like. My colonies were pushed to 100% production and i built a massive fleet of 100 ships. At that stage I was able to demolish any resistance I encountered and upon setting my fleets upon an enemy planet they all just orbited around the planet doing nothing. My ships did not have planetary invasion modules and the technology wouldn't be available to my ships until much later in the game.
Remember what 4x means. Explore, Expand, Exploit, Exterminate. Endless Space 2 does the first three quite well but fails at extermination.
Minor and weak factions that expand and leave their bases undefended shouldn't be allowed to live and I don't understand why I need planetary invasion fleets when I should just be able to bomb their defenseless colonies from orbit or redirect a space rock and cause an extinction level event?
Performance wise I experienced some micro stuttering during game turns, and later encountered exponentially longer load times between turns as the game seems to want to caculate everything your enemy factions are doing. Quite noticeable after 50+ turns. Hoping for some performance tweaks by the time the game is released.
I like the unique flavors of each faction. The tech tree definitely needs work as it is not enjoyable the way it gates gameplay options or tactics. I like the use of heroes to improve systems or fleets. I like how easy it is to build improvements from systems view or galaxy view. I like that the UI is fairly intuitative and despite not having a tutorial in game it's not difficult to explore the game UI and figure out the mechanics. It also helps that the UI and game art is so pretty.
Overall I'd say TRY IT.
On the condition that performance issues are resolved and the tech tree is reworked. Gating technology that is vital to early game play tactics is an oversight.

I always had a thing for turn based strategy.

This. Game. Is. Amazing.

-It is imo by far the most visually appealing game of it's genre.
-It has a low skill floor. I don't know how high the ceiling is, though. I play more casually
-I immediately felt comfortable with the mechanics. Turn-based games often want to add depth by adding complicated mechanics and you end up either being thrown into the cold water or being confronted with a 100page tutorial (looking at you crusader kings). -there are 5 different factions so far and they are very unique, in that they all have very different play styles. In other games different factions would maybe have some altered stats or a unique building/unit. In this game however there is at least 1 factor that alters your game heavily.
I hope the devs continue to listen to their alpha players and also add more content. So far it's already a really good game and it's not even finished.

(Minor spoilers) This game is awful. Interrogations make no sense. People with no reason to lie regularly withhold information, all you really have to go on is facial expressions. And it's so stupidly easy to interpret them how the game wants, there is zero intrigue. Interviewee looks at the ground or eyes dart back and forth? Even if it happens only once and you believe the statement, doubt what he's saying.  Which leads to my next complaint - Half the time, the truth and doubt options are completely arbitrary, whatever you choose, your guy yells at and or calls the interviewee a liar, prompting the interviewee to complete the statement that you chose to believe or doubt before it was really even finished. And you would think that any and all information in a case would be available to present to suspects etc. But no. For example, while questioning a man about the last time he saw his wife, there is no way to pick at his statement about things getting "out of hand" before he left, despite the fact that a neighbor has told you that she saw a black eye on the wife after the fight. But at other times, you're expected to doubt a 15 year old girl who just found out her mother died, when she tells you she never really payed attention to the jewerely her mother wore. You have no reason at all to doubt this-you just met the girl and all you know is that the mother has had jewerly forcibly removed from her body and there's no trace of it in the home. And if you do choose the right answer, and doubt, she'll go on to tell you exactly what her mother wears in what is essentialy worded as the second half of her statement, as if your prodding jogged her memory. If you select truth, you suffer the wrong answer penalty and the girl doesn't tell you about her mom's jewerly. So often a characters tone will be totally out of context. You snap at just about anyone for anything. Half the time you select truth, you still call the person out for lying and or withholding something. The overarching story and my respect for Phelps as a character is ruined by moments like the one in a flashback to WWII in which he's shown defending the Japanese attack on pearl harbor: 'What would we do if another country cut off gas to run OUR cars?' Which is just stupid, considering the oil embargo was a result of Japan's imperialism. A game about solving mysteries face to face is devoid of logic and natural human reactions.

Where do I start?
Warframe is a game where you play as a ninja - in space. It's mostly a PvE game where you cooperate with a squad of four people. But you can play solo if that's what you prefer. There is also a PvP area, but it's not very popular.
And I think my hours on it can speak for my love of this game. I've only been playing for about 10 months (as of this review). And can say that it's got the best free to play model I've seen from any MMO I've played. This game is no where near pay-to-win. You don't have to pay anything to get anything you want in game as long as you don't mind spendng the time working for it. You can pay the game's premium currency to get things faster, but the currency can be gotten through trading prime items you earn in game to other players. You don't have to pay for anything - unless you want to! The only thing I've ever spent money on for this game was some exclusive (tennogen) cosmetics. Other than that, I've been playing like somebody who's never spent money on in-game currency, I never had to!
The community is probably one of my favorite aspects of this game. Everybody is pretty nice and fun to be around. There's only a handfull or two of times I can recall running into some rude or mean players in the game since I started playing. Most players experienced players are helpful and courteous to new players and don't hesitate to help them out, most of the time - you've just got to ask!
The story and world building that is there is very good, but much of it is still incomplete and they're still adding more to it with every quest they add into the game. (Which is pretty frequently, might I add.) But you don't get to the REAL parts of the story until later on in the game, so if you wanna play this for the story, you'll have to be patient. Because you don't really get to it until you're over halfway through the starchart. So if you want a completely fleshed out story right off the bat, you might not get what you want with Warframe. They're still working on it!

I always had a thing for turn based strategy.
I liked some Total War games, loved Civ5 and got into Sci-Fi. I played Galactic Civilization 2 and 3 and the old Endless Space.
And now this.
This. Game. Is. Amazing.
Some points why I like it the most so far:
-It is imo by far the most visually appealing game of it's genre.
-It has a low skill floor. I don't know how high the ceiling is, though. I play more casually
-I immediately felt comfortable with the mechanics. Turn-based games often want to add depth by adding complicated mechanics and you end up either being thrown into the cold water or being confronted with a 100page tutorial (looking at you crusader kings). You won't feel that way in this game, guaranteed.
-there are 5 different factions so far and they are very unique, in that they all have very different play styles. In other games different factions would maybe have some altered stats or a unique building/unit. In this game however there is at least 1 factor that alters your game heavily.
I hope the devs continue to listen to their alpha players and also add more content. So far it's already a really good game and it's not even finished.

After playing this game over the past couple of years on and off, I decided to write a review. The premise of this game is great, two factions fighting eachother with numerous different game modes, different classes with their specific jobs, and even a new co-op mode for those who don't like playing player vs player. However, I don't recommend this game to anyone currently and to look for another one. The reasons are the game mechanics. It's not realistic at all and it breaks the immersion. For example, a vanguard would be fighting three different people, instead of taking a defensive position they'd just walk backwards and forwards swinging their Zweihander like they are blind infinitely. There's also the weird mechanic of looking directly at the ground while overheading to get a super fast overhead that is most of the time impossible to block. And there's the mechanic known as "matrixing" where you would crouch down and look at the sky, manipulating your player model so that the other person can't hit you even though they are right in front of you. I really wanted to like this game but it isn't for me, maybe I'd come back to it just to finish the achievements or when they bring updates to the mechanics.

I feel that the best way to review this is to show my progression and feelings through a timeline.
Just-Bought-The-Game= (Level 1)  "OMG LOL HIS HEAD JUST EXPLODED THIS IS SO FUN!" XD
-You will die.  A lot.  Expect this.  However, you can play on rookie servers until level 15ish, effectively separating you from the diehard vets.
New Player= (Level 2-15)  "I'm starting to get the hang of this; it's pretty fun"
-Your limbs stay connected.  Most of the time.  Still in rookie servers.  Starting to find out what classes and weapons you like.
Average Player= (Level 15-19)  "Oh dear god I want to go back to the rookie servers!"
-You will die more than you did when you were level 1.  Veteran players will decapitate you in every embarassing way with no mercy, often taunting you by repeatedly thrusting their groin onto your decapitated corpse.  This is the make or break point- stick through it or quit.
Experienced Player= (Level 20-30)  "I'm able to hold my own."
-Experience does not mean skill; many players in this catergory range from amazing to below-average.  You've managed to stick with the game and can survive for longer than 2 seconds against a veteran.  Good for you.
Veteran= (Level 30 and up)  "Just another day in Chivalry."
-Again, veteran does not mean highly skilled.  You could be a whirling, unstoppable, bladed tornado of death, or a complete derp.  You can take the game as far as you want now.  Good luck.
Overall the game is fun, quirky, and entertaining, though with a fair share of bugs.  Not a game that I'd put hundreds of hours into, but a it's solid buy.

Clicker Heroes embodies a monumental turning point in the progression of video games as a medium: the beginning of the end. Much as the Dada movement did to art, it brings into question the fundamental concept of video games, ultimately reducing it to absurdity and bringing to light the futility and meaninglessness of such endeavors.
Many years ago, a friend of mine posited a hypothetical game composed of a single button which incremented the player's displayed score when clicked. He said that people would still pour hours into playing such a mind-numbingly minimal game. I laughed. At the time, the very notion seemed ludicrous to me. It's humbling to see how far gamers have fallen.

LA Noire is a rather interesting title. It's a Rockstar game but it was developed by an Australian developer named Team Bondi. Why this is relevant is many of the developers from Team Bondi made an eerily similar game called The Getaway which also focused on cinematic action.
LA Noire is unlike the Grand Theft Auto games it gets compared to. A big focus of the game is it's cinematics and it's interrogation mechanic. Where the player is required to tell if a character is lying or not. While I would say it was implemented fairly well, unfortunately the developers confuse you every so often with the range of options. Sometime a suspect isn't lying but rather just not telling enough information. And instead of selecting lie you're supposed to select "doubt". Thankfully the developers also implemented a lifeline style mechanic where you can ask the community what the most commonly selected responses are.
While I would say LA Noire was an excellent game unfortunately it was an imperfect one. The game starts out exceptionally well and the quality of the writing stays consistant until the middle. After the homicide desk the writing begins to get worse and worse, to the point when you get to the ending you begin laughing at how ludicrous the entire thing is. I wouldn't say the experience isn't worthwhile but don't go into this expecting it to be Red Dead Redemption levels of satisfaction.
It's unsurprising to find out this game had two entire desks cut (of which 4 remain in the final release) considering the storyline remains just a little half baked. It's unfortunate to see with such an ambitious game, but since it was in development for 8 years it's surprising that it came out at all.

This is the best detective game on Steam at the moment. You play as Cole Phelps, a veteran who went into police work in order to keep serving his country and dispense justice. As you play, you say to hell with procedure and take the initiative to solve the crimes the lazy detectives are glossing over. This gets you promoted to become a full-time detective, and you make your way up the hierarchy of crime investigators.
I'm not gonna bother dividing these things into pros and cons. If you need a detective game in your life, buy it.
If you don't, read this review and buy it.
GAMEPLAY:
You're not buying the game for this:
- This is a third person open world game, yet it has nearly nothing to find or do in terms of free roaming. Between missions you may accept a street crime side mission, but they often boil down into a chase, a car chase or a shoot-out, all of which probably won't get your blood pumping. Do yourself a favour and just follow the story; it's pretty long.
- The combat is boring and generic. The weapons bear no real feeling of impact and you can take a lot more bullets than the bad guys. Melee combat is practically unexistant. The combat is merely a way of prolonging the game and supplement the story.
- No reward or change if you decide to go for a non-lethal arrest.
- The driving is nothing spectacular. It's far less enjoyable than in most Rockstar games in that it's pretty slow and car chases force you into just trying to keep the driver in sight until the game decides that he's arrived at his final destination. Occasionally you will be able to have your partner shoot out the suspect's tires, which feels alright, but you won't be aiming.
- Interrogation is a pretty fun mechanic which is probably what this game is known for. You have to read the suspect/victim's facial expressions and pick up on uncertainty or curious claims, then decide if they're lying or telling the truth and reveal more info/clues if you answer correctly. Sometimes you'll be dealing with good liars that the game won't tell you about, who tell you their side of the story very rigidly and confidently, but without the facts adding up. This is to make sure you know have an overview of the case and it's a very nice touch.
- Facial features and animations are great, since a fairly thorough facial motion capture method was used for every character and gels very well with the story. As a result, every character in the game looks like the person who performed the voice.
- The game is locked to 30 FPS for the facial motion capture to work.
STORY:
The reason this game is nothing short of phenomenal:
- Between cases, you will sometimes get a clip that goes back to Cole's participation in the war in Japan after the attack on Pearl Harbour. From the very beginning of the game, you'll be seeing these clips/flashbacks and they will play into the story as you progress. The way the game creates parallel story lines that eventually cross into eachother is absolutely fantastic.
- The cases are often connected to eachother in some way; I can't say much without spoiling it.
- They're also fairly devoid of plot holes and create a comprehensive and complete experience.
- The job eventually expands into your personal life, even though it initially doesn't seem like you even have one.
- Characters from the story occassionally appear in the side missions (street) crimes, which is a nice touch but it won't mean or matter much.
- The atmosphere is extremely immersive and convincing; when you launch this game, you turn into L.A.'s top detective in a realistic city based on real places with real landmarks.
The music amplifies the detective noir vibe and is probably the final aspect that gets you into the role.
Every character wears clothes and sets their hair in a way that is true to the time period as well.
- The voice acting is absolutely beautiful and convincing in every aspect. Team Bondi really scratched together some very talented people.
L.A. Noire does what is does very well, and as long as you're willing to look past the FPS cap and just follow the main story line, you will be an experience richer.
The interrogation mechanic might get dull after a while; for this I recommend you consider what you'd answer in a situation and then look up the correct answer in a guide to keep you trekking along.

Crusader Kings 2 is a strategy game from Paradox Interactive.
It was released in 2012 and is still playable. why you might ask?
The game is a grand strategy game that lets you play as the head of any European, Minor Asian, North African or Indian dynasty, what happens when you die? Well, you continue playing as your heir!
The easiest way to think of this game is like a slightly more historical Civilization but with elements of The Sims (The family planning) because you are not only ruling your kingdom, you are spending time with your wife, marrying off your daughter, plannings feasts, etc.
There are endless of replayability in this game since everytime you play you and all other AI characters wont stumble upon the same problems, or victories. One game you might marry a cute blonde, have a genious child who later conquers half of Europe, but in the other you might not even get a kid cause you apparently are sterile and your incompetent brother inherits your kingdom, throwing it into a decade long civil war!
You'll have to look after your faith, your family, your kingdom and your destiny!
Will you end up in the glorious battles of the Crusade, or will you fall to instant death after your
wild son "by mistake" pushed you from your balcony while inspecting your capital.
This is probably one of those games which I really never will stop playing, not only are the possibilities endless, but the creators are still adding content to the game even after 2,5 years, and I shouldn't stop there! The modding community is fantastic with creating mighty mods like the Game of Thrones mod, or even the Elder Kings mod!
I will end my review here, cause I need to get back to my save where I started as a Croatian count, and are soon about to form the Roman Empire once again!
Glory to Rome and godspeed!
Five years later and the game is a million times better!

I'll be honest with you. As much as I would love to recommend this game to everyone I simply can't. The balance is awful, the spacing between players makes no sense, and the damage is absolutely atrocious. I bought this game a while back because I absolutely loved the idea of it and still do to this very day, but the way that the devs went about making this game just saddens me.
Balancing in this game is a major issue to me. The best way I can describe this is by telling you my testimony on the matter and allowing you to draw your own conclusions. So there I was, firing my crossbow at the hordes of enemies attacking the villiagers I was supposed to be protecting, feeling glorious and brave and admiring the beautiful scenery (despite the burning huts and the battered brains all over the ground). That's when I noticed a Mason Knight charging at me with his very large hammer. I decided to take action and pulled out my small dagger. Now, I'm not saying that I should have been able to do this and this is certainly not the part I'm going to complain about, but he swung his nearly 100 pound hammer at my head...and I blocked it with my small 4 pound dagger no larger than my forearm. What happened next? Well, I began swinging my dagger at my foe: one hit, two hits, three hits, blood covering my arm and screams coming from the enemy. That's when it happened: this knight covered in armor from head to toe that probably weighs three times his own body weight began running in circles around me swinging his heavy hammer like it was a straw. Guess who died? Now, I'm not calling for perfection here, but does it make sense to everyone that a guy wearing hundreds of pounds of metal on his body swinging a giant block of iron could run in circles around someone without them being able to turn fast enough? Not exactly.
The spacing is another complaint. So as I do enjoy a bit of realism I can't help but notice the fact that this game makes no sense with the way that weapons work when they are swung. For example, I have a 6 foot longsword and I am going to swing it, naturally when I do the weapon goes back behind me a little bit obviously due to the fact that it is a long weapon and it reaches a great distance when swung. The problem is that when someone swings a giant sword like this, you could be standing directly behind them and die in one hit from the backswing of their giant sword...not a very nice feature. Why isn't this a nice feature? Simple. It gives players with long weapons the ability to kill from any direction, no matter which direction they are facing. It's pretty annoying when you're using a long weapon and you swing your sword at an enemy and you accidentally kill three of your teammates behind you in the process. On the other end of the spectrum, it's very annoying also when you're trying to take an enemy from behind and he swings his weapon and ends up killing you without ever knowing you even existed.
Now comes the final problem that I can think of off the top of my head that completely ruins the game for me: damage. I'll just get right into it by asking a question: does getting shot in the head with a crossbow hurt? Not sure, ask any of the knights in the game because even though they have the most health, their faces are somehow invulnerable to crossbow bolts. What happens when you shoot them in the face with a bolt? Their helmet falls off. Yep, that's it. Not only that, but a few hits with a broadsword kinda hurt, but one with with a slightly bigger broadsword is super deadly...
All-in-all, this game is really cool, if you can get past the fact that most of the things that happen in this game make absolutely no sense. It's sort of enjoyable otherwise.

The original, the best, the only worthwhile clicker game.
You think it's a game, but this really pokes fun at gaming with tongue-in-cheek text.  It exposes all the math underneath the game.  Do you understand the difference between arithmetic, geometric, and exponential progression?  That will help you more than anything for this game.  Progression requires exponential power, but it's given to you at a lesser level.  That means that eventually you hit a wall and have to "ascend".  This starts the game over, but parts of your progress you retain for the next "life".
A recent patch added an additional level of "starting over" called Transcension.  This wipes out an additional level of stuff but allows you to progress further and faster next time.  So you are replaying the same game hundreds of times... I'm on life (ascension) #888, transcension #13.  Most of those ascensions are from before that patch, hence the over 5000 hours of gameplay.
You can click (no aiming necessary) and progress, but the game supports an idle style as well.  Clicking will eventually win out, but you can wait a day or two before you start that part.  Autoclickers are now part of the gameplay, as long as you are willing to "pay" for it.  You can pay for rubies as an in-game currency, but a purchase is not necessary.  The game also awards you rubies for clicking on certain items, and I swear it gives me more when I'm not looking.  These can be used to purchase in-game auto-clickers (as opposed to external programs that send clicks to the window).  I paid for a couple of things because I wanted to support the devs.
Other than the numbers, there's no real reward.  No story line.  Just higher and higher exponents, like now I've sacrificed 7.597 x 10^30  hero souls.  What other game makes you read floating point notation (like 7.597e30) to understand the game?
And what the heck is Transcendent Power?  I'd have to explain the whole game to get to that point, but then this would not be a review.  Read up on the Clicker Heroes subreddit, start yourself out slowly.  You'll be bewildered for a while, but slowly you'll come around.
Pros:
* The dev team is very active and is still updating gameplay with new ideas and improvements.
* Active player community with dev invovlement on reddit (/r/ClickerHeroes).
* Number watching is somehow thrilling.  Is my nerd showing?
* Game well-balanced and thought out.
Cons (all very minor):
* Relics are largely useless, except where they boost your Atman level.  Even then not so much.
* Mercenaries die far too randomly, IMHO.  Revival can cost astronomical and economically unfeasible amounts of rubies.
* The wandering click-on animal to activate a random skill is also largely useless.
* Does anyone actually send their mercenaries out on skill activation quests?
* The first ascension is painfully slow and requires a lot of handholding.  Requires "tricks" of play to reduce this problem, but it is not fully eliminated.
* Raids don't give a lot of hero souls, but perhaps because I'm the only one in the guild.
* Relic levelling is awkward to accomplish and unreasonably expensive after the first few levels.  A high-level relic costs the same 1 core to increase by one level as a low-level one, but this always increases quadratically per added level (not the existing level of the relic).

Ok I think it's about time I gave a review for this. I've been playing for about 3 months and I've got to say DE has put quite a bit of care into their game. It may not be up to par with some AAA titles but, I'd personally say it gives some a run for their money. I'm not going to compare this to Destiny or Destiny to this. They're unique and similar in many ways but this is about Warframe. When this game was first released I shunned it. I played it once around the time it was released and never picked it back up. A couple years went by and decided to download it again. When I launched it back up I immediately noticed the difference in the game from when it was first released. You now got a daily login reward for playing it each day. Amongst these packs came platinum discounts (in-game currency), boosters for resource in-game, free credits (other money), etc. One day upon login I received a platinum discount of 50% off. So I decided to spend a bit of cash and it helped with my progress in the game. When the game was first released it was so much of a grind I gave it no chance at all to change my mind about it. Now the game is easier for solo players, players who have families or other things to do besides play games all day. They added new enemy types, a heap of new weapons and frames to use. I really enjoyed the fact the everything in the game can be earned rather then bought, with plenty of hours to grind out that precious loot.
The combat seemed a bit more fluent/fluid. One thing I immediately noticed was the movement of the character, it was different than other games. Acrobatically flying through the air; get a running start, crouch slide, jump high into the air, do a second jump, latch onto a wall, shoot a couple enemies, jump off that wall onto another, wall run, jump off that wall, crouch slide again, melee strike an enemy and walk away like it was too easy.
Not all players are against paying and helping out developers. The ones who decide not to spend any money still enjoy the game because they like the game for what it is. The one problem I have with DE's F2P model is there is basically an incentive to spend real money on fake money, hidden behind "platinum" currency walls (in-game currency that is bought). I personally have spent money of the game as I don't like really grindy games and I also have a full time job. This has helped me tremendously progress in the game and not have to invest 100's of hours leveling up. Unfortunately these packs of currency aren't cheap and I usually wait til I get a daily login for 50% off or more. There are 24 ranks in the game as of right now. I am currently rank 17 almost 18 and have 320 hrs in the game. If I chose not to spend any money, that time would probably be doubled.
At first it seemed the game had no point besides going from planet to planet and clearing out missions. Sadly only 2 missions show the full capabilities of Digital Extremes love for their game. Those missions are The Second Dream and The War Within. Those two mission will say more about the game then anything else will. I hope they go more in depth or add more story later as it would be appreciate by myself and all fans of the game. With Warframe being F2P, DE has to focus on content rather than story. Have to keep players occupied or the game would die rather quickly. By the end of the year Digital Extremes will be releasing a brand new update and a whole new open world mmo style area called the Plains of Eidolon and it will add a whole lot more to the game. If you think you found your perfect weapon now, just wait til you can craft your own!
Overall I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys RNG or 3rd Person Shooting

Another complaint from people is the DLC. Wildcard had released a DLC titled, "Scorched Earth" Where players take on the sandy dunes and fight fierce dragons, or Wyverns. Due to the early stage of Ark at the time, players did not approve this from the amount of bugs the players can face during gameplay. Some loopholes excist that will leave permanent marks on yer playthru or even break your game, but hey, just load up the same turn from autosave, and yer in the clear again.
Controls are simple and easy, has high level of costumizing of units, good costimuzing of Heroes, and there is vast supply of information upon wich to base your next decission. There are no right or wrong decission in this game, only informed or misinformed ones. Any kind of play-style will work on any of the races as long as you make informed decissions about your race's current strenght's and weakness'. The AI is pretty easy to beat in battles (too easy atm), but they will outclass you in growth and economy if you make 'bad' decissions. However i feel certain tech should be placed in a lower era, for example the major faction diplomacy. It just feels to slow and if i were to want to win in diplomacy. I would want to start making friends in era one besides minor factions. However diplomacy victory is disabled so i'm just thinking ahead, haha. Combat need's a little work, For example. Playing Lumeris, when era 2 starts i rush the tech for fleet size and to get the frigate. Having a fleet of frigates with all missles, using prudent and sniper for combat, makes everything easy. I've never came across the penalty being troublesome, so i can just colonize willy dilly. There is a tech that gives you trading companies, which i really like, but needs work. Around turn 90 frames start to drop and the process to end turns take longer. Another great feature this game has is quest. In endless space we only had random events. Now, not only we get events, we also get quest which ties to whatever political party you focus on. Talking about political parties every x amount of turns, your empire votes for which goverment to lead for x amount of turns. In this feature there are laws which give you bonuses, for example, being a pacifist you can get a 50% dust tax increase to your system... who doesnt love dust, haha. Overall game is still Early Access, more content will come over time. So if you decide to buy it.. dont complain about whats lacking, be patient.

First off, players may complain about the extreme price for Ark. They have raised the price of Ark to $60, leading to a high quantity of bad reviews. I personally think this game is worth $60 because of the fun and laughter that has occured in this game for me. From taming cages exploding and releasing the wild Therizinosaur, to exploring a tightly packed cave full of half-naked people around a campfire, this game is definitely a game worth playing.
Another complaint from people is the DLC. Wildcard had released a DLC titled, "Scorched Earth" Where players take on the sandy dunes and fight fierce dragons, or Wyverns. Due to the early stage of Ark at the time, players did not approve this from the amount of bugs the players can face during gameplay. Many bugs are still present, and Ark needs to work on bug fixes, as some players may say. I would agree with this, although I do not focus on these bugs from the humor that can result from these.
That is all I have heard of by negatice reviews, as I tend not to focus on these. Be aware, I'm sure Wildcard is working hard to get those bug fixes into the game and entertain the players with more exploration, featured mods and dinosaurs to tame.

First of all, the game is fun. Imagine it a bit like GTA, but this time you're a cop. When I first read about the game, it sounded quite deep. Doesn't feel deep, though. But Rockstar isn't exactly known for "deep" games anyway. Also, I read that the parts of LA you haven't discovered yet are black-white. Can't confirm that either, it's all colored.
Game runs stable and fluid so far, no crashes, no serious bugs encountered.
Anyways, about the game itself.
You play Cole Phelps, a cop in Los Angeles in the year 1947, as he solves cases and advances through his career.
Personally, I enjoy driving that old car through the nicely detailed streets of LA, although it can be a bit annoying at times. But if it gets too much, you can let your partner drive (though you don't get any side missions that way).
You get to solve cases by finding clues on the crime scene, questioning witnesses, interrogating suspects (can be rather difficult as you will need to decide wether they're telling the truth or lying, and back up the latter with proof), pursuing vehicles, persons, and occasionally exchange fire with hostiles (which will play like a cover shooter). So the gameplay is rather diverse, which is good.
Driving through LA can be a bit annoying. The AI of the other cars isn't exactly sophisticated. I've seen cars actually standing on overrun pedestrians, their drivers (or other pedestrians) not even caring. The other cars tend to get in the way a lot - they don't notice you coming unless you use the siren. The siren, however, simply makes them stop. While occasionally, they try to change the lane to make way, they more often than not just stop, usually right in front of you. If you don't crash into them, you must overtake them (hopefully there's no opposing traffic).
Like in GTA, the car is hard to control at high speed. Especially when you're pursuing, as precise movement isn't possible. I tried the keyboard and the controller, and found that the keyboard is actually easier to use. Why? Because the controller gives you a false sense of being more in control. However, it's not so bad, any failed case or side mission can be repeated.
There's only one one real downer here. One, you get no save feature. The game will save automatically in certain points, but this will only help if you failed or died and must repeat. You can not reload a savepoint, you can only restart a case.
If you do restart the case, you get to watch the whole intro and stuff again, which is the only type of cutscene that cannot be aborted.
Anyways, if you're into GTA-like games but want to play on the "good" side for once, this game is for you. You can, of course, still wreak havoc on your environment, and other than in GTA, you won't get punished for it (at least all I gotwas a sum-up of the damage I did after I completed a case).
