ES2 is obviously not complete yet,  just being able to play 125 turns before a score victory proves such, but it already shows as much, if not more promise than all the other wonderful titles Amplitude Studios has released. The distinction between factions through their playstyles surpasses that of ES1 and is certainly close to on par with the distinct playstyles Endless Legend provides. Many of ES1's systems were heavily changed for ES2, now including eras like EL instead of 4 tech trees. There's also a new system upgrade feature that allows you to use luxury resources to provide a large bonus to oneof your systems, along with whatever extra resources you get from improvments with yields dependent on system level. Combat features are limited due to early access, but it allows you to use a variety of strategies, like long range, which keeps your ships near where they entered the battlefield, and missles.Strategics and modules/equipment is now more like EL, as in you gather resources over time instead of getting X resource for each node you posess, and modules are now limited by slots, some of which only accept certain components, instead of the weight limit in ES1. My only complaints are that diplomacy isn't very deep yet, and the AI being able to force a truce(I've never been losing a war, so I don't know how this differs for the player). Much of the ground combat is inspired by ES1: Disharmony, with manpower and different types of units (Currently mechs and soldiers, are the only researchable ones) Overall, ifyou want to support Amplitude, liked ES1 or just think this looks interesting, buy it, it may be unpolished now, butit can only get better. (Apologies if any spaces are missing, my keyboard has an insensitive space bar)

Although Chivalry: Medieval Warfare does have a few issues, its basis is extremely well thought out and truly seems to replicate the feel of medieval combat. The well-honed combat system adds huge enjoyment to this super looking and incredibly fun medieval warfare game, yet a lot more could have been done to increase the variety of content within the game; like maybe a single player game mode and much more character customisation.
+ The combat system is honed to near perfection and is massively enjoyable thanks to its balance.
+ The visuals are stunning and the in-game aesthetics carry through the medieval style of the game.
+ Compared to modern games, Chivalry: MW makes for a refreshing release amongst the many FPSs.

- A single player mode could have worked really well with the combat system and look of the game.
- The complete lack of plot is a bit of a let-down, even though this game is only multiplayer.
- Character customisation falls short and just isn't up to scratch for an online multiplayer game.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is a nicely made Hack N' Slash, deathmatch styled game which places you in the shoes of one of four classes of Medieval warriors. Archers, Men-At-Arms, Vanguards, and Knights. The game is a simple "Red Vs. Blue" concept, and is comparable to every good online FPS game that's out there.
As such, Chivalry can be compared to Counter-Strike, except that in this case, it's in a medieval melee format for the most part. The exception to this is archers, ballistas, etc. The fun comes in when you play one of the several Team Objective matches, where you and your team must accomplish certain objectives in order to claim victory for your side There are several different game types, and variation in terms of maps and upgradable weaponry and armor, as in all of these styled games.
This is where the game gets a bit annoying because of the expensive DLC content. It doesn't make much sense to pay $5 dollars for a piece of armor or a sword. However, you can keep playing and upgrading your character, eventually getting better weaponry and armor. You can skip the DLC. But definately buy this game.
- Very fun Medieval concept, melee combat system (with some projectiles).
- Hilarious voice overs and sound FX.
- Chuckle at the ragdoll physics and the semi-gore
- Addicting play
- Very simple setup, no tutorial required (Can learn controls while games load)...
...
- "Training" Tutorial for those who want practice in Medieval combat is available.
- Also, leveled lobbies for beginners or advanced players.
- Dozens of different weapons, with 4 different classes on either side. Will you choose the Mason Rebellion, or fight for the true King of Agatha?
- Game can get a bit glitchy/lag at some points. Not so much that it's a bother.
- While the ragdoll deaths are funny, sometimes there tends to be a bit of texture popping going on. You can see right through the character at its' pivot points (Those of you who play know what I mean)
- Some beginners may experience a little difficulty with fighting (in which case there are some great YouTube videos to watch to give you Tips on playing and training also)
- Still seems like it has some work to be done, even though it was released in 2012.
- Ridiculously expensive DLC featuring $2 - $5 weapons and Armor. While completely optional, it is still offensive that these arent simply at
$0.50.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is an extremely fun and addicting online melee deathmatch game. Just the idea of it being melee/projectile (Throwing axes, arrows, etc.) oriented is very original to me. The play varies with who and what map you're playing with. There is also a full workshop with which to play with. All in all, my experience with this game is highly positive. I would buy this game again and again.
- A great play with much potential, but still has a lot of room for work.

EDIT: It's insane that this has gone long enough that I need to point it out in the review, but someone else has copy/pasted my review over their own:
If you need proof that I am the original author, well, just look at my review history and look at theirs, it should be readily obvious that I wrote this myself. If that's not enough for you, also check out this long post I wrote on the dev forums that further elaborates on everything I said here:
Please report him if you can; frankly, it's absolutely unacceptable that Valve has allowed their review to stand for as long as they have. You'd think after the steam mods fiasco they would have changed their minds about letting users steal content from other users? Anyway, the review starts here:
This is a very painful downvote to cast. It's hard to argue with Amplitude's track record - Endless Space, Endless Legend, and Dungeon of the Endless are all fantastic games, but after Endless Space 2, I have to admit I have much less confidence in their ability to produce a sequel.
The fundamental problem with Endless Space 2 is that it's barely recognizeable as a sequel to Endless Space. In fact, this game is far more like a sequel to Endless Legend - the tech tree, Influence system, minor factions, and many more are taken straight from EL. Aside from the fact that ES2 has a starmap and EL has a hex grid, the games are nearly identical; and quite frankly, it all worked better in EL. The tech system is completely incompatible with the rest of the game, there's new mechanics like force truce which are broken and underthought, and many other frustrating and questionable changes have been made.
Even if they iron out all of the problems underlining every core mechanic of this game, unless they completely overhaul them, this game will never be a sequel to Endless Space. The tech tree was one of the most unique and compelling features of ES1, and it's been completely removed in this game. Diplomacy is completely alien to players of the first, and appeasing other empires can be done with compliments instead of resources. Resources themselves are now accrued and stockpiled, rather than simply being collected perpetually. And that isn't to say any of these mechanics are BAD, but as a sequel, "not being bad" is absolutely not a justification for changing core mechanics. You have to be able to say that the new mechanics are BETTER; that gutting the tech tree and redesigning diplomacy and all the other stuff doesn't just make for a good game, but for a good ENDLESS SPACE game. It does not seem any consideration was made to this end; even the developer blogs all talk about the mechanics as they are now, without comparison or acknowledgment of the original game.
To be honest, I was surprised at first that this game is rated so highly. Maybe that's because Endless Space was always my favorite game by Amplitude, and I was mostly lukewarm on Endless Legend. Keep that in mind when deciding if this game is right for you - maybe I'm in the minority in not enjoying Endless Legend as much as Endless Space, but if you also find yourself in that minority, you should wait until this game is much further along in development and then assess how it lives up to the original. But as of right now, developer comments in their forums suggest that they are committed to making these changes work, and are not considering removing or undoing any of the changes. Myself, I'm far too disappointed in this sequel to keep playing it, and I doubt it will ever provide an experience comparable to the first Endless Space.

The gameplay, such as it is, requires you to search for clues at crime scenes and then interview relevant people in order to find out 'whodunnit' and arrest the perp. So far, so good. The problem and frustration lies in the interview stage. When questioning people you are have three option of doubting their evidence, accusing them of lying or believing them. THIS IS TOTALLY ARBRITRARY. No matter how you read their face or body language there's no way you'll be doing anything other than randomly guessing which choice to make. If you interview people in the wrong order you can even fail to make the case at all. If you don't play through and do things exactly as the game developers want then you won't win.
This renders the game worse than a MUD with a very pretty GUI. You will be frustrated because the game tells you that you're wrong, CONSTANTLY but at no time will you be able to point to any clue in the game that showed where you went wrong. You're just wrong because you didn't do what the game developer wanted you to do.
If you can get past this stupid gameplay design then maybe there's a story here. I can usually forgive silly game design if the story is compelling. The setting alone should have been but it's not. I don't care about the protaganist because he's a Mary-Sue with a stick up his♥♥♥♥♥and way too boy scout for 21st century tastes. The game design just made me want to play Super Mario Bros because as least in that game if I screw it's all on me and not bad writing.  Uninstalled. Hidden from game list. No surprised the developer went bust even though the facial animation is exceptional. Pretty and shallow game masquerading as deep and open-world.

L.A. Noire is an amazingly new and fresh concept, in a market that only tries to repeat itself.
L.A. Noire is an investigative game in which you are brought to solve many interesting cases as a L.A.P.D. detective.
The cases are varied and amazingly well written, ranging from Traffic cases, to Arson cases, ending with Homicide and Vice.
From time to time, while you solve these cases, you have to perform other tasks like shootouts or car chases ecc...so the game keeps things interesting for the player.
The best feature of the game is the connection you enstablish with the main character.
It's not just a linear progression of cases to solve, but you actually follow the intriguing story of the main character Cole Phelps, and all the cases are all connected into a hidden understory which is very engaging.
The topics that are dealt with are different, but the atmosphere reminds of L.A. Confidential.
The overall graphics are pretty good and the game features a groundbraking facial animation technology which feels strange at first, but then delivers some of the most realistic facial expressions seen in a game, and the best thing is that they are not just for show, they are very important for the gameplay, since you have to check suspects facial expressions (even the smallest details) during interrogations, to spot if they are lying or not.
The Los Angeles reconstruction is incredible; the city is ENORMOUS! It almost feels life-size.
The player is immersed in a very realistic and detailed representation of the most glamorous city in the world (L.A.), in its prime time (the 1940s, after the war).
A great experience, and if you are a patient player you'll be rewarded with one of the best games available on the market.
Pros:
- The Main Character, which is more multi-layered and constructed than it might look at the beginning
- Amazing cases; the developers had great ideas for every case, and you feel engaged to discover the truth
- Varied experience (The case-solving is alternated with other activities)
- Brilliant interrogations system (you need to take care of the clues and the interrogated person's facial expressions)
- L.A. is detailed and beautiful
- Engaging story, linking all the cases togheter
- Long game
Cons:
- There's a bit of aliasing, even if you activate antialiasing
- Needs a patient player to be appreciated and completed (Not a negative point, but it's just to let you know)
- The city is BIG...maybe too big, and some driving phases are a bit boring
Recommended!

My 4x experience is limted (Civ 5, Endless Space [ES] and Endless Legend [EL]), and Endless Space beat me to a pulp the first go round, but again, that's why I came to love this franchise.
When I see "Early Access", lack of content is the first thing to cross my mind. It should be expected. ES2 has minimal factions, turn cap, maps, and lack of multiplayer. Nevertheless The fact that there are several new mechanics to gameplay (some an obvious, and to be honest, expected combination of mechanics from EL and ES) such as "minimilistic" ground combat engagements, political systems, and minor factions just to name a few. I had no problem (in my 2 game, 6.7 hour run so far) feeling connected or invovled to the game as a whole. I was pleasantly shocked by the beautiful design of the UI and maps. The unique artwork, something that drew me to the series, continues tenfold into Endless Space 2. Revamps to the combat system(s) are epically excellent, simpler, and capture my attention. It's great to see that Amplitude has joined with SEGA, so the quality assurnace is there.
As hardware goes, I have no trouble running the game on mid - higher end display options (and I'm running a CAD machine with the minimum required 1.0 gb graphic memory on a NVIDIA Quadro 2000, granted with 16gb of RAM at my disposal). Things do tend to get laggy and slow into later turns after exploring a good chunk of the available map.
All that being said, the expectation for E-A games continues.It needs work here and there. There is no doubt of it. Per the usual, "content and bug fixes will be added in future updates" blah, blah blah...
...and I look forward to it.

L. A. Noire, just like Rockstar’s later titles, is a controversial game. On one hand, it was advertised as some realistic detective simulator and crime drama, which is a blatant lie. On the other hand, it provides a clichéd, yet well-crafted story, some decent acting and quite a few enjoyable individual cases. Just don’t go besides the main plot: none of the side content is worth it in any way.
Although L. A. noire was initially marketed as a detective simulator, don’t fall for that: it’s about as realistic as any Hollywood blockbuster. All of the clues are in the open, almost all of the cases involve shooting and killing somebody (the story mode’s bodycount is higher than GTAIII’s), and your average everyday cop will be involved in cases that feature a Jack the Ripper style serial murder, city-wide political conspiracies, international espionage (where you’ll have to massacre a US Military compound all by yourself) and drug trafficking that would put the Columbian Cartel to shame.
Add in some very sluggish controls, the most boring and frustrating collection minigame and side missions that are literally all the same, and you may think that anyone who gave positive reviews about the title were paid large sums of money.
So why the thumbs up? Because of the story. It’s quite decently acted– the biggest weak point is Aaron Staton’s performance as the protagonist, who just looks and sounds perpetually annoyed– and even though the plot is as clichéd as you can imagine, it uses these clichés to their best. Sure, this will eliminate most of the surprise at the plot twists, but they aren’t even set up as something to be surprised of.
Plus some of the individual cases– especially for the Traffic and Arson desks– are pretty damn interesting. They are well-written crime stories, worthy to be an episode of a classic police drama. Sure, the overall plot pales in comparison, but some of the cases are so good you may want to play them again, separate from the main story.
So, in conclusion, L. A. Noire is the kind of title which you should play from start to the end once, and never again. Luckily, the main story is more than 12 hours long even if you use a guide to get past the clue-collecting phases, so you get decent amount of entertainment for your money.

L.A. Noire is an amazingly new and fresh concept, in a market that only tries to repeat itself.
L.A. Noire is an investigative game in which you are brought to solve many interesting cases as a L.A.P.D. detective.
The cases are varied and amazingly well written, ranging from Traffic cases, to Arson cases, ending with Homicide and Vice.
From time to time, while you solve these cases, you have to perform other tasks like shootouts or car chases ecc...so the game keeps things interesting for the player.
The best feature of the game is the connection you enstablish with the main character.
It's not just a linear progression of cases to solve, but you actually follow the intriguing story of the main character Cole Phelps, and all the cases are all connected into a hidden understory which is very engaging.
The topics that are dealt with are different, but the atmosphere reminds of L.A. Confidential.
The overall graphics are pretty good and the game features a groundbraking facial animation technology which feels strange at first, but then delivers some of the most realistic facial expressions seen in a game, and the best thing is that they are not just for show, they are very important for the gameplay, since you have to check suspects facial expressions (even the smallest details) during interrogations, to spot if they are lying or not.
The Los Angeles reconstruction is incredible; the city is ENORMOUS! It almost feels life-size.
The player is immersed in a very realistic and detailed representation of the most glamorous city in the world (L.A.), in its prime time (the 1940s, after the war).
A great experience, and if you are a patient player you'll be rewarded with one of the best games available on the market.
Pros:
- The Main Character, which is more multi-layered and constructed than it might look at the beginning
- Amazing cases; the developers had great ideas for every case, and you feel engaged to discover the truth
- Varied experience (The case-solving is alternated with other activities)
- Brilliant interrogations system (you need to take care of the clues and the interrogated person's facial expressions)
- L.A. is detailed and beautiful
- Engaging story, linking all the cases togheter
- Long game
Cons:
- There's a bit of aliasing, even if you activate antialiasing
- Needs a patient player to be appreciated and completed (Not a negative point, but it's just to let you know)
- The city is BIG...maybe too big, and some driving phases are a bit boring
Recommended!

What a frustrating and disappointing game.
The most basic flaw with the game is the poor and inconsistent logic that's used to govern interrogations, which is the game's primary mechanic and conceit.
Interrogations work like this: you ask a witness or suspect about a topic, and he gives a response, at which point you have to choose between three options to characterize that reply -- Truth, Doubt, or Lie. If you choose Lie, you must select a piece of evidence that contradicts the interviewee's statement. A correct choice nets you experience and possibly a new clue or lead, while a failure may shut down the rest of the interrogation.
The problem is that sometimes you will have evidence that suggests a person is lying, but the game expects you to choose Doubt instead. Other times, the game expects you to accuse the interviewee of lying in cases where you're not calling out a specific lie, or where the evidence that the game wants you to use to substantiate the accusation does not clearly contradict the interviewee's lie.
Here is an example; I'll be a little vague and change some names and details so it shouldn't be too much of a spoiler:
Towards the end of a case, I was in a room with a crook that we'll call Tony. In Tony's office I found some clues, including some forged documents that were noted as having come from a corrupt businessman that I'll call Levy, as well as hard evidence that Tony had leverage over Levy. Also worth noting is that I had interviewed Levy earlier, and Levy's records helped lead me to Tony's location.
During my interview with Tony, my character asked for information about co-conspirators -- this is apparently so you can learn about Levy, in case the player has not already encountered him in the course of the investigation. Tony stonewalls, saying he acted alone. To me, the correct response to this would be to call him out on the lie, and cite either the forgeries (which had Levy's name on them), or the evidence that shows that Tony has leverage over Levy (though it's really both of these pieces of evidence COMBINED that make Tony's lie obvious). But no, the "correct" response is to Doubt, which gets Tony to give up Levy as co-conspirator.
In the follow-up question to that, my character asked who Levy is and where I can find him. This was completely stupid as my character had already interviewed Levy and knew exactly where he was. The stupidity was then compounded when Tony claimed that Levy is one of the gangsters I shot dead on my way in to Tony's office. However, I couldn't think of any evidence I could cite that contradicts that lie ("the fact that I know Levy's face" is not a selectable piece of evidence in my notebook) so I selected Doubt. Wrong answer. Apparently, THIS is the spot where I was supposed to call him on the lie, by citing either of two pieces of evidence that did absolutely nothing to disprove Tony's claim that one of the dead gangsters is Levy.
Those two pieces of evidence were a log in Levy's possession that showed that he sold the forged documents to Tony, and a scrap of paper that another detective gives you that basically just has Levy's address on it. I guess by the game's twisted logic, these two pieces of evidence each serve as a proxy for your own character's knowledge of Levy, because if you have the former evidence, or if you followed up on the latter evidence, you would know what Levy looks like. Instead that nonsense, why couldn't the game be scripted to simply check that I've encountered Levy and bypass the whole co-conspirators line of the interrogation, and just credit me with the rewards for having done the earlier legwork?
It's because the game has a system, and even though that system isn't robust enough properly handle the situations that are written into the game, I guess they felt the need to stick to the system for the sake of consistency, even though the logic the system ITSELF uses is anything but consistent.
The above situation also demonstrates how the game's writing can be a bit weak. What did Tony have to gain by saying Levy is one of the dead guys? He's making a false statement to a cop when he knows we already have enough evidence on him to convict, which is just going to add time to his sentence. He'd already given me Levy's name, and it would take a truly inept cop to not follow up on that and find Levy. He could be trying to protect Levy, but that doesn't make a lot of sense either -- the game makes it seem like Tony was just using Levy. At that point, Tony should've either stayed completely quiet, or he should've sold Levy out, without playing any more games. The self-incriminating middle ground approach that Tony takes is simply a contrivance to create one more piece of gameplay for the player to work through.
This is just one case, but I experienced things similar to the above in basically all of the early cases. Too often you can have a solid understanding of the situation and the characters, but the mystery you face as a player does not lie in the details of the case -- but rather is figuring out what the game itself wants from you.
The game also has some other issues. One annoyance is that you can drive from crime scene to crime scene, but as far as I can tell it's fairly pointless and boring. Either you end up driving around recklessly in GTA fashion (which doesn't make sense since you're playing the role of a notoriously straight-laced cop) or you sit at red lights and navigate city traffic with overly sensitive arcade-style controls. Fortunately, you can have your partner drive to your destinations for you.
Another problem is that you can't directly review evidence you've collected after you've collected it. You do have access to a LIST of the evidence you've collected and a brief summary of it, but the summaries sometimes lack important info. I encountered one case where I acquired two separate pieces of evidence at different times -- both were documents that had a lot of information on them, but where it wasn't immediately apparent which details were important. You'd have to cross-reference them to draw a useful conclusion, but you CAN'T directly cross-reference them because the summary of each document that you have in your notebook doesn't include the pertinent info.
Another thing worth noting is that this is a bad port. The aliasing (jaggies) are absolutely horrible, and the in-game AA feature seems to do absolutely nothing, even cranked up to 3X, which for some reason is the maximum. The frame rate is locked at 30 FPS (apparently due to the technology utilized in the facial animations -- a reasonable compromise would've been to have capped the frame rate during dialogue/cinematics, but uncap it elsewhere). Anistropic filtering is limited to 4X for no apparent reason. Screen tearing is rampant and there is no V-Sync option to address it. The game looks pretty bad, but would look fine if these technical features could be enabled and worked the way they are supposed to. It also seems to be poorly optimized -- I have a i5-2500k, GTX 670 and 8 GB of RAM, and at high/balanced settings, there was still some noticeable stutter.
I haven't played deep enough into the game comment on the overarching story, but from what I have heard, it is also not one of the game's strong suits. I have since learned that there is a plot twist that I would've found infuriating if I had put more hours into the game.
Overall, the game doesn't have any strong suits, other than the quality of the animation and performances during interrogation scenes, and there are some nice period touches that help capture that Noire feeling. But that alone isn't enough to make a game, in my opinion.

I’ll start off by saying that I wasn’t a huge fan of ES1. The game was competently done and had interesting unique features, like system management over single planets management.
But the diplomacy system was flawed, with lifeless AI contributing to a general lack of « soul », of personality. Hence I found the game to lack appeal in the long run !
Then ES2 happened, and before it Endless Legends, a rich 4x wich has an obvious (good) influence on this « sequel ». Of course you shouldn’t hope for a complete overhaul of ES1’s system, but then again it is not the point.
ES2 benefits from Amplitude learning from their mistakes, turning it into a deeper and improved version of ES1, well worth the money even in Alpha stage (I only encountered one real bug in more thant 10 hours of playing).
Here are some elements I consider to be important, both positive and negative.
I shall update this review after each significant change happening to the game.
IMPROVEMENTS AND NEW STUFF
* Galaxies are more beautiful to look at, same things for planets
* Colonizing a planet does not mean owning the system automatically anymore. A bit like Beyond Earth, colonization begins by installing an outpost, growing into a full-fledged colony after a few turns. You can spend manpower, Dust and Influence to speed up the process.
This way, if there is already an outpost in a system but yours outgrows the other, you gain the system- and the other outpost !
A great way to do early competition.
* Scouts now have probes, which can be used to explore space, or more importantly, explore anomalies for loot, quests and random events. Way better than juste popping out in a system and getting random stuff at your face.
* Freshly imported from Endless Legends, each faction (in addition to a better-crafted background) has a faction quest, many steps reaping different rewards based on your choice.
Makes the game more lively.
* Improved battle viewer, and no more tactics cancelling others ! Honestly I never watch battles, but I can understand the appeal.
* The new political system and its parties allows different laws to be applied, with frequent elections- something to keep an eye on if you want your empire to stay the course you have decided.
* Systems are conquered via groud battles, not with fleets staying in orbit a certain number of turns
* Minor Factions make their entrance, to be conquered or assimilated
SOME ELEMENTS NEEDING TINKERING
* Buyout costs are not properly scaled
* You should have at least one basic option to convert industry into another ressource (dust preferably).
* AI make wacky calls. No, Lumeris, it’s not reasonable to declare war on my Cravers’ hive while I have a complete fleet fully upgraded and you don’t.
AI grow restless too easily and underestimate your power. Sophons, when the most powerful faction is your neighbour, don’t make silly hostile comments. It ends badly.
* Forced truce are just an Alpha thingie, right ? Even so, it’s quite annoying.
* Turns still take a bit long to process
* Some techs and buildings specific to a faction should be available without quests. Speaking of
buildings, I hope we won’t have to wait a DLC to build Galactic Wonders/ Special Projects.
* Some quests are unbalanced, leading to sub-optimal gameplay choices, or delaying/failing them. Yes, I look at you, «Those darn kids ». I can’t build only science improvements and have better things to do that stuff those hangars with vessels !
* The techs needed to colonize different types of worlds need to be reworked. Is it useful to have at the same time a different tech for snow, ice and toundra planets ?
* At present, the factions are unbalanced. Further analysis just below.
THE FACTIONS
- Sophons. Nothing much to write home about. They still do science and can easily lead the score if left at their own device. More probably, they are gonna be bullied by an aggro faction.
- Cravers. They enjoy a huge boost of ressources (+50%) but all their planets eventually become barren (-50% on all ressources). The depletion rate is slow enough, combined with huge fleets right at the start and no interest into diplomacy whatsoever, to make them quite menacing.
Keep eating other factions like a Craver should, and I think going Craver is the easiest way to win for now.
A bit bizarre to see them having conflicting political interests with a Hive Mind- but if they had free reign here, they would be definetely too powerful.
In other words : Cravers are still bad news.
- Lumeris, dust-driven. They don’t use colonization ships, instead magically buying outposts,
wich is more reliable and considerably faster. Dust is also used to ensnare minor factions instead of Influence- again, more reliable and faster. With the right law(s), Dust is overflowing with this faction. In addition to the previous advantages, you can quickly enough mass buyout stuff, like a complete fleet in one turn.
So, if they have a good start, Lumeris could be quite tough to be stopped. So much Dust can be useful for pretty much anything else !
- Vodyani. Clearly based on the Broken Lords from Endless Legend, with the major difference that they suck. See, they have those nice Arks- powerful ships needing to stay at a system to control it. The good thing is that an Ark colonize every planet in a system- provided you possess the adequate technologies.
The very bad thing is that a new Ark can only be created via Essence. And you can only gather Essence by leeching population from an enemy system. It forces you to build a very early fleet of fragiles ships to do some leechin’.
Even if you happen to have a faction not too far from your home system, they will not be terribly happy about your population theft and will attack as soon as they can. Yeah for diplomacy, right ?
Even in ideal conditions, colonization with the Vodyani will be delayed. They can convert their dust production to Essence, but it will cripple you for the duration of the process and you will lose money fast.
They desperatly need an early building to have a steady, if modest, income of Essence. Because the wound needs to be salted, each Ark costs more essence than the last one !
They have bonuses to all FIDS, except Food with a -50% penalty, but it is clearly not enough to compensate this Essence thingie.
	All in all, for now, I would recommend the early access mostly if you’re not new with Amplitude 4X. Of course you can enjoy it otherwise, but I would take more time to adapt.

I recommend this game, but not unequivocally. This, as of right now, is a game for the 'few', not the 'many'.
General Description: This game is unfinished and unpolished(but not buggy). This is a 4x game. There is a lot of data(seriously, unless you enjoy options menus to some degree, beware). You can(and probably will) get lost. There are a lot of screens to go through. There are a lot of things to manage. There is a text-dependant narrative. If these things sound good, consider the game.
Comparison to Endless Legend and Endless Space: If you scrapped EL's upgradeable cities, the 'policy' mechanic, the fun RTS battle system, and the minor factions trolling your improvements, and shoved the remainder into ES, I beleive the result would approximate Endless Space 2. This is my favorite of the three at the moment, assuming the studio finishes the rest of the factions, heroes, victory modes, lets you turn off the timed vitory, and fixes the tech tree(and does nothing else).
The devs seem committed to fixing questionable/unpleasant elements of thier game. Really love that. The first update killed a lot of the major issues I had with the game(forced peace, locked planets, forced game end). Too many game devs are so married to thier original notions that they pull the 'artistic integrity' card every time thier product is questioned. I will stop cheerleading Amplitude now.
I really love the graphics, story, UI presentation, art, and ship customization elements of this game.
Really love the intro videos for the factons(Seriously, even if you don't buy the game, check out the Empire's video I love it).
The factions are awesome. See below for summary of each.
VODYANI: Really love the Vodyani(space-vampires). You pretty much choose a couple factons to PO and suck thier souls to build your empire. They are capable of exerting immesne political pressure, but have agonizingly slow expansion and reproduction rates. Thier ships are long, futrusitic, with triangular shapes dominating them. If a Quarian was raised by thier 40K Space Marine uncle, and made to live indefinetly, you'd get something like the Vodyani.
LUMERIS: Cool gangster space-gungans.They can make a ton of money, expand quickly, but can collapse under thier own weight and are prone to political instability. Thier ships look like they used to be merchant vessels. Too shabby for me.
SOPHONS: Didn't like them this go-around. They're the 'science' faction. Thier ships are ovoid apple products and look awesome.
CRAVERS: Instatialble insectoid horde that devours worlds. Conquest faction. They can eat themselves to death, and cannot be at peace. Never tried them. Thier stuff looks like it came from Raxus Prime(Star Wars: Force Unleashed I reference). They're brown and have tubes going places. Angular plating covers the central main body.
EMPIRE: Haven't played them, just watched the intro video. Looks like they're HEAVILY inspired by Warhammer 40K(Never played the game or read lore, friend of mine's a Warhammer 40K nerd). Thier playstyle is industrial/military, and thier ships are rectangles rotated at  45-degree angles with guns along the side, engines and a stubby bridge attached to the rear, and a prow brace in the front. Beware of making the AI the Empire. It had almost triple my score on easy. Paridoxicially, it made no effort to fight back as I destroyed his capital.
RANDOM: Full disclosure: I am a Broken Lords fan. Still hoping the Sheredyn and/or Sowers come back. Unfortunately, I now doubt they will.
Really love the random events(which have all been political as of yet). Adds 'mirco' narrative in a game whose genre is defined by 'macro'-focused mechanics.
The music is pleasant. Personal taste is a large part of this, though. I strongly believe some tracks are faction-specific.
-Lumeris music reminds me of the softer, more epic/fantastical music Ninendo puts out.(i.e. Fire Emblem, Super Smash Bros)
-Craver music reminds me of Tron, in the best way possible.
-Vodyani music reminds me of Mass Effect.
-Sophon music, at least for me, is forgettable.
-The Empire is either a more techno version of Metroid-esque music, or a 31st century rendition of Lord of the Rings music.
The minor factions just don't 'wow' me like other elements in the game. So, it looks like two minor factions spawn. Friended the Hissho, integrated them into my empire, and re-named thier system 'Palaven'. No benefit except a smile, and a planet with a cool improvement I couldn't build at that time.
Your population will leave if approval is low enough. This makes sense but two issues.
1: Where do they go?
2: Why, if they are griping about over-population, not go to a low-population or empty planet you own? This is a beta, so I'm not too irritated about this. Still annoying, however.
The sounds for ship guns seem glitchy. Watched several battles and all I could hear was the music. I have heard them in the loadout screen for ships, and they do sound
cool. I beleive this has been remedied, but not 100% sure yet...
The planet preview screen. Every planet looks like it generates disapproval if colonized. Don't know if this is an error on my part. HOWEVER, the rest of the planet preview mechanics are solid and clear.
(The 'tech tree' critique was removed beceause the studio responded to community feedback and changed it back to the tech web of Endless Space I)
The ground invasion system and subsystems. This is a horrible system, plain and simple. The art for these options is (like the rest of the game art) stellar. If you need a space 4x with a cool invasion mechanic, look elsewhere. Endless Space II will definetly disappoint you.
The various political mechanics seem half-finished. Don't know if they will change or not. I was still wondering what I'd do with the 5,000 influence I had laying around when I won. Hadn't passed new laws in (about)60 turns beceause I like the first two, and don't like the last two(which cost a
more). I finally passed a military scavenging bill midway through the game. Also, playing as the Lumeris. The politcal system also goes the other way. I was playing as a mono-party Vodyani. Stability was great(but a little boring). I was building every improvement I could as the Lumeris, I have
political parties. Too many government changes, give me a one or two party system anyday. Third parties are bad, more are even worse.
Not being able to purge enemy outposts is lame. They mature into colonies, which are full-fledged systems. Personally, I'd just like the option to orbitally bombard the outpost into oblivion.
This review was written on 10/10/2016, updated on 11/30/2016, and reflects Endless Space 2 at that time. I have played 17 hours of the game at the time of writing this.

Every weapon and frame can be slotted with with mods (freely reusable modifiers) to further customize them.

Everything in the game aside from some cosmetics can be aquired without purchasing Platinum (the premium currency).
Platinum itself can be aquiered easily by trading mods and prime parts with other players, allowing you to obtain even the cosmetics without paying a dime.

POST RELEASE UPDATE:
It pains me to bad mouth this game, if you read my initial post you will understand. It has a lot going for it and it is still cheaper than the Civ games, but SEGA put their fingerprints all over this. It felt very rushed, the fighters and bombers for some reason haven't been put in yet, broken tool tips/names (displays like "@%nocost&-!"), the AI is lack luster and inconsistent, win conditions are pretty uneven, and a few other things that bother me.
The game has a lot going for it and it is gorgeous. I highly enjoy the custom race option and you can tell they have learned a lot from previous games but it all of a sudden feels like yet another AAA title that was released too soon because deadlines and money are the only thing SEGA cares about. I'm happy this series is hurting Civ's bottom line because they are money hungry at firaxxis as well, but I am on the fence about this game. I like the historical aspect of Civ but the endless games have so much more going for them.
I will leave this as a thumbs up but with a really big warning. It's cheaper and better than civ imo, but is not without its faults. This is not polished and beware if they start charging soon for DLC without the main game being fixed.
INITIAL EA POST:
I'll start this off by admitting I'm kind of a fanboy when it comes to the Endless games. I've liked them all and while they each had their shortcommings in my opinion, they were great and most importantly, different from other games. ES2 is off to a good start and I can't wait to see where they go with it. I know the store page says it but remember THIS IS ALPHA, don't buy this right now if you are looking for a full functioning game. Its a handful of races, some galaxy creation settings, and the core game with only a few win types. Get into this now only if you want to help flush out bugs and support this team while they finish the product. That being said, it is still a gorgeous game as is and you can still have some really fun games even in barebones form. If you are a return player from ES1, you'll notice the Cravers and Sophons are back along with 2 new races that are interesting to play with. Overall its a good looking start and it doesn't seem like we have too much to worry about from the partnership with SEGA, feels like a good step forward from EL and ES1.

Gameplay - 9/10 ~ I played through L.A. Noire using an Xbox One wired controller so my rating for this aspect of the game could be flawed because Keyboard>Mouse but in this scenario I played through the game on my 40" Television so a keyboard and mouse was less than optimal. However, the gameplay is very fluid and solid in L.A. Noire. I did notice a hint (maybe?) of auto-aim when in combat so that was nice but there were some other weird glitches such as crazy ragdolling and NPC drivers driving stupid, such as switching lanes into you when you have your sirens on among other annoying things. Overall I give the gameplay portion a 9/10.
Story - 11/10 ~ Why? This is one of the most well written stories I have ever played through on a video game. There a definite "twists" and "turns" at every corner! You honestly have no idea what to expect next and that is the mark of a wonderful story! It took me close to 20 hours to beat the game and that was with zero exploration; it was straight through the story. So for a game to be able to deliver that length of story to you without having filler crap in the middle is wonderful! This is why I give the story portion an 11/10
Tech (Graphics, Sound, Animations) - 10/10 The graphics in L.A. Noire are nothing to really write home about but this is coming from a game from 2011 so standards have sure changed in that short time but to me it wasn't really a knock on the game because of the other elements in the game. Sound: All of the sounds in L.A. Noire are industry-standard and they hired some really good actors for the voice work and facial work which i'll get into later. The Soundtrack, oh the soundtrack. TRULY AMAZING! I have never really wanted to buy a soundtrack until I got into L.A. Noire. That main menu music though! PERFECT! It absolutely fits the style/genre of this game and is well crafted and perfect for L.A. Noire.   Animations: L.A. Noire introduced a new facial technology so that the words coming out of the characters mouths would match their mouths movement perfectly and this is something I wish all game developers will start adding into their games. It takes the experience to another level and is vital for a game such as L.A. Noire where you have to try and "read" people when interrogating. I would give this category a 11/10 due solely to the facial/voice tech but the graphics knocked it down to 10. (not too bad I assume).
Overall I give L.A. Noire a 10/10. An absolute brilliant story with revolutionary technology that could help push facial animation in video games to another level. Team Bondi I give you two thumbs up. Bravo gentlemen.

Game is absolutely amazing. There are some pros and cons and I am more than happy to tell you.
Pros
+Plenty of content to do once you start
+Huge helpful community in region chat
+Ton of weapons
+Ton of warframes
+Every weapon and warframe is unique
+Special currency known as platinum can be obtained without buying (starting plat is not tradable)
+Multiple mission types with varying levels and multiple enemy types to keep you on your toes so you don't get too carried away
+Ton of mods to customize your every weapon with anything you may need like fire, electricity, corrosive and many more each effective against specific things like shield and armor
+Multiple means of survival
+Knowledge is power
+It doesn't need to be META to be useful for the most content game has to offer thanks to mentioned mods
+Enduring punishment for long time in missions with rising enemy level is rewarding
+Daily login reward milestone rewards are great and it only counts days you have logged in so no resets
+Clans are a fun addition and gives a real feel and by researching you can get access to some nice stuff
+Syndicates which rewards you for everything you do wearing their sigil and doing their missions
+Despite being power creeping Prime variants offer improved stats and allow you to have good equipment even without too much mastery rank since they rarely got any mastery rank requirements and just make higher levels easier despite only higher levels are found in sortie of day
+Sortie which is 3 mission series can reward you well and got varying levels for those who are too strong for levels 30-40 since level rises each mission going 40-60, 60-80, 80-100
Cons
-Sortie rewards can be a bit bad too no lying
-DE is a little sensitivy about their game and got improvements to be made
-Some warframes are a little off therefore not used (mainly abilities and all that which also makes them a bit useless or make you question why)
-Prime Vault=sucks, primes come and go, they stick around quite a while but once they get vaulted there is little to known chances to get the primes without ton of relics
-So called power creep, which means primes bring better stuff to tabels and therefore makes some guns or at least normal variant of gun useless
-Daily login rewards rarely are too good
-Once you pass specific point in the game all the new content is trivial to get and clan research is just a extra thing to get you contribute for research and join clan which is probably done quite fast
-Clans that are inactive and don't have research are pointless and probably contain middle tier players that can't be as much help to you as experienced veteran
-Some things despite giving something to work towards require ridicilous amounts of things like nitain extracts that you can only obtain from alerts and as reward from one mission I can't remember however trying to get it that way is not effective at all, so if you're busy or otherwise happen to play for short periods of time only sometimes you will have hard time with nitain extract alerts that show up about 4 times a day (oxium is another material that at times can be a pain despite 300 oxium alerts and dropping from enemy since something like Vauban Prime requires 7000 oxium and 20 nitain extracts to build)
-Long waiting times
-Lack of slots for weapons and warframes that you can get only buy with platinum
- + Mastery rank is a huge restrictor since extra standing cap and void trace along with trades per day cap are determined by it (but luckily you can climb ranks fast up to 10), but it keeps some weapons and other stuff so game age extends (if weapon is unlocked in low mastery doesn't mean that it is bad since mastery 2 unlock Sonicor finds popularity among lot of people)

I’ll start off by saying that I wasn’t a huge fan of ES1. The game was competently done and had interesting unique features, like system management over single planets management.
But the diplomacy system was flawed, with lifeless AI contributing to a general lack of « soul », of personality. Hence I found the game to lack appeal in the long run !
Then ES2 happened, and before it Endless Legends, a rich 4x wich has an obvious (good) influence on this « sequel ». Of course you shouldn’t hope for a complete overhaul of ES1’s system, but then again it is not the point.
ES2 benefits from Amplitude learning from their mistakes, turning it into a deeper and improved version of ES1, well worth the money even in Alpha stage (I only encountered one real bug in more thant 10 hours of playing).
Here are some elements I consider to be important, both positive and negative.
I shall update this review after each significant change happening to the game.
IMPROVEMENTS AND NEW STUFF
* Galaxies are more beautiful to look at, same things for planets
* Colonizing a planet does not mean owning the system automatically anymore. A bit like Beyond Earth, colonization begins by installing an outpost, growing into a full-fledged colony after a few turns. You can spend manpower, Dust and Influence to speed up the process.
This way, if there is already an outpost in a system but yours outgrows the other, you gain the system- and the other outpost !
A great way to do early competition.
* Scouts now have probes, which can be used to explore space, or more importantly, explore anomalies for loot, quests and random events. Way better than juste popping out in a system and getting random stuff at your face.
* Freshly imported from Endless Legends, each faction (in addition to a better-crafted background) has a faction quest, many steps reaping different rewards based on your choice.
Makes the game more lively.
* Improved battle viewer, and no more tactics cancelling others ! Honestly I never watch battles, but I can understand the appeal.
* The new political system and its parties allows different laws to be applied, with frequent elections- something to keep an eye on if you want your empire to stay the course you have decided.
* Systems are conquered via groud battles, not with fleets staying in orbit a certain number of turns
* Minor Factions make their entrance, to be conquered or assimilated
SOME ELEMENTS NEEDING TINKERING
* Buyout costs are not properly scaled
* You should have at least one basic option to convert industry into another ressource (dust preferably).
* AI make wacky calls. No, Lumeris, it’s not reasonable to declare war on my Cravers’ hive while I have a complete fleet fully upgraded and you don’t.
AI grow restless too easily and underestimate your power. Sophons, when the most powerful faction is your neighbour, don’t make silly hostile comments. It ends badly.
* Forced truce are just an Alpha thingie, right ? Even so, it’s quite annoying.
* Turns still take a bit long to process
* Some techs and buildings specific to a faction should be available without quests. Speaking of
buildings, I hope we won’t have to wait a DLC to build Galactic Wonders/ Special Projects.
* Some quests are unbalanced, leading to sub-optimal gameplay choices, or delaying/failing them. Yes, I look at you, «Those darn kids ». I can’t build only science improvements and have better things to do that stuff those hangars with vessels !
* The techs needed to colonize different types of worlds need to be reworked. Is it useful to have at the same time a different tech for snow, ice and toundra planets ?
* At present, the factions are unbalanced. Further analysis just below.
THE FACTIONS
- Sophons. Nothing much to write home about. They still do science and can easily lead the score if left at their own device. More probably, they are gonna be bullied by an aggro faction.
- Cravers. They enjoy a huge boost of ressources (+50%) but all their planets eventually become barren (-50% on all ressources). The depletion rate is slow enough, combined with huge fleets right at the start and no interest into diplomacy whatsoever, to make them quite menacing.
Keep eating other factions like a Craver should, and I think going Craver is the easiest way to win for now.
A bit bizarre to see them having conflicting political interests with a Hive Mind- but if they had free reign here, they would be definetely too powerful.
In other words : Cravers are still bad news.
- Lumeris, dust-driven. They don’t use colonization ships, instead magically buying outposts,
wich is more reliable and considerably faster. Dust is also used to ensnare minor factions instead of Influence- again, more reliable and faster. With the right law(s), Dust is overflowing with this faction. In addition to the previous advantages, you can quickly enough mass buyout stuff, like a complete fleet in one turn.
So, if they have a good start, Lumeris could be quite tough to be stopped. So much Dust can be useful for pretty much anything else !
- Vodyani. Clearly based on the Broken Lords from Endless Legend, with the major difference that they suck. See, they have those nice Arks- powerful ships needing to stay at a system to control it. The good thing is that an Ark colonize every planet in a system- provided you possess the adequate technologies.
The very bad thing is that a new Ark can only be created via Essence. And you can only gather Essence by leeching population from an enemy system. It forces you to build a very early fleet of fragiles ships to do some leechin’.
Even if you happen to have a faction not too far from your home system, they will not be terribly happy about your population theft and will attack as soon as they can. Yeah for diplomacy, right ?
Even in ideal conditions, colonization with the Vodyani will be delayed. They can convert their dust production to Essence, but it will cripple you for the duration of the process and you will lose money fast.
They desperatly need an early building to have a steady, if modest, income of Essence. Because the wound needs to be salted, each Ark costs more essence than the last one !
They have bonuses to all FIDS, except Food with a -50% penalty, but it is clearly not enough to compensate this Essence thingie.
	All in all, for now, I would recommend the early access mostly if you’re not new with Amplitude 4X. Of course you can enjoy it otherwise, but I would take more time to adapt.

I recommend this game, but not unequivocally. This, as of right now, is a game for the 'few', not the 'many'.
General Description: This game is unfinished and unpolished(but not buggy). This is a 4x game. There is a lot of data(seriously, unless you enjoy options menus to some degree, beware). You can(and probably will) get lost. There are a lot of screens to go through. There are a lot of things to manage. There is a text-dependant narrative. If these things sound good, consider the game.
Comparison to Endless Legend and Endless Space: If you scrapped EL's upgradeable cities, the 'policy' mechanic, the fun RTS battle system, and the minor factions trolling your improvements, and shoved the remainder into ES, I beleive the result would approximate Endless Space 2. This is my favorite of the three at the moment, assuming the studio finishes the rest of the factions, heroes, victory modes, lets you turn off the timed vitory, and fixes the tech tree(and does nothing else).
The devs seem committed to fixing questionable/unpleasant elements of thier game. Really love that. The first update killed a lot of the major issues I had with the game(forced peace, locked planets, forced game end). Too many game devs are so married to thier original notions that they pull the 'artistic integrity' card every time thier product is questioned. I will stop cheerleading Amplitude now.
I really love the graphics, story, UI presentation, art, and ship customization elements of this game.
Really love the intro videos for the factons(Seriously, even if you don't buy the game, check out the Empire's video I love it).
The factions are awesome. See below for summary of each.
VODYANI: Really love the Vodyani(space-vampires). You pretty much choose a couple factons to PO and suck thier souls to build your empire. They are capable of exerting immesne political pressure, but have agonizingly slow expansion and reproduction rates. Thier ships are long, futrusitic, with triangular shapes dominating them. If a Quarian was raised by thier 40K Space Marine uncle, and made to live indefinetly, you'd get something like the Vodyani.
LUMERIS: Cool gangster space-gungans.They can make a ton of money, expand quickly, but can collapse under thier own weight and are prone to political instability. Thier ships look like they used to be merchant vessels. Too shabby for me.
SOPHONS: Didn't like them this go-around. They're the 'science' faction. Thier ships are ovoid apple products and look awesome.
CRAVERS: Instatialble insectoid horde that devours worlds. Conquest faction. They can eat themselves to death, and cannot be at peace. Never tried them. Thier stuff looks like it came from Raxus Prime(Star Wars: Force Unleashed I reference). They're brown and have tubes going places. Angular plating covers the central main body.
EMPIRE: Haven't played them, just watched the intro video. Looks like they're HEAVILY inspired by Warhammer 40K(Never played the game or read lore, friend of mine's a Warhammer 40K nerd). Thier playstyle is industrial/military, and thier ships are rectangles rotated at  45-degree angles with guns along the side, engines and a stubby bridge attached to the rear, and a prow brace in the front. Beware of making the AI the Empire. It had almost triple my score on easy. Paridoxicially, it made no effort to fight back as I destroyed his capital.
RANDOM: Full disclosure: I am a Broken Lords fan. Still hoping the Sheredyn and/or Sowers come back. Unfortunately, I now doubt they will.
Really love the random events(which have all been political as of yet). Adds 'mirco' narrative in a game whose genre is defined by 'macro'-focused mechanics.
The music is pleasant. Personal taste is a large part of this, though. I strongly believe some tracks are faction-specific.
-Lumeris music reminds me of the softer, more epic/fantastical music Ninendo puts out.(i.e. Fire Emblem, Super Smash Bros)
-Craver music reminds me of Tron, in the best way possible.
-Vodyani music reminds me of Mass Effect.
-Sophon music, at least for me, is forgettable.
-The Empire is either a more techno version of Metroid-esque music, or a 31st century rendition of Lord of the Rings music.
The minor factions just don't 'wow' me like other elements in the game. So, it looks like two minor factions spawn. Friended the Hissho, integrated them into my empire, and re-named thier system 'Palaven'. No benefit except a smile, and a planet with a cool improvement I couldn't build at that time.
Your population will leave if approval is low enough. This makes sense but two issues.
1: Where do they go?
2: Why, if they are griping about over-population, not go to a low-population or empty planet you own? This is a beta, so I'm not too irritated about this. Still annoying, however.
The sounds for ship guns seem glitchy. Watched several battles and all I could hear was the music. I have heard them in the loadout screen for ships, and they do sound
cool. I beleive this has been remedied, but not 100% sure yet...
The planet preview screen. Every planet looks like it generates disapproval if colonized. Don't know if this is an error on my part. HOWEVER, the rest of the planet preview mechanics are solid and clear.
(The 'tech tree' critique was removed beceause the studio responded to community feedback and changed it back to the tech web of Endless Space I)
The ground invasion system and subsystems. This is a horrible system, plain and simple. The art for these options is (like the rest of the game art) stellar. If you need a space 4x with a cool invasion mechanic, look elsewhere. Endless Space II will definetly disappoint you.
The various political mechanics seem half-finished. Don't know if they will change or not. I was still wondering what I'd do with the 5,000 influence I had laying around when I won. Hadn't passed new laws in (about)60 turns beceause I like the first two, and don't like the last two(which cost a
more). I finally passed a military scavenging bill midway through the game. Also, playing as the Lumeris. The politcal system also goes the other way. I was playing as a mono-party Vodyani. Stability was great(but a little boring). I was building every improvement I could as the Lumeris, I have
political parties. Too many government changes, give me a one or two party system anyday. Third parties are bad, more are even worse.
Not being able to purge enemy outposts is lame. They mature into colonies, which are full-fledged systems. Personally, I'd just like the option to orbitally bombard the outpost into oblivion.

Overview:
A wonderful game you'll love to have in your library for enjoying some quiet down time. You'll find you keep coming back and you'll learn to love the phrase "just one more turn!" -- 10/10 Better than Civ, AOE, C&C or Total War
Pros:
Beautifully artisitic and highly detailed, in every way
Some of the most modern infographic menus and interfaces I've ever encountered
Endless hours, 100, 200, 300+ of highly addictive gameplay with no reason to stop going back
Soundtrack [best experienced on headphones] is mystical and engaging, and very relaxing to listen to
Logical game mechanics that make sense - if you go to war, militarist voters will probably win the next election. If you go bankrupt, you'll face a series of austerity measures and cutbacks. If you build a big fleet of starships, you'll need an even bigger pot of cash/'dust' to pay for the upkeep
Definitely still FEELS like Endless Space!
Multiple victory conditions that are equally balanced. You can win through military, scientific or diplomatic means. Gone are the days of kill everything to win - in fact that's the most boring way to win this game!
Cons:
Slow gameplay until at least 1hour of play
No realtime battles (personally I like it this way, but a disappointment to some)
If you are new to the genre, this game is unimaginably complex with only textual tutorials in-game
You commit 100hrs to a single campaign, you win, then it's game over. Your empire is gone forever, and you just start again.
What I'd like to see improved:
Audio dialogue tutorials giving a quick 5min gist of the component of the game, to include getting started, strategies and pitfalls
More diverse space battles, with a slightly greater emphaisis on the player's abilitynto influence (formations, tactics, etc)
Some form of progressive post game system of rewards would be fantastic - How you conquered one gaalaxy could determine your factions traits for the next game?

POST RELEASE UPDATE:
It pains me to bad mouth this game, if you read my initial post you will understand. It has a lot going for it and it is still cheaper than the Civ games, but SEGA put their fingerprints all over this. It felt very rushed, the fighters and bombers for some reason haven't been put in yet, broken tool tips/names (displays like "@%nocost&-!"), the AI is lack luster and inconsistent, win conditions are pretty uneven, and a few other things that bother me.
The game has a lot going for it and it is gorgeous. I highly enjoy the custom race option and you can tell they have learned a lot from previous games but it all of a sudden feels like yet another AAA title that was released too soon because deadlines and money are the only thing SEGA cares about. I'm happy this series is hurting Civ's bottom line because they are money hungry at firaxxis as well, but I am on the fence about this game. I like the historical aspect of Civ but the endless games have so much more going for them.
I will leave this as a thumbs up but with a really big warning. It's cheaper and better than civ imo, but is not without its faults. This is not polished and beware if they start charging soon for DLC without the main game being fixed.
INITIAL EA POST:
I'll start this off by admitting I'm kind of a fanboy when it comes to the Endless games. I've liked them all and while they each had their shortcommings in my opinion, they were great and most importantly, different from other games. ES2 is off to a good start and I can't wait to see where they go with it. I know the store page says it but remember THIS IS ALPHA, don't buy this right now if you are looking for a full functioning game. Its a handful of races, some galaxy creation settings, and the core game with only a few win types. Get into this now only if you want to help flush out bugs and support this team while they finish the product. That being said, it is still a gorgeous game as is and you can still have some really fun games even in barebones form. If you are a return player from ES1, you'll notice the Cravers and Sophons are back along with 2 new races that are interesting to play with. Overall its a good looking start and it doesn't seem like we have too much to worry about from the partnership with SEGA, feels like a good step forward from EL and ES1.

Eventually, after buying a few warframe and weapon slots, you start to feel that your character's A E S T H E T I C does not represent the hours you've put in to leveling. You've put about 100 hours in these past 2 months, and you already feel like a pro. So why the hell not? You buy a cool looking "syandana" thing, and it has flames coming out the back so you already feel twice as powerful!
Within your first 6 months you have amassed a few color palattes, a few prime frames, and cool looking armor. You've roped your friends in so you can all feel like space-pirate-power-rangers together.
Then maybe a glitch happens, or your files corrupt, or you move somewhere with internet that can't even handle your search engine, or worse, DE releases another update the size of Texas and instead of being excited, you decide to take a hiatus. Do you even like this game?
You try playing other games, but it doesn't feel the same. You miss being able to jump 50 feet in the air and turn invisible. Nothing quite matches the feeling of winning a level by fingering W and E harder than a doctor examining a prostate. Or maybe it's just because you've spent more time and money on this game than you care to admit.
Reluctantly, you rope yourself back in. Things have changed since the last update. Solar map X.0 is very different from solar map (X-3).0, but you eventually forget all about it. However, when you notice all your friends are now 5 mastery ranks ahead of you, a switch goes off in your head that sends you into absolute lunacy. You haven't kept a budget since, well, you don't remember, so you stock up on plat. It is 75% off as per your conveniently rewarded log in bonus. There are even more things to build, level up, paint, dress up, and hoard, so you figure you better get started.
Within a week or two you've caught up. You have 7 pets in stasis, and all of the prime warframes. No, wait, you're missing (however many are vaulted) of them! You never thought you'd ever buy prime access, giving in to your carnal desires for shiny things that no one else has. Alas, it comes with a free warframe slot so it's worth it, right?
After a while, the game gets way too easy. You can speedrun Alad V as easily as wiping sauce off a pasta bowl. You and your friends regularly do sorties and raids to show off your progress and how overpowered you've become.
Panic! You just got an alert! Is it gift of the lotus? Is it nitain? Tellerium? A formorian you have to sweep away? No, it is from your bank, and your checking accound has just gone into the negative. But wait, you thought you were good with money?
Upon checking your transaction history, you are shocked. This free to play game has just sucked you dry. You realize you haven't been to work in a while. What does a flower smell like again?
This game has become your crack, your liquor, your scientologist preacher! It's taken all you own, and for what? Shiny robots with voluptuous curves?
You try to run away. But much like Tom Cruise, you realized you've spent too much money on this thing to give it up entirely, and so you become a stronger advocate of the game than ever. You play for hours on end, hoping to get as far as you can with what you have already spent. You learn to actually manage your inventory for once, and get involved with the trading economy, selling off your more valuable items for precious plat. You beg more people to join! This game is the best game ever made! Look how funny the glitches are, and how hilariously the grineer talk! Watch what happens when I press 4 and then 5!
Denial is in full swing now. This has been time well spent. You even go out of your way to write a positive review of the game.
You know what, I don't know what all the fuss that I've been making is about! This game is fantastic. The randomly generated levels and carefully selected and well thought out game types never get repetitive! Interception missions are my favorite, even more so if they are arcwing based! Shotguns are so useful; I'm glad they get all of the good mods, but too bad they rarely drop! And riven challenges aren't annoying at all! I don't miss fusion cores: magic dust and credits are much more intuitive! Don't even get me started on fissures, and the lack of survival missions for them doesn't make me want to cry. After all, fighting randomly spawning enemies that are 10 levels higher than the regular ones in the middle of a spy mission isn't annoying at all. Baro K'teer always has what I'm looking for, and at a reasonable price! Darvo Deals are not a scam!
And most importantly, remember: Warframe is not a cult.
Im really excited to play this game as it slowly progresses into something so much bigger! Playing it with my friends and discovering cool stuff together is awesome!

L.A Noire is a game set in Los Angeles after World War II, during the "Golden Age of Hollywood". You play as Cole Phelps, a detective who must work his way through the LAPD, solving cases and making arrests. This is one of the best games I've ever played, and I sincerely congratulate Rockstar on their fine work.
Firstly, it should be known that the voicework and character animations in this game are fantastic; without this, the game wouldn't work half as well as it did. The characters move and interact seamlessly, due to the innovative use of motion capture technology. During interviews, the player has to read into facial expressions and determine whether a suspect is lying or telling the truth. Due to the impressive animations on display, you can read every eye twitch, uneasy posture and downward glance. These interview sections are the highlight of the game, and it was genuinely entertaining to complete them using evidence and intuition.
The basic game mechanics function just like any other Rockstar game; a large (beautifully made) open world, in this case, the grime and glamour of 1950's Los Angeles. You can roam the city on foot or in a vehicle, resolving street crime cases and responding to pleas for police intervention. During a case, you'll often have to travel around the city to meet suspects and other characters, so you'll easily notice the size and attention to detail put into the open world. Additionally, during a case you have to analyse different pieces of evidence, and you'll quickly learn how to integrate these pieces of evidence into the case. It was truly immersive to act like a proper detective, and fans of old crime shows will be delighted here.
Without giving anything away, the story is quite investing, and you'll find yourself truly interested in Cole Phelps' story. I don't want to spoil anything, but Rockstar really knows how to make a decent narrative.
The only flaw with this game is the horrible optimisation for PC; the graphics are high quality and very consistent, but the port is not well optimised at all. I can barely maintain an acceptable framerate throughout the game, but I persisted due to the quality of the game content. This may be my own error due to using an AMDD Graphics card.
Overall, L.A Noire is a highly worthwhile and entertaining experience. The immersive story and gameplay really held me right to the end, but the poor optimisation is the only thing holding this game back from a 10. Well crafted, and I'd love to see a sequel to this one. 9.5 / 10

This game was utterly fantastic at immersing you into the atmosphere of the late 1940's.  Hats off to the developers.
The detective work was fun, but It sort of had its own subtle way of holding your hand, ex. sound cues, a limited amount of hints, giving you the option to skip a sequence if it becomes troubling to you, etc.  However, these things can be turned off in the options menu, giving the hardcore detective wanna-bes no conflict.
My single playthrough gave me nearly 30 hours of content, including the dlcs.  I did every side mission (street crimes), but didn't obtain the entire exploration extras; real life landmarks, hidden badges and film reels, and collecting the cars from the time.
I gotta tell you, after finding the hidden vintage cars...That was some serious eye-candy.  If you are into restoration or you are a vintage collector you will probably turn ecstatic.
The gameplay was okay but nothing really special
The graphics were nice, but had the occasional texture pop-ins.
Last, but not least, the realistic character face imagery was awesome.  The purpose was using it to decide whether a person was lying or telling the truth.  Some of the reactions were hilariously overblown and gave an obvious sign of deceit, giving the game more of a "helping hand".
If you like this period or like detective games, I say make the purchase.  I'm sure you won't be disappointed.

+ Realistic weapon hits. If you hit a wall then your weapon will bounce off it instead of just keep on swinging. So if you have a low ceiling and a long sword you can forget about down swings.
-Fps is capped at 62. You can manually unlock fps which REALLY helps sense this is a twitch based game. I am playing on a 120Hz LED LCD TV with 2ms refresh rate so your experience may vary. You can claim that the human eye can see a differance between 60fps and 120 fps but if you have the hardware to try it then actually try it. You wont go back.
-Accelerated attacks need to be fixed. People will look up or down in order to exploit hit boxes on their weapons to make a weapon hit sooner than if you were to actually look at the target and swing. This happens because anywhere you weapon swings your weapon will hit.
-Team mates can be dumb. Sometimes it feels like they are trying to feed me into a meat grinder because I need to move back to dodge an incoming attack but my teammate is trying to hump my leg which prevents me from moving back. Then there are the idiots that think I have eyes in the back of my head so they think I will move out of the way of their attack while they swing from behind me at an enemy in front of me. This often results in the loss of a limb.
-Ping really matters. Anything about 200ms is results in lots of teleporting and such. So play a server near you if you don’t want to get kicked. dont expact to live on the west coast and play with a friend on the east coast. one of you will have a bad time.
Overall I would recommend this game to anyone that wants a skill based game. It’s not about who’s weapon is better that whos. It’s not about what class is better than the other. Yes, classes do better against certain ones but that’s not the deciding factor of who wins the fight. In the end it’s all about who did better.

Look, do not play this if you want instant gratification. 4x games aren't like that in the first place. Even less so with a developer that released on EARLY ACCESS before. EARLY ACCESS kiddos is where a developer cares about your constructive input to make the game better.
Now, onto the content I've discovered. Many of the old mechanics from Endless Legend and Endless Space 1 are combined to help bring this new era of Endless Space 2 much more lively. Diplomacy, for the races that CAN use it, includes an evolving internal political structure within your races empire.
You focus on tech that is industrial? That party will potentially grow in power. There are events you make decisions on that will effect what laws you can pass. As well as what heros you can hire. Do you decide that a docile animal species is for eatting or making pets? Impacts your political structure.
Probe the hell out of the all the things. Planets have either loot or resources you scout out with probes. These are also used to scout ahead into potentially enemy territory or to find constelations not on your usual star lanes.
The Vodani don't seed planets with colony ships. They have massive Arks that can pack up all their tech built and be a titan force itself to be recokend with as a fighting ship. In order to build more of these titans you need an additional resource unique to them. Essence. You either convert dust to essence or you harvest other planets existing colonies to get that precious resource.
The Lumeris can buyout new potential colonies as an outpost and invest in their growth. All their tech bears down on dust. Dust make the universe go round. Utilize diplomacy to its greatest degree with this race. Trade new planets, tech, whatever. With enough dust you can conquer everyone.
At the core of the game are race specific story arcs that can be ignored or focused on explain in depth their driving nature.
These guys make a return but I have not played them yet.
The Sophons are Scientific Geniuses. It is best to research all of the things.
The Cravers consume plantes as they conquer them. The species created by the Endless to do just that. They have no other purpose. Go to war, consume more planets.
