First of, I don't say it's not a good game.
It is a good game, but it lacks the soul of it's predecessor.
Endless space had it's own way of aproach to 4X game and it's wonderfuly simple yet thought out design.
Endless space 2 is trying to make things more simple.
You no longer can adjust taxes to get out of hard times.
In combat you choose only one of three options for aproach and there is no reason to watch the fight real-time, since you can't change anything mid-battle.
Customizing ships is no longer by filling up tonnage, but instead you have hard points that can be filled with weapons or some other module.
And few other things I forgot.
Then they also try to use some of the features from Endless Legend, like the science eras and quests. For me racial quests shouldn't be part of the 4X games, but I don't have nothing against event-like quests.
They also added some features that are completely new for endless.
Like political parties and multiple species on a planet. So far I can't say wether I think those changes are good or not.
But one thing is interesting, and that's laws. You can use political parties to pass laws that affect your faction, like for example that other races can't increase population on planets under your control. (I played religious fanatics and this is the only law I remember)
I'm not saying it's a bad game.
I was completely taken by the original Endless Space and to see them change the thing that I liked about it means that I just can't recomend it.
But maybe it's the game for you, so look at some other reviews and decide for yourself, if you want to try it.

Welcome to L.A in the late 40's, where everyone is a racist ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in America. I've beaten L.A Noire before on Xbox, but that was when it came out. I have recently purchased it on Steam and it was a nice trip. Now I'm going to say this, the game is underated to me but I can totally see why people do not enjoy it as much as I did. It's a simple, yet complicated game. It's your standard Rockstar game at its core (open world, shoot, explore, nice story) but not your standard Rockstar game at the same time. First of all, not really open world. You do not get to explore the world whithout any kind of restriction because you're always on a case or mission. You could start a mission, forget it and just explore L.A , but to say the truth, it isn't that interesting compared to other open world games. It's a third person shooter, but you don't shoot a lot in the game since you are a Policeman, but when you do, it's fun yet way too easy (only need 1 bullet to the head and BAM!). The game, did not age that well, but the facial animation still impress me and all. The story of the game is very good I find, but really feels rushed towards the end ♥♥♥♥♥♥ending). What really makes the game shine to me is the way you do interagations. You are a cop, you try to solve murders or crimes, you need clues and you will interogate possible suspects. The interagation is simple, by looking at someones facial animation or tone of the voice, you decide if someone is telling the truth, lying (backing up with clues you find during the case) or if you doubt (which is lying but that you don't have any proof to back it up). The second thing I like about the game are the characters. No, I do not like Cole Phelps (main character), he's an angry prick and I don't find him interesting. But all your partners you have in the game to help you are all very interesting and different. Also the game has a really good sountrack IMO.
In the end, the game doesn't feel that open world, a little easy on the combat side, a really good story (gets bad towards the end :( ), amazing facial animation and great characters. I give this game a 8/10

Look, do not play this if you want instant gratification. 4x games aren't like that in the first place. Even less so with a developer that released on EARLY ACCESS before. EARLY ACCESS kiddos is where a developer cares about your constructive input to make the game better.

You focus on tech that is industrial? That party will potentially grow in power. There are events you make decisions on that will effect what laws you can pass. As well as what heros you can hire. Do you decide that a docile animal species is for eatting or making pets? Impacts your political structure.
Probe the hell out of the all the things. Planets have either loot or resources you scout out with probes. These are also used to scout ahead into potentially enemy territory or to find constelations not on your usual star lanes.
The Vodani don't seed planets with colony ships. They have massive Arks that can pack up all their tech built and be a titan force itself to be recokend with as a fighting ship. In order to build more of these titans you need an additional resource unique to them. Essence. You either convert dust to essence or you harvest other planets existing colonies to get that precious resource.
The Lumeris can buyout new potential colonies as an outpost and invest in their growth. All their tech bears down on dust. Dust make the universe go round. Utilize diplomacy to its greatest degree with this race. Trade new planets, tech, whatever. With enough dust you can conquer everyone.
At the core of the game are race specific story arcs that can be ignored or focused on explain in depth their driving nature.

The Cravers consume plantes as they conquer them. The species created by the Endless to do just that. They have no other purpose. Go to war, consume more planets.

First of, I don't say it's not a good game.
It is a good game, but it lacks the soul of it's predecessor.
Endless space had it's own way of aproach to 4X game and it's wonderfuly simple yet thought out design.
Endless space 2 is trying to make things more simple.
You no longer can adjust taxes to get out of hard times.
In combat you choose only one of three options for aproach and there is no reason to watch the fight real-time, since you can't change anything mid-battle.
Customizing ships is no longer by filling up tonnage, but instead you have hard points that can be filled with weapons or some other module.
And few other things I forgot.
Then they also try to use some of the features from Endless Legend, like the science eras and quests. For me racial quests shouldn't be part of the 4X games, but I don't have nothing against event-like quests.
They also added some features that are completely new for endless.
Like political parties and multiple species on a planet. So far I can't say wether I think those changes are good or not.
But one thing is interesting, and that's laws. You can use political parties to pass laws that affect your faction, like for example that other races can't increase population on planets under your control. (I played religious fanatics and this is the only law I remember)
I'm not saying it's a bad game.
I was completely taken by the original Endless Space and to see them change the thing that I liked about it means that I just can't recomend it.
But maybe it's the game for you, so look at some other reviews and decide for yourself, if you want to try it.

L.A Noire is probably the most innovative game released by Rockstar. It is also probably one if the best stories delivered by Rockstar in recent years. L.A Noire has you playing as an LAPD detective in post WWII Los Angeles. The setting is fantastic not only because of how faithfully the city is recreated but the incredible ways that the city reminds you off the time period. Posters for Richard Nixon adorn the streets, new housing developments are omnipresent and history topics like the GI Bill are brought up plenty of times.
L.A. Noire's facial capture technology is at the forefront of this game and it certainly delivers. Actors' faces are fully captured and although the stiffness of the rest of their animations looks creepy, it is hard not to respect the technical achievement.
L.A. Noire has an amazing story that should not be spoiled at all. Unfortunately, this is also the game's biggest problem. The game is divided into "cases" where you have to investigate a crime scene, interrogate suspects and find the culprit. This is really fun... for the first 5 cases or so. The game then seems to feed you an stream of long cases where the story barely advances. This is made worse by the fact that the outcome of each case is not affected by your detective skills. You can mess up just about every interrogation and crime scene investigation and it won't affect whether you suceed or fail. That said, when the story does pick up near the end, the game draws every detail from the game together into and ending you will never forget.
Note: You need a good computer to play this game. If you can't experience LA in its full detail, it isn't even worth playing.

It's Endless Space with all of the best additions from Endless Legend added in, plus a few new things of its own. The production values are through the roof and I'm excited for future development.
Amplitude's 4x games have only become better over time, and they also manage to be familiar to 4x veterans while rebelling against the mold created by other games in the genre. Everything is just slightly different from MoO or Civ in exciting ways. On a subjective note they have engrossing worlds with heaps of lore and references to their other games (For example, Endless Legend, the fantasy 4x, takes place on the planet Auriga, which is a unique planet found in Endless Space).
At the time of this review the game is in a VERY early stage, do not purchase it right now expecting a full game - you can play through to a game's conclusion but there are only 4 factions, very few galaxy options, etc.
I also purchased the first Endless Space and Endless Legend in a very Early Access stage and was impressed at how quickly they were developed - Amplitude is no amateur indie studio and they don't dilly-dally when it comes to developing their EA titles.

Warframe is "the" definitive game for people who like to GRIND and trade, while sporting a sweet S&M Suit.
It follows a satisfying cycle of see something cool you want to wear or use -> Find out how to build or aquire it -> Grind for it or its materials -> Build it -> Master it (level it) -> Repeat endlessly.
Every weapon and frame is unique, some more than others.
Every weapon and frame can be slotted with with mods (freely reusable modifiers) to further customize them.
Mods themselves are another whole layer of grindable gear essentialy.
Combat is very fast paced and gets faster once you master the movement system provided.
Some missions allow you play a stealthy ninja, some let you mow through endless waves of steadily strengthening enemies like an unstoppable beserker demigod, and some are somewhere between those.
Everything in the game aside from some cosmetics can be aquired without purchasing Platinum (the premium currency).
Platinum itself can be aquiered easily by trading mods and prime parts with other players, allowing you to obtain even the cosmetics without paying a dime.
With some guile and determination, you will experience growth and profit....GROFIT!
This one really is free to play and I wish more devs would follow a similar model.

The story of "Why I love this awful game..."
This game is bad... really bad... You are given this big city in which you are not allowed to do anything. Literally, you can run or drive around, hoping to find crime scene in which you start totally generic and boring missions where you do few thing over and over again... You are trying to catch someone, or fight, or shoot... It's always more or less, the same...
Not including gun fights, which are somewhat ok, melee fighting and running is awful... Hand to hand combat looks like two ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, trying to hit each-other, and running controls are usually too sensitive, and there are some obstacles that you cannot jump or pass, although they are easily accessible... The worst part of running is that, you usually cannot outrun anyone... You just run until they are cornered in which case you either start a hand-to-hand fight (OMG!!!) or just catch them... And, hand to hand fighting almost always starts when they "hide" behind the corner and wait for you to pass and "surprise" you... Ofcourse, you see them, they are standing there, their hand is there, dangling around the corner, map shows the big dot of your assailant, but you can't do anything, you just need to pass and be hit like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moron...
Car driving is also pretty dull... All cars feel pretty much the same, and, given the time period, are pretty slow, but that is understandable...
And, the most awful thing is actually trying to follow someone... Be it either on foot or in the car... You just need to be extremely slow, and if they catch you, do it all over again... Ok, that is the point of following, but THAT IS NOT FUN! And this is the game, and if you really need to do it, don't do it 100 times... It's boring...
So, when you think that questioning system is nice... It is, really, not... Whenever someone answers your question, you must either say that they are telling the truth, you can doubt their answer or tell that they are lying (in which case you must have the evidence)... In the first half, you can easily tell when someone is not telling the truth, so just doubt it, if you have no evidence... But near the end of the game, there are some questions, when you just can't tell if someone is telling the truth, and you don't have evidence for lying... So... good luck, 50/50 doubt or truth... Well, ok, it's not supposed to be easy, far from that, but I want it to be as near to perfect as possible, and you cannot load conversation again... :/ This is not so important and bad as those problems mentioned above, but could've been better...
But... As the title said... Why I LOVE this awful game...
Although whole game is really bad in terms of almost any game mechanics... It is one fantastic interactive movie... Voice acting is great, facial expressions are fantastic and story just feels real almost all the time... Especially when you reach the Arson department, when things start to unroll...
Characters also feel real, and I really started to understand their motivations, fears and emotions... From that point of view, this game is amazing...
So, TLDR; This game should have been a movie... It is an awful game experience, with absolutely amazing actors and story writers... I will recommend it just for that, because when I finished it, I really wanted to "play" it again and see all the characters, their stories and ends...

This is a very painful downvote to cast. It's hard to argue with Amplitude's track record - Endless Space, Endless Legend, and Dungeon of the Endless are all fantastic games, but after Endless Space 2, I have to admit I have much less confidence in their ability to produce a sequel.
The fundamental problem with Endless Space 2 is that it's barely recognizeable as a sequel to Endless Space. In fact, this game is far more like a sequel to Endless Legend - the tech tree is the same, Influence system, minor factions, and many more are taken straight from EL. Aside from the fact that ES2 has a starmap and EL has a hex grid, the games are nearly identical; and quite frankly, it all worked better in EL. The tech system is completely incompatible with the rest of the game, there's new mechanics like force truce which are broken and underthought, and many other frustrating and questionable changes have been made.
Even if they iron out all of the problems underlining every core mechanic of this game, unless they completely overhaul them, this game will never be a sequel to Endless Space. The tech tree was one of the most unique and compelling features of ES1, and it's been completely removed in this game. Diplomacy is completely alien to players of the first, and appeasing other empires can be done with compliments instead of resources. Resources themselves are now accrued and stockpiled, rather than simply being collected perpetually. And that isn't to say any of these mechanics are BAD, but as a sequel, "not being bad" is absolutely not a justification for changing core mechanics. You have to be able to say that the new mechanics are BETTER; that gutting the tech tree and redesigning diplomacy and all the other stuff doesn't just make for a good game, but for a good ENDLESS SPACE game. It does not seem any consideration was made to this end; even the developer blogs all talk about the mechanics as they are now, without comparison or acknowledgment of the original game.
To be honest, I was surprised at first that this game is rated so highly. Maybe that's because Endless Space was always my favorite game by Amplitude, and I was mostly lukewarm on Endless Legend. Keep that in mind when deciding if this game is right for you - maybe I'm in the minority in not enjoying Endless Legend as much as Endless Space, but if you also find yourself in that minority, you should wait until this game is much further along in development and then assess how it lives up to the original. But as of right now, developer comments in their forums suggest that they are committed to making these changes work, and are not considering removing or undoing any of the changes. Myself, I'm far too disappointed in this sequel to keep playing it, and I doubt it will ever provide an experience comparable to the first Endless Space.....

I have never made a review out of an online game or even mobile game, because I never felt I had the right to do so and the experience to give a proper review. I just hit around 1000 hours in game and I think that maybe it's time I share the sheer joy of playing this game to others. Surprisingly and sadly, only a few people know about it. All I want is for people to know more about this game and to support the developers. I love it. The physics, the graphics, the fluidity, the customizing, the community, and so much more. Let us also not forget about FASHION FRAMING :)) Anyway, I'll break down my review into bulletpoints to highlight the good things about this game and what makes me keep coming back to it. Before I start, I would just like to clarify that everything I will be explaining and sharing is based solely on MY OPINION and with the hope of other gamers also desiring to play this game and support it's developers. Forgive me also if I explain things to vaguely.
- You do not really need to spend any real money to enjoy this game. It focuses on farming and gathering materials which turns off many people but for me I think it is a needed mechanic. You may acquire everything without dishing any cash but perpare to WAIT for a while before getting the things you desire. Personally I bought some stuff after playing a couple hundred hours or so just to say thanks to the developers for such a nice game. I never bought a single frame or even a weapon. This things I bought were literally cosmetics haha. But the game offers lots of other cosmetics that do not even need real cash. The TENNOGEN ib steam is to die for haha.  Trading is key. You are able to obtain the things you want through trading with other people except certain cosmetics.
-Speaking of people, this game seriously has the best community I have ever encountered in an online game. Anywhere you go, there will always be rude people, but I almost never encounter them here in Warframe. The rude ones are mostly people who are in a hurry or if you waste their time. Everyone just wants to help everyone. Scamming is not even possible because the trading system is very well thought of.
- Cool weapons, Warframes, powers, and etc. This game makes you create your own machine of death personally customized from the color of your gun to the content it spits out towards your enemy. The customization is huge. Of course there's a meta like all games do, but the combination and creativity you can do with all the power of the frames and the weapons almost feels limitless.
-Graphics is beautiful, the lighting and the skills look so beautiful. I feel like i'm worshipping this game already with my review hahaha
- Gameplay, better if you just try it out. Very fluid and satisfactory. Especially melee and hitting those red crits. It feels glorious haha.
Anyway I am gonna cut things short since I kinda feel lost on what to share anymore and I feel like i'm blabbing stuff. I am not sure I am able to explain quite clearly.

At the moment the game is very much unfinished. There are quite a few features missing. It is basically more Endless Space, but shinier, looking better. UI is very nice, even if a bit hard to get used to at first.
Personally I'd like the devs to add more into research trees, more buildings/improvements as there are not many at the moment. Also the only difference at the moment between different Era weapons are colors and strength, nothing interesting.
While the combat is very, very cinematic, aside how you plan your fleet to move into combat, everything is automated. No cards whatsoever like in Endless Space, no control at all like in MoO.
The customization of hulls is improved upon Endless Space, but I feel the hero ships could use way more customization in the way of looks, ship types or hull sizes. At the moment hero ships look all like red/white hospital cars.
I've ran into some heavy overpopulation/over colonization problems that the game didn't explain at all, which is okay for early access, but even after spending quite a lot of time trying to figure out how to counter it, I didn't find a way. Most of my planets went into Rebellion over it, at which point I had enough Dust to try and fix things but for some reason I couldn't use Dust to purchase anything even though I unlocked the research (game kept telling me I already purchased X/Y).
At the moment, I wouldn't recommend buying the game. I'm sure the developers will put more work into it, just have to wait and see though.

Note: This is an early access review, therefore I am reviewing the game - as it stands - in early access.  The game as it stands in a year, or 10 years, does not apply to this review.
I have returned again to this game after a couple of patches, something I always do with Early Access titles every now and then.  My initial impressions were extremely negative, however, in the following patches many of the problems I had with the game were improved: such as the balance of the races, the technology UI, and complete lack of combat interaction (there is now a very small interaction with card choice, soldier composition, etc).
That said, I still recommend people who are considering purchasing ES 2 to hold off.  What I said previously about many people overgushing in the first few hours of play still holds true.  This game has problems many seem to be ignoring.
Memory leaks are probably the most egregious.  After a few hours of gameplay, the entire game will begin slowing to a crawl.  Even auto-calc battles will cause a lag in the game and there are random lag spikes every few seconds.  Crashes are also a thing, though far less common than most early access titles.
Probably the biggest mark against picking up the title is that many features are still missing (several races, the ability to create a huge galaxy, the ability to make a custom race, and a lack of mod tools amongst many other features).  The tech tree also is incomplete with many percentage symbols and placeholder text.  The game, however, is being sold at full price so it should be noted that if you purchase the game it will not be a complete experience despite the price.
Overall, however, have I enjoyed the game?  Somewhat.  I question whether this is an improvement over its predecessor or Endless Legend (both of which are still good games).  I'm not entirely certain that this game has done enough different to truly stand out on its own and justify a full price purchase.  However, if you can grab it on sale it will probably be worth it if you enjoyed either EL or ES 1.

It's Endless Space with all of the best additions from Endless Legend added in, plus a few new things of its own. The production values are through the roof and I'm excited for future development.
Amplitude's 4x games have only become better over time, and they also manage to be familiar to 4x veterans while rebelling against the mold created by other games in the genre. Everything is just slightly different from MoO or Civ in exciting ways. On a subjective note they have engrossing worlds with heaps of lore and references to their other games (For example, Endless Legend, the fantasy 4x, takes place on the planet Auriga, which is a unique planet found in Endless Space).
At the time of this review the game is in a VERY early stage, do not purchase it right now expecting a full game - you can play through to a game's conclusion but there are only 4 factions, very few galaxy options, etc.
I also purchased the first Endless Space and Endless Legend in a very Early Access stage and was impressed at how quickly they were developed - Amplitude is no amateur indie studio and they don't dilly-dally when it comes to developing their EA titles.

Written 10/7/2016:
As a massive fan of the first Endless Space, my heart skipped a beat when I saw Endless Space 2 recommended to me via Steam. I had massive expectations, and I'm happy to say they have been pretty much met.
TL;DR - Endless Space 2 in its current phase is an exciting, stunning, atmospheric and promising foundation for a potentially amazing game. Even in its current state, it blows away the competition from other 4x games that are backed by bigger budgets, bigger studios, and longer histories in the industry. With that said, this game is in VERY early access; if MANY locked features, lack of tutorials, and a lack of a diverse alien roster bother you, you might want to hold off for a bit.
(Note: Below, I personally like to read/write Cons first, as deal-breakers are kinda important in purchasing decisions. But don't worry, there are definitely Pros.)
-The Bad-
Any problems associated with Early Access: I didn't quite know where to put this point, but it's fair to emphasize it once more as they ARE charging full price for what is an incomplete game. Many features are locked, balance is still iffy, and there are only 4 major factions to play (where the first game had a whopping 12 AND a custom major faction creator). With that said, you can trust the many video game critics (both big and small), a history of healthy sales figures for previous games, and myself when we say that this studio DELIVERS with its promises. I'm genuinely excited to see where this game goes!
Lack of Tutorials/Accessibility: If you haven't played the first Endless Space, then good luck to you. As a matter of fact, "Newbie" and "Experienced" difficulty levels are locked; only "Expert" level (which explicitly states that the game assumes you've mastered the first Endless Space) is available. Do with that as you will.
UI: There is a LOT of information on screen at all times. Even as an experienced player in the first Endless Space, it took me a while to orient myself. Adding in new game features not included in the first game further complicates that. If you're okay with spending time learning how to play a game, then it's no big deal. But many of us are not. Again, you the buyer makes that decision.
-The Good-
Visuals: My god is this game gorgeous. From the ships, to the planets, to the aliens... it’s like a decaffeinated J.J. Abrams; juuuuust right. And that skybox! (spacebox?) Oh my that skybox! And that gorgeous map, that just begs to be explored. Each major faction has its own visual flair, from the cartoony to the menacing. Each alien species is bursting with character that emphasize their own personal lore (and even their gameplay!) When that diplomacy screen pops up, you'll immediately know what kind of opponent you're dealing with. That's the marking of good design.
Atmosphere: Superb. Other-worldly. From the gorgeous music, to the ambient sound, to the din of your empire grinding away. Drones being launched across the vastness of space, ships firing their pew pews, and the music worthy of a space opera. Did I mention I loved the music? The UI, despite my reservations of complication, is absolutely breath-taking and strangely immersive. As corny as it sounds, there were plenty of times when I forgot I was sitting at my desk, and imagined myself a galactic space leader looking down at my space interface to rule my space empire. Look, let me live my life alright?
Narrative & Lore: Between you and me, I'm also surprised this is even a category on a 4x space game. Each major faction has its own lore, its own unique characteristics and playstyles, and even quests. Playing a "main quest" as the Sophons (a playable race) gave my empire a surprising amount of identify; when pirates or other invaders attack my planets, I feel a genuine need to save "my people". In terms of immersiveness, I consider that an achievement.
-The So So-
Gameplay: Though I consider this the most important part of any game, I must also admit it is difficult to find a handle on a game so early in its development. Many of the same features and dilemmas you can find in other games can be found here; planet colonization, exploration, ship customization, ship combat, diplomacy, and trying to find a balance between expansion & development. The addition of politics and rewards from quests add an extra wrinkle to that, but we’ll see how much gets changed/tweaked. I look forward to more features opening up further in development to write a better thought-out section on the gameplay aspects.
- All in all… -
Endless Space 2 in its current phase is an exciting, stunning, atmospheric and promising foundation for a potentially amazing game. Even in its current state, it blows away the competition from other 4x games that are backed by bigger budgets, bigger studios, and longer histories in the industry. With that said, this game is in VERY early access; if MANY locked features, lack of tutorials, and a lack of a diverse major faction roster bother you, you might want to hold off for a bit.

Legitimately a great game, and not at all what it appears at first glance.
That's true of any good clicker, but this one in particular is a long and interesting fight through a huge collection of powerups, bonuses, and tradeoffs. It is NOT a game you play by clicking your mouse constantly (or even often), and it's also not a game you'll necessarily want to leave running in the background. This is a game you genuinely play.
A typical session consists of only a minute or two of clicking monsters, then some sorting of treasure; a few decisions about which heroes, artifacts, or demigods to level up; a handful of silly but fun distractions, and contemplation or planning for the next ascension. This last is a prestige-style restart where you cash in your earnings ("hero souls") for a considerable DPS bonus, which you can then use to get past the next hurdle (difficult bosses, expensive heroes). If you don't mind sacrificing some of the direct DPS boon, you can spend your hero souls leveling up your demigods and applying bonuses to your heroes.
None of this requires impressive math skills, but it definitely scratches an itch somewhere, and people with impressive math skills have poured their hearts out in countless guides and theorycraft articles. Most importantly, there's a gut-level fun to the whole thing once you get in a ways. I'm tempted to make a Busy Box comparison, except for the game's one real failing, which is in the sound department. Very few sound effects, and one song on repeat forever. With more bells and whistles and a few extra tunes, Clicker Heroes would be damned near perfect. For the time being, it's probably the only game I've ever made a habit of playing with the sound completely turned off. And I still love it.

L.A. Noire's absorbing investigations and intoxicating sense of style make it an unforgettable journey through the seamy side of the City of Angels. Your journey takes you from filthy flophouses and hobo camps to elegant mansions and the sleek, modern offices of a company that's shaping the development of postwar Los Angeles. The architecture, which includes cookie-cutter housing developments that are springing up in droves to capitalize on the return of soldiers from the war, as well as jazz clubs where cops and gangsters alike relax after night falls, is authentic and makes this Los Angeles an absorbing and immersive place. And it's not just these big things that the game gets right. As a detective, your work investigating crime scenes is often about the smallest details, and the richness of these details in L.A. Noire makes rummaging around grisly crime scenes and perusing the personal effects of victims a compelling process. The homes of murder victims feel lived in as a result of pictures on the walls, notes pinned on refrigerators, and clothing tossed on the floor and forgotten. Pick up an official document while rummaging through some files and you'll see that it looks genuine right down to the fine print. This attention to detail makes the often unsavory business of being a detective deeply absorbing. On top of this, the period fashions, actual automobiles, and music of the era--along with a score that evokes the style of some of the great composers of film noir--weave an intoxicating spell that's sure to stir the heart of anyone with a fondness for 1940's style.

First, the taunts. There are so many taunts and things you character can say; it never gets old. You can also just let out a good throat-rattling battlecry right before you decapitate your enemy or shoot him through the eye.

You can play as an archer, light melee character, heavy melee character, and so forth.
Weapons include swords, mauls, maces, spears, axes, bows, crossbows, daggers, fire bombs, and more.

On some maps, you can use catapults and ballistas.
There are a few familiar game types--team objective (medieval style warfare like dumping bodies in the well, slaughtering the royal family, etc.), FFA, and team deathmatch.
There is a wide array of maps, some of them player-created.
There isn't a very large player base, though, so you will have to compromise and wind up on servers with high ping, which is bad for archery.
The player base is a mixed bag, but generally 90% of the time it is easy to votekick trolls, cheaters, racist people, etc. Sometimes votekick can be abused by trolls, and with the low number of servers to choose from, this can be annoying.

WARNING: Possible spoilers ahead, read at your own risk.
Pros:
A very well put together narrative, which catalogues the rise and fall of it's characters, in typical Film-noir fashion.
Strong, believable characters with excellent delivery both from their respective actors and the awe-inspiring motion-capture technology utilized.
Your partners. Their random banter and distinguished personalities are a joy to behold, they act both as the lancer and the foil to Cole's personality, and do an excellent job of playing off of Cole's own musings.
Meh's:
Lack of penalty for not upholding laws (especially when dealing with traffic), Cole can drive as recklessly as he wants, even right next to other cops without them giving a damn.
The structure of the cases, especially between Homicide and Vice. In Homicide, you just finished solving a case that had made a mockery of the LAPD, and in turn, acted as a very rewarding end to that desk. BD would have served as a greater case to end the game with, although given the circumstances, I'm inclined to believe that the narrative was constructed before the individual cases, and that the cases merely served to facilitate Cole's fall from grace.
Cons:
The save system is check-point based, which is fine, until you realize you have to restart a case and lose an hour's worth of gameplay because the game decides to auto-save after a failed interrogation.
Combat, atleast on the PC version, is rather finnicky and temperamental. The gunplay itself works, but the cover system is unresponsive and has baffling key-binds.
All in all:
If you're willing to deal with slow gameplay coupled with investigatory work and puzzle-solving, this game is right up your alley. It's not a masterpiece, but it will serve as the industry-wide standard for detective games in the future.

L.A. Confidential and Chinatown are two of the greatest neo-noir films of all time. Set in Los Angeles in the late 40’s and early 50’s, the films are a microcosm for America in the post-war era. No game has really explored this period until now.
L.A. Noire was developed by Team Bondi and directed by The Getaway’s Brendan McNamara. The game is an open-world, investigative adventure game with driving and third-person shooting. During the long development time, a trailer was released back in 2005, the game garnered controversy regarding the work ethics stressed on the team. Hopefully it was worth it.
Story
L.A. Noire is a detective story set in 1947 that creates a stunning recreation of Los Angeles after the Second World War. Cole Phelps is a purple hearted veteran who returns home to work the streets of downtown L.A. as a beat cop. After some cunning detective work on a case no one was working, Cole finds himself promoted to detective in the traffic department, investigating vehicle related crime scenes. Through promotions and demotions in the police ranks, Cole gains notoriety not only with the mobs of L.A. but also the corrupt cops he calls partners.
The story is linear with occasional flashbacks to Cole’s time in the Pacific war, which provides an interesting back story that helps understand his motivations. The game also switches perspectives to give an all-round view of the story. The homicide department supplies the game’s strongest narrative arc that culminates in a very shocking twist. However, the game’s story dips in quality somewhere around the vice department when the motives and actions of characters get muddled, which concludes in a rather disappointing ending. Many of the themes reflect the social instabilities of the time with racial segregation, sexism, corruption and capital punishment being at the forefront.
Gameplay
This might have driving and third-person shooting in an open world but this game differs from Grand Theft Auto and has a much slower pace. L.A. Noire can be likened to a modern interpretation of an adventure game. Most cases begin with a briefing at the station before driving to the crime scene. Cole can then speak to a patrol officer guarding the scene for any information on suspicious activity or the coroner to diagnose the cause of death. Cole will then inspect the body for injuries and search the area for personal affects and clues to determine the next cause of action. Often the clues can lead to the last known whereabouts of the victim and potential suspects that were in contact with the victim around the time.
Brooding music is played during the crime scene investigations, which builds tension without pushing the player to move on to the next section. The music is sublime throughout with period jazz, big band and torched song immersing the player into the era. When the player is satisfied with the clues, it’s time to move on to the interrogations. Cole will talk to the citizens who were first at the scene and reported to the police and this is where L.A. Noire’s realistic facial capture animations come into play. Based on evidence gained from surveying the scene and the facial expressions the characters convey when answering questions, Cole can either press them for more information or accuse them of lying. Correctly guessing each of the responses as truth, lie or doubt will present further leads to follow-up the investigation. This is very innovative but sometimes the facial expressions can be a bit too exaggerated making it far too obvious at the beginning but the suspects become more subtle later on requiring constant referral to Cole’s notebook to study the evidence and alibis.
Further into the investigation, Cole will find suspects that will try to evade capture. This is when the action set pieces kick in with foot chases across rooftops and streets, car chases and eventual brawls and shootouts. Foot chases are very enjoyable with Cole interacting with each obstacle automatically; something that has now been implemented in Grand Theft Auto V. Although, the option to fire a warning shot it the air is only occasionally given to the player. Even if the option was given but it didn’t work would’ve given more nuance to the chase scenes and made them feel less scripted. The hand to hand combat has also inspired the recent Grand Theft Auto V with a good block and counter mechanic. As with Rockstar tradition, L.A. Noire features a cover mechanic with third-person shooting that feels adequate but can only be used in limited scenarios. The driving is also adequate but doesn’t feel as responsive as Grand Theft Auto IV although it includes classic real world cars with a lot of attention to detail and beauty.
When the prime suspects are detained in the police station it’s time for the final interrogation that can determine who will be tried in court and sentenced to prison or death. The player is scored at the end of each case depending on how many clues were found or if the right person was locked away and the captain will either praise or criticise Cole’s performance. However, no matter the outcome of the previous case the next case will start without the repercussions carrying through. It would’ve benefited to have consequences that affect the game in order for the player to take the time and care during investigating.
Technical
Los Angeles is authentically recreated to its former glory without the highway system of today. The map is large, famous landmarks are beautifully restored and many buildings include stunning, detailed interiors. Every single aspect has been handled with care from the tram system to the fashion of the times. When investigating, objects are brought in closer to Cole’s eyes for inspection and feature extremely detailed textures that are almost photorealistic. Occasional graphical glitches occur such as characters not in the right place; cars sink into the road and sometimes the framerate drops but the game is still attractive. The facial capture is very impressive but the characters look as if they have stiff necks a lot of the time. Maybe Team Bondi’s next game, The ♥♥♥♥♥ of the Orient, will feature full body performance capture. The sound is great, especially when Cole’s spats echo on marble floors in large halls. The soundtrack is beautifully nostalgic with the in game radio seamlessly blending into the world.
Verdict
L.A. Noire achieves its goal of recreating Los Angeles and making an intense detective drama. The voice acting and facial capture are marvellous, although the gameplay could’ve benefited with more variety and less scripted events.

Path 0.1.19 (Update 1) Edit: My opinion of this game has not changed. There have been numerous improvements since the initial earlly access release although I probably will not thouroughly update this review until near or after final release. If my opinion changes, I will update this post with the reasons why, though I do not expect I will have to do so. Bear in mind some of the issues mentioned below may have been fixed in Update One or in future updates.
Update 1 Edit 2: There are currently a few game breaking bugs that appear mid-late game for many players. So I would hold off until they are fixed. I will remove this when it is fixed.
TL:DR -> If you don't want an unfinished game, don't buy it until closer to or after release. Otherwise, I recommend it and from Amplitude's record I think they can deliver on anything that is unfinished or needs tweaking.
After playing almost two matches, here is my review of an extremely promising yet still unfinished game. This title is in Early Access, which means that it won't be done until Amplitude say it is done. Promising a full release in approximately six months from now, they have big shoes to fill, but ultimately I believe they can deliver.
Pros:
+ Beautiful UI and Graphics for a 4X game.
+ Each of the four current factions are varied and interesting. (There will be 8 on release)
+ You really get a feel of managing an empire, especially with the political parties.
+ Combat is very fun assuming you accept it for what it is.
+ Added really fun exploration mechanics with probes and constellations as well as random rogue systems.
+ Kept the interesting tech tree style from Endless Legend, which really emphasizes choice if you want to keep up in technology.
+ Feels like a living galaxy with minor factions and all the events and quests.
+ Managing your political parties is fun and interesting, especially when outside events make it difficult for your favored party to stay dominant (I'm looking at you militarist party, stop dominating my senate when people declare war on me).
+ Outpost system feels realistic and contesting systems can be fun.
Fixes needed
- Camera in space battles is janky and often doesn't show interesting angles.
- Score Victory is sort of arbitrary and leads to short games.
- Incomplete Tech Tree. Only goes up to Era 3.
- So many different technologies to research in order to colonize different kinds of planets.
- Lack of luxury resources meaning advancing system levels are difficult in some games.
- Forced truces in a war can feel very unsatisfying in some situations. It's hard to keep up a war in this game, but when you can, it feels like forced truces really hinder the experience.
- Happiness system feels incomplete, would like some way to influence it like the tax system from Endless Space 1 or some other interactive system.
- Repairing ships is too expensive (this will be fixed).
- Other unfinished features.
Feature I'm missing the most since they're still working on it: Automation on star systems. I don't use it all the time, but come mid/late game sometimes I'd rather manage all the larger things than simply scrolling through every system. isn't a big deal in the current build, but I can't wait until they put that feature from ES1 and EL back in.
Overall: I recommend this game completely. Knowing Amplitude Studio's track record, I believe that once they get into gear, all of these problems will be addressed in some form. If you're looking for a complete game however, I would hold off for a few months or wait until the full release. While it is more interesting to play than ES and EL, it does currently lack features or contain unfinished features. I don't have a real con list until more things are added to the game. There are some downsides, but I don't feel like they're worth going that indepth about until closer to release, I do mention a few down below with some more indepth thoughts.
Exploration: I love the probes and constellations as well as random star systems sitting in the middle of no where with no space lanes connected to them. While it might be annoying to build scouts and stuff, I feel like this adds a really good feel towards a galaxy that is worth exploring. Probes able to explore planets for anamolies and resources is a nice touch too.
Expansion: Outposts feel a combination of really good and boring. I love the idea behind it, though waiting a bunch of turns is annoying. Outside of the waiting period, contesting a system by trying to finish your outpost before the enemy completes their's was interesting, though I have only experienced it once. I can imagine it being annoying for some people though. Colonizing planets can be annoying because you need to research tech for almost each planet type, though they make it a bit more satisfying by tying other bonuses to researching the planet tech. Sometimes being able to colonize a type of planet isn't the main reason you research that technology. I also don't think it's intended that you colonize every star system on the map, not until late game at least as it can get very difficult to manage everything.
Exploitation: There are a myriad of technologies to research in order to develop your star systems and your populations feel very dynamic for the most part. Political parties can rise and fall in an instant and influence a lot of things about your empire. Your ability to manage your population is huge in this game. Keeping your scientists in power is hard when trying to ally with a minor faction brings your pacifists into dominance, and tempering your population's militarist uprising is difficult when an enemy declares war on you. Keeping your favorite party in power to keep some needed laws is challenging and fun. Technologies to develop your star systems feel good for the most part and even researching the right technologies is difficult and rewarding. A lot about this game is managing short term vs long term and I feel like all these systems in concert bring an excellent feel to a game that few are able to implement well. I suspect with more polishing, this will get even more satisfying. Some people might not like the research system though, as you most likely won't unlock every technology in every era.
Extermination: Combat is overall very satisfying. I feel some work on ground battles is needed to make them feel a little better, but they feel pretty good, better than ES1 atleast. I really wonder how the reinforcement fleets will work out. One of ES1's biggest downfalls in combat was amassing large numbers of fleets felt really stale when you'd have 10 fleets all fighting. At that point it just turned into auto resolving everything and it seems like they might have something to address it coming in the future. Strategy helps a lot in this iteration and I feel the customization of ships is vastly better than ES1. I do wish there was more than three ways to move your fleet formations in though and maybe they'll address that in the future. Some people won't like the more hands off approach, but these aren't for a tactical master, these battles are for the strategist, who will meticulously plan out their victory from 10 turns earlier, who studied enemy ship designs in previous battles and who will choose the battle formations that fit their ship compositions and then watch the fruits of their labor engage in battle.
Keep in mind these are only my thoughts, some of what I consider great things, you might not. Thank you for reading.
Edit1: Changed the pros (-) to (+). Clarified a few more things in indepth stuff and fixed some spelling.

The mid-20th century is often portrayed as wholesome, happy and and full of possibilities -- a better time for America and Americans. But Rockstar and developer Team Bondi's L.A. Noire shows another side; a time when racism was rampant, drug abuse was growing, and violence was all too common. You play as Detective Cole Phelps, a good hearted cop whose time spent fighting in the Pacific during World War 2 has left him with a whole slew of baggage. PC players can finally bring the heavy hand of justice to the sinners of Los Angeles in the great PC port. I don't want to ruin the plot (since that makes up the bulk of the reason to play L.A. Noire), but the story entertains from start to finish. Sure, it isn't entirely original with its narrative and plot devices, but the themes in the story hit the right notes for what the game's trying to do. The title says it all, and Team Bondi has nailed the "noir" feeling of the world with its camera work, music and settings. Noticeably repetitive gameplay moments aside, L.A. Noire offers a different and delightful take on the open-world formula that Rockstar’s refined over the years. You can explore the world if you want, but I love how focused the story is, that you can simply go from point to point and rocket your way through the cases. The awesome performances and great facial capture make every interrogation and investigation a riveting affair. 10/10

This is one of the best F2P games you will find out there, being almost completely free and giving unique gameplay.
I'm going to start why this game is "almost completely free". Unlocking new slots for weapons and warframes requires Platinum, but Platinum can be aquired by trading and there's always someone wanting to buy something, so it's not a big deal, really. You also start with few slots to have some variety.
What exactly is this game?:
It's a Third Person CO-OP RPG Shooter focused in PvE. You play in third person, level up your character and gear, look for new loot to make your stuff better (Upgrade cards also know as "Mods" in-game that you fit in your gear and Warframe), you're also equipped with weaponry and capable of parkour. Playing with other people is optional.
Story and Progression:
I'm not really sure about other people, but the story really attracted me to the game, most planets also having their own unique enviroment is a really nice touch. I was always wondering "What will happen next?" or "What i'm going to see next?" or "Can't wait to try this weapon!". But after finishing your Star Chart, all the missions and killing all the bosses, it can get boring and repetitive very quickly, but it's good to remind you it may take a while to finish this game.
Gameplay:
The gameplay is extremely unique. Play as a Warframe capable of stomping so hard it stops enemies in time, or another one that's literally Dio (Limbo) capable of freezing everything in time just like Dio (
This video shows a accurate example) and many others, however we can't forget the guns.
This game has 3 categorys of weapons: Melee, Secondary and Primary. Your primary weapons are Assault Rifles, SMG's, Grenade Launchers, Charge Weapons, Laser Weapons, Tesla Guns and many others. Secondarys have your standard revolvers and pistols, while also having traps, SMGs, machine pistols, kunais and uuh... stuff that i can't remember. Melees also have a huge amount of variety, but they also have stances that unlock diferrent kinds of "Fighting styles" with that melee weapon.
The Grind:
Alright, let's talk about the elephant in the room. Honestly, i never felt this game was grindy. I've completed this game (Full star chart + All bosses killed + All missions done + 2 Prime Warframes (Nekros and Vauban)) in 2 weeks. Yes, 2 weeks. It's true that most prime content is hard to acquire, but you don't really need it. You can acquire the non-prime version of most stuff and do just as good. Unless you're playing like in the hardest survival mission possible for over one hour or something and every stat point matters.
Performance:
This must be the most optimized game i've ever played in my entire life. When i saw gameplay videos or screenshots i always thought "it's never going to run in my computer, look at these graphics... but it's F2P, so i should give it a try i guess." but it runs amazingly smoothly.
Conclusion:
Warframe is a fantastic game, giving unique gameplay, allowing you to play as Space Ninjas with anime characters superpowers, capable of working even on a potato, a great story and a surprisingly amount of content for a F2P game the bad side is that once you get everything done, it can get repetitive, but that's the only downside i could find.
If you haven't played Warframe you should give a try, it's an amazing and unique game you shouldn't miss this opportunity it's Free after all! Remember that you can also bring friends to play with you!

Utterly gorgeous, even in alpha. The core systems from ES 1 are here, but with the addition of so much more. Before I start, a quick warning - the game only goes as far as turn 126, and the only victory conditions are conquest and score. There's still plenty of extra to add into the game, and I can understand the focus on getting the early game-mechanics sorted, but it's a little annoying to get into a game to realise it's almost finished.
On with the review:
Combat  - The first thing that hit me was that it's been completely revamped - there's no more 3-phase, pick a card combat. It's still very hands-off - you pick your attack range, and hope for the best. It looks like there is more to it later game - it seems like the star system might be able to provide bonuses to combat, etc. Ground invasions are also now a key part of the game, with what looks like a Rock-Paper-Scissors approach to troops. Overall, a lot simpler combat, but still looks pretty.
Politics - very similar to the edicts system in EL, except you use the influence to pass laws which in turn give bonuses to a particular playstyle. However, to pass these laws, your particular party has to have enough political clout to get them through - elections every ~20 turns can shift the balance of power away from your party. This in turn unlocks new laws, but disables ones that need a huge majority to pass. You can try to focus exclusively on your party, or become more populist, depending on your playstyle.
Exploration - there's a lot more emphasis on free movement from the start. Wormholes aren't around until late game (well, late for the alpha), so you're reliant on drifiting between constellations. Luckily, probes have also been introduced - just fire a probe off in a likely direction, and hope it comes across a new star. The worlds look much more impressive, and the way it gives an overview of a new system shows off any likely candidates for colonisation really well.
Races - A few familiar faces are back in the game (Sophons and Cravers) with a huge improvement in their looks and character, while some (like the Hissho) are in as minor factions. At the moment, you can only spend influence with them and occupy them as an ally, or just conquer them outright - though there could be room later for quests to convert them to your empire much like in EL. In the current alpha, there's also two new races - the Vodyani, nomadic technologists who go from star to star in massive Ark ships, and the Lumeris, who are very much the traders of the galaxy. As your empire expands, other races populations start to join your worlds, bringing unique traits and bonuses to their chosen planet type.
Research - No more tech web, it follows the Age system in EL where you need to research X techs in one age to unlock the next, but *what* you research is down to you.  Again, due to the alpha it's limited to Age 3, but even with the Sophons, you won't get past it before the turn limit.
Presentation - Simply impressive. The menus flow really well, and look a lot more exciting than in ES1. Information is presented well, but it can be a challenge finding what you're looking for at first glance. The addition of the "scan mode" also gives you a way to see things like diplomatic connections, the ouptut of your worlds, all from the galaxy map. While unfinished, it also has the potential to be very useful.
Summary - Again, it is an Early Access title - by it's nature, it's unfinished and the developers have made no concessions. However, for what it is, it's incredibly well designed, looks amazing, and honestly has me wanting more. The community also has a very active role in development - having seen the input from fans in ES1 and EL, you can guarantee that the devs will be listening here too. If you want to try it now, go for it. If you'd rather wait, that's fair enough, but definitely add this one to your follow list.

L.A. Noire is an open world neo-noire police / detective game made by Team Bondi and published by Rockstar Games. It features crime scene investigation, interrogations, arrests, and possibly, for the first time in the Rockstar games portfolio, police chases where the player is the police.
If you like movies such as L.A. Confidential (specially this one), Chinatown and The Untouchables, you'll definitely might want to give this game a try.
+ Facial Animation: -The selling point of L.A. Noire is possibly the facial motion capture technology that was employed. It is this technique that makes the game's interrogations as close to realism as possible for the 'truth / doubt / lie' mechanic to work.
+ Atmosphere: -The devs have done remarkable work recreating the wonderful city of 1947 Los Angeles. Although it may not be exactly how it was back then, it's still a large and magnificent city to explore. From the cars, the clothing, the buildings and the radio, Team Bondi certainly nailed the 1947 atmosphere.
+ Investigation: -From examining clues to following leads, LA Noire delivers a great police / detective mechanic that provides fun and exciting experience.
+ Sound: -Great voice acting, great selection of 1940s classic hits, a bit of radio news from that time, good sound effects and some very classical OST vibe. The voice acting makes for some very memorable characters with unique personalities.
+ Playtime: -The game is extensive and will require some time to finish. From the main story, DLC cases, Street Crimes and Collectibles, there are a lot of things to do which is more than enough to make you feel that your money was well spent.
- 30 FPS: -According to the devs, the reason for this was that the motion-capture technology would not function properly if it was not locked at 30 FPS. Be that as it may, most PC gamers would still expect certain games to run at 60fps minimum.
- Awkward Body Movements: -I kinda feel they focused a bit too much on the facial animation and severely under developed the body animation. Most character movements are awkward and the bodies seem to move like they were made from cardboard or cement.
-  No reward for Non-Lethal Arrest: -The game has optional 'Street Crimes' which can be solved by lethal or non-lethal methods (depending on the Crime). Unfortunately, there is no reward in trying to chase down a fleeing suspect and it would be much easier just to shoot them in the back. This disappointed me a lot.
GOOD GAME for a GOOD PRICE. L.A. Noire captures the classical 1940-70 police / detective movies that once graced the silver screens but with a bit of modern sprinkles to it.
Sale or full price, this game is worth every penny.
I suggest that potential buyers of this game purchase the 'Complete' Edition which includes the DLCs because they extend the gameplay by providing additional 'Cases' for each of the game's chapters.

Written 10/7/2016:
As a massive fan of the first Endless Space, my heart skipped a beat when I saw Endless Space 2 recommended to me via Steam. I had massive expectations, and I'm happy to say they have been pretty much met.
TL;DR - Endless Space 2 in its current phase is an exciting, stunning, atmospheric and promising foundation for a potentially amazing game. Even in its current state, it blows away the competition from other 4x games that are backed by bigger budgets, bigger studios, and longer histories in the industry. With that said, this game is in VERY early access; if MANY locked features, lack of tutorials, and a lack of a diverse alien roster bother you, you might want to hold off for a bit.
(Note: Below, I personally like to read/write Cons first, as deal-breakers are kinda important in purchasing decisions. But don't worry, there are definitely Pros.)
-The Bad-
Any problems associated with Early Access: I didn't quite know where to put this point, but it's fair to emphasize it once more as they ARE charging full price for what is an incomplete game. Many features are locked, balance is still iffy, and there are only 4 major factions to play (where the first game had a whopping 12 AND a custom major faction creator). With that said, you can trust the many video game critics (both big and small), a history of healthy sales figures for previous games, and myself when we say that this studio DELIVERS with its promises. I'm genuinely excited to see where this game goes!
Lack of Tutorials/Accessibility: If you haven't played the first Endless Space, then good luck to you. As a matter of fact, "Newbie" and "Experienced" difficulty levels are locked; only "Expert" level (which explicitly states that the game assumes you've mastered the first Endless Space) is available. Do with that as you will.
UI: There is a LOT of information on screen at all times. Even as an experienced player in the first Endless Space, it took me a while to orient myself. Adding in new game features not included in the first game further complicates that. If you're okay with spending time learning how to play a game, then it's no big deal. But many of us are not. Again, you the buyer makes that decision.
-The Good-
Visuals: My god is this game gorgeous. From the ships, to the planets, to the aliens... it’s like a decaffeinated J.J. Abrams; juuuuust right. And that skybox! (spacebox?) Oh my that skybox! And that gorgeous map, that just begs to be explored. Each major faction has its own visual flair, from the cartoony to the menacing. Each alien species is bursting with character that emphasize their own personal lore (and even their gameplay!) When that diplomacy screen pops up, you'll immediately know what kind of opponent you're dealing with. That's the marking of good design.
Atmosphere: Superb. Other-worldly. From the gorgeous music, to the ambient sound, to the din of your empire grinding away. Drones being launched across the vastness of space, ships firing their pew pews, and the music worthy of a space opera. Did I mention I loved the music? The UI, despite my reservations of complication, is absolutely breath-taking and strangely immersive. As corny as it sounds, there were plenty of times when I forgot I was sitting at my desk, and imagined myself a galactic space leader looking down at my space interface to rule my space empire. Look, let me live my life alright?
Narrative & Lore: Between you and me, I'm also surprised this is even a category on a 4x space game. Each major faction has its own lore, its own unique characteristics and playstyles, and even quests. Playing a "main quest" as the Sophons (a playable race) gave my empire a surprising amount of identify; when pirates or other invaders attack my planets, I feel a genuine need to save "my people". In terms of immersiveness, I consider that an achievement.
-The So So-
Gameplay: Though I consider this the most important part of any game, I must also admit it is difficult to find a handle on a game so early in its development. Many of the same features and dilemmas you can find in other games can be found here; planet colonization, exploration, ship customization, ship combat, diplomacy, and trying to find a balance between expansion & development. The addition of politics and rewards from quests add an extra wrinkle to that, but we’ll see how much gets changed/tweaked. I look forward to more features opening up further in development to write a better thought-out section on the gameplay aspects.
- All in all… -
Endless Space 2 in its current phase is an exciting, stunning, atmospheric and promising foundation for a potentially amazing game. Even in its current state, it blows away the competition from other 4x games that are backed by bigger budgets, bigger studios, and longer histories in the industry. With that said, this game is in VERY early access; if MANY locked features, lack of tutorials, and a lack of a diverse major faction roster bother you, you might want to hold off for a bit.

L.A. Noire is an open world neo-noire police / detective game made by Team Bondi and published by Rockstar Games. It features crime scene investigation, interrogations, arrests, and possibly, for the first time in the Rockstar games portfolio, police chases where the player is the police.
If you like movies such as L.A. Confidential (specially this one), Chinatown and The Untouchables, you'll definitely might want to give this game a try.
+ Facial Animation: -The selling point of L.A. Noire is possibly the facial motion capture technology that was employed. It is this technique that makes the game's interrogations as close to realism as possible for the 'truth / doubt / lie' mechanic to work.
+ Atmosphere: -The devs have done remarkable work recreating the wonderful city of 1947 Los Angeles. Although it may not be exactly how it was back then, it's still a large and magnificent city to explore. From the cars, the clothing, the buildings and the radio, Team Bondi certainly nailed the 1947 atmosphere.
+ Investigation: -From examining clues to following leads, LA Noire delivers a great police / detective mechanic that provides fun and exciting experience.
+ Sound: -Great voice acting, great selection of 1940s classic hits, a bit of radio news from that time, good sound effects and some very classical OST vibe. The voice acting makes for some very memorable characters with unique personalities.
+ Playtime: -The game is extensive and will require some time to finish. From the main story, DLC cases, Street Crimes and Collectibles, there are a lot of things to do which is more than enough to make you feel that your money was well spent.
- 30 FPS: -According to the devs, the reason for this was that the motion-capture technology would not function properly if it was not locked at 30 FPS. Be that as it may, most PC gamers would still expect certain games to run at 60fps minimum.
- Awkward Body Movements: -I kinda feel they focused a bit too much on the facial animation and severely under developed the body animation. Most character movements are awkward and the bodies seem to move like they were made from cardboard or cement.
-  No reward for Non-Lethal Arrest: -The game has optional 'Street Crimes' which can be solved by lethal or non-lethal methods (depending on the Crime). Unfortunately, there is no reward in trying to chase down a fleeing suspect and it would be much easier just to shoot them in the back. This disappointed me a lot.
GOOD GAME for a GOOD PRICE. L.A. Noire captures the classical 1940-70 police / detective movies that once graced the silver screens but with a bit of modern sprinkles to it.
Sale or full price, this game is worth every penny.
I suggest that potential buyers of this game purchase the 'Complete' Edition which includes the DLCs because they extend the gameplay by providing additional 'Cases' for each of the game's chapters.

Well if you are familiar with another turn-based 4x titles, you will not find any difficulties in playing this game, although i must say, the length of the game itself is pretty short in comparison to other 4x titles.
The idea of having different political parties in your own faction really stirs up the game, giving you a new challenge in the game.
Each political parties in your faction could give you different bonuses to your faction which edicts you could active with influence points. Some of the edicts is really OP, I hope this could be fixed in the future
The Game also feature an Election system, which depends on your Empire state, which means, buildings and units have a direct influence of Faction Popularity and the votes that the Faction will receive, so if you are a Militaristic Empire, make sure you have ample amount of Military buildings or don't blame me if your empire suddenly turn into a Pacifist Empire.
This directly affect edicts that you could enact altogehter
(This is also stated in the Interview from Angry Joe with the developer, the developer state that if you want to wage war againts other empire, you need to influence your citizens/population)
The game also gives you a tons of quest, starting from exploration, research and etc., to keep you immersed in the game and make sure that you are not bored with just the plain 4x strategy gameplay.
Another thing that’s great from the Endless Series is the customisation. You can customise your ship and heroes’ ship with different weapons but it’s quite limited to the weapons and modules, not only that, some of the modules must be earned through quest which is great, that means that the game itself encourage you to follow the story.
The only problem about the gameplay that it’s too short, research tree is really lacking, The AI is not really good.
I finished my 1st play through in only 2 hours, which is really short (well, I do start with default setting, since I want to try and learn the game) and 1 hour into the game as the Sophons , I already finished half of the tech tree.
Research screen is also quite confusing at times, since it’s divided into 4 big category like Endless Legend, but in Endless Space 2, it gives you a big screen with all 4 Research category content splatted in your face,
Another thing is that, since I played as the Sophons, the Cravers is ranked the 1st at the overall screen, but after a few turn, their empire suddenly destroyed, which is considered impossible, since Cravers is a militaristic empire and their military strength is at the top of the list, this could be possible only if the other 2 empire Lumeris and Vodyani are allied, but, after the Cravers is destroyed, Soon the Lumeris Empire fell too only after a good 10 turns, which left me and The Vodyani on the board, I don’t know if this is a bug or it’s just the game, but this really makes me wonder of what’s happening on the other side since there is FOW in the game.
~8/10
If you are familiar with the Endless series, you should know that the soundtrack and music of the game is superb, Endless Legend 2 also has a great futuristic theme music that not only soothing, but also it actually gives you the commanding atmosphere, the sound of the guns is also great, especially when you watch the Battle, although sound of the gun impact is a bit lacking IMO
Endless Space 2 has been a really promising title in the future, though some improvements is needed in order to bring this game for example, more research, better pacing and so on

If you like 4x Tactical Turn-Based Strategy game, then I really recommend this game for you, but if you are a newcomer, it’s better to watch tutorials on the site like Y*utube since the developer is still building a beginner tutorial, though, Endless Space 2 is a really great addition to your library and definitely a proud one to have

I do not expect far too much from it, as the content is limited (as of right now, anyway). As the game is right now, it is very barebones, as expected from a game that is in Alpha, in terms of the gameplay itself. There isn't much news about them adding too much of the incomplete content soon (or maybe as soon as I'd want it). Don't expect a full experience if you buy this, at this stage, theyre just wanting feedback on their balancing, UI, visuals, and mechanics.
Pros:
-Aesthetically pleasing to the eye
-The OST is one for the books (I do miss the old music, though.)
-UI is sleek, responsive, streamlined
-The entertainment value just for the lore itself is superb, faction intros will pull you in instantly
-Dev team is taking any and all feedback on the game VERY seriously
-None to Minimal performance issues/drops
Cons
-As someone who's played ES 1, I don't think I can compare the two at the moment
-UI is kind of large; text covers up large portions of the screen
-Replayability is limited at its current state
-Not too much mechanics/tecnologies/content, as it is in Alpha
Overall, right now, it's a must buy if you want it for the discount and wait, or you can play test it and give feedback as you discover what could be improved. Just don't recommend going into this expecting a full experience, as the game even tells you and give you an "Agree/Disagree" screen, so they don't have to explain to players twice about the game's current state. These Devs are the most caring company ive support, ever, and I have a feeling they'll take this game to a new height that you don't often see in 4x Strategy.

This game ♥♥♥♥♥ all over any other competitive FPS title, Dynamic battle's that change as objective are completed or failed. As one army you may find yourself pillaging a whole village, laying siege on a castle and finally killing an enemy king. And in a totally different map you could be pushing a siege weapon through town with checkpoint objectives as the cart traverses the enemy city, all so you can lay waste to the knowledge that your enemy keeps locked away in their castles library. It's great every map has different objectives.
There are 4 Main gametypes: Team Objective, Team Deathmatch, Deathmatch, and Duel's. And also a few great modded gametypes: Horde (Waves of NPC orc's, skellingtons, ghosts...), BlackKnight mode (Think Monty Python limbs flying everywhere). Giant Killer's (the more you kill the bigger you become).
The combat is brilliant provided you play server's locally as bad ping will get you rekt everytime, if your ping is above 80 - 90 on any given server you will likely not get many kills.
