L.A. Noire is reminiscent of a lot of us. We’re decent people sure, but we’ve become bloated with wasted potential. Maybe I should go ahead and compare Noire to a high-end escort. Sure, her parents are disappointed but she’s certainly bringing something different and enjoyable to your evening. You should definitely play L.A. Noire but like me you may walk away feeling that it could have been much more. There are also a slew of problems both technical and performance but the experience is fresh, invigorating, and will keep you playing through the night.
L.A. Noire is heavily influenced by film noire. If you despise that genre maybe this game isn’t for you. The story is smothered in a thick layer of atmosphere with character personalities practically picked from the classics. Sure, some of the characters are definitely cliché but this plays to the games benefit. It’s supposed to be reminiscent of film noire and it does a damn good job at it. I won’t go too much into the characters or story because that’s something players should experience firsthand for themselves. It’s good and you should play it.
The story can be described as paced and methodical. Unlike other Rockstar titles you won’t be blowing through waves of armed baddies every moment of the day. You’ll play as Cole Phelps, a veteran of World War II turned by-the-book detective in late 1940s Los Angeles. Because you’re a detective you’ll spend less time in shootouts and more time investigating crimes, interviewing suspects, and driving around in style.
The investigations continue to introduce diversity in their story and characters but the central process generally stays the same. You’ll interrogate witnesses, chase down suspects, and sort through crime scenes for clues. The most prominent game mechanic is of course the interrogation mechanic in whom you judge whether your witness/suspect you believe the person you are interrogating is telling the truth, you doubt them, or they are lying. This is where MotionScan shines the brightest. The depth of the character’s expressing is fantastic and you’ll have to use those expressions to figure out whether they are telling the truth or not. At times dissecting the truth from the lies is rather difficult but most of the time it wasn’t too hard. A lot of the character’s tells are regurgitated over and over and the facial expressions are generally overdramatized. Regardless it is a ton of fun to interrogate someone to get one step closer to solving the case. Be careful though, there are consequences to doing a bad job.
Outside of the main storyline there is little to take part in. There are side missions called “street crimes.” Unlike the campaign they are more or less regurgitated and not at all worthwhile in my opinion. You can also drive around and find all of the landmarks or try to find hidden cars. For such a large world there really isn’t a whole lot to do with it. You're free to explore the world but there is simply not a whole lot to see or do. It's like a fantastic themepark tucked away in some beautiful place but with only one ride.
I first played L.A. Noire all the way back in 2011 on the Xbox 360. I fancied another play and decided to snag a copy for the PC. The unfortunate reality is that the PC version doesn’t offer much more than the Xbox 360. The game is locked to 30fps and suffers from some of the performance issues that the Xbox 360 suffered. I feel as if the game must have been rushed for its PC release. I suffered the occasional stuttering and even tearing despite have vsync engaged and more than enough hardware to handle the stress. The draw distances appear to be as short as they were on the consoles. I feel as if the game could have been made to better utilize the PCs superior power. Unfortunately it appears that this wasn’t the case. While the game is certainly playable these performance issues can be distracting and I feel as if they shouldn’t have ever been there in the first place. The most glaring annoyance is the FPS limit which may be more than a mild annoyance to PC gamers. Now, I have heard that the FPS limit was for the benefit of the facial animations. Apparently there is a FPS unlocker created by someone but I have yet to see how the facial animations work at higher frame rates.
I decided to play the entirety of the campaign using my gamepad. Like Grand Theft Auto the game, in my opinion, is much better enjoyed with it. The driving was on-par or slightly above that of GTA IV. The combat mechanics feel unrefined and clunky, a problem that was equally persistent in bothering me on the 360. Fortunately combat is not the focus of L.A. Noire. I would consider the controls functional but not superb.
The audio including the voice acting and background audio are no less than top notch. While you’re driving you are treated to period music and commercials. The voice acting and music score are engaging and enjoyable. Everything works seamlessly together to make you feel as if you’re really a detective in 1940s L.A.
The recreation late 1940s L.A. is impressive. It is evident that a staggering amount of attention to detail was applied in its accurate depiction of the time. This applies to everything from the clothes, cars, hairstyles, architecture, and interiors. The game used a technology called MotionScan to record and transplants real actor’s facial expressions into the game. Overall this brings a truly unique cinematic experience and supports the games interrogation mechanic. It is a thrill to see so much detail in a game character and brings the world and experience alive. MotionScan could certainly use some polish and refinement but the implementation of the technology is definitely a good one.
A handful of character animations are strange wonky. I wish some more attention could have also been applied to the more action-packed cinematic cut scenes. I know the game was made all the way back in 2011 but there’s a few that look downright silly. The game does a fantastic job of getting you absorbed in the world but there’s moments when an unpolished visual moments pulls you straight out. There exists the occasional discrepancy between textures. Some texture is lovely such as those for cars and interiors. On the other hand the gun textures (and reloading animations) are poor at best.
Despite flaws L.A. Noire is an enjoyable and enthralling adventure. The game introduces new game mechanics, a story, and an environment that truly sets the game apart from the rest of the pack. It doesn’t matter that it came out three years ago, give this game a play.

After getting some free time to sit down and finally play some Endless Space 2, I believe this is a worthy successor to the original Endless Space. I appreciate Amplitude for aggressively fixing issues and releasing patches. If you can deal playing with minor bugs and issues then go ahead and get the game now. Just don't complain. Instead contribute to the solution by going to
and submitting your feedback and bug reports. This is the summer of 4X games, but there has been no runaway winner so far. I am giving ES2 a 7.5 out of 10 and hoping it will improve over the next few months.

After a long awaited year after it's announcement, Endless Space 2 is here and it is every bit as great as it's original predecessor, maybe even more after it goes through it's Early Access growing pains. Now, most people would be bothered or held back by Amplitude's recently being bought out by SEGA, but this entire game is nothing but Amplitude's hard work and dedication to it.
You wont find shoddy, unfinished code here. This game has underwent such a polishing process just for to be placed in EA, and bugs are there, but minor and non-gamebreaking.
They have taken everything that worked from the previous Endless Space 2 and added various elements from their other game, Endless Legend, and made it into something entirely new, while still feeling like Endless Space.
The music is great, created by FlyByNo, who have previously worked on all Endless Games (Space, Legends, Dungeon), and they really nailed the setting for it.
Now, for the obvious detracts.
Yes, there are only 4 available factions out of 8 (with one new one being made by the Games2Together Community), and yes there is a turn limit(they have stated the turn limit will increase as the EA goes on and they balance Mid/Late Game) and no Multiplayer yet, but the initial game already has PLENTY to go through and multiple playthroughs to do.
To close it all, Amplitude Games might be one of the very few who does Early Access right, and Endless Space 2 is already shaping up to be a great game.

L.A. Noire is built around giving players the ability to, as the name perfectly implies, unleash the Force. This is a version of the Force that really hasn't been seen anywhere before, with over-the-top uses of things like Force Push. When you go to push a stormtrooper away from you, he won't just fall over, he'll fly. You can Force Grip soldiers and toss them into oncoming TIE fighters, stab someone with a nicely tossed lightsaber that happens to be electrified for extra coolness, or use a good old bit of Force Repulse to shove a group of soldiers away from you and off the side of a suspended bridge (which will also result in the bridge buckling from the blast).
When you first take control of Vader's secret apprentice, he's already pretty powerful with Force Push and Force Grip in his repertoire. But by the time you reach the end of the game, he's incredibly powerful. Stormtroopers that previously took a few swipes of a lightsaber to down now hit the floor in one swoop, and your Force powers will recharge quickly for repeated use. Being able to Force Push one guy off a ledge, electrify the guy next to him, slice down a third trooper and then Force Repulse all of their bodies off your standing within a couple seconds is flat-out awesome.

Saul: It's almost a shame to smoke it. It's like killing a unicorn... with, like, a bomb.  "Put This in Your Pipe and Smoke It." Pineapple Express is one of my favorite stoner comedies of all-time. It "hits" all the "high" points that it needs to. It also pulled a great and soon to be classic performance out of James Franco as Saul the drug dealer/stoner. Everything he does, from his mannerisms to how he talks to what he says is a perfect parody/impersonation of a stoner. His performance doesn't reach the level of say Sean Penn in Fast Times, but it is one of the best stoner performances I have ever seen. Dale and his drug dealer, Saul, end up on the run from a corrupt cop and a major drug kingpin Ted. Their experience takes them through shootouts, fist fights, car chases, and wooded adventures. There are some classic scenes in this film. I especially love the woods scene. It's a perfect piece of pothead paranoia and is actually not far from some experiences you've had while smoking the cannabis.  The film has its share of problems. I won't deny that at all. Still this is a film that I can watch and re-watch and watch again. People who aren't laughing after the first scene where we see where the prohibition of marijuana came from should just give up on it there, because it's a sign of the humor to come. This is strictly a drug comedy. Sure there are elements of other forms of comedy, slapstick and sex comedy included; but as The 40 Year Old Virgin was to sex comedies, Pineapple Express is to drug comedies. If you're a fan of this genre, you'll absolutely love this film. If you aren't, you still might like it because it's better than 90% of drug comedies. So give it a try. You may not like it, but then again you may be like me and won't be able to stop laughing. If you want a little help with the experience, toke up beforehand. You'll be howling.

As an avid 4X fan (and having played quite a bit of Endless Space), I knew I had to get ES2.
And is it a good game? In short, yes. There are some large caveats however that I'll go over below;
The game lacks a lot of depth at the moment, especially when it comes to research and planetary development. Not much has been added since ES, and it feels very bland in its current state.
Every research gives 1-2 unlocks, usually one on an empire level, and one on a planetary level. They feel simple and the progress feels linear. There are very few decisions to make in the research tree (would love some specialization and/or more branching paths - now it's mostly just a big pile of research options thrown at you, X required from each era to unlock the next) and most don't feel very significant. (Except the research options unlocking colonization options for certain planetary types.) Personally, I would've loved more hierarchial research, where some things lead to others, and/or where some research have innate risks/events involved. Or at the very least unlock more things or lead to more interesting developments.
Planetary development (or the lack thereof - hoping that will increase down the line) is minimal, as all construction is done on a star system level. Population management is limited to just moving them across the planets in a single system. The different races is an interesting concept, but the control over it is, again, minimal. And the depth/the effect they have, seem small at first glance. Would've liked to see certain races have a certain affinity for different types of planets, and an increased chance of breeding at, or moving to, such planets. Interbreeding and evolution would've been two nice concepts to add to that functionality as well. The minor civilizations (similar to how EL did it) are a nice new feature - would love to see that concept expanded further.
Internal (for now, there's only trade between empires) trade routes are another addition that would be good to see.
Leaders are simple, virtually nothing have changed since the earlier Endless games. They even seem less useful now, as their stock bonuses are close to zero. Levelling up gives options to increase stats for either system governing or fleet commanding, usually just stat bonuses, nothing really unique or particularly interesting.
There are so many additions that'd increase depth - asteroids and mining rigs/space stations are things that are sorely missing. (Yes, there are asteroid belts, but their functionality is extremely simple.)
Ground combat is another great concept, but it's so very simple in its current iteration - no fortifications/defenses, just three different types of units (where you need to research quite a bit down the line to even get the "armor" unit) and no tactics/strategy at all.
Ship variety seems poor for someone who doesn't spend all too much time on ship customization, few types and the roles are very dumbed down ("attack", "defense", "explorer", "colonist", etc.) - would be nice to see more default templates and types/subtypes, ship sizes and roles.
The UI seems intuitive enough, responsive and rarely clunky. There are some things that feel off so far - I'm really missing an option to easily switch between the star systems when zoomed into (and controlling) one, rather than having to zoom out and manually go to it. That the UI is transitioning automatically between galaxy and system view when zooming with the mouse scroll can be disorienting, but after getting used to it, it works well enough.
And why isn't dust shown in exact numbers, but rather truncated, even in the thousands? (When the dust levels reach extreme levels, I wouldn't mind truncated numbers.)
Moving ships from system hangars to space is a bit clunky, and you wont get notified about idle ships when they're constructed (which is a pretty big annoyance to me), as they're stationed in a system hangar by default.
The "system scan" view seems overwhelming at first, and as it isn't fully implemented (by the looks of it), it's hard to make heads or tails of it. Diplomacy seems simple as well - gonna have to go through the research tree for a while to virtually do anything with it at all.
AI-wise, it seems overly aggressive - even on Sandbox, it colonizes the entire map rapidly, and is more than happy to declare war without any provokation or shared influence borders. Playing as a pacifist race becomes tough.
When it comes to bugs, the ones I've seen so far are mainly related to spelling, grammar and formatting - few in terms of actual gameplay. Impressive! (AI turns can take some time, more than I would've liked, but that's about it.) Devs need to go through the writing a bit though, it really feels unfinished at the moment. Wont hold it against them at this time, it's still Early Access.
A good run-of-the-mill 4X game with really good potential - it could use *a lot* more depth though.
Will update review as the game gets updated - for now it's a cautious recommendation, a 6.5-7/10.
10/10 Wouldn't Be Hyped For $30 Sequel Again

As of 2/2/15 the devs have admitted to abandoning this game while it's in a heavily broken state. Don't let the low sales price tempt you, the player retention (game has sold 2 million+ copies, only has around concurrent 1-2.5k players) speak for itself on the game's quality.
If you want me to elaborate on what I mean by heavily broken:
-Bugs that have been in the game since RELEASE are still not fixed
-Lack of any balance changes for months, 90% of weapons are useless and the game has been made into a massive spamfest of messers and mauls.
-Lack of optimization: I have a pretty beefy PC and so do many of my friends who play this game, some maps WILL tank your fps regardless of graphical settings or player count. I don't even think a quad SLI titan rig could get more than 50 fps on the battlegrounds map.
-Constant crashing/server browser errors. It also doesn't help that all of the official servers are hosted by multiplay so they're incredibly laggy.
-Lack of competitive support from the developers. Think of how much Valve supports the competitive TF2 community. Yeah.
-Poor animation quality, swings/body movement look incredibly jittery and rough even at 120fps, which causes a lot of problems such as desyncs, in a fast-paced game like this.
-Vile. hate-filled community, on par with MOBA/CoD communities
Some alternatives if this game interests you: Mount & Blade Warband (or Bannerlord which isn't out yet.), or the Slasher Project.
I would highly recommend this game put i do prefer to play with mods.

I'm much into 4X, strategy, sci-fi games, I know and own all Amplitude games, as well as probably all 4X games. So why do I not recommend Endless Space 2 yet? Buy it, if you buy 4X games anyway, but wait until release or Steam sales after release if you are happy with Endless Space 1, the new Master of Orion, or Stellaris. I am not an Amplitude fanboy, so I try to explain, okay?
When Endless Space 1 came out, it filled a gap. 4X was supposed to be dead, and sci-fi 4X was always a strange playground. But 2016 all the sudden Stellaris AND a new (not so great) Master of Orion came out, so how will Endless Space 2 compete with these?
Pro
- Game engine. Better graphics.
- Ground combat. But it feels much like MOO2, tbh.
- Political system etc. Some influences from Endless Legend etc., which could be good.
Contra
- UI. Basically Apple fanboy design, with the same glossy glass blur textures. iOS. Not so cool. But UI is clean, yo.
- Lack of innovation. You basically play Endless Space 1, just slower and more complex, with more info/stats everywhere.
- Complicated. I don't mind complex strategy games, like VERY complex, but here it feels unnecessary, compared to Endless Space 1 and the new Master of Orion. You play like Endless Space 1, but with more options, stats and slower.
Everything else is pretty the same, imho. Dust. Star lanes. Ship design. Heros. You know it. Cold War. Minor changes here and there, but if you have a new Master of Orion at hand, ... you might feel that Endless Space 2 could be either a Master of Orion or Endless Space 1 mod, or Endless Space 1 with Endless Legend adjustments.
Overall, I feel that the devs don't know what to do with Endless Space 2. Endless Legend feels more interesting. They roll out their Endless Space/Legend thing every 2 years, so it seems, but ... this time it feels repetitive, less innovative, so maybe they should think again what they want from a 4X game. It needs fresh air. Since it is Early Access, I hope for the future. There are so many ways, ideas, concepts what can or could be done in and with sci-fi 4X, just check the forums.

It's almost 4AM, so naturally I thought it's the perfect time to write a better review about Chivalry, since I wrote my old one at about 50 hours of playtime. Now that I am at almost 600 hours, I think I have a better feeling of the game.
It is undoubtedly the best melee-oriented game I have played. So much so, that to me, all other games with melee now feel very shallow and weak by comparison, and I think that anyone who has put a lot of time into this game can also attest to this feeling. It sets a new standard of melee combat.
Chivalry will not appeal to everyone. It has an extremely high skill ceiling that very few players will even remotely approach (seriously like less than 1% of people who own it probably). But for those who do enjoy it, they will spend an ungodly amount of hours on getting gud.
There are four distinct classes with relatively diverse play-styles, and even though this is the case, I have mostly trudged through the last ~600 hours as a knight, and it never really got boring. You will probably find a class you like best early on, and habitually stick to it primarily. Maybe not, but most players seem to be this way.
This game has the best voice-acting ever. All of the classes on either team have a lot of character in the amusing taunts and compliments, even though they are rather generic in all other ways.
Even though the game was released over two years ago, the developers continue to update it and add content. The community is still active, even in the Australian/NZ servers, which is excellent. As you play more, you will see a lot of familiar faces. People just like you, who have sold their soul to this game. Then you will kill them.
There are some ongoing balancing issues with weapons, some bugs appear and disappear... but it's relatively minor at this point.
We don't talk about the Deadliest Warrior expansion (IT DOESN'T EXIST LALALA). Otherwise, buy this (and play it)!

Chivalry is a proper pc game, and no I don’t live under a large enough rock that I don’t know about the port to the console. That being said, it is a proper pc game. It is difficult enough that you have problems when you start off, getting chopped up like a Spanish Moore during the Inquisition. Doorways, stairwells, and bridges, become a satisfying mosh pit where you can hack your way through and jump back in. The archer is a class I fellate humongous bee hives when playing but some manage to blow my bonce to smithereens. Vanguard is fun and rather fast paced. They are surprisingly effective for an all-rounder. The knight is an over powered, over armored strand of teenage testosterone because they can’t play well. Just kidding, though I think all fights kind of lean in the favor of the knight.

PROS:
*Originality- This is the first game I had ever played (Or seen for that matter) that is detective work. And it does it very well. This is one of the best games I have ever played all year. One of those reasons is because this game is because of how different it is compared to other games.

*Interactivity- This is the first game since the Mass Effect series that I feel like the progress of the game depends on what I can find at crime scenes and get out of suspects.  But if you don't find much evidence, good luck getting confessions out of suspects at all.
*Realism- This game does not go light at all. It goes from abandoned cars, to racism (This game takes place in the 40's), to murder and leaving naked bodies in public, to arson. There is no point in the story at which you feel like the game is going easy on you just to not make you feel sad.
*Gameplay- This may seem like the most important thing in games to a lot of people. It wouldn't matter if the gameplay mechanics were inherently bad, the cinematics would probably make up for it. But the gameplay is very good. So good at being like actual detective work, that you will have no idea where to go with a case sometimes.
CONS:
*Engine- It is clear that this game uses the GTA IV engine. This annoyed me at the beginning of the game because of how similar it was to GTA IV. If you don't think about it, you will be able to see past it.
*Repetitive- This game can get repetitive if you play multiple missions in a row. It is best to wait a couple hours between each   case in order to get a good experience from this game.
*Controls- Just like GTA IV, this game is very tedious to play with a keyboard and mouse. Controller worked perfect for me.
All in all a great game. I would say 9.5/10

LA Noire is a game that completely nails the gumshoe detective atmosphere but loses a bit on the overall narrative.
Each case is about 1.5-2 hours long, and replayability is non-existant if only because by the time you finish the game you're tired of the simplistic mechanics. By "simplistic mechanics" I'm referring to the GTA style driving- and shooting-mechanics.
Aside from that, the meat of the game is in detecting people's reactions to your pointed questions. The ability to see a doctor put his hands behind his back and suck on his lower lip as a telegraph that he isn't telling the truth is something that is very difficult to pick up at first but once you get the hang of it you start to really appreciate the development work that went into making it more about sussing out liars and cheaters than about reaction time and purchased upgrades. This game comes highly recommended also because of the way it draws you into post-WW2 Los Angeles: a city that is exploding with the popularity of movies and the pursuit of the american dream.
The connecting narrative involving the eventual conspiracy scenario really didn't do too well to provide a driving force from case to case. The villains in the game seem very static and aren't fleshed out too well. As a result, actually finishing the game took some determination because you really don't care by the end.
That being said, I highly recommend playing this game which is now super-cheap in 2014. There are quite a few memorable experiences in it and the concept and execution of the atmosphere is well-worth it.

Recommended for fans of traditional MMOs and Metal Gear Rising. Fans of both, not one or the other. The game features incredibly fast and mobile combat and an incredibly, ludicrously fair business model for a F2P game, but it also features what some would consider the "worst" aspects of traditional MMOs.
Warframe is what I would describe as a cooperative pseudo-MMO in the vein of Dragonball Xenoverse; missions can either be run solo or in groups of up to 4, or meet up in large group hangout instances, for trading, recreation, celebration, and recruiting.
The meat and core of Warframe is, much like many older, traditional MMOs, grinding for base materials, crafting them into weapons and Warframes(which are like classes), and then grinding for EXP for those weapons and classes, and again like many older MMOs, crafting something in warframe has an arbitrary wait time associated with it, usually between 12-24 hours, with some notable outliers as quick as 1 minute or as long as 48 hours.
From there, another huge part of Warframe is applying "mods" to your weapons and Warframe, which augment them in a variety of ways; Every weapon and Warframe caps out at level 30, but the enemy level cap is at least 150. Though this may seem dramatically unfair, the sheer power offered by min-maxing your mods and properly managing the elemental damage types you're dealing allows you to easily deal with these overwhelmingly powerful foes--but these mods, much like materials, are dropped by enemies, and must be grinded for, and many of the mods can't be equipped without the use of an item called a "Forma", which effectively halves a mod's cost when placed on your weapon/warframe, which, again, must be crafted over the course of 24 hours from rare materials.
I think you can get the picture. This is what Warframe is about. There is no goal except to collect as many resources and mods as possible, and then collect every Warframe and weapon and get them to the highest rank possible.
Of course, I should also mention that you have the option to use Platinum, the game's premium currency, to buy any weapon or Warframe, or instantly complete anything you have crafting, but this is entirely unnecessary, and is purely a quality of life thing. You can absolutely, positively, access every single little bit of content in this entire game, from beginning to end, from minute 1 to hour 1812, without spending a single
on this game, and many people do. There is literally nothing in the entire game you can't do as a free player, and the only items you absolutely need platinum for are cosmetic items--and even if you decide you absolutely
to have that fancy new weapon skin, you can very, very easily acquire Platinum
from trading with other players. So at the very least, the business model is ludicrously fair.

Everyone really only uses two handed weapons, usually the large majority of people opting for the vanguard class as it's weapons have the largest reach.  You'd think "well I like one handers because they're faster, and without armor (say Man at Arms class) you can dodge.  Unfortunately, the folks at Torn Banner don't understand tradeoffs, and the above is not the case.  The "good" players do things like "accelerate" their attacks by looking down while stabbing or looking left or right in a cleave swing.  With these "accelerations" in the game there is no point to using any other weapon other than a two hander.  Add to this that while playing as a Knight or Vanguard, your movement speed IS slower; if I had to guess how much after playing, I'd say you're ~5% slower as a vanguard and 10% slower as a knight.  In the game, this translates to almost zero difference and generally everyone plays as Knight or Vanguard.  The Man at Arms crowd are generally trying to show off their prowess in the game, but areat a great disadvantage all around.
Lastly, I bought this game in 2012 and nothing but the menus and purchaseable alt armors has changed.  The game could be great, but Torn Banner isn't interested.   ITry it out if it goes on sale sub-$5, but I'd guess the vast majority of players will get some cheap laughs and move on after a couple hours of play time.

L.A. Noire is everything you expect and more. An honest detective simulation of the highest standard set in the open world of, you guessed it, L.A. Created by Team Bondi and published by Rockstar Games, I had a feeling this game was going to be fully fledged out, and they certainly delivered on that.
You start off as a police officer with a strong justice driven ideological view, hellbent on making something of himself. You are given the opportunity to make your way up the law enforcement food chain, meeting new chracters and learning parts of the main character Cole's past life. I am only 6 hours in to the game as I write this but the cases so far feel very genuine.
The game has a good sense of humour as most Rockstar games do but this one touches on some very dark material. I personally feel that this is a good thing and doesn't give the player the feeling that they are being babied.
Although the game doesn't give too many incentives to go out exploring as some other open world games do, the world is huge and feels like a very authentic, and I'm not sure it would make sense in a game like this. The real draw to the game is the detective work afterall.
There are some interesting side missions that you can get called in for but generally they all play out the same way. Bad guy breaks the law. Catch or kill the bad guy. Still, the setting is always interesting and it is something to do if you aren't satisfied by the campaign when you have completed it.
My favourite part of the game was the interrogations. When interrogating a suspect/victim you are given the opportunity to decide whether you beleive they are lying or telling the truth. Using some impressive technology called "MotionScan" the faces of the NPC's in game almost feel real, albeit a tiny bit creepy at times. Thoug the system was fun and required thinking, I couldn't help but feel that sometimes it was impossible to tell if a character was being truthful or not. Maybe I'm just terrible at the game but it felt like sometimes I was required to guess rather than read the NPC's expressions.
There are some cool ideas in the game that help keep you immersed in the game. An example of this are the doors in the game having golden handles when you may enter them, which means that you never run from door to door to check which are openable and which aren't. There is also no fast-travel feature in the game, but that doesn't mean you have to drive yourself everywhere. You're a cop, therefore you have a partner. You can tell that guy next to you to drive you from case to case which will skip to the area you need to go, but not before you and your partner's dialogue for the sequence is played to you.
A particularly intriguing feature of the game is the ability to search crime scenes. This is a very fun feature that requires you to walk around the area and find clues. They are well explained to you as you find them so as a rule you should never feel like a clue is irrelevant. I did find that after a few consecutive crime scenes without breaks that finding the same beer bottle or cereal box on the floor became a little annoying, but completing a crime scene after finding all the clues in the area was a great feeling every time.
Driving in L.A. Noire is fun but a little arcadey, which some people may like while others may not. I personally feel neutral towards it because I got my partner to drive me around everywhere after the first few hours and the is more about thinking intelligently than the actual gameplay mechanics.
There is no lock-on system in L.A. Noire. Shooting can be a pain in the bum if you are using a controller to play the game, but you do it so briefly and so rarely that this should not prevent you enjoying the interesting gun scenes. In other words, guns are certainly not overused. Speaking of violence in this game, there is a boxing mechanic in the game that pops up when a suspect decides to engage you in hand to hand combat. This is as simple as blocking and punching and I found that mashing the attack button usually got the job done. I'm not too fussed about it because as I mentioned previously, the real gumption of the game is the detective mechanics.
The main character of the game is interesting. He is quick witted and seems to be a very highly-principled officer, a nice change from Rockstar's usual hardstyled criminals we are usually made to play. I did feel that he could be a little spontaneously aggressive at times and he doesn't seem to treat his partners that well.
The setting of the game is realistic. The game does not shy away from a lot of protruding themes of the time including racism, Nazi Germany and sexism. I will say that I feel Rockstar used these effectively to help you distinguish between the characters you are supposed to like and the characters you aren't even though for the time a lot of these things were considered "normal."
Overall, I would certainly recommend this game to anyone looking for a good story and some engaging mechanics. The game requires you to think about what you are doing without punishing you too much for making a mistake. The game doesn't baby you and a lot of the content is certainly aimed for an older audience, but if you are interested in an immersive interractive experience look no further than L.A. Noire.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare may be a few years old now but it has managed to keeps its high ranking postion of most unique multiplayer game.
Most games these days are some form of multiplayer be a shooter game, MOBA or MMO we seem to be connected online with any game we play so we have to learn to addapt to this new formula of always online. Chivalry does this as it brings fun combat from a game like skyrim which is singleplayer enhances the combat tenfold and then turns it into an online game in the formula of a fps game. In Chivalry you compet in free for alls, team deathmatches and objetive type games. Each game helps you work towards reaching the next level as well as leveling up your sword/axe/bow into the next far better one.
There is no endgame only the pride in knowing you have improved yourself from when you first started playing, being able to kill everyone in a free for all makes you feel good inside as you stand their hacking away the limbs of one of your enemys. This game is gory enough to make killing someone with the three diffrent swings really intresting each time as you don't know which limb will fall off first.
There are four diffrent classes which all bring something diffrent to the battlefield, Archers are the long ranged characters which stand at a distance and use a variety of diffrent medieval ranged weapons none of which have amazing accuracy so provide a chalenge as you get used to aiming and figuring out the best time and place to shoot the enemy at. You have the man at arms which is the quick moving quick attacking character that runs in and runs out which allows for small amounts of damage to be inflicted before one of the heavier more damaging charachters comes in to finsih the enemy. Their is the character who is sortof in the middle quicker moving then the tanky class but slow enough to inflict damage they have a charing attack which can allow them to enter the battle quick but once they are in the skirimish they can't leave easily. Finally there is the very tanky very slow class which goes into battle and if played wells dismebers the dead coprses at the end.
The game offers a lot of variety and unique gameplay elements that most games these days dont offer. I hugely enjoy playing this game with my friends with skype as it leads to a enjoyble time. I hope you play this game for yourself and figure out your own stratergy to become the master of the battle field and lead your troops to victory!

Constantly I am swarmed by troodons that knock me out effortlessly and I lose all of my belongings to them, and by the way, there is no way that a fresh spawn can fight off a pack of troodons.  Standard rates for collection, taming, etc; are still too slow.  Stable progression is
IMPOSSIBLE to perform in this game on the official servers.  This game still crashes and glitches a ton even on PCs with good hardware.  I do not believe the developers seriously put effort into this game at all, everything in the game looks so odd that it is confusing and the difficulty is almost unbearable for fresh spawns on official servers.  Optimization has gotten better, but unless your computer seriously has a good dedicated graphics card it is nearly impossible to play this game at a flattering graphics setting with decent framerates.  I may revisit this game in the future if I hear of a big update and huge optimizations with new, productive additions to the game, but the way this game has gone downhill just discourages me from buying any DLC or anything from these developers.  This game simply is not polished enough to be called a final release, if someone told me this was still in alpha I would have believed them, but I can't believed the developers of this game just threw their hands in the air and considered this game complete.

Out with the guns and in with the swords! Chivalry is a nice change from the countless first-person shooters available. Instead, it takes the first-person viewpoint and throws in a melee style combat experience.
Being able to get into close combat with others is fun and there's a nice range of attacks that can easily be used by using different buttons on the mouse, as well as the scroll wheel. This control system works great and feels very intuitive to use. There are a number of different classes, such as a Knight, Archer or Man-at-Arms, each with their strong and weak points and it creates some great tactical gameplay. Be sure to try each class and find the one that fits your play style – I tend to prefer playing as a Vanguard as it has a nice reach, though they lack a shield which can be really helpful! If you decide to get the Deadliest Warrior expansion pack (which is definitely worth it if you enjoy the base game), you can get to play as a Pirate! Jack Sparrow even makes an appearance!
Overall, Chivalry is a really fun game and something that makes a nice change from hectic gun battles. The way the game plays creates a much more satisfying experience and has a perfect learning curve.

What an Incredible game! One of the deepest and richest storylines for any game I have every played. Not only do you feel good after solving a crime, but you actually feel like you are in the game with Cole Phelps and his partner. The searching of evidence is extremely easy with music and sound effects making almost impossible to miss a clue, but remember, not every clue is necesasary to the case! The driving is absolute perfection but I felt that at times, the car felt terrible for how far in the story you were (not a spoiler). I feel once you progress further, the car you drive should get better. The action mechanics are awesome, chasing down a baddy and tackling him to the ground is a satisfying thing. Though the shooting mechanics of the game take time to adjust to and some enemies take at least a full magazine of ammo to kill if it is not a headshot, it is easy to adjust to. The interview process of the game is extremely detailed, where a simple swallowing of saliva, could show the persons doubt. Make sure you look at your notebook and check every piece of evidence to make sure the accused isnt lying. This game has some small flaws, but are easily overlooked and one of the best police/detective games ever!

I am on the fence as far as this game is concerned.
I do really like the gameplay, and the art style/graphical design of this game is absolutely superior to most other free to play games. There are games on the market that rival it in raw graphical fedelity (Partical effects, explosions, bloom, things like that) but the art style and unique attention to detail for all the characters, weapons and ships are top notch and really make this game stand out in the graphical design.
The gameplay is incredibly fun and fast paced. You really do feel like an absolute killing machine designed for nothing else, basically a futuristic Samuri/Ninja that just flies around the map incredibly quickly, raining death and destruction with your abilities (There are tons of "Warframes," that basically serve as unique class with different trains and abilities) from above and below alike.
Yet after the initial few levels you do also realize that the game isn't just a pushover with difficulty, and managing your health and sheild becomes extremely important after the first couple of missions.
That is quite a rare balance for PVE based games - In most games the AI is so hard and the levels are so crammed that you progress very slowly and fail more than you win. Or it is so easy that you barely have to try and even if you screw up, the rest of the team will easily bring you to victory.
Warframe balanced it perfectly - Makes you feel powerful against your foes, while also making you respect them in many situations and not be so aggressive.
The game is very fun, and it is a pleasure to look at.
It also has a story. Not a particular deep or interesting one. But it actually makes sense, and allows you to actually understand why you are fighting the enemies you are fighting. Rather than them just being faceless beasts. With full voiced dialouge for many of the missions, it actually gives the game a sense of continuity.
Whereas most COOP based games don't really have much of a reason connecting various levels/stages making all of the levels/missions feel generic and disconnected.
It is a fun game. There is no denying that.
Which brings me to my main qualm with Warframe -
The Grinding.
To get anywhere you have to play massive amounts of time. Albeit I have not spent much time in the game, I have noticed the mission rewards are not much in comparison to what you need to either craft things, or buy new Warframes/weapons/gear.
It starts out extremely slowly, and talking with a more seasoned player (the one who suggeste I play it in the first place) he told me it took him nearly 13 hours of gameplay at first just to unlock a second warframe. This is someone who is absolutely elite with grinding type games and does them faster than most.
Meaning someone like me it would take far longer.
I would recommend Warframe as it is very good if you like a bit of a grind and have lots of time to kill.
It is pretty.

I fully recommend this game, for those who like crime-solving games, games with mystery or suspense, or for those who enjoy the '50s noire detective/gangster theme. I myself enjoy all three of these elements, and so find this game incredibly addictive and enjoyable. The game is designed so that mistakes can be made during clue collecting (ie, you miss a clue) and interrogation (ie, you fail to call out a witness on a lie, or accept a lie as the truth) without a failure-state; it simply makes it more difficult to come to the correct conclusion at the end of the case, or it leads to a decreased score on the case. Each case has a very powerful film noire feel, and the cases are often based on historical cases from the 50s. You play Detective Phelps, an WW2 veteran who has turned to detective work for the LA police, and you interact with diverse, interesting characters, all with great voice acting and motion capture. To sum it up, there's not really any other game like this one, so if it appeals to you, get it! If you get it today, it's on sale for 4.99, but if you get the complete edition for an extra 10 cents, it comes with a couple extra cases and other DLC. What a steal!

Game is a great idea, one of the finest idea's for a game ever.
The developer is however, demonstratably incapable of finishing this product.
You will find that the game has a new 500mb update every few days with minimal changes - such small changes that the patch size clearly does not reflect the changes being made. It's a decent enough game underneath, but any good-will  is buried beneath the Developers unethical practice of releasing DLC for their unfinished game.  True they never said they wouldn't do this - but having a game in "Early Access" heavily implies that the base game will be finished; before resources are devoted to making new things - which the backer wont have access to at completion. To anyone having issues with Rockstar Social Club freezing at Syncing screen here is the Feedback from Rockstar that finally fixed it for me. Many systems on Windows 8/8.1 may have this issue, both of mine did and it took me months to find a solution.
Reinstalled L.A. Noire just to make sure my other fixes didn't mess it up.
Went to the Steamapps and into the L.A. Noire folder and found the LANoire launcher .exe
Right clicked into options and disabled all compatibility modes for me ( And the All Users ) included, unchecked all boxes.
Then set Run as Admin for all users and myself (Duh) and did the same thing for Steam launcher on desktop.
The game froze for about 4 minutes on a smaller windowed mode and then continued and launched Rockstar Social Club just like normal, even my Xbox stats were there.

Saul: It's almost a shame to smoke it. It's like killing a unicorn... with, like, a bomb.  "Put This in Your Pipe and Smoke It." Pineapple Express is one of my favorite stoner comedies of all-time. It "hits" all the "high" points that it needs to. It also pulled a great and soon to be classic performance out of James Franco as Saul the drug dealer/stoner. Everything he does, from his mannerisms to how he talks to what he says is a perfect parody/impersonation of a stoner. His performance doesn't reach the level of say Sean Penn in Fast Times, but it is one of the best stoner performances I have ever seen. Dale and his drug dealer, Saul, end up on the run from a corrupt cop and a major drug kingpin Ted. Their experience takes them through shootouts, fist fights, car chases, and wooded adventures. There are some classic scenes in this film. I especially love the woods scene. It's a perfect piece of pothead paranoia and is actually not far from some experiences you've had while smoking the cannabis.  The film has its share of problems. I won't deny that at all. Still this is a film that I can watch and re-watch and watch again. People who aren't laughing after the first scene where we see where the prohibition of marijuana came from should just give up on it there, because it's a sign of the humor to come. This is strictly a drug comedy. Sure there are elements of other forms of comedy, slapstick and sex comedy included; but as The 40 Year Old Virgin was to sex comedies, Pineapple Express is to drug comedies. If you're a fan of this genre, you'll absolutely love this film. If you aren't, you still might like it because it's better than 90% of drug comedies. So give it a try. You may not like it, but then again you may be like me and won't be able to stop laughing. If you want a little help with the experience, toke up beforehand. You'll be howling.

It's like Law & Order without the Order, but with some GTA style gunplay, driving, and fisticuffs.
Honestly, the reading of peoples faces during interrogation ranges from super easy to extremely subtle.  Played it with my wife to see if we could work together to catch all the facial tics and we got close but still got fooled on occassion.  This attention to detail is the main thing that stands out in L.A. Noire.
The 1950's Los Angeles setting is beautifully done and pretty accurate. The clue-finding mechanics are simple yet effective enough (a little chime when you approach a clue, that you can disable if you want).  The backstory is confusing (reveled through newspapers and flashbacks) but I haven't finished the game yet so maybe it all comes together.  FInally, the driving is standard GTA style with oldschool sedans.  Not really anything new there.
The crime-solving aspect of it is great, and the progression through each case is pretty fluid and creates a dramatic story arc.  There is a little too much driving for my taste, since the real fun is had in interrogating witnesses and taking down suspects with guns/fists.  But I would reccommend this game to anybody that likes mystery and crime stories.  It is one of a kind.

I love how all the negative reviews state that Warframe is repetitive and brings nothing new to the table and how they quit after so many hours. I would like to point out that we will be getting a lot of new content and it isn't repetive if you switch your gear often and play different missions and mission types constantly. You probably get bored from grinding mastery constantly, but its fun to take it at your own pace. Also, name your loadouts with a witty name to add for some hilarity. For instance, my Harrow loadout is called Pope Francis, which amuses me giving me a good laugh everytime. Don't be afraid to switch it up. Not using the meta constantly is also a way to make the game fun. One of my favorite set-ups is Wukong with the Iron Vault augment and a Jat Kittag with Vulcan Blitz for some powerful slam attacks. This game has  so much potential, not to mention that we will be getting open-world areas sometime in September, along with custom weapons we will be able to make using various parts. I like to think that the Devs and the players who enjoy the game see the potential and the draw that this game has. This game makes me think that I'd rather stay awake when I'm asleep because everything is never as it seems, when I fall asleep. They put very minor details into this game, such as, the planet Earth turns slowly. In levels that are at night there are lots of fireflies that some might even say "I get a thousand hugs from ten thousand lighting bugs." To quote someone famous about how great this game is "You know it, I know it, everybody knows it." Thank you for reading my review on warframe and I hope it helped some people out.

Recommended for fans of traditional MMOs and Metal Gear Rising. Fans of both, not one or the other. The game features incredibly fast and mobile combat and an incredibly, ludicrously fair business model for a F2P game, but it also features what some would consider the "worst" aspects of traditional MMOs.
Warframe is what I would describe as a cooperative pseudo-MMO in the vein of Dragonball Xenoverse; missions can either be run solo or in groups of up to 4, or meet up in large group hangout instances, for trading, recreation, celebration, and recruiting.
The meat and core of Warframe is, much like many older, traditional MMOs, grinding for base materials, crafting them into weapons and Warframes(which are like classes), and then grinding for EXP for those weapons and classes, and again like many older MMOs, crafting something in warframe has an arbitrary wait time associated with it, usually between 12-24 hours, with some notable outliers as quick as 1 minute or as long as 48 hours.
From there, another huge part of Warframe is applying "mods" to your weapons and Warframe, which augment them in a variety of ways; Every weapon and Warframe caps out at level 30, but the enemy level cap is at least 150. Though this may seem dramatically unfair, the sheer power offered by min-maxing your mods and properly managing the elemental damage types you're dealing allows you to easily deal with these overwhelmingly powerful foes--but these mods, much like materials, are dropped by enemies, and must be grinded for, and many of the mods can't be equipped without the use of an item called a "Forma", which effectively halves a mod's cost when placed on your weapon/warframe, which, again, must be crafted over the course of 24 hours from rare materials.
I think you can get the picture. This is what Warframe is about. There is no goal except to collect as many resources and mods as possible, and then collect every Warframe and weapon and get them to the highest rank possible.
Of course, I should also mention that you have the option to use Platinum, the game's premium currency, to buy any weapon or Warframe, or instantly complete anything you have crafting, but this is entirely unnecessary, and is purely a quality of life thing. You can absolutely, positively, access every single little bit of content in this entire game, from beginning to end, from minute 1 to hour 1812, without spending a single
on this game, and many people do. There is literally nothing in the entire game you can't do as a free player, and the only items you absolutely need platinum for are cosmetic items--and even if you decide you absolutely
to have that fancy new weapon skin, you can very, very easily acquire Platinum
from trading with other players. So at the very least, the business model is ludicrously fair.

This game is really what you make of it.  If you use the crutches in game options it's a fairly straight forward game with movie quality characters and story.  If you turn the crutches off, you'll ride the highs and lows of being a police detective in the 1940's, so much so that after a bad case you're gonna want to go on a bender and slug your wife.  Don't do it though.
I used the crutches playing the tutorial cases and it seemed fairly easy getting all the clues with little music tones and hints where they are and the music stops you've found them all in an area, then it was a little challenging during interrogations trying to find the right approach and use the right evidence when catching them in lies.
Then I discovered how to turn EZ mode off.  Go to game options and change "Clue Music" to ON so there's no music indicator for when you've found all the clues, and turn "Clue Hints" to off so there are no hints to where clues are.
Once you take EZ mode off, the game is really fulfilling as the successes become oh so sweet, and the failures are absolute facepalm.  Without 100% certainty of finding all the clues, it gets REALLY frustrating as suspects lie to your face but you don't have the evidence to nail them, and the facial animations are so lifelike that you'll seriously want to backhand people as they roll their eyes and smirk during questioning.  Great game, well worth the money, and I'm only halfway through it.
(Warning: my play time doesn't reflect how long the game actually takes to beat because I've had to spend alot of time on the pause screen.)

First of all, this is not Grand Theft Auto. LA Noire is about looking over evidence, questioning witnesses, figuring out who's lying and why. The game has fine sense of style, it's plot and characters taking inspiration from noir film and literature of the 40's and beyond. It's pretty fun collecting clues, putting together the big picture and pinning the suspect. However, for all it's fantastic concepts, LA Noire stumbles in it's execution. There's a big open-world to explore, but no real reason to do so. Some of it's abitrary 'game-ness' can interfere with the actual mysteries you, as a player, try to think though and the writers sometimes have a different opinion of what 'evidence' is.
BUT. It's arcing story and development is what drives the game home and getting around a world of 40's noir charm is great. There are few big games out there that try to do what LA Noire does and I don't regret spending 20 hours staring at Andrew Staton's face.

Поначалу выгоднее заниматься 'ручной работой' и самолично убивать врагов, но уже спустя несколько первых часов ознакомления у вас появится альтернатива — ничегошеньки не делать.
Idle жанр построен именно на бездействии. Вы занимаетесь лишь менеджментом, изредка закупая солдатов и поднимая им эффективность нанесения повреждений, а уж дальше они сами по себе. Некий симулятор хитрого полководца, который один раз вышел на поле боя, а дальше лишь отсиживается на стуле в ожидании окончания войны. Но мощь противника слишком велика и попросту непреодолима, поэтому грубой силой зло не побороть. Все эти кактусы, котики и картофелины должны получить по заслугам! Для этого один из героев готов предоставить особую услугу по искривлению временного континуума — повернуть время вспять. После такого ритуала вы возвращаетесь в самое начало пути и снова проделываете то же самое, но уже с некими преимуществами. А вот враги будут всегда находится на одном и том же уровне развития, что позволит с каждым 'перерождением' прорываться всё дальше по бесконечным зонам и уровням.
А зачем это всё?
Главный вопрос всегда нависал над жанром Idle — "а в чём же его смысл?". Ну улучшил ты воина, ну начал заново и нанял теперь уже двоих... Для этого и существуют дополнительные возможности. Прежде всего, система достижений, которая добавляет некие бонусы к урону, сохраняясь между перерождениями. Пройди сотую локацию, победи миллион монстров, кликни 35 раз в секунду (да, это возможно!) — существует целый список подобных квестов для любителей бить рекорды и брать золотые медали. Альтернативно, можно стремиться нанимать предельно доступные количества героев или же вступать в форумные баталии и доказывать там всем, что именно у тебя самый длинный показатель урона.
В конце концов, игра служит сугубо для расслабления — показывает некую видимость прогресса, совершенно не обременяя геймера. Лично я уже с месяц сижу на ней и всё никак не пойму — "ну почему я всё ещё здесь?". Возможно, именно длительная продолжительность стала главным фактором появления у неё столь огромной популярности со времён Cookie Clicker. Разработчик постоянно добавляет новый контент, рассчитанный на уже опытную аудиторию, вдыхая жизнь в этот, по сути, бессмысленный окоченелый труп.
Выводы
Если подходить с точки зрения текстовой игры, то Clicker Heroes хороша. Но, адекватно осмотрев её с ног до головы, можно заметить множество недостатков. Надоедливые звуки с очередной мутацией музыки из "Пиратов карибского моря" быстро утомляют слух, поэтому их лучше сразу выключить. Графика и анимация неплохи, для браузерного проекта, но они могут замедлять работу компьютера, поэтому и от них стоит избавиться, поковыряв местное меню настроек. Реальный прогресс происходит очень медленно, заставляя вновь и вновь повторять одинаковые, порой занудные, действия, но с каждым перерождением уже чуть быстрее. Ко всему стоит добавить странную необходимость ручного сохранения перед каждым выходом, иначе можно потерять весь вложенный труд. Да, тут сражения происходят даже с выключенным компьютером, но плюс ли это, ведь нужно иметь постоянное онлайн-соединение.
Всё, что выходило в этом жанре ранее, теперь смотрится крайне неубедительно и даже смешно, а на саму Clicker Heroes уже успело появиться пару десятков клонов (это о многом говорит). Так что нельзя ни в коем случае назвать сей проект провалом — просто тут всё рассчитано на особенный контингент. Подход необычен, а результат и вовсе сомнительный, но платить деньги за игру не нужно, так что терять вам нечего. Хотя и есть возможность поддержать разработчика, покупая случайные апгрейды войска или иные разовые бонусы. Один из наибольших минусов таится в отсутствии внятного обучения: вам придётся лазить по всяким форумам и сайтам в поисках важной информации да советов — иначе получаемый в процессе игры опыт не будет раскрывать весь заложенный потенциал.

ARK can be a great experience for all of those who enjoy Dinossaurs, Adventure, the Primal, the Primitive and Taming or just Appreciating Dinos, (which most you can ride and teach to do things for you).
The Pros: You get to play a Survivor dropped in 1 of 3 maps and from there you have to grow your Exp. by harvesting materials, hunting the fauna, and collecting items from the flora, using them to build your home and utilities. To do so, everytime you level up you get EP (Engram points) that'll be used by you to learn Engrams which will provide you with the specs (blueprints) and materials you need to build your stuff. Also as you progress in the Level ladder you will get to spend Points on your Abilities (like Strength, Stamina, Speed, underwater Breathing, Fortitude) which will make things a lot more easier to survive in the game and into taming the stronger Dinos. In overall, this game is a great experience and a must for everyone who loves Dinossaurs and a good dose of Primal adventure. The game just got nerfed a few months ago so things are way easier obtained and once you get the hang of it (which may take a couple weeks) you'll have a glad fun time.
The Cons: the bad aspect about ARK would be sadly and in fact the players.. if you join a PvP server, I highly recommend that you join with friends (create your own tribe or get them to join a bigger Tribe with more game experience). If you are coming into play alone, it is of the utmost importance that you either join an already existant Tribe (who'll teach you the perks of the game and give you stuff) or stay very well hidden at all times to ensure Survival (which in most cases it doesn't work, certain Flying Dino Mounts can spot you or your base from miles away up in the sky). Also, players in this game can be very xenophobic both in real life ideology or in-game. Alpha Tribes can pretty much destroy everything you hold dear and worked hard to build or create, be that for territory, to steal your stuff, to steal your Dinos, or simply for the fun of not liking you.
If you're new to the game I highly recommend that you join a PvE server, at least until you learn the basics, and then move to a bigger PvP server. Also PvE is ideal if you're more into building huge territories and buildings and more focused onto taming Dinos.
Now if you enjoy battle, killing other tribes, don't really care about the size of your base, and are into taking raiding rival tribes and stealing their goods, then PvP is the right choice for you. Just remember that the same way you did to them, it can also be done to you. So think wisely on who you attack, why you attack, what are you stealing and what for, and have your base protected into a well-hidden strategical position or it can also be your doom.
Nothing else to add, I personally play on PvE cause Im Dino-taming focused, I've played on PvP for enough time to realize nothing you build lasts in a long-term duration so.. Measure your options wisely, and ARK can become a great, fun and innovating experience for you ;)!!!

Rockstar does a fantastic job creating a "noire" atmosphere in a 1940's cop procedural format.  The problem is that after playing other Rockstar titles like GTA, the linear nature of gameplay feels overly confining. The voice and character acting are top notch (I noticed they recruited half the cast from Madmen for lead and supporting roles).. really better than I have ever seen.  But in order to keep their script and story cohesive I am afraid that the game authors sacrificed the sense of open world that I have come to expect.  You do get the chance to respond to all points bulletins to stop robberies, etc, but these are small blips in the experience, and I found them too easy to be satisfying. If you want to insert yourself into a movie with a set script and help click your way through a storyline that is engaging and extremely well acted, this is is the game for you.  If you know you're a player that revels in side-missions and breaking the mold (storyline be damned), look elsewhere.

You're one of the LA's finest, a former military veteran who is looking to build a successful career out of law enforcement in 1940's post World War II L.A. with fancy suits and muscle cars. It's men's world.
Playing L.A. Noire is like taking part in an interactive movie. It's more than just watching the action as you get to take part in it. And the outcome of the cases is determined on your gut, your attention to detail, and interrogation skills rather than just wating the actor to state their line. If there is at least a tiny bit of detective in you and you want to get to the bottom of things then you'll find the storyline captivating and it will drag you in like honey.
As of gameplay, mouse & keyboard combo is tolerable. Walking and running around with keys and using mouse to look/aim works fine most of the time. Driving is slightly awkward when you want to drive straight or especially when trying to take sharp corners in high speed due to the fact that the camera turns slowly behind the vehicle unless your mouse hand is in sync with your keyboard hand. Many times I've ended up smashing bumpers with oncoming traffic or rear fender taking contact with nearby mailbox or lamp post. However, as this is not the most important mechanic I bare with it. Car chases are still fun.
Interrogation of people is the one that gives you the most "what ifs". Do I believe what this person is saying with their eyes rolling out of their heads or do I push my luck to squeeze the last bit of information they have? Or do I dare to state they're lying and then provide them with evidence that I know what the real case is? And you'd better have the evidence with such allegation or the conversation may be short lived.
The gameplay involves occasional chases both on foot and on wheels, some gunfights and brawls. They play out decently not getting too much attention from the story itself. In overall, there's a nice balance of action, seeking and dialogue to my taste and it keeps me tempted to replay a case after a case until I get the gist of how it should have been.
If you have no patience and you couldn't care less about the story then this might not be the game for you. But if you're into the era and the mysteries of police detectives then I highly recommend L.A. Noire.

I'd recommend this game for anyone who is looking for something a little different in the fast-paced shooty games genre. The art style is refreshingly unique, the combat is super-satisfying with lots of different weapon movesets. The ninja-like flips and wall-runs and high jumps are great fun as is the rather impressive lineup of warframes one can play.  The story quests are, for the most part, very interesting & engaging -- they're probably my most favorite aspect of this game, to be honest.
There are downsides that can end up eroding one's desire to play, the big one for me being the severe lack of variety of enemy designs. One gets tired after a while killing waves and waves of the same ugly grineer, the same boring corpus, the same tedious infested.  The maps suffer from the same monotony, too.   There really needs to be more variety in this game, something to make it feel less like you're just running through re-arranged tilesets and more like you're in a living, breathing, diverse, dynamic universe.  (Edit: The Plains of Eidolon update has provided some of that much-needed variety; it's really nice to be able to run and flip and fight in an outdoor setting.  I hope Digital Extremes makes more of this kind of thing on other planets!)
That said, Warframe is worth playing, even sinking a few dollars into it (**BUT WAIT TO GET A 75% OFF COUPON FIRST, OR AT LEAST A 50%, AS YOUR DAILY REWARD!**); play it until you get bored -- it's a good time until that happens.  Cheers!

The city is unnecessarily big and, sadly, feels quite empty. Perhaps the game would have been better off without the forced sandbox feel. However, I enjoyed the majority of the cases and would deffinitely want something similar to be developed in the future - just without the aforementioned faults. I'd rate L.A. Recommended for fans of traditional MMOs and Metal Gear Rising. Fans of both, not one or the other. The game features incredibly fast and mobile combat and an incredibly, ludicrously fair business model for a F2P game, but it also features what some would consider the "worst" aspects of traditional MMOs.
Warframe is what I would describe as a cooperative pseudo-MMO in the vein of Dragonball Xenoverse; missions can either be run solo or in groups of up to 4, or meet up in large group hangout instances, for trading, recreation, celebration, and recruiting.
The meat and core of Warframe is, much like many older, traditional MMOs, grinding for base materials, crafting them into weapons and Warframes(which are like classes), and then grinding for EXP for those weapons and classes, and again like many older MMOs, crafting something in warframe has an arbitrary wait time associated with it, usually between 12-24 hours, with some notable outliers as quick as 1 minute or as long as 48 hours.
From there, another huge part of Warframe is applying "mods" to your weapons and Warframe, which augment them in a variety of ways; Every weapon and Warframe caps out at level 30, but the enemy level cap is at least 150. Though this may seem dramatically unfair, the sheer power offered by min-maxing your mods and properly managing the elemental damage types you're dealing allows you to easily deal with these overwhelmingly powerful foes--but these mods, much like materials, are dropped by enemies, and must be grinded for, and many of the mods can't be equipped without the use of an item called a "Forma", which effectively halves a mod's cost when placed on your weapon/warframe, which, again, must be crafted over the course of 24 hours from rare materials.
I think you can get the picture. This is what Warframe is about. There is no goal except to collect as many resources and mods as possible, and then collect every Warframe and weapon and get them to the highest rank possible.
Of course, I should also mention that you have the option to use Platinum, the game's premium currency, to buy any weapon or Warframe, or instantly complete anything you have crafting, but this is entirely unnecessary, and is purely a quality of life thing. You can absolutely, positively, access every single little bit of content in this entire game, from beginning to end, from minute 1 to hour 1812, without spending a single
on this game, and many people do. There is literally nothing in the entire game you can't do as a free player, and the only items you absolutely need platinum for are cosmetic items--and even if you decide you absolutely
to have that fancy new weapon skin, you can very, very easily acquire Platinum
from trading with other players. So at the very least, the business model is ludicrously fair.

With almost 600 hours of gameplay I feel fairly qualified to review this game.
If you're looking for a game where you can stealth around the map, go in guns blazing, slash and dash hoards of enemies, or just tank for days, this game is for you.
If you're looking for a very fun, totally free*, constantly improving, great graphics game, then this game is for you.
Warframe lets you jump straight into the action, but I would highly recommend useing the wiki page to help you out with learning how to optimize mods/frames/weapons/etc.
*(you can spend your cash to get things faster, but EVERYTHING in the game can be earned through trading or just grinding),
Warframe can be played solo or with groups of up to 4 players. If you have no friends (because you play video games all day), you can join a clan. In fact, you should join a clan anyway, since some content is only obtainable through the clan dojo (clan base).
Warframe can be difficult to start out as a newbie, but once you get some quality gear (low level I would recommend the Ember or Frost suit, Galatine or the spiky whip, lex or aklex (or just get a hand held tri-grenade launcher and accidently kill yourself with it), and a Dread or Syndicate shotgun.
Speaking of syndicates,
You can ally yourself with 3 (4 if you can manage the grind) syndicates. Leveling up with them will unlock special gear mods, and items. Getting rank 4 or 5 in a syndicate will allow you to trade the unique items for platnium (the In game currency). Early on you want to spend platnium ONLY on upgrading your weapon and warframe invantory.
Honestly, Warframe is probably one of the BEST f2p games of all time. It's highly rated for a reason. I would highly recommend trying this game out, but bewarned: it's pretty addicting.

This is a different and fun kind of game. You do a lot of interviewing of suspects, investigating crime scenes, driving from place to place in the LA area. It's interspersed with bits of more action-y type activities, like car chases or gunfights with bad guys. There's also optional emergency calls that come through where you can go stop some petty criminal in action. The interviews were really my favorite part; trying to pick the right interrogation technique, when to mention certain pieces of evidence and so on, was fun to do.
There were some less awesome parts of the game. They designed this huge city for you to drive around in, but you can't enter ANY of the buildings except the police stations and whatever building is active for your current quest. It kind of left me feeling cold and disconnected from the city - I couldn't just wander around in and out of shops and houses.
Also (SPOILER ALERT!!!) you end up finishing the game as a completely different character. It was frankly a little odd. I got very attached to the main character, then 2/3 of the way through, you start playing as someone else - who was, throughout most of the game, kind of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that you worked against. Having to suddenly play as him really annoyed me.
But even so, I still consider this a fun game worth at least one playthrough.

The game is amazing. For the most part, it plays very smoothly and the graphics are stunning. It includes a very interesting RPG based crafting system that is essential to survival in game. Also, the game can function both as an MMO and as a single player game- it's your choice! The FPS weapons you can craft also add a very fun element. But if you're like me and you love animals - especially dinosaurs- you'll be thrilled to know that you can breed creatures!!! Also not JUST breed, but you can also wind up with biological mutations resulting in different colors and patterns. It's also not just dinosaurs. You can breed animals like moose (magaloceros), sheep (ovis), sharks (megalodons), dolphins (ichthyosaurus) and wyverns (fire, poison, lightning and ice)! However, the wyverns are not actually "breedable". You must go out, find and steal wyvern eggs that can be hatched into babies. You can also breed big cats like sabertooths or elephants like mammoths! Even giant predatory birds and bears! Or wolves! You can tame the adults or raise babies and level them up, edit their stats, get them saddles for riding and even deck out those saddles with amazing weapons- like laser cannons, for example.
You can also plant whatever seeds you can find in crop plots ranging from small to large. This is a definite recommendation for being one of the very first things you try to do in game- especially if you have a Narcoberry seed on hand. Make an irrigation system out of stone, set down a small crop plot, plant your Narcoberry seed and turn on the tap above it! You'll be needing a load of Narcoberries for when you plan to start taking down larger animals for capture.
The only drawbacks I can find are that single player still seems to have to be reached with online access and that there are also the occasional glitches that sometimes come out when the team releases new patches and packs. But the glitches are not as bad as some would think. It seems the ARK team has a good reputation for fixing the new glitches with every new patch. My only suggestions for the team would probably be to make an additional 'offline' option for single player and to add more small mammal species, such as voles or mice or shrews that could be an extra source of food or maybe small reptiles like lizards. Maybe an iguana that sits on the player's shoulder and can help forage or attack enemies. Just a few suggestions. Or maybe one of the small mammals can be a new forager for players.
