TL;DR: Don't buy it. It's new content built on mountains of bugs. Think you can do better with a private server? Nope.
I wrote a review pre-release, and I was ecstatic for the potential in the game. Aesthetically pleasing environment, interesting creatures, building, and exploration. I had such high-hopes. However, I have since returned only to find a sadly pitiful excuse for a released game. Buggy to the point of unplayability, even for server admins who can insta-tame - but who wants to continually instatame a summoned dino because ".whoops! There went a dino through the world again!" I can't imagine trying to play on an official server, if it's as difficult to remedy accidents as it is on a private server. I can't control for updates, so that streamers and players can plan for play-time. I can't control for mod issues, or base game issues, by updating when I'm ready, rather than the instant it happens.
Furthermore *no* I shouldn't have to rely on each player to understand computers in order to download and resolve base-game problems. They should be able to log in without that worry, that's my job. They shouldn't have to reverify files which constantly corrupt. They shouldn't have to wait anywhere from 8 to 45 minutes to log in with PCs usually used for any other game. They shouldn't have to "figure out" that if a mod needs downloaded, they have to log in, wait for it to time out, wait for it to download and not even clearly know that it is or is done, then do it again in a few seconds, and be timed out and WHOOPS the game crashed AGAIN, like it does randomly. These people are from all over the world, with different PCs. That's unacceptable.
I can't return dinos 90% of the time, only replace them, even when they clearly fell through the world and should be *somewhere.* Even if I could, it's often a waste of everyone's time as it could take me several hours to locate and return it.
The modding community is attrocious, and it probably is a direct result of the frustration and disappointment with dealing with base-game limitations and bugs. People are rude, they harass one another, they demand money, they refuse to maintain mods. Don't tell me this is normal, because it isn't. There are many games with well-respected modding communities which produce top-notch mods. This isn't one of them.
There is no reason I shouldn't be able to use a dino ID to summon or teleport it to me when it's lost; especially when it fell through the world, and a player didn't just forget where it was placed. There is no reason we should even be dealing with dinos consistantly falling through the world, at this stage in the game. This should be a rare occurance, not a common one. This should be built into admin commands.
There is no reason the commands should be so horribly clunky, and counter-intuitive. There is no reason to have such a lack of control of my environment, as an admin. There is no reason a server can't have it all server-side, rather than client-side, especially when the game devs built modding into the game - it's not like everyone is hacking it. What is the point of allowing people to play-my-way, while simultaneously making it mind-numbingly difficult? Why even allow private servers? I spend more time trying to replace and fix base-game bugs for players, often through weird round-about ways and mods, than playing the game, and unfortunately so do they since they have to wait in line for me to try to fix it.
Clearly, someone in charge doesn't care about this game. The game devs will respond with how they work their rumps off, and maybe they do, but it doesn't show. This means the priorities are all wrong, and their time is being wasted. It's a huge shame. I don't understand why the devs don't prop up their modding community and focus on the core game stability. Let players create dinos and new content. People love to give their time for free when they have fun and can be creative.
P.S. thanks for adding handcuffs to the game. So much fun being locked in a box for hours on end. That's clearly what new players want to experience!

TL;DR: Don't buy it. It's new content built on mountains of bugs. Think you can do better with a private server? Nope.
I wrote a review pre-release, and I was ecstatic for the potential in the game. Aesthetically pleasing environment, interesting creatures, building, and exploration. I had such high-hopes. However, I have since returned only to find a sadly pitiful excuse for a released game. Buggy to the point of unplayability, even for server admins who can insta-tame - but who wants to continually instatame a summoned dino because ".whoops! There went a dino through the world again!" I can't imagine trying to play on an official server, if it's as difficult to remedy accidents as it is on a private server. I can't control for updates, so that streamers and players can plan for play-time. I can't control for mod issues, or base game issues, by updating when I'm ready, rather than the instant it happens.
Furthermore *no* I shouldn't have to rely on each player to understand computers in order to download and resolve base-game problems. They should be able to log in without that worry, that's my job. They shouldn't have to reverify files which constantly corrupt. They shouldn't have to wait anywhere from 8 to 45 minutes to log in with PCs usually used for any other game. They shouldn't have to "figure out" that if a mod needs downloaded, they have to log in, wait for it to time out, wait for it to download and not even clearly know that it is or is done, then do it again in a few seconds, and be timed out and WHOOPS the game crashed AGAIN, like it does randomly. These people are from all over the world, with different PCs. That's unacceptable.
I can't return dinos 90% of the time, only replace them, even when they clearly fell through the world and should be *somewhere.* Even if I could, it's often a waste of everyone's time as it could take me several hours to locate and return it.
The modding community is attrocious, and it probably is a direct result of the frustration and disappointment with dealing with base-game limitations and bugs. People are rude, they harass one another, they demand money, they refuse to maintain mods. Don't tell me this is normal, because it isn't. There are many games with well-respected modding communities which produce top-notch mods. This isn't one of them.
There is no reason I shouldn't be able to use a dino ID to summon or teleport it to me when it's lost; especially when it fell through the world, and a player didn't just forget where it was placed. There is no reason we should even be dealing with dinos consistantly falling through the world, at this stage in the game. This should be a rare occurance, not a common one. This should be built into admin commands.
There is no reason the commands should be so horribly clunky, and counter-intuitive. There is no reason to have such a lack of control of my environment, as an admin. There is no reason a server can't have it all server-side, rather than client-side, especially when the game devs built modding into the game - it's not like everyone is hacking it. What is the point of allowing people to play-my-way, while simultaneously making it mind-numbingly difficult? Why even allow private servers? I spend more time trying to replace and fix base-game bugs for players, often through weird round-about ways and mods, than playing the game, and unfortunately so do they since they have to wait in line for me to try to fix it.
Clearly, someone in charge doesn't care about this game. The game devs will respond with how they work their rumps off, and maybe they do, but it doesn't show. This means the priorities are all wrong, and their time is being wasted. It's a huge shame. I don't understand why the devs don't prop up their modding community and focus on the core game stability. Let players create dinos and new content. People love to give their time for free when they have fun and can be creative.
P.S. thanks for adding handcuffs to the game. So much fun being locked in a box for hours on end. That's clearly what new players want to experience!

Of all the free-to-play games that I have played over the years, none have quite kept me playing as Warframe has. I say this after a 2 year absence from it's first release on Steam. Sadly missing out on some now vaulted prime warframes and weapons (this would be my only annoyance with the game, so far).
It's fast and furious action, along with the wide arange of warframes, weapons and gadgets to collect can leave you with many options to suite your playstyle. As each warframe and weapon can be modded, with hundreds of mods at that, you can alter your frames and weapon to become a powerhouse of pain. Mod alteration also becomes important when you need to do the correct elemental damage to the correct mob/boss.
If all out shoot/slash-fest is your thing, or you like playing a bit more stealthly (which to be honest can become somewhat pointless, unless you have the right warframe/weapon combo) then this game could be for you, and with the acrobatic movement system, ie. wallrunning, gliding, bullet-jump can have you darting across the map in no time, turning a hail of bullets into body parts. Controlling the battlefield with crowd control powers, while you slash away at their helpless soon-to-be-eviserated corpses can be very satisfying, and if you really want to see an enemy fly away only to dance like a bad marionette then grab one of the bows and give them a little headshot.
The game can seem like a grind-fest...because it is. Trying to build warframes and weapons, especially the primed versons, first requires you to farm parts from enemies and missons, all with random loot tables (this can be frustating when you only need one more part and you only get the others). But shooting your way through hordes of enemies or blasting away with your suit's powers can be exciting and somehow you forget that you've probably done the same mission dozens of times before; especially when hundreds of enemies come at you all at once.
The game will soon release it's first open, MMO style area, promising new quests and objectives, so I'm keen to see how well this is done. The trailer looks impressive from what you can see.

L.A Noire
+ A very cool and well thought-out detective thriller set in 1940's California, U.S.A. Playing as Coles Phelps you investigate homicides, thefts, drug trafficking and fraud, identifying crime scene clues and speaking to witnesses to gather evidence.
+ A really nice feature of this game is the facial expressions used by characters. A lot of effort was put into this by the developers. After carefully observing how a person of interest behaves or talks, you can doubt what they are saying, judge whether they are lying, or believe them. If you're successful, you'll squeeze more information out of them leading to additional avenues in the case. This is good because it rewards the player for engaging in the game and playing it properly.
+ Nice shootouts with several different types of weapons, although confrontations aren't that frequent. Use tommy guns, pistols or shotguns to take down foes. There's 40 street crimes to complete separate from cases.
+ An intriguing storyline of crime, love and flashbacks of Cole Phelps life in the Marines during World War II. The ending is one you won't really expect. Really enjoyed it.
+ Around 40-50 hours of gameplay with all DLC, trying to do your best on every case.
+ Graphics are decent.
- The graphical quality of the game world could be improved. As it stands it still looks fine, but stunning visuals really do add to immersion.
Overall Score: 9/10

I loved the first 40% of this game.  It's a great game, it really is.  However, the reason I wouldn't recommend it to anyone else is the broken save system and because of the Rockstar Social Club integration.
Concerning the save system, I somehow managed to upset the progression of missions.  According to the game's wiki, there are something like 21 missions in the complete edition.  I'm missing almost half of those.  If I run through my last mission again, I might be able to resume progress and get things to unlock again.  I don't know if that will work though.  I looked around for a way to download and install a save file with the missions unlocked instead and apparently your save game is dependent on your Rockstar Social Club identity.  So, that's no help.
The Rockstar Social Club integration would be cool if 1) anyone really cared about it and 2) if it provided extra features quickly and quietly and without slowing the game's startup time significantly.  However, it does none of that.  So, it's a burden.  Additionally, it's a burden which plays a part in crippling the save system.
In short, while you're playing this game, you will likely have a blast if you like linear style hybrid AAA games.  However, if your save game breaks or you somehow run afoul of the Rockstar Social Club integration, then it will severely try your patience.
EDIT:  I did manage to finish the game by simply replaying a case through again to get to the point where things went off the rails for me.  The game is still great, possibly one of my all time favorites, but the above mentioned features gone wrong still leave a sour taste.  It's definitely a 5 star game besides that though.

1,755 hours doesn't lie, I've practically wasted my life on this game, I love it to death to the point where I've gotten multiple friends and my girlfriend into it. There's a very slight learning curve when you first start, but just remember, mobility is key. Once you get the movement down, everything else will be a cake walk.
Playing solo is fairly fun as is, but I would definitely recomend grabbing a group of friends and having a damn good time on it, that is definitely where the game shines. A close second is the community, sure with the massive player base, you got a few stinkers here and there, but I've met some genuinely amazing and kind hearted players on pub matches, especially when I was first srtating out.
The devs are incredibly dedicated to this game, and it really shows. There's frequent updates inbetween larger content drops, that fix up little things here and there to make sure everyone can enjoy the game. Warframe is trully a labor of love.
Moving on from that, let's get into the core aspects- the graphics are pretty damn nice, even on lower settings. Sure, it's not the best, but I'd give em a 7-8/10. Gameplay, as stated earlier, is really fast paced, mobility is key, though if you want to play a bit slower- don't worry, that's definitely acceptable, just know how to dodge and you'll be set. There's a large stash of content, from the games warframes, to a vast stock of varied and unique weapons, and we definitely can't forget cosmetics, with more added extremely frequently. Each month you can expect to see at least 2 or more new weapons or cosmetics.
The warframes are all unique and each have different playstyles, and with more of those added every so often, I guarentee there will be one that you wil fall in love with. Like a warframes playstyle but don't like how it looks? Don't worry buddy, the steam community is here to help with a vast array of community created skins and helms to give your warframe a special flair, not to mention delux skins added in every so often by the devs.
Now as this is a free to play game, you can spend money on it, that's a given. Personally for me, I really never saw myself spending money on it in the beginning, but as I spent more and more time on the game and kept having more and more fun, I wasn't all too unhappy to toss some money towards it, however, you don't have to. There's a trade economy where I've heard people being able to buy all the frames in the game without having to drop a single real world penny, it's all up to you. Just know that this game isn't pay-to-win. you can buy a good frame, and a good weapon, sure, but not only do you have to level them yourself, but all mods you have to find, collect, and level up as well. You have to put in the work or you're not going anywhere, no matter how good you think a frame is.
Hopefully this helped a little, I think I touched on most of the key points. The game is extremely fun, but it's not for everyone, just give it a try and you might be surprised.

When this first came out, the first thing that came across my mind was Mafia II. And let me tell you, I like Mafia II a lot. So I thought this would be just a Mafia rip-off with only difference being the protagonist. Not a gangster, but a cop. Graphics looked similar, fighting system looked pretty  much the same and the setting was very similar too. But that was just me judging by simply looking at trailers. The differences are actually major.
Later I received this game as a gift from my friend and, to be honest, I was quite impressed. That was after I managed to run it properly though. The game was rather choppy at first (which didn't suprise me since it was a well-known fact). I must admit I didn't even need to change too many things to make it playable. I probably got lucky.But enough of that, let's see what the game has to offer.
Graphics is nice and the city this game takes place in, Los Angeles, is huge. It's very detailed and despite the impressive scale there are hardly any bugs. You'll find many types of cars and many character models with different textures. Almost everybody knows about the famous face expressions in this game. And yes, they did a good job with it, even though some people look more scary than real. I wouldn't call it a huge help during interviews with suspects either, because LA seems to mostly consist of professional liars. But don't get me wrong, it's a nice feature.
Another good thing about this game is the music. And not only the score that puts you into right mood, but also great hits of the 1940's you will hear in the radio. Voice acting is provided by the same persons whose faces you actually see in the game, so the whole thing feels authentic. Sounds of weapons, cars and the city are your normal average sounds.
Gameplay takes some time to get used to, but it's not bad. Walking, driving, shooting... You'll learn all that quickly. Then we have the other stuff that makes this game special. That means searching for clues and interviews. It might seem little confusing at the beginning, but there's a whole chapter of tutorial that also serves as an introduction for out protagonist - disciplined police go-getter named Cole Phelps. Sooner or later searching for clues will become a routine for you and you'll eventually get better at interviews. Those are made well too. You can either believe the suspect, doubt them or even accuse them of lying. But be careful! You must use correct clues to prove they're lying to you.
And then we have the story. Is it good? Hard to say. It's mostly just cases to solve with a flashback cutscene from the war every now and then. Later in the game, Cole's personal life will get more space, but I won't be spoiling.
I can absolutely recommend this game, even though there might be problems running it properly and you might need to find some tips on how to make it run smoother. Some cases are brilliant, some are annoying, but that's what life itself is like, so why not? Overall it's a great experience with lots of interesting stuff. In many ways unique too.

The short version of this review is that the grind combined with the lack of purpose leaves me struggling to understand the appeal.
--
For some background, I played this with a friend on a private server.  I turned some of the time to train dinosaurs and other menial activities down due to earlier reviews I had read.  Even then, the game was still very grindy.  Refunded after just short of two hours.
When you knock out a dinosaur, you must feed it berries while it's unconscious to train it.  Essentially you stand there and put berries into its inventory.  I did this for 20 minutes on one of the “entry level” dinosaurs and that was on ~300% speed.  I cannot imagine how long it takes on the more advanced dinosaurs or how people tolerate this on standard settings.
While I hate the grind, the bigger issue to me is that I could not figure out what the fun part of the game was.  The environment is not hostile and resources are plentiful, so just surviving isn’t the challenge.  I could not find any interesting areas near me, so exploration isn’t entertaining.  Building seemed to have potential, but blueprints are locked behind the leveling system. Ideally for me, the blueprints would be hidden in the world or the materials just in dangerous areas, but they went with the grind instead.  Dinosaur taming, as mentioned above, was extremely tedious and even afterward all I had was a mobile storage unit that had to be fed.  Advanced dinosaurs obviously have more utility but I have no idea when that happens or how insane the time investment is.
I don’t know who I would recommend this game to.  Obviously, some people like it since they have invested thousands of hours into it (probably feeding dinosaurs), but I have no idea why.

Ok, so I participated early on in this game. The concept is fantastic and there are no other competent medieval fighting games. Unfortunately, it's necessary to say there are NONE at all, because this game is far from competent. I stopped playing a few months after I got this game, for the following reasons:
--The pace and quality of updates was not up to scratch.
--The game was laggy on every server.
--The hitbox's were RIDICULOUS. It's hard not to rage when your well timed, precise hit misses for no reason and your opponents' wild swing from 20ft away with a dagger decapitates you.
--The network was so unstable that people were going undamaged from clear hits and teleporting around after a blow, sometimes to right behind you, making a sneaky sure kill and rage inducing death.
--Ranged weapons were poor, boring despite variety and suffered from network and lag tremendously during flight.
--Teamkilling was far to rampant and un-penalised. Kicks were rare due to disinterest and the fact that everyone was doing it. The game needed proper long term penalties for rampant game ruining teamkilling spree's.
--Models and textures were sub-par, though I could forgive this in the game's early state.
--Maps had great variety, but suffered from an aesthetic design, rather than keen thinking on how to channel combat and provide wide options.
Now, no fixes were on the horizon. Dev feedback was poor in terms of actually fixing issues and providing real updates. So I quit, to return later on down the development cycle. If the game survived that long. I was quite surprised to see that it did. I guess enough people enjoyed 20mins of quick slashing and never became disillusioned as I did. That and the novelty of a medieval game, which remains unique in it's genre.

So I logged on after over a year of not playing today, and pumped a few hours into the game. I'm not sure how to put into words how epicly, truly and deeply disappointed I am. Absolutely NOTHING has changed. Actually I lie, the menu and customization screen has changed. And they introduced microtransactions. Yeah, EA style money-grabbing for a new sword skin. I could live with that, had a single one of my points above been fixed. The atrocious hitboxes, awful network lag teamkilling, it's all still there. You still can't climb up a ladder without juddering half the time.
Now don't misunderstand, this is no 'rage-quit induced rage-review'. I've been here from the start and I'm still, even with a relatively low total time of play (spread between early access and recent gaming), pretty awesome at this game. First game after a year and I landed 59/12 K/D. So belive me when I say that my review is based on observation rather than the usual rage. 10 out of 12 of those deaths were due to teleporting enemies, swipes from weapons WELL out of range, my weapons spontaneously doing zero damage etc. I could go on, but you get the point. The other two were from hugely enjoyable duels that I was outsmarted on. That 'potential' mechanic is the only remaining draw for this game. And given its 'barely' early access state despite being over two years old, I must stress that it remains a 'potentially' awesome mechanic.
In conclusion, the devs have made no effort here. Two years of development has left a buggy mess of a game that still managed to introduce competent microtransactions. Effort well placed... The gameplay is no different from release day and despite me destroying the enemy team every game (which is admittedly ego-boosting ;) ) I cannot truly enjoy a game in such a state. One man indie games have been released into an Alpha state that still beat this game in polish, depth and stability. Maybe I'll return in another year...

LA Noire is one of the most sophisticated games i have played - it is a strategy game, yet implemented into an open-world area, therefore whilst doing cases (main missions) you can respond to "dispatch calls" or just general roaming around.
LA Noire is one of the most immersive games i have set foot on. It really endulges you into the genre of late 40's America, with the new "automobiles" and the distinctive detective suits.
SOUND - 10/10 - A truly immersive factor about the game, its background music and themes are FANTASTIC and get you really into the mood of its era. Some music is even Taxi Driver (Robert De Niro movie) remenicant and transforms the map into a grimy, vice city that LA is. Also there is some top notch voice acting done by all characters and basically everone who's face is in the game!
PLOT - 10/10 - Of course, R* is renouned for their storylines, and this one offers it all!
GAMEPLAY - 8/10 - Although the graphics or feel of the game is very relevant to the genre, it is still pretty clunky and lacks the vividness of a GTA game. The gunplay - although you dont get much of it - i though was pretty decent, but not as good as GTA titles.
GRAPHICS - Eventhough the PC port is locked at 30FPS, its there for a reason - in order for the face technology to work. The GFX in the game are very good and the dark greys/blacks/browns you get from this game reflect the genre (la NOIRE). Also the face thingy is a very unique and fun thing to watch.
TL;DR - I love what R* has done with this game. If you are thinking its just GTA in the 40's - THINK AGAIN, because in reality, it is way, way more than just that. Its the best R* i've played, and thats saying a lot!

Great game, though it didn't port well to the PC.  A series of small glitches add up.  Frame rate lags, moments where Cole Phelps gets immobilized, unpredictable and imprecise driving controls (in a game where car damage brings down your score), poor menu controls (switching between mouse & keyboard), un-skippable cutscenes (for when you are re-trying a crime scene for the nth time).  It amounts to a bunch of issues that should have been resolved with a few decent beta-testers, but it seems the developers simply pushed it to get to the PC too fast.
The game is sometimes unclear on how to succeed: in interrogations, the subject gives a statement that cannot be true or false, so asking whether he's lying or not is aggravating.
Otherwise, though, the cases are well written and engaging.  The story moves well.  The environment is fantastically realized, especially the cars and the radio entertainment.  Some problems with uncanny valley effects, but I won't blame the developers for that.  I'd give it an 8.5 (higher but for glitches).

LA Noire is a strange game, in that it is a combination of 4 action games (car chase, foot chase, fist fight, gun fight) and an adventure-y detective game that is focused around interrogations. Since all these elements are woven around the same story, it really works, at first. After about five or six cases, it loses its luster somewhat. The foot chases, gun fights, and fist fights are too easy. The car chases are easy too as long as you remap your keyboard so that you are driving with two hands. The interrogations are HARD. Even if I read all your evidence carefully, and review your conversation log, and look carefully at the expressions of the suspect, I still get the answer wrong almost half the time. When you get an answer wrong, you often miss out on evidence that is necessary for later interrogations. So once you start bad, things just go downhill. The case always "solves itself" at the end no matter how bad you screw up the interrogations, and it does this in a very confusing way. It is very frustrating because you can tell you have missed out on half the story. I have replayed some of the cases using a walkthrough, and found out there were big chunks of the story that I completely missed because I botched the interrogations. I replayed a few cases hoping that I could learn to do better on the interrogations, but it hasn't helped yet. The concept of the detective part of the game is very cool, but in the end too difficult and frustrating. The action part of the game is a little too easy and a little too repetitive. The graphics are very good, the facial detail, the period music and details are great, clearly a AAA game in terms of production values. It seems like this game went straight from concept to game, without any play-testing to calibrate the gameplay to a level where it is challenging but still fun.

Delve into a world where brutality and weapon mastery make or break the future of each battle you enter. Only the most experienced and hardened of fighters will go back home to their wench and feast on mutton and mead. You must battle alongside your comrades with trust in their capabilities and your own inorder to survive until the next skirmish with the those godless heathens from across the river. We do what we must do in the name of Agatha or the Mason Order.. and we do it well.
Your battle master will show you the ropes before you can step headstrong into battle first though. We wouldn't want peasants shielded in armour protecting our kingdoms now would we? Learn how to slay training dummies, side step away from the dangers of sheep, pretend to swing at the air and massacre targets with trebuchet and ballistas. Yes that's it, you're a natural! Now off to battle you go recruit! Shield up, face forward and don't die right away! Live long enough and you'll have the honor of fighting again!
Choose from an archer, a nimple man at arms, a brave vanguard or a knight in heavy armour. Learn their weapons well and choose your favourite. There's not sweeter satisfaction that to ping an enemies head right off with a crossbow from across the battlefield. No greater feeling than to save your comrad from certain death by cleaving his attackers limbs right off. Nothing more adrenaline pumping than the battles cries before forces clash together and screams of pain and glory are heard all over the battlefield.
Prepare to die, and prepare to exact immediate revenge. Chivalry: Medevil Warfare is a breath of fresh air from the typical multiplayer games you've played. There's an enormous amount of return value, and worth spending countless hours honing your skills. Beautiful landscapes and arenas are only a small fraction to the amount of detail and content put into this game. Be warned, this game is not for beginners and may frustrate new comers. Hold on and it'll find it's place in your heart.

GREAT game!  Seriously, this game is amazingly well done!  The story is very interesting and really fun -- a nice blend of foot chases, shoot-outs, trailing suspects in your various vintage cars, searching crime scenes, and role-playing detective work.  Also, I have to say that this game has, without a doubt, some excellent character animation.  The skins of the characters are based on real actors (some of whom you'll be sure to recognize from TV and movies) and the facial espressions, mannerisms, and body language of the in-game characters is suberb!
The interrogation/questioning of suspects aspect of the game is, admittedly, a bit hard to learn, but once you get the hang of it it actually is one of the most interesting parts of the game.
Oh, and about those vintage cars: They've also recreated an amazing rendition of late 1940s Los Angeles that you can cruise around  via your vehicle.  If you search around, you'll be able to find lots of interesting rides (rare sports cars, an ambulance, etc.).  I've thoroughly enjoyed taking cars that aren't mine and driving them to death, literally, by jumping off embankments, taking out mailboxes at 60mph, and other things we've all wanted to do with a car at some point.  By the time I'm done, my ride-of-the-day is a smoldering wreck on the side of the road.  Totally fun!
Anyway, I haven't completed the game yet; I've played about 10 hours into it.  But so far, it's awesome.
P.S. The DLC is totally worth it too, in my opinion.

The year 1947 the case "The Red Lipstick Murder", a woman is found murdered and brutally beaten then dumped at a park just across the LAPD Police Station. Your job as a new dectective is to scout the scene, find clues, find the suspects and interogate them using your intuition and facts to chase down the killer. This is just one example of fantastic cases that you have to figure out and bring down the killers and criminals who commit crimes across L.A.
You play as Phelps, a World War 2 veteran and all around do-gooder. Phelps is an honest man who has a strict honor system and puts his all into a case that he is working on. Phelps starts out as a common on the beat cop who likes to put his nose where it usually doesnt belong. He quickly excells through the ranks and without giving any spoilers he becomes a hero cop and is promoted to detective on the trafiic cases. I find this incredibly interesting since you dont immediately start out as this recognized protaganist in a game filled with crime and criminals. But these guys and gals you come across in L.A arent people you really expect to be murders and rapists. These people are your average run of the mill, hard working citizens who just try to make a living in the city.
But looks are deceiving. Some of the citizens are actually complete psychopaths!
While the core story is really interesting the gameplay is somewhat lacking and the visuals if inspected have small bugs. I found on serveral occasions that some doors i tied walking through would sometimes bug and stay perma shut until i restarted the game. I dont know if that was a problem with my PC or just in general a problem. However I have never encountered it another game. Anyway combat reminds me alot of Red Dead and they are made by the same developer so it was good to see that the combat was very detailed and carefully made. Combat really only comes into play every now and then so if you are a gamer that needs tons of action L.A Noire is not for you.
Gamers with patience and pay very close attention to facts and facial expressions will succed in L.A Noire on some occasions. (there is a part where you have to deal with an actress, nasty buisness and very deceiving) L.A Noire also requires gamers who are very mature because there is nudity in L.A Noire and it will go into detail about the cause of death. So if you are quesy I wouldnt recommend this game for you.
Finally the last thing to talk about is the enemy mechanics and investigation mechanics. These are really the most important parts of the game and sometimes they do incredibly well. On very few occasions the Ai would suddenly come out of cover shooting but instead of returning back to cover, they stayed there trying to shoot me. Once they needed to reload you could easily gun them down and fire at the next enemy. Like I said, this rarely happened so i wouldnt really be too concerned about it. The criminals who arent firing at you are usually running away from you or trying to fist fight you. Never once encountered any problems with the runners or the fighters. Fighters usually ended with you knocking them out and arresting them, and the runners could completely take a turn for the worst. On one occasion, the criminal took a man hostage and you have to gun the criminal down but be careful not to shoot the hostage or then you will be bagging a body and letting the criminal have the last laugh. But in another spot, there is an  insane man that you have to run down and catch before he can fatally hurt himself. I loved parts of the game like this and suggest you do the side quests that come up as they have their own unique part in the game.
Now to the investigation mechanics, these are incredibly well thought out and cleverly displayed! When you enter a crime scene a chime and mystery music begins to play. This all together adds to the atmosphere of a late 1940s crime thriller and does an excellant job at setting the mood. Also the music plays a part when you are investigating, when you here a chime that mean that there is something that could be a clue. I think this is all together inventive and really nails a video game thriller. I recommend this game but am going to give it a
7.5 / 10

A brilliant fusion of the detective point and click genre and action games. This game is never boring as gameplay constantly changes up. One minute you will be looking for clues, the next minute you will be questioning suspects/witnesses, and five minutes later you might find yourself in a shootout, fist brawl, stakeout, foot chase, or car chase. While things might not progress in that particular order, the point is that you will find yourself doing all of these things throughout the course of the game, or even within the same case. The game starts to feel like many games combined into one, but the transition is seemless. This game is a must buy for those that want something different and wouldn't mind role-playing as a cop. The game itself is genre breaking and doesn't quite fit into any one genre, which is a good thing in an age where many games stick to stale tried-and-true formulas.

The only major flaw with the game that I've found is the building system. It's clunky at times, and at its worst (such as when building on a round tree platform) it's downright frustrating.
I feel like this game has gotten a bad rap from bitter early access people who don't feel the game has improved "enough" to justify the price hike. As someone who bit the bullet and paid full price, I'd say it's worth it. Does it have a few issues? Sure, but they're not game-breaking. It looks great, and it runs fine on my computer (which is six years old). I love taming the different kinds of dinos, and I can't wait to find every explorer note scattered across the map by previous castaways. I love being able to level up from stone age weapons to assault rifles and beyond. I just love this game. Period. And I think you might love it, too.

This game is evil. It's the quintessential clicker game:
- you click on things, the numbers go up
- you hire help that clicks on things for you, the numbers go up
- you appease the Gods, the numbers go up
- you transcend this plane of existence, the numbers go up
- you click on the same enemy as your clan members, the numbers go up
- you do all of the above in the most efficient, optimal way, the numbers go up
My numbers are pretty big now. But they still get higher.
Yes, these games are easily addictive. Yes, most of the time you don't do a whole lot. And yes, they are actually just intricate math puzzles that take a super long time to lead to the solution. After which the problem just gets another level. If you try this game out, use caution. If you immediately think that all of this sounds pretty stupid, you are right and you are right in never touching any of the clicker games.

When you think of F2P games, you always think of games like tiny tower, Roblox, in general lower quality games. Games that sometimes are very simple, or in Roblox's case, kinda broken. When you think of a F2P you don't usually imagine a game running in 1080p, 60FPS, triple A title. Welcome to Warframe.
First, I'd like to address the first question people will obviously have about the game.
"Does it have paywalls?"
No.
In Warframe there's no paywall in any shape or form at all. Anything you see in the game you can do/get completely free. Granted, it might take longer to get there without paying, but it's possible. The only things you can't get without paying are some cosmetics, which are of course cosmetic and not necessary. In Warframe, you don't actually buy weapons or characters (warframes), rather you craft them.
In order to get a new frame or weapon, you need to get the blueprint, and whatever else the blueprint calls for in order to be completed. Sometimes this is the barrel, receiver, and stock of a weapon, or some simple parts you collect on missions. An alternate way to get new frames or weapons, would be to buy them with platinum, or plat for short.
To get plat, you can do one of two things: A, use money from your steam wallet/credit card, or the free and better method, B, trading. In Warframe the best way to get plat is simply to go into trade chat and try to sell your rare weapon or frame parts to someone who will pay in plat. A lot of people are willing to trade, so this is the best way to get plat. This is why there's no paywall in the game, because you can trade to get plat completely free.
So you're probably wondering, "if there's no paywall, what does plat do?". When you craft something, it takes IRL time to be done. For example, it takes 3 days IRL for a frame to finish, but that can be rushed with plat. Or, you could buy a frame outright with plat. In laymens terms, Warframe is a P2P, not pay to play, but pay to progress. If you put in plat, you can buy weapon parts, rush weapons, ect.
But now let's move on to some negatives about the game. My biggest issues with the game is the grinding, and the devs.
In Warframe, the only way to get the parts for weapons/frames, ect, is to just grind it out. This week I was trying to get a Rhino Prime Blueprint. I kid you not, I had been playing literally all week, and all day, since I have nothing else to do. In order to get the blueprint, I need relics which contain the blueprint. Basically, I need to grind for a chance to get the relics, then grind again to open the relics and HOPE they contain what I want. In the end, I never did get the blueprint, I just traded things for plat, then bought the blueprint off of someone who was selling it.
If you don't like grinding, Warframe probably isn't for you. If you don't mind it, however, it may be a game you like. Also note, me taking an entire week to get rhino prime is extremely rare and just very bad luck, and I should've traded for it sooner.
However, grinding isn't the only issue....
The developers, Digital Extremes, can be rather shady. I've heard several cases where they have banned someone for talking bad about the game. Not trolling, but geniunely giving thoughtful, negative feedback. DE tried to take legal action  against a data leaker, who leaked things like what the percentages of getting a certain item is, where it's found, what rotation a defense mission is, ect. We pretty much HAVE to have this data in order to play the game properly, and DE doesn't give it to us for whatever reason.
In general, yes I would recommend you at least TRY the game. If you like it, maybe put some money to progress or get some cosmetics, but it isn't necessary. Watch out for the shady devs, and clem on!

I run my own server and play this game with friends. I enjoy this game, especially if played with friends. Mods make this game even better, the developer has been doing great things helping mod creators. That said this game is far from being "released" quality.  There are far to many fundamental issues with the game that have yet to be addressed most have been issues for a very long time. The developer appears to be oncentrating on new content over fixing issues. If your patient and willing to wait for the game to load (and let it crash periodically) its fun. Game play is good, taming, crafting, explooring, dying all fun and enjoyable.  However
- Networking has issues.  Expect rubber banding, timeouts, timing glitches even with low ping.
- Expect crashes when browsing servers.
- Expect crashes when connecting to servers.
- Expect more crashes when connecting to modded servers.
- Expect hangs when connecting to servers.
- Expect more hangs when connecting to modded servers.
- Loading when connecting to servers is slow.
- Loading when connecting to a modded server is laughably slow.
- Graphics are very unoptimized, expect many rendering issues and visual gliches.
- For your sanity any any assemblance of fun disable Ichthyornis, the most horrible creature in the game.
- If you run a server for others to play on this game updates annoyingly frequently often requiring server to be updated.
Once connected this game is pretty stable.  About as stable as any AAA game all of which seem to have periodic crash issues. Its too bad that steam only does thumbs up or thumbs down reviews.  This review is mostly thumbs up 6 outta 10 if you like the genre. If the fundamental stability, graphics, mod and network issues were fixed this game would have a solid 8 outta 10.
At this point for most players I woldn't recommend this game unless you really like this genre and can live with the issues. Also only buy on sale its is most definitely not worth $60 and all dlc are over priced as well. Wait till its on sale for 50-75% off. I fortunately purchased this game on sale when it was still pre-release and was much cheaper. This game really should still be a pre-release game with the fundamental issues it has.

Hello fellow gamer! :) I wanted to do a review on this game for so long for the simple fact that i have loved it for so long and it has provided me so much fun, and as such i find this as my way to say thank you but also as a way to maybe convince at least some of you out there to give it the chance that it TRULY deserves.
Let me start with the game's economy, because in a lot of free to play games it becomes our primary concern. Is this another pay-to-win game? The answer is "not by any chance". Digital Extremes has done a phenomenal job of actually keeping this game in the most pure form of free to play. You are able to trade the in game stuff you find in missions (e.g. part of a weapon) with other players for Platinum, the currency that is obtainable with real money. So everyone has access in the shop currency without the need to spend real money. Farming items to trade for this currency isn't hard either, it usually comes down to clever negotiation, or just spending a bit more time farming than others are willing to.
Now when it comes to gameplay, we are talking about a fast paced, action packed 3rd person game, where you can kill different types of enemies in MANY, MANY, MANY different ways! :3 Do you want to kill everything with a bow with explosive arrows? A shotgun? A rifle? A ballista? A pistol? A hammer? A katana? Dual wield knives? Oh btw, all these categories and many more not mentioned have many different actual weapons that you can craft, with different stats and types of damage.
I know what you are thinking:
"Ok man, you can kill stuff with different weapons.. big news, it's 2K17, we 've seen it elsewhere..."
Just keep on reading. :)
As the player you get to control warframes, battle suits that each have different abillities covering different types of roles in a mission. Then you select a primary, a secondary and a melee weapon and along with other friends (co-op PvE) you jump into a mission, of which there are several types (e.g. capture, survival, exterminate, defend, rescue etc.)
All of your warframes and weapons are modified through mods, which you find as drops from enemies you kill during missions. These mods give you extra stats or modify completely the way you would use this specific weapon or warframe. There are countless cool builds and countless mods available that you can use and experiment with on all the different weapons, allowing you to make your own gameplay style.
Have i talked about how cool this game looks? O.O Well, you can see gameplay videos for that, you don't need me! ^^ What i can tell you though is that this game is really well optimized, making it a lot easier to play even with older, lower on specs pcs.
It actually has an interesting story to follow which is brought to you with the form of quests that have really well done cinematics but also SUCH good music! You are greatly rewarded by following them with good rewards at the end of those missions and new mechanics or abillities unlocked for you!
For our PvP friends out there, there is the conclave, the place where you battle against other warframes, using PvP specific mods, in stages designed for PvP. There are different modes (1v1, 4v4 etc) but there is also a sports PvP where you actually play a form of team based ninja - handball/basketball called Lunaro.
Game rewards you for playing with alerts that have cool rewards, events that happen quite often and with the Developers being actually close to the community. It is one of the few games where I have seen such a nice and close relationship between the Devs and the player base, with mutual respect towards each other, pushing the game to be the best that it can be.
All this said, there is nothing perfect in this world, as such i have to honestly lay out a couple issues that you might find on your journey. One of those unfortunately, is the start. The game doesn't do a great job of allowing new players to get quickly into the game. At first you might feel kinda lost, not knowing what you should next, what to farm, where to go. That's where the community has stepped up immensely and helps as much as they can in game each other, but still the start is just a rough one. My best advice would be, follow up the linear progression on the planets, try out all the types of missions and try out different weapons, at first just enjoy the ride without worries of where it leads. Then try and join a clan with helpfull people, become an active part of the community and there will be for sure players to help you out on the further steps of your journey, since it's actually one of the friendliest communities i 've had the pleasure to be a part of!
Also, a loooong way after the rough beggining, comes a rough "late game" point. You 've spent lots and lots of hours, you 've farmed and ranked up so many weapons, warframes and mods. You might feel a bit burnt out from the grind / repeated nature of the farm. Eventually you just might want to drop the game for some months, let it bring new challenges and stuff for you to have to have to grind anew.
All i can say for sure is that it's a trip that is SURELY worth it! :) Thank you all very much for your time, i hope to see you all in Warframe! Have fun! ^^
P.S. I am really sorry for any mistakes in advance, english is not my native language so please forgive any small mistake here and there. :)

A great game, with fascinating cases that will make you think, and a very fun, if occassionally very very obvious lie detecting feature. However, as with most Rockstar PC ports, this one has its problems, the most notable being that driving is damn near impossible on a keyboard, and youll spend most of your time letting your partner drive. However, many cases have chase sequences, ad youre fored to drive at very high speeds, which is by far the worst part of the game. You can try to find collectible cars, but this requires driving around which is annoying, and even though these cars are all unique and at times better than normal cars, You loose them once you finish a mission, making finding these only important to the most obsessive of completionists. In addition, the entire city is fully explorable, making you think the game might be a sandbox similar to GTA. Sadly, once you arrive on the scene of a case, youll have little chance for exploration, and the game is otherwise very linear. In addition, most cases have only one ending, and the ones with multiple endings are relatively minor in their overall impact on the story. Combat always feels sluggish, regardless of if youre using a gun or your fists. It clearly wasnt a heavy focus of the game, which is unfortunate, since most cases ultimately boil down to combat.The soundtrack gets the job done, but isnt anything spectacular, just a very stereotypical Noir mystery soundtrack that fills in the gaps between dialogue. It never grates on your ears, but it isnt meorable by any means.
Sound: 5/10. Average. Not terrible by any means, but average
Story: 8/10. All the cases feel complete and do a great job of making the player feel like a detective. The ending comes a little too soon, and theres very little choice in your actions, which is okay, but a bit dissapointing
Gameplay: 7/10. Dialogue/lie detecting bits are ceaselessly fun, and analyzing evidence adds to immersion. Though there are hints, the game does a good job of letting the player figure things out on his own. Combat is slow and tedious, and only detracts from the overall experience. Driving feels like controlling a garbage can with banana peels for wheels, and should be avoided at all costs.
Overall: 7/10. Nice game, very unique gameplay, gets bogged down by Team Bondi's attempts to widen appeal by adding in combat and chasing, both of which are not fun at all. Cases all feel well written, well acted, and are all unique from one another. Worth your time if you enjoy solving mysteries, but avoid at all costs if piloting a bar of soap that looks like a motor vehicle seems like it would be too much for you.

I thank Torn Banner for creating Chivalry simply because it was an important stepping stone in the melee combat genre. Future games will use it as an example of what works and does not work in this type of game, and that is really important for progressing such a niche and unexplored concept. I enjoyed Chivalry while it lasted, and don't regret playing it, but in its current state it's pretty much an unplayable trainwreck. The techniques that experienced players know are unintuative and frighten new players away, there's zero decent learning tools, and without new players the game's community is slowly withering away.
There was a point when I would have said Chivalry is potentially one of the greatest games of all time. It was rough around the edges, but with proper care and decision-making it could have been shaped into an absolute gem. Unfortunately the developers squandered the opprotunity and decided to neglect much-needed changes, both balance and mechanical, and eventually left the game to rot and die. Bugs and exploits that existed in the earliest stages of the game, nearly 5 years ago as I am writing this review, are still prevelent even today.
Chivalry gives you full freedom of your character, and is both a mechanically-deep and highly-punishing game as a result. To have an unforgettable game all Torn Banner needed to do was clean things up, fix animation issues, rework the netcode, and tweak the game's balance. However it became clear over the years that Torn Banner was incapable of fixing the game and unwilling to listen to their communities feedback. Even if it was a general consensus from both the highly-skilled veterans and your average player, Torn Banner would not make even the most minor changes to improve the game.
Rather than trying to improve the game, they threw in some paid cosmetics, did free-weekends and flash sales to sucker in new players, and eventually abandoned the game altogether to go make their new disaster: Mirage Arcane Warfare. Mirage is similar to Chivalry's Deadliest Warrior DLC (which was also a huge failure that nobody wanted), except instead of pirates and ninjas, it has magic. Not only is Mirage just as poorly-constructed and mechanically-flawed as Chivalry, but the addition of spells makes the game even less consistent and puts a wet blanket on the melee combat that makes these types of games good to begin with.
Thankfully, there is a good ending to this rather grim tale. A light at the end of the tunnel... and that is a game called Mordhau. Created by Triternion, Mordhau is an upcoming medieval melee combat game that is very similiar to Chivalry. It is created by a team of people who have played Chivalry and Mount & Blade for thousands of hours, who love this concept but are disappointed by the shortcomings of other developer's attempts. I've already put 30 hours into Mordhau's closed alpha test which came out about a week ago, and it's fantastic so far. Even in its early alpha state, Mordhau is already a much better game than Chivalry ever was.

Warframe is a game that seems decent at a casual glance but has numerious serious problems that ensure I could NEVER give this game a positive review score. Playing money to support this games ensures its poor and sloppy design decisions and greedy monetization will be copied by many new games to come.
Very unfun and unfriendly decisions are completely motivated by monetization. There are tons of free to play games out there that don't heavily compromise game design, and focus on selling cosmetics. This game shamelessly lets you buy a massive number of powerful items.
"Orokin Reactor" and "Orokin Catalyst" are two items you can buy for premium currency that DOUBLE the mod slots on your warframes or weapons. Mod slots are the primary method of gaining survivability or damage in the game. The way that mods are poorly balanced in this game has resulted in making many mods can stack damage multiplicatively. The end result is having one of these makes you not 2x stronger but often 4x or 6x more powerful! If you are a free to play player, good luck even getting one of these for your main weapon early on, since they are tied to random timed events and can't easily be farmed. If you pay a decent chunk of real money, you get a free reactor or catalyst for every purchased item. If this isn't pay to win, I don't know what the heck is.
Player progression is tied to rank, which increases by leveling up weapons and frames. Each weapon has a relatively low max level so you need to grind LOTS of weapons to progress. You can directly buy weapons and frames with premium currency crippling progression for those that don't pay.
Inventory space is EXTREMELY LIMITED. You only have space for 2 frames and 6 weapons! Each loadout incudes a 3 weapons, so that is just enough space for 2 sets of weapons with no space for spares. Digital Extremes actually DECREASED inventory space in an update to increase "monetization pressure" on the player. I personally had items DELETED from my inventory when this happened and support refused to acknowledge it. Inventory slots can be expanded with premium currency only, so if you don't pay, you'll have to constantly discard levelled up frames and weapons. Also the level of weapons is tied to the weapon, so if you re-buy the weapon later it is reset to level 0! Expect to have a very unfun time deciding which weapons and frames to lose if you don't pay. Oh, but don't worry, purchased items come with a "free" inventory slot.
I hope you like Wikis, because this game does not explain it's mechanics well. Examples: Orange Crits, Elemental Procs, Crafting material locations.
Disrespects player's time. Login streaks. 24 hour rank up timers that block access to missions and main story progression. First wait 12 hours, login to click something, then 72 hours to build frames. They employ every method you would expect from player behaviour training garbage chinese mmos. If you like to play in short bursts, this game is not for you.
Now what about the actual gameplay? It is actually a kindof basic shooter. If you've played any Unreal Engine 3 shooter game, you have played this more or less. You would think having a variety of frames would really mix up gameplay, but it does not all that much, especially since they all use the same set of weapons. Shooting things is generally fun, and this game relies heavily on that to keep the grindfest from being boring. The abilities are and weapons aren't all that different compared to what you have seen in other games. The only thing that will keep you playing this game is pure addiction --- the need to get loot drops and more gear, not the strength of the gameplay.
I am very sad that this game has been financially sucessful, because there is a strictly better version of this game with better balance that was made for player enjoyment instead of monetization that could have existed. Tolerating this game only pushes pc gaming in the direction of the mobile market.

There are games you know when you play that there hasn't been any real work put into it and most of the budget went into marketing. But there are some games that when you play, you KNOW that the sheer amount of creativity put into it and the expenses made to craft the experience and make a world has paid off.
And then there's LA Noire.
This game sets a new standard for the storytelling experience in games, not only with it's technology, but with it's excellent integration of good gameplay mechanics and using that as a way to unravel for yourself the world and it's mysteries.
The gameplay involved in solving the cases is pretty solid, with you scouting for clues that will later be used in interrogations. Though the clue-hunting is little more than a game of click-everywhere-until-something-happens, the meat is in the driving sequences and the interrogations. The driving sequences make full use of the fact that there's a big open world out there and anything could happen. Simply driving from one place to another is a nice experience as you see in full glory the love and patience with which Team Bondi recreated 1940s LA. Of course these can be skipped but you'll be missing out on the side missions which dot the city from time to time and can only be discovered if you take over the wheels.
But the true flavor comes from the interrogations. They used this technology masterfully in order to not only make the interrogations engaging, but also accessible with some exaggerations on the part of the actors which was done on purpose knowing full well the limitations this technology could have. Simply reading the expressions isn't enough since you also have to back up your accusations with evidence. This requires some thought and patience on your part and you need to read the descriptions of each clue carefully before using them. Suffice it to say that the game is worth it for these sequences and there are a LOT of them.
The story too is quite excellent with many noire elements, plot twists and an overarching conspiracy. LA Confidential, the 1997 movie set in around the same time, was a considerable influence for the game.
There are a few negatives though. Some cases felt like I wasn't really solving them. Even though ALL the cases have definitive culprits, there were a couple of cases where I felt I was simply going through the motions. The shooting isn't very good. The chase sequences on foot aren't really great as there are some navigation issues. Though the game is HUGE with MANY cases and the DLC also contributing to the list, there's not much to do outside the story missions which somewhat ruins the fact that these guys toiled so much to recreate this beautiful city. The PC port, though it has many of the features other PC ports lack like a good options menu and reasonable mouse support, it still is quite wonky though I wasn't too distracted by it.
Minor faults don't bring down this excellent game though. It is something I would definitely recommend to any gamer who wants to play a linear story-driven non-action intensive game. Suffice it to say that after I was done, I missed the game and felt just a little hollow inside.
It's a clicker game.

**EDIT: after quizzing friends that have played this for a long time, and personal experience, changing things a lil bit.  Mainly taking out the gripe about in-game lore as a seperate strike and lumping it into the category of lack of info.
Keep in mind that this is all my own personal opinion...  I see this game as a "love/hate" relationship.
This can be a beautiful game that runs well.  Lots of action.  But for me, this game promises huge potential and delivers very little on it.  The game relies FAR too much on grind and farming for my tastes.  Most items must be crafted using a system that requires TONS of materials and not in a realistic fashion either.  I purchased a blueprint for some kunai that were usable by my "mastery" level, and it cost me most of my credits, but I was fine.  "Space ninja uses Kunai" sounds cool.  But when I go to build it, it costs alot of materials I don't have.  4k more salvage than I had at the time plus 2 sets of materials that weren't available on any of the planets available to me.  And even after that, it'll take 24 hours to craft.
Several hours later, I'm still in the same spot: no dent on salvage amount and still haven't reached a planet with the required materials... Oh, but it's available to me IF I SPEND REAL LIFE CASH.
Pro's ( + ) and Con's ( - ) (combined, cause... you'll see.  Prepare for QQ...):
+ + + + + Still actively supported by the devs with new content all the time.
- - - - - - - - - - - Tons of info, some of it being vitally important info needed to play the game, is never given to you or is given in a half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥manner.  Example: Mission info is given on the map as a short tool tip showing location name, mission type and Expected enemy level ( not suggested player level.  Will it be sparse population or will you be swarmed the entire mission?  Enter to find out. ).  Not terrible until you encounter the road block system put into place where you have to complete multiple objectives in this planet or across multiple planets just to unlock the FIGHT that unlocks the next planet.  Want lore?  Normally, games make you collect it.  Warframe does this as well but neglects to tell you that you need to buy a pack of scanners from the cash shop in order to collect the nodes needed to get the lore... Seriously devs, hire someone that knows how to make a "How-to ---".  This is my BIGGEST gripe against the game.
+ - The aforementioned scanners can be bought rather cheaply in a pack of 25 for a measly 500 credits (in-game currency). Why make it so they can only be bought in a pack of 25?  Why not just a single purchase of a reusable blueprint?  Or maybe just give it to us automatically.  Considering how much scanning is in the game, for the sake of lore and a few crafting materials we can otherwise pick up, you've needlessly complicated this.
+ + Supports control pads...
- - - - ...but acts like it doesn't WANT to.  The only game of its kind that I have played that supports control pads but refuses to tell you how to play using the control pad's input.  You have to drastically slow down and go from game to options menu to decifer what does what in translation between keyboard and controller.  This should not be an issue for a game this old, especially when it's on TWO consoles AND PC.
- - - - - - Returning to the game?  I can't speak for the current tutorial of the game cause the only tutorials available to me now are moving screenshots that are not showing what the tutorial is about while text is on screen showing me keyboard and mouse inputs when the game knows I'm using a controller.  That or, in the case of "Mods", a small box on teh side of the screen that displays text paragraphs at random for a few seconds at a time.
+ + Character/ship/weapon Customization
- Almost all of it, even color palettes, are locked behind a pay wall.
+ Supposedly, you can earn cash shop muns in game
- I have yet to see this.
+ Lots of players
+ Fast paced action
- So fast that if you are new and team up in a PuG, prepare to be left in the dust while the bigger boys thrash everything in sight.  People don't like to slow down for *anything.*  Some players will even yell at you in chat to go faster.
- - - Typical F2P model: Sure, you can play the game, but it'll be a struggling and grueling grind to get anything good (albeit, WORSE in this game, cause you have to grind to unlock the grind to do things).  Conversly, look at how much FUN you can have if you just spend money cause you can get so much good stuff NOW!
+ Can swap Warframes on the fly while aboard your ship which effectively changes your class...
- - - - - ...Gender locked classes.  ( I HATE this!!)  Apparently you are a genderless and amorphous blob within your Warframe cause some of the frames are very clearly female while others are clearly male.  And the game clearly treats you as a person/entity wearing a suit!
- Female Tenno have potato butts, apparently  :(  (A closer look shows it's just very poor modeling / IK rigging.  Don't believe me?  Pick a warframe that shows the hips well and then do the "Meditation" emote.  Look closely at the crumpled scrunching pinch of your hip joints...)
- - - - Effort it takes to craft an item to free you from the parasitic mind control of an undead cyborg enemy: 30 seconds crafting time and uses very few materials, all of which are common and easy to obtain.   Effort it takes to craft a decent set of throwing daggers: over 5k salvage, some common items, and nearly 1000 rare items only found on the opposite side of the solar system (or in your convenient cash shop), requiring you to fight your way back and forth across the planets and then 24 hours of actual crafting time.
+ If it makes you feel better, the aforementioned throwing knives have a pretty ribbon on them.  And are better than a semi-automatic pistol.
- - - Can't trust the stats given.  Stats are very mutable in this game due to the "mod" items you can equip to practically everything.  But also, item performance itself weighs heavily.  Example: the aforementioned daggers.  Accuracy rating: 100.  The pistol I'm replacing with them: 18.2.
Using them while carrying something else forces you to wield them one handed.  There's a bit of a throw curve to them, but it can be compensated for and you can still reliably hit targets.  Not carrying anything else makes you to dual wield them.  Every throw alternates hands.  But there is now an offset to the offhand.  The 2nd dagger will land well below your targeting reticle.  And the offset/offhand throw stays for a good while if you just throw one with the main hand and decide to wait for a minute.  The 2nd throw will always be that offset.  This is not 100 accuracy.
So many people hail this game as something new and innovative, but I'm honestly seeing something done before in many other mmos... but with space ninjas thrown in.  It's just interesting eye candy to me without proper knowledge on how to play or knowledge of what to do.
I shouldn't be forced to go to youtube, a website or beg people to explain things to me.  Thing that really upsets me here is that another game that I enjoyed more, Firefall, did almost everything this game does and failed.

Introduction:
This game simulates the nostalgia of film noir, enriched by elements from classics of the genre, such a China Town and The Third Man. It constitutes a beautifully structured story, that builds it's momentum with twists and genuine tension.
The game is divided into different cases during which the players are also able to focus on different side quests like dealing with street crimes and finding different cars and landmarks.
Pros:
-gives you a genuine feel of it's character, L.A.P.D. detective, Cole Phelps, in the 1950s.
-the city of L.A. in the 1950s really comes to life
-interrogation scenes are done really well and will exercise your attention
-great storytelling
-the graphics are good and aged well, facial animation is still looking good
-from the sound effects to the songs and shows on the car radio as well as the music that's been carefully selected to feel right in different situations, everything in this game sounds just right.
Cons:
-30fps locked
-limited freedom (not an open world game)
Conclusion:
I recommend this game for those who are interested in deep narrative and focus on masterful storytelling.

L.A. Noire is an innovative and unique game. Set in the late 1940's Los Angeles, L.A. Noire grabs you with its rich Noire atmosphere that's maintained throughout the game. Late 1940's Los Angeles is beautifully and meticulously recreated. The game is open world, so you can drive around at your leisure. You play as Detective Cole Phelps, a world war two veteran who climbs his way up the LAPD, wanting to clean up the streets. You investigate crime scenes, engage in shootouts, and partake in interviews and interrogations.
During interviews and interrogations you'll have to read someone's body language (Defensive positions such as crossing of arms and little details like fidgeting) and facial expressions (Darting of eyes, sudden change in expression)  to tell if they're telling the truth, or lying. If you suspect them of lying but don't have sufficient evidence then you can choose to doubt them.
L.A. Noire does have action sequences, car and foot chases, shoot-outs, and brawls. Happening fairly often, they act as a nice way to break up the cases. On a side note, driving recklessly is discouraged, during a case it will significantly impact your overall case rating.

This game isn't for everyone,  the story has a slow pace, which'll quickly tell you if you like Detective stories or not. As a downside, the open world is lacking. L.A. is massive, the game has collectible golden films, cars, and landmarks. The landmarks are okay, but the cars are tedious, You'll just end up borrowing cars from citizens over and over again. There are fifty gold films scattered around L.A. which just makes them a dull chore, making you dart around the city. I felt they could've done more with the open word.
The game has 26 main cases and 40 street crimes, which makes it a damn long game to tackle with at least an hour for each main story case and maybe about 5 mins. for each street crime. Love this game.

I enjoyed this game immensely!  If you enjoy crime dramas or just want to experience a game world similar to the movie 'LA Confidential', then this game delivers!
The best feature of this game is the acting and motion capture.  If you watch a 'making of' video, then you'll see the incredible tech they put in place to capture actors face reactions and performances as part of the characters in the game.  This makes the game highly immersive and helps to deliver many interesting stories (crime cases).
In some ways, sovling crimes is like playing an interactive story more than a game.  However, I found it a really enjoyable and entertaining experiece!  You do feel involved and in control, so it's not a QTE experience.
The game does borrow heavily from the Grand Theft Auto style of open world play.  I was not a big fan of this style of open world play.  You can discover mini-cases or bust robberies in progress as you drive around the city, but none of these are very compelling or story driven.  Thankfully, this part of the game is completely optional.  In fact, even driving is optional as you can have your partner drive you straight to the scene of the crime!
I simply loved this game, and hope so much that Rockstar does a sequel in the future!
This is a game about detective, you need to find out who have killed, stolen or done some other bad things.

Calling this game "GTA for good guys' doesn't do it justice or an honest review. Sure, it's a classic Rock Star engine - but it's also more. What's been done with mo-cap for the actor's faces and body language is something I found myself hoping doesn't end up just be a one and done gimmick. It really helped that feeling of immersion along into a classic film noir experience filled with faithful reproduction of 1940s LA geography, classic cars, star struck hopefuls and the human collateral damage that inhabit The City of Angels.
It took me more than one false start to give this the shot it ultimately deserved, in no small part due to the unnecessary social framework tossed on top of the game that has since been made optional (I speak of the social club here). In the end that was my biggest problem with the game and I wish I hadn't let it get in the way as long as I let it. Fans of sandbox games, detective novels or classic film noir entries should definitely get their hands on this game - it would be hard to be disappointed!

It's a quite interesting game with some unique gameplay mechanics and excellent facial animations, but...It is somewhat let down by horrible driving controls that are extremely over sensitive and the cars handle like tanks.
All the movements in general have a really weighty, clunky feel to them, and there are many times when performing simple actions, such as climbing over a wall during a chase fail because you initiate it at slightly the wrong angle. Quite frustrating and difficult to get used to.
The investigation mechanics are the only thing the game really has going for it, and they are great, but I can't help have the feeling that the game would have been a LOT stronger overall if it focused more on that side of things than on crappy gunplay and drawn out driving sequences.
Probably the most irritating thing is that cut scenes are unskippable...So if you restart a case, you have to sit through all of the dialogue, then drive back to the crime scene etc....This is bad in any game, but in a game that relies heavily on story exposition it is pretty unforgivable.
It does have an interesting story as well. Probably worth picking up in a sale if you are interested in the premise, but don't expect an action game, or rewarding gunplay, or enjoyable driving experiences.
