A great game that has an interesting setting and gameplay mechanic.
The game world is based around post-WWII LA.  The story is focused around detective work on various cases that range from traffic crimes, to homicide, to arson, and vice cases.  Each case has clues you have to discover as the scene and from the various people you question about the case.  Finding more clues gives you more options in questioning.  The question mechanics involves you paying attention to how the person acts, basically you’re trying to tell if they did the crime, had a part in it, or are innocent.  This mechanic also extends to trying to get information out of some people, i.e. do you gently try get more information or go on the aggressive and force them to tell you.  The better you do at questioning and clue finding will result in a higher case score.
If you have trouble questioning people there are points you can spend to either narrow the choices or if you’re online can see what the majority did.  These points are earned through various success levels on completion of a case, i.e. the better you do the more points you get.
The cases are divided into the various desks you work at while on the force.  Each desk also represents a promotion in rank on the force.  Due to the theme of the game some of these cases can be extremely graphic and like with the age and culture your dealing with the language can also be mature.
Gameplay involves you or your partner driving to the scene of the crime.  If you drive you'll be able to do side missions, street crimes, that come in from dispatch while you’re on the road.  These street crimes are not the best element of the game as they mostly have you running and gunning down criminals, they get repetitive quickly.  Once at the scene of the crime you’re able to look for clues and get information from other characters (other officers, the coroner, and witnesses), from there it tracking down leads, questioning people, and the occasional car chase.
Overall, the game does provide a unique experience and is definitely worth picking up.  However, you should buy the Complete Edition as it adds a number of cases that extend gameplay, without them, I wouldn't advise picking up the game.  The reason is because there are some desks that don't have many cases and the additional content adds a lot more meat to the game.
If you don’t own the game and see it on for a 75% off or higher sale I’d highly recommend picking it up.  Game length would be about 40-50 hours if you do most or all of what it has to offer.

Great Game, flaky behavior from Devs. Enjoy the world, but temper expectations whenever Studio Wildcard tweets out updates or content.
This game is a great open world survival game. The theme of dinosaurs and light medieval fantasy invokes that childlike sense of wonder and excitment that you experienced upon learning that these behemoths once walked our earth. The crafting and exp mechanics create a bit of grind but no doubt this is par for the course when it comes to games in this genre. The landscapes are typically beautiful and picturesque but at times can feel a bit empty and hollow. The featured creatures are rendered beautifully though some of the older models could dow ith updates to their in game model and animations, both active and idle. With the addition of idle animations and behaviors for some of the wild mobs (ex. a pelican ancestor diving into the water to catch fish) the world does a passable job of immersing you. The game is well worth it's retail price despite all of the controversy surrounding it price hike.
That said I still wouldn't recommend this game. Despite all I have listed in favour of it, the actions of the developers continously kill any feeling of excitement I may feel. They do this by teasing updates and ideas, setting ETAs for them to arrive, causing the community to get excited, people then schedule days with friends and get days off work lined up so they may enjoy the new content, only to find that it has been delayed weeks sometimes evens months later. We all understand that the field of game development is tumultous and that evershifting, however when you hype up your fanbase for updates continously and then let them down at the last minute over and over, some of them are bound to get burned. This cycle of hype and the let down also coincides with their announcements of paid DLC and we can't help but speculate that the paid DLC was prioritized over that of the free updates. Wildcard is a company and their only obligations is to make money and please their shareholders first and foremost, this is true and not anything special (or bad for that matter). They have every right to do so, virtues and and values don't feed stomachs or pay rent after all. However when you promise content, then set an ETA, post pics, tweet and hype us up, only to then at the very last minute, changed the ETA to three weeks later, then announce your latest paid DLC, you can't blame those dedicated fans, who plan their weekends, holidays and days off around these updates, to feel a little burned.

I would ONLY recommend people buy this game for solo play or play with friends. Going into an online server alone in this game is easily one of the most cancerous, toxic experiences you can have in the gaming world. You'll be berated, trolled, and harassed. Many servers simply have traps laid around the spawns, so that the moment you spawn in you are surrounded by someone's base with a ton of turrets that auto kill you. If you go to the PvE servers? Don't you DARE ask for help or any such thing or again, you'll be berated and treated like the lowest of low trash.
The game is horribly slow and grindy, which honestly stinks because most of this game is based around the endgame survival. Being level cap, getting geared up and going around raiding other players, or forming groups to take on the dungeons in the worlds. But the reality is you will spend hours upon hours just trying to level up and be useful. Like most survival games, you can build a base, but there's no point when anything but metal can be torn down by people looking to steal your stuff and kill you in an instant. All the way up to stone tier, the doors can be chopped down with mere hatchets and melee weapons.
But the other problem is the game is just, dead. Playing on an official server is just, painful, and you will actively spend more time trying to feed yourself than you will farming resources. I'm talking like, getting 2 stone or 2 wood every second swing at a rock or tree.
But then you try to play on an unofficial server. Maybe find a modded one or one that's just set to 5x rates. But that won't work, because you go to the unofficial server list and it just looks like:
0 players
0 players
0 players
1 player
0 players
0 players
0 players
So you may as well just be playing solo, but with the added bonus of having lag spikes constantly.
So I say again, my ONLY recommendation for this game, is to buy it to either play solo or make a small server with a group of friends. And when you do, set the rates of resources and xp and all that to like, 5x. Beyond that, it's an incredibly horrible experience in multiplayer. I would relate it most to crawling slowly through the mud during a storm, while a bunch of people stand at your side jabbing you with pointy things, hoping there is something better at the end, but having the sudden realization that you never get out of the mud, and that those people who are jabbing you with pointy things have, and always will be the dominant players, and will always be the ones poking you and others with the pointy things. You will never be the one poking them back. That's about how fun it is.

I owe this game a review. Easily one of the best values on steam. The game has a large player base and is constantly being updated and balanced. Simply put, LA Noire is a steaming pile.
Somewhere along the way developing the impressive technology, art direction and amazing facial animation, LA Noire forgot that first and foremost, a game must be fun to play.
The one thing that I absolutely can not stand about the game is the sluggish controls. Even when walking around as Phelps, I feel like I'm driving a tank. Attempting to finesse my avatar to examine a piece of evidence in a crime scene is an exercise in frustration. When not driving the tank that is my character, I'm driving around in cars that feel just as unresponsive, except that I'm required to chase another vehicle in crowded streets. The only section worse than the driving and investigating is surely the shooting. The developers must have known these sections were terrible, because after you fail a number of times, you are given to option to skip the action sequence.
LA Noire is not without some redeeming qualities. The crime scene investigation (when you're not fighting the controls) is very interesting and the interrogations are definitely the golden nuggets amongst the pile of dirt.
However, this concept sounds familiar... Isn't there another game with these fantastic game mechanics, except without the cumbersome mess of action sequences? That's right, it's called Pheonix Wright: Ace Attorney.
If you're looking for crime scene investigation and perp busting action, look no further than Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney!
On a side note, my heart goes out the to development team that produced the amazing art and technology for LA Noire. It must be devastating to work so hard on a title only to have it crippled by terrible game design and then losing your job because the management of Rockstar Bondi is as incompetent as the design decisions.

Let's start with the graphics. For starters I was actually amazed that L.A. Noire was the first console game that had near-flawless if not flawless anti-aliasing. I kid you not, you could take a look at the telephone wires from up close or from afar and there would be no jaggies. Nevertheless, I attempted to convince myself that my mind was playing tricks on me and that some anti-alised objects were just polished to perfection. I was partially right; it's only the telephone wires, cars and some other objects that have no jaggies.
The graphics settings for the PC version are:
Antialiasing: 1-3
Anisotropic Filtering: 1-4
Ambient Occlusion - Yes/No
Facial Quality - Quality/Performance
Texture Quality - Quality/Performance
Shadow Quality - Quality/Performance/Balanced
Lighting Quality - Quality/Performance/Balanced
Environment Map - Quality/Performance/Balanced
Level of Detail Quality - Quality/Performance/Balanced
Screen Space Ambient Occlusion - On/Off
Global Detail Level - Quality/Performance/Balanced
And there's also a command line for various set-up options.
If you have a high end PC you can get 30 FPS if you pick all Quality.
However, if you choose Performance, you ALSO get 30 FPS.
So they converted the game to PC yet they forgot to raise the FPS cap, hmmm weird. Honestly, I did not notice much difference between the PS3 and the PC version graphic-wise. I mean all those extra graphics options are nice for the ego-boost but I had a hard time telling the difference especially with the frequent texture popping.
What I mean is that the game's graphics suffer immensely when you drive your vehicle for instance. Objects just pop out of thin air and grow out of the ground slowly enough for you to notice. You may drive and look ahead at some of the box-like buildings when all of a sudden they begin to acquire the necessary features such as windows, doors, color, etc.
Also, in many instances the game practically plays by itself. Again, that was done with the controller movement in mind. You may run after someone through the rooftops, fire escape ladders, alleyways and what not and be automatically redirected to pursue the suspect. The game GUIDES you forces you after the suspect because it assumes you may not be able to make that sharp turn with your controller; all you'll have to hold is the "forward" button.
-----
Part 2
Make no mistake, this is not GTA set in the 1940's. There are no friends to call, bars, memorable and charismatic characters, outrageous cinematics, funny encounters, motorcycles, TV shows, dating, witty radio broadcasts describing the decadent elements of American Culture. This is a very mature, somewhat dry and serious game, perhaps it is too serious. There is a fair amount of thin adult humor that might not even catch your attention but the dialogue is extremely well written to say the least. The game plays and feels just like one of those black and white detective movies. Maybe the game is too serious in fact, there is little room for fun. Nor is there a single set objective mission to complete per se. You just keep the L.A. populace safe from petty and serious criminals.
If anything, the game is divided into chapters much like in Mafia 2 and there are some miscellaneous missions to complete aside from the main story. Each story starts with a few seconds video showing what happens to the victim. There are actually clues within those short videos that might help you solve the crime better and faster. So this is like a sand box game with no toys to play. Sure there are 30 secret cars spread out around the city to find and there are badges and newspapers to look for (if you like achievements) but otherwise there is little to do in the city.
The driving is very unrealistic, it feels arcadish but at least you don't get annoyed every time you try to make a sharp turn and attempt to regain controls. However this unrealistic consolish driving feels out of place in this serious game. I guess they had to make it easy for the controller. At first you may think to yourself "wow, how did I manage to make that turn, not run over the pedestrian and still be able to pursue that vehicle" - again, the game helps you do all that.
For the most part the shooting is okay except when it's not. True, I still prefer the mouse to a controller but once you enter a confined area, the constricted camera speed will force to you aim as slowly as you would with one of those analog sticks.
Crime-solving is where the game shines, or supposed to shine at least. Sometimes it will get tedious and samey even though the scenery, the objects, the part of town and the characters are different. At least it got tedious sometimes in my case because I had to pay attention to almost everything. If you have an analytical mind, it will help. If you have a short-attention spam, then good luck. Every case requires your utmost attention and even if you mess up with most clues, facts and interrogations you will still complete the mission only with a low rank. As a result, you will advance slightly slower in the game and have access to less suits, fame and what not. So there is no real sense of danger or fear of messing up HOWEVER you cannot reload your game if the interrogation goes awry for one reason or another, not unless you want to start the chapter all over again. So there is plenty of incentive to not mess up; you want gain those experience points and exchange them for intuition or ask the community option to help you conduct interrogations more effectively.
In the end, the 6-year period to make the game and a million dollar debt among other things forced Rockstar to close down their Team Bondi Studio. What can I say, next time, try to make the game faster and RELEASE THE PC VERSION ALONG WITH THE CONSOLE VERSION TO INCREASE THE REVENUE.
Thank you very much.

I have slightly mixed feelings about Warframe, but the good parts of the game like the combat, visuals, and worldbuilding outweighs the neccesary "evil" that is the buisiness model of a free to play game. That being said, just about everything in the game aside from cosmetics can be obtained without buying the in game Platinum. Gameplay wise, this is the closest thing to Destiny you will find on Steam (and when Destiny 2 comes out in September you'll have to play it on the Blizzard app). You're meant to play the same environments multiple times with different objectives, and each environment is designed as modular tilesets so despite the repetitive design it still feels fresh. You are a Tenno, a soldier that utilizes different Warframes to combat warring factions. These Warframes are all different, each possesing different looks and abilities that fit different play styles and needs. They are very satisfying to play and are complimented well with the massive armory you kill hordes of enemies with. As a Tenno, your agility lets you traverse the game levels with great speed and elegance. Not only is it fun to use, but the controls are easy to make you feel like a parkour god. The varying Warframes, interesting guns, and enhanced mobility makes controlling your character extremely fun. It's always a bonus too when the game is optimized good enough to enjoy at 60fps. I can manage max settings on my slightly outdated machine!
So the business models for free to play games usually lock people who don't pay out of most of the fun, but Warframe's "Platinum" is closer to letting you buy in to things earlier. The only parts the game locks off with Platinum is cosmetics for Warframes like skins, cape-like Syandanas, and colors to customize item appearances. The cost for these things is moderate, color palletes for example are 75 Plat, which is around eight dollars. Warframe limits the amount of important items you can have like slots for your suits and weapons. You can expand these for Plat as well, and they are vastly cheaper than cosmetics. You can buy two slots for weapons for a meager 12 Plat. The lowest priced bundle will give you plenty of Platinum to increase the amount of things you can use. Despite all that you don't always have to shell out for the goods. Platinum is tradeable among players. There's a possibility to get a very rare blueprint or item to offer to players for their Plat. You can also get some in the daily login reward or giveaways by the devs.

Ah, ARK, a game both loved and hated. The premise seems simple enough. We'll start with the single player experience. You wake up on a beach with nothing and go about collecting resources. It will seem innocent enough as you see simple-minded dodos wandering about and gentle parasaurs strolling along the beach. You will be in awe of the beautiful graphics, (If you have a computer that can handle them). The water will shimmer and you may even see a friendly Icthyosaurus in the shallows. You will continue to venture down the coast, thinking all is well, then just like a scene out of Jurassic Park, you will be mercilessly assaulted by the not so friendly fauna. Acid in the eyes from dilos, mauled by raptors, or better yet, you become a bite sized snack for a rex.
You'll shout your lungs off as you die and are swiftly gobbled up. Then you will respawn again, maybe on a different set of beach, maybe the same one, but regardless of where you spawn, you will know one thing for certain. You need to gear up. So, you will commence trying to take things more seriously, building huts and weapons. Knocking out and taming every animal you see by shoving drugs and food down their gullet. Little by little you will grow more powerful, though not without dying a few thousand more times, quite possibly by the same pack of jerk raptors that tore you apart the first time.
You'll grow frustrated, but you will refuse to give up. You will conquer this land, by Odin's Beard, you will make this land yours! Then after many hours, many days, maybe even many months, you will finally have your mighty fortress. You will have all the Tek gear, laser guns and jetpacks! Tek armor for your favorite rex! It will be great, you will feel all powerful! The land will finally be yours! You will be its god!
Then maybe you grow bored. You've explored every cave. Built a base in every biome. Tamed everything you possibly can. Everything is too easy now. So, you decide to play multiplayer. Test your skills against someone real on the other side of the screen. You spawn in fresh and new on the beach, just like you have a thousand times before, but this time before you even make it ten feet, or better yet, while you are still in the spawning animation, you die. You were killed by "insert inappropriate name here." You shout and rage at your screen. Yelling profanities at this son of a biscuit for killing you. You weren't doing anything. Just trying to get started, make some friends, and have some fun in this new land. You swear vengeance upon them, and you go about grinding. Gathering resources and taming once again. A smile creases your face as you get your thatch base built in record time, your loyal pack of dilos by your side. You know at this rate, within a week you will be able to take on the player that killed you. You fantasize over how great it will feel to have them watch as their base crumbles in front of them, but your daydream is cut short as flames light up your thatch hut. You scream in horror as your mighty dilo army dies in seconds to the flame breath of a fire wyvern. A fire wyvern ridden by none other than your arch nemesis.
At this point you will have several options, try again with a new plan, change servers, go back to your singleplayer, or rage quit the game for a few months. This is the cycle of ARK. It is ever repeating, a horrible cycle of death and loss, but yet, inevitably you'll come back for more.
I absolutely love this game. Even with the rage and frustration, I still keep playing. Maybe I'm a masochist, but this is by far one of my favorite games. Yes, there are flaws. The game can be glitchy and buggy. Mine often crashes from memory leaks. Sometimes, I magically teleport through the world, usually on my favorite dino that dies from the code wormhole of death. My favorite is falling into a small ledge and being unable to get out. I'll be stuck floating in the air, and be unable to damage myself in any way. This usually leads to a rather long wait before I finally die of hunger or dehydration. Mind you, all games have glitches and bugs, and the ARK devs have done a lot to fix them. I've seen the improvements, and over time, there will be fewer problems like the ones mentioned above I have no doubt.
Then there's the other players. If you go onto an official server, be prepared to have your belongings destroyed by the Chinese alpha tribe. Later down the line, I'm sure it will be someone else, and guess what. The same thing will happen. That's just how most alpha tribes are on official, regardless where they are from. Oh, and no matter what kind of server you play on, your many hours of hard work will inevitably be wiped at some point, even if just by a server wipe. Now if you want a fun, less challenging or less frustrating time on multiplayer, go onto an unofficial server. Most of them have boosted rates, and many of the popular ones have great communities. Hell, if you're into RP, there's a fair number of servers that have strong role play communities. Epic castles, steampunk, future themed. You name it, it's out there. Mods make this game even better, and there are some very talented Mod developers constantly making new content for the game. Some of them have even had their work officially added to the game.
Now for the game mechanics. Survival sandbox is the genre of ARK, and it is great in that regard. I must warn you first off, this game is a time sink. You will lose everything at some point. That's just how it goes. As to progression, there's a tier and engram system used to unlock craftable items. It starts with basic primitive stuff. Throw some rocks, fiber, and wood together and you got yourself a pickaxe! Later on, there's wood structures, stone, metal, and then Tek. Basically, you go from having a slingshot to a laser rifle! I'm sure you get the idea. Yes, some of the creatures need to be better balanced, but the ARK devs are constantly working to improve this. A great example would be the giganotosaurus. At first it was waaaaaaaaaay too overpowered, but over time it has been nerfed in the updates. This was for the better by far. Now, I will tell you, whenever they say a major update or DLC is coming out, be prepared for it to be delayed. Some get upset by this, but have patience, it's worth the wait.
Finally, is this game worth the price? I for one bought the game when it was still early access, so I had think would I buy the game now for $60? My answer, is yes, I would. It's worth the price tag, and if you don't want to pay that amount, wait for a sale to come on and grab a bundle with the DLC in it if you want the maps. Don't want to pay extra for the maps? That's fine, there's several that come with the game, and several well optimized Mod maps. Dinos from the DLC can still be spawned or downloaded even if you didn't buy the DLC, so you aren't losing a whole lot if you don't want to pay for DLC. Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who loves survival games or dinosaurs, even with the rainbow of emotions it has put me through! Starts as an awesome game, it gives everything a new player wants: amazing missions to make, lots of planets to explore with new events every few minutes, loads of weapons and warframes to try to get and it's all unlockable since the beginning, a fast-paced third-person shooter with lots of action and parkour elements to evade and outplay your enemies. But then after just a few hours in and most people buying platinum to get the late game items early like warframes (which altough are all possible to get without spending money, you will be stuck with your first frame to grind through all the planets until you get to the planets with the assassination contracts that drop the blueprints that you actually need, then you need to actually gather the resources and wait like a week before irt is done building), you realize that most weapons and all those parkour elements are obsolete, as the late game levels are just a f*ckload of enemies thrown at you and it is up to you to kill them all... So yeah, that high single-target damage shotgun you had? That amazing head-shooting bow that you put dozens of hours in and customized all the mods to fit your playstyle? Useless, get yourself an assault rifle and some akimbo pistols. Stealth? Non-existent in late game. Overall, it could be an amazing game I was more than happy to spend hundred of hour in and it turned out to be a P2W grind fest with dull combat and repetitive missions.

Ok to start off I played this game on PS4 when I was younger so like 4 years ago and picking it back up on PC was a great decision. Currently in between major game releases this game is extremely fresh and fun. Very grindy but in my opinion thats fine. Maps and missions are pretty plain and repetitive but I think this game likes to focus on the combat and movement the most which it does GREAT. So satisfying to cut threw enemies with Excalibur and go into a slide animation while shooting my bow off and pegging enemies to the wall with the arrows, hold down your right click while your jumping with a ranged weapon and you go into a "slow mo" state where anything you can think of looks and feels amazing. Every character has unique and fun abilities that change up the play very well. Even though this game is F2P it holds up so well, especially since its been out for 4 YEARS!!! The player base is still here and people are very helpful and nice if you have a problem (by far one of the best communities ive been apart of). In missions you can face by yourself or with a squad of 3 other friends, but what is great if you do go in by yourself almost every mission has other players searching for it (except for the starter missions). Also there is a HUGE economy and trade market in this game, go over to the trading tab in the chat and see how many people are trading and discussing trades. Overall this game is 9/10 for its combat and movement, 3/10 for level design, 10/10 for the player base and community, 8/10 for trading. and a 100/10 for the FUN only played this game about 4hrs so far but I do not intend to quit anytime soon!! 9/10 for the constant updates that bring new content and even more fresh fun to the game
Final Verdict: 8.5/10
Highly Recommend!

So you wake up on a beach and there's dinosaurs everywhere. You quickly gather some rocks and sticks to make some basic tools and a spear, gather up a bunch of leaves and make some pants while you cram your starving face full of berries. After fighting a couple Dilophosaurs to the death, you carve them up and cook their meat on a campfire as the sun begins to set and the chill sets in, hoping that Carnotaurus can't climb up on the rock you're erecting a thatch hut on.
As you huddle half-naked next the fire eating dinosteaks, you see the flashes of automatic weapons fire in the nearby forest and hope none of that finds its way to the small bit of relative safety you've carved out in the world.
A week later and your pack of trained attack-raptors is tearing apart some rando who you were trying to help, maybe recruit into a tribe, but he accidentally touched you too aggressively by clicking the wrong button.
That's Ark and I love it.

Although I will forever be a fanboy of Pirates, Vikings and Knight II over Age of Chivalry, Chivalry is a solid game that does melee deathmatch games justice alongside Mount&Blade (but not War of the Roses, let's be honest).  It has decent and fun combat as well as varied maps and game modes.  Additionally, it has a large array of weapons for each of the four classes.
Unfortunately the game suffers the same fate as M&B and WotR: its classes are not perfectly balanced, it has a lot of weapons that are considered sub-par, if not useless, and there are bugs as well as issues with hit detection.  The maps and game modes get boring after a while as well (although they've recently released more).  There are also "gimmicky" weapons as well as fighting techniques that the "skilled" players use to wreck everyone else, which is always frustrating.
The balance issues and persistent bugs also leave a bad taste in my mouth, even if now (years later), it's mostly fixed.  But all-in-all, I'd recommend the game if you just want to lop off limbs, use the funny voice macros, and scream at your teammates for not actually doing the objective.

Although the interviewing aspect of this game needs some work, the story line and graphical detail is amazing.  Interviewing is incredibly frustrating, for a number of reasons.  You are required to read the interviewee's body language and tone of voice to determine if they are telling the truth or not.  There is then the option of "doubting" what the subject is telling you, essentially saying that they are lying, but you cannot prove it with evidence.  Perhaps it is because I do this daily (active Law Enforcement) or because I am over-complicating the game dynamics, but I found interviewing people to be downright infuriating, nearly resulting in a broken computer monitor.  My belief is that eliminating the right/wrong response to  your choices, and just letting the game flow with the decisions the player makes, would significantly help the gameplay.  Also, having only one "correct" piece of evidence to confront people with to prove they are lying is not realistic whatsoever.  Sure, there will be a best-case-scenario piece of evidence, however the option to inquire about a person's knowledge of any piece of evidence would also be of use.
Despite my frustrations with what is, essentially, the core of the game, I am quite pleased with the overall result.
There were a couple of questionable moments within the story that left me wondering what happened, or why certain things were the way they were, however, overall I was quite satisfied with this game.  Think Grand Theft Auto mixed with a point and click detective game.  Looking forward to a sequel.

Chivalry is a breath of fresh air in an industry that seems to be stagnating; Chivalry: Medieval Warfare delivers the innovation and creative rebirth for us that have been craving something new.
Though not the first Melee Medieval FP game, Chivalry: Medieval Warfare takes from Mount and Blade: Warband and exands on it ten fold.
Pros:
-Addicting, fast-paced and intense gameplay and sword fights will have you losing track of time                                              -Swordplay is heavily skill-based, and requires you to dodge, feign, overhead, stab, strafe, duck, and use directional swings, but for the love of god please watch your swings in a mosh pit.
-Weapons are incredibly satisfying to use, and both feel and are powerful.
-Well designed game-modes and objective based games let us experience the true potential of team based gameplay.
-Although built in the over-used Unreal Engine, the game still manages to look beautiful, from god-rays to the detailed armor and gore.
-Classes are relatively well-balanced overall.
-Map designs are varied, from sand enviornments to lush forests to keeps and castles and desecrated citidals.
Cons:
-Archers are still OP. (Look into your heart, you know this to be true)
-The balance and fairness of some weapons remain up for debate.
-Teammates do not know how to use overheads and stabs and will likely decapitate you in a mosh pit.
-Server browser is slow and a painful experience to work with; joining friends could be easier.
The game is great. Playing with a buddy is massive fun. But for your own sake, please do the tutorial and ALWAYS go into teamfights with the assumption that your teammates have no idea what they're doing, because they WILL get you killed, especially since this game does go on free-to-play weekends pretty often.

Chivalry Medieval Warfare is a multiplayer game with your typical Team Deathmatch and Free for All modes, with a unique objective mode that has tiers of objectives to acomplish and unlike War of the Roses, Chivalry takes place in an alternate universe instead of a real existing place.
If you enjoyed games that involve melee, this one, being a sword fighting game, is the best at his genre.
Most games that have some type of melee combat, all you have to do is face and point at the target and attack.
In Chivalry you have to forget that. You have to remember that what does damage, is your sword, not you.
If you don't change your mindset from past melee games, you will most likely hate or keep getting killed in Chivalry. Chivalry is easy to get into but still offers a learning\mastering period to become good in fighting.
Like I said, remember that your sword is the only thing that does damage. Sword attacks have a clear weight and cience to them. You can be standing with your back turned at your enemy and still hit him.
It doesn't matter if you are facing someone when you attack. The moment you perform an attack, the sword will hit anything from point A, the start of the attack and point B the end of the attack.
Its a complex system that no other game offers.
In Chivalry you don't fight by having a button to attack and one to defend. You fight by knowing how fast your sword goes, how far does it reach and how aware you are of the enemy and your swords trajectory.
Even though the main focus here, is the combat system I still must talk about the other aspects of a video game too.
Soundtrack isn't the most awesome but that is not to say that it isn't good. It simply is a game where you don't have that perfect song come in at the perfect moment, or that one song  that makes you wanna listen to it or when you hear it you instantly relate it to the game and makes it stand out. But it gets the job done in setting the tone for a war of steel hitting steel and steel ripping flesh and crushing bone.
Chivalry relies solely on multiplayer player to player action to keep it alive and I think it suceeds in it. Chivalry is extremely fun to play and epic, you can have some epic duels and large fights and its a lot of fun.
I don't see any problems with graphics or content wise, though having more content and a steady support of the game is always something good. And from time to time Chivalry releases some updates with new maps which are just great.
The maps are amazing and even though, like every other game, Chivalry brings to the table the typical Deathmatch modes and what not, it never feels short, the combat mechanic in Chivalry is what really sells out.
And you can always play objective mode which is the best mode in my opinion.
Objective mode will take you through a series of objectives in order to win the match, which will take you through a series of maps as well.
For example, one team needs to protect the village while the enemy team needs to kill the peasants and burn the village, if they suceed, they will move to the second stage of the match and need to move the battering ram to the castle gate and ram it down, moving on to the third and final objective which is to assassinate the King (which is a enemy player).
If you are looking for a sword fighting game, Chivalry is it. The combat mechanic amazed me so much when I started playing, its just perfect. It allows for great fights and epic battles while rushing through the castle gates or protecting your King from being killed.
And even though Chivalrys aim wasn't to make a realistic History wise game, not even being set in a real place and by real Orders but I think they suceeded in it. Because in real life, things end in an instant. You can bet that when these battles waged a thousand years ago, it wasn't the epic duels you see on movies that last 10 minutes of people fighting and dodging blows and doing impressive maneuvers with swords and by the end of the battle are alive, after having killed 100 man alone if necessary.
Thats not how things are and without even knowing, Chivalry portraits medieval fights very well. Its a bunch of man clashing at each other, surrounded by people swinging their swords, where they swing their sword at a person and kill or stab the person behind them accidently without knowing, and miss on the person they were swinging at, and end up killing the person at the end of the swing. This is how things were. Things were decided with one or two swings.
When man swing their swords, blood is spilled, heads roll on the ground and arms fly through the air.
Chivalry excells in being a medieval fighting game! You will often see heads rolling on the ground and arms flying while hearing swords ripping through flesh and hear the sound of steel clashing and people screaming in agony or doing a battlecry.
Chivalry is a lot of fun to play and easy to get into but yet you can still learn a lot and become really good. You have to be aware of your sword and your body. Just because you are facing your target doesnt mean you will hit them or not hit someone that you are not seeing. And just because someone is swinging their sword at you, doesn't mean it will hit you if you dont deflect it. If you are aware enough of your body you can crouch and use the mouse to look at the floor, by doing this, you are reducing your characters height and the swing will be a total miss.
Chivalry is fun, has a great combat mechanic like no other game, community is alive, still gets updates and portraits medieval battles very well even though that wasn't the intention. Hope this review helped you in figuring out wether you should buy Chivalry or not!

Having spent a thousand hours on this game, you could actually wonder why I do put a negative review to this game.
The concept of the game is inheritly good; which is what made me and some friends play hundreds and hundreds of hours of this game. The early levels are the best ones, you feel threatened by everything, from dilos and raptors to rexes. You build your small base if you have the chance to find a nice spot. First time cave exploring is epic as well; loaded a ton of consumables, arrows and weapons on a raft and sailed for 15min to reach the cave only to get ambushed by a Croc when stepping out of the raft ... Epic fights, epics moments and epic fun.
- The very problem of the game is that Wildcards priorities are just not right. It's acceptable for an early beta game to have bad performances; it's okay for an early beta game to have server crashes and slow support. That's the phase the priorities are on finishing the game. But when you are near what you actually had in mind for the game, priorities MUST shift to stopping new content and stabilizing old content. This is a phase Wildcard never have commited enough to.
Pushing new content and early access PAYING DLC's instead of focusing on fixing bugs as old as 2 years and server crashes, rollback, duping was NOT the right decision. Artificially pumping the DLC's life length through stupid 4 days of no sleep milk-hunting again is another very bad decision.
- A second very problematic aspect of the game is the absence of proper support and gamemasters. PvE servers are full of people pillar spamming everywhere, leaving little to no space to buildfor newcomers. And there are no gamemasters to punish such behavior. In the end, if you don't pillar the same way, you're just gonna get pillarded all around your base, basically disabling you from expanding and playing the game. So everyone is just pillar spamming everything.
Wildcard support? I actually believe it's a legend. We've had tons of server issues, disappearing dinosaurs, offline deaths, stuck in textures ... Have we ever had an answer from Wildcard support ? Never and i kid you not, never.
- Official launch. Launching the game resulted in a BUG FREE GAME. Not because the game was actually bug free, because THEY DELETED THEIR BUG BACKLOG. Same thing goes about support tickets. If you had a ticket open at the release launch (which means if you ever had sent a ticket), Wildcard actually sent you a direct e-mail telling you all your tickets and bug reports were deleted, screw you basically.
- Transfering dinosaurs, survivors and gear from server to server with no delay at all was what killed completely the game. It was the worst idea ever. After that, every mega tribe of every server could offline raid you with their 50 lvl 400 Giga and 5000 C4/Rocket launchers.
- Dinosaurs are balanced like sh17 (read this with leetspeek). Some Vanilla dinosaurs basically are just tank and spank dinosaurs while other ones have stupidly powerful abilities. Why the hell does raptor, parasaur, rex and tons of other basic dinosaurs not have any special ability at all when you have stupid troodons killing everything on sight, flying Thylacoleo pinning you down from 500 feet high trees, Cnidaria perma stunning the biggest dinosaurs your have ever seen ...
Wildcard basically perfers pumping out new "Dinosaurs" (Bears, Bees, snails, fire and ice golems, ice and fire dragons didn't know this was Game of Thrones ?) rather that flattening the playing field and updating old epic dinosaurs like raptors and rexes.
- Servers are actually unplayable when over 15 people are connected at once. Try joining a 15-20 people server and enjoy the 500ms delays (although server stats tell you you have 30 ms ping), the rollbacks (up to 24h rollbacks when servers hardcrash), the disconnects in the middle of flying over the ocean/lava.
Not try plaing Hardcore. Try to not cry.
- People duping dinosaurs, gear, structures for months before anything was even attempted. This of course goes very well with transfering duped stuff from server to server to annihilate months of people's efforts to build bases.
- Some people were actually holding entire server hostage by perma ddosing them. Did Wildcard do something? They did as they did with all tickets ... Never answer.
- Launching the second paying DLC ONE DAY before official launch (you know, at the same time the bug backlog was wiped empty) was the nail in the coffin. Remember when i talked about wrong priorities ?
- Forgot to mention the game takes 10Giga of RAM and 100+ Giga of SSD/HDD Space. The smallest update the game has every done is probably 500 MB when they corrected a typo in a Dinosaur name.
- Game's price has tripled right before launch. You used to be able to buy this game for 15-20€. Now it's 60€ WITHOUT ANY DLC.
Tldr:
Concept of the game is good (++)
Everything else is bad (----): Too few servers, unstable serveurs with laggs, rollbacks and crashes. People ddosing entire servers for weeks with no Wildcard support. Very bad customer support and no in game support. Official launch and bug backlong wiped is a joke. People duping explosives and high end dinosaurs can invade any server of the game and wipe your base while you are offline. Lead designer is fan of Game of Thrones which is why this game has dragons spitting ice and fire in stead of actual proper dinosaurs. Paying DLC, same price for everyone even if you supported the game during whole Early access. Very poor optimization. Priced more expensive than AAA-game but indie-quality development

The premiere Medeival Combat game/simulation. All the depth of multiplayer battle arenas and all the sillyness of the dark ages. The counter-strike of melee. the TF2 of team objectives. It's a masterpiece.
On a more serious note, this game's learning curve is pretty steep. At first, you will likely do nothing but die and attempt to control your frustration. Experience is the only teacher for Chivalry, although the loading screens do actually offer tips that will improve your play (for once).
Is it worth it to buy Chivalry? Only if you have the time to put into it. A casual chivalry player will have a lot of fun but eventually become overwhelmed by the difficulty. Fortunately, there are many servers dedicated specifically to new players (listed as Official Low Rank servers) that will provide an excellent place to hone your skills and feel out the combat system. It is also worth mentioning that unlike other battle arena games, Chivalry is glorious amounts of fun without any friends to play with! For that reason alone I would say it's worth the price if you have the patience.
Cons: Although there are many official servers, often times during weekdays and work hours there are just a handful of servers filled and a few other players online. Servers usually don't provide flawless ping, but the game is such that a few ms delay won't matter as much as you think. One swing of your weapon, string of an arrow, etc takes a good second or two anyhow. Regardless, if you live on the east coast you will most likely have to avoid 1/3 of Chivalry's servers in order to avoid lag. Another thing: in Chivalry there are a good deal of weapons available to the four different classes BUT they must be unlocked by getting kills with a less complicated weapon. Usually there are three tiers of unlockable weapon (the first tier being default). This is a con if you don't like waiting ofc, but mostly its a con because your first several hours of chivalry will likely be without many kills. Unlike other unlocking systems (which are often just a way to trick the user into wasting money or time) Chivalry's system simply rewards you for practicing. By the time you leave the Low Rank servers you will find yourself having unlocked almost all the weapons anyhow, but it is still a notable con. Personally, I felt like a fool using the default weapons when i started playing and it seemed like other players had better weapons when they got me, but I learned later I was just bad.
This review has already been too long, but I'll mention one last thing; Chivalry is absurdly fun and atmospheric. Every level (I mean the standard game modes and maps since there is SO much opportunity for modding) is well themed and competitive. I've never head a player anywhere get frustrated by an abusable location or strategy. There are numerous voice commands (again similar to TF2) and every class spouts them out in classic medeival tongue. Classes each spawn with a certain voice that is likely to change each time you respawn. It sounds silly that i'm making a big deal about it but it's certainly what made the game enjoyable when I started and still entertains me immensley.
TL;DR If you love the medeival era or semi-competitive TF2/CSGO style combat this is for you. If you dislike a heavy learning curve and large time investments, it's probably not for you.

This review covers the Deadliest Warrior DLC:
Bottom Line - If bought on sale, this DLC can be quite fun, but glitches and lack of maps detract from making it a must buy.
Deadliest Warrior DLC for Chivalry pits dissimilar classes (Samurai, Ninja, Pirate, Spartan, Viking and Knight from MW) in a variety of modes (Free for All, Team DM, Last Team Standing, Duel, Hold the Banner, and CTF).  The classes are quite different in terms of speed. armor and weapons and requires the player to learn the advanatges/disadvantages for every class.
When played on a server with players with similar ping and skill, DW can be quite enjoyable.  The overall problem with the game is:
1.  Lack of servers/server with good ping/latency
2.  Lack of maps
3.  Lack of will/time/interest from the developer to fix the current maps or add new maps.
4.  Exploits from experienced players
It may seem that I've listed more negatives than positives for this game, but with over 700 hours invested into it for about $10 USD that's a value that cannot be beat.

Really liked this title.
First thoughts were that this game has a fairly unique system. Sort of something for everyone here. The game's system allows for someone who wants to play seriously to do so but also allows for someone who wants to just blow through as fast as possible to do just that. I really loved looking for clues, posing questions backed by evidence, and uncovering plots in cases, some of which are clever stylized recreations of actual cases from the time period.
Interesting story lines converge in a pretty well written overall story and feels pretty good when all is said and done. Play time is even better than most 3a titles anymore, at around 35 hours.
The game is set in 1947 L.A. and I loved the fact that when you got in a car you could hear radio brodacasts from stock footage from the time. The Jack Benny Show, old news broadcasts, and of course music from the 40's. The cast of characters is pretty massive and there are a lot of recogniseable faces and voices. Commercial actors, and T.V. and Movies actors alike, not just voices but whole guest apperances. pretty cool I thought. Also cool was the fact that vehicles are real vehicles, Hudson, Chevrolet, Ford, Packard etc.
You spend a lot of the game performing interviews to get along in cases and you have to pay attention to people's faces and voices to get an impression of truth or lies. The result is a really incredible looking facial animation set. It's like actually seeing people talk, no choppy dubbed looking animatronic movements. The only complaint in this subject is that the voice acting isn't always very good. gets a little campy here and there.
The game is gritty and covers a lot of situations. Marital problems, drug use, mental health, corruption, political standings etc.
Definately a Rockstar title, lots of shooting and language but I felt it fit pretty much every situation so it didn't detract from game play except for some of the street crimes ( optional side missions)
All in all I'd say get this and play it if you're looking for something cerebral and engaging. If you just want a run and gun though you're not going to like L.A Noire

General Synopsis: A clicking game that simply takes time to advance and has no real goal other than something to check up on in the background every now and then.
Difficulty: 0 (of 10)
Cost: Free (has extras you can pay for)
Good:
-No learning curve as long as you speak English.
-Something resembling a tech tree / strategy of sorts with the "Ancients" you can acquire over time.
-Very low resource hog, no matter how far along you get
-Runs in the background so you advance while ignoring it
Bad:
-Susceptible to the Cheat Engine program for modifications (good to ruin what satisfaction you COULD get or to test higher levels on your system)
-No real entertainment or excitement factor as you don't really have to /do/ anything
-If you Google it, you can find a cheat manipulator to REALLY make the game boring
-No end goal other than buying all the heroes and continuously leveling them and acquiring ancients/achievements
Results:
As something to have running in the background, just for something to do every now and then when you check up on it, the game isn't bad. It's also something good to keep a very young child entertained for a few minutes before they get bored once they use up all the gold/money and then find themselves with nothing to do. As a game meant to entertain, no good.  But for what its intended purpose/type of game it is, is, it's a good play.
Happy playing,

It’s funny to go back and read in light of L.A. Noire. In many ways, I think L.A. Noire, as a game, is exactly not game noir as Gaynor describes it. L.A. Noire took hundreds of people seven years to develop, and it ranks alongside such heavy hitters as Halo 3 and Metal Gear Solid 4 with the immensity of its budget. At the time of its release, it was one of the most expensive games ever made. The development team painstakingly recreated 1940s Los Angeles, complete with landmarks familiar to anyone who has paid a visit to the city, recorded many hours of dialogue, and developed their own cutting edge facial animation technology for use with every major character in the game. So is the end result good? Sure, with some reservations. I think having creative ambition is important to making a good AAA video game, and in that regard, I can’t fault L.A. Noire. This is an impressive feat of adventure game design, with a truly mechanics-focused dialogue system(I’m talking about the famous interrogations here), and very little “adventure game logic”. The voice acting tends to be pretty good, and it’s fun to see the faces of the actors in a very true-to-life way. You can even recognize them at a glance. But I burned out somewhere around two thirds of the way through the game and will probably never finish it. I think that this has to do with Gaynor’s description of what “game noir” would be, or rather the logical conclusion about what “game noir” wouldn’t be. L.A. Noire is bloated. I would gladly have finished the game if I knew I only had two or perhaps even three hours left to play(I was around 14 or 15 hours in), but as far as I could tell, I could have as many as ten. I felt like this was a game bogged down with too much pointless fluff. There are forty irrelevant side missions; I did several of them, and they seemed to largely consist of shooting, which is by far the game’s weakest type of gameplay. There are dozens of cars to collect, but no reason to collect them, and roughly nothing in the game’s themes to suggest that this is an interesting thing that the main character would actually be doing. There’s a large open world, but it’s a facade. The illusion falls apart as soon as you try to walk around in it, and realize that it’s sterile, built only so marketers could pompously brag about the game’s true reconstruction of Los Angeles. This is pure spectacle. So L.A. Noire is a game with too much. Too much empty space. Too many cases, which taken individually don’t tend to be all that interesting. Too many irrelevant and unmemorable characters. The veneer of film noir - fedoras, suits, and cover-ups - is a novelty, but I didn’t feel that it served a broader purpose. I thought while playing the game that even The Witcher ultimately told a better noir story. So I didn’t finish it, and I probably won’t finish it. I will continue to claim that I liked the game, however, and I think any interested parties should give it a shot. Just be ready for something a little flawed.

The epic Hero of this... tale? Is not a pre-made Japanese high-school Boy/Girl controling demons; not a princess possessed by a mighty Valkyrie; not a ex-prisoner destined to defeat dragons.
...no, you are neither one of these above.
The Epic Hero of this game is... you. You the guy/girl who plays this game - No character creation, no avatar, no classes - just you and your mouse and keyboard.
The story of Clicker Heroes is... well, the characater *description and the
will tell you more. You can also find out more about the story on the forums and in the wiki.
*I am not sure if I am the only one, but the character descriptions are gone for me. I had to go online to read the characters descriptions.
As far as the story goes... that's pretty much it - no cutscenes, no plot twists, no ancient evil, no sibling rivalry, no female companion to comfort you - just character descriptions.
You play the game with your left mouse-button and the 1-9-keys... and shortcut keys on your keyboards.
You kill monster and get their gold. When you have enough gold, you buy even more powerful heroes to help you kill quicker. et cetera, et cetera and et cetera.
But then... when you go past level 99, you get Hero Souls(HS)... what do you do with HS? well, that's simple, you buy ''Ancients''. Ancients are upgrades that will make things easier for you.
You also collect Ancient Souls(AS) for
AS makes things even more easier.
...apart from these things above, you also Click, Click, Click and Click.
Music is just one looping song. And most sounds are you hitting, killing and collecting monsters gold.
One sound-piece that sticks out is the special ''jingle'' when you click on the
tab.
...aaaaand that is it for Music and Sound.
I really don't know what else to say about Clicker Heroes. I have played Clicker heroes since 2015(since ver. 0.20). I even payed 9€ to Clicker Heroes just so I could get Steam Trading Cards.
I am addicted to Clicker Heroes... and I hate myself for it :). But... man, I need more HS and AS and I don't know why.

The success of the investigative action, the player will depend on how will be fully disclosed to the picture of the incident.
In addition to the story missions, players can receive calls on the police radio. In the game these tasks are called street crimes (eng. Street Crimes). Players can walk, and on different machines, which are opened along with the main character in the service. Besides the machines, the player is available for ten costumes for the character (4 of them are DLC). Some suits have special properties, such as increase of protection from damage or increase accuracy when firing.
Unlike other games Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto, players are prohibited from unrest and kill citizens, since the main character of the game is the detective police.
IN THE «L.A. Noire» the emphasis is not on the creation of an open world, as it was in previous games «Rockstar» (in particular, Red Dead Redemption of series Grand Theft Auto), but quality of story line. According to the developers, their project must erase the existing border between games and movies». The main hero - patrol officer Cole Phelps, who, thanks to the diligence and seriousness of attitude is gradually moving up the career ladder. Translation into the new Department each time accompanied by «adaptation» to the new companion, which can not always find understanding. In some investigations Phelps will have to face not only with the criminal world of Los Angeles, and former colleagues, with whom he fought in the Second world war. Even though it has considerable flaws, I really enjoyed this gme and respect it for it's grand ambition.  This is a sprawling narrative set across at least 25 hours of gameplay, and it has all the classic hallmarks of film noir detective movies.  Half LA Confidential, half Gangster Squad, the game does suffer from a bit of schizophrenia when it comes to gameplay - some of the time it's a sedate investigaiton simulator, other times its all about tense interrogations, and then sometimes you're shooting up half of LA like your playing Mafia.
The facial motion capture technology is very impressive, but unfortunately it's mostly wasted on poorly done interrogation scenes. Essentially LA Confidential: The Video Game. The similarities between the two are remarkable, although I'm guessing most of the inspiration originates from the books the movie was based on. LA Noire is not without its problems, but if you approach it thinking it's more like an interactive movie than a video game, you'll probably enjoy it. It just oozes atmosphere and setting. The acting is really good, and due to the incredible facial animations it's not just voice acting that you're watching.  You'll probably recognize various actors from other roles they've played (mostly on TV). It's really like nothing else I've experienced in a video games.
The problem is the gameplay. There's a few parts to it: finding clues, questioning/interrogating witnesses and suspects, and fighting/driving. Finding clues isn't all that bad, although it can get kind of tedious. Questioning people is the fun part, as you have to pay attention to character's facial expressions (that originate from the actual actor that played the part). The combat, however, is pretty bad. It's clunky, shallow, and repetitive. Fortunately, it's not a major part of the game, so it's bearable.
Overall, if you want to enjoy gritty, noire detective stuff, this game is for you.

So i have been playing this game for a while now and it just recently took over as my number 1 most played game at 440 hours played. When i first got the game i thought it was just a simple clicker game like one of the Steam Summer Sale Minigames they had i think in 2015.
Turns out there is sooo much more depth to it than just clicking...
In a nutshell, you can only go so far before you need to ascend (start over losing all hero upgrades and skills while keeping Gilds, Ancients and Hero Souls). At that point you ascend over and over levelling up your Ancients as you go to increase your DPS and Hero Soul gain. Eventually you can then also Transcend which is similar to Ascending but instead you lose literally everything and start over completely but gain Ancient Souls which can be used to increase DPS and Hero Soul gain and you will never lose those bonuses.
Its a never ending cycle of ascend, transcend, ascend, transcend and it honestly is incredibly addictive. Its very easy to leave playing in the background while you do other things too. All in all, its a free to play game with real money purchases that are not necessary since you earn rubies in the game without paying anything and i very highly recommend the game to anybody.

I typically loathe shooters and multiplayers, but Warframe's an exception. It's one of those shooters where you can use at least limited tactics to get the upper hand, or to survive really bad odds. There's a ton of warframes, weapons, mods, and gear that cater to all sorts of playstyles - snipe, tank, go glass cannon, play support, or be an all rounder whenever you want.
It's heavy on loot farming, but there's enough of a variety of settings, enemies, missions, events, and warframes to keep things fresh.
You can solo quite a lot of it if you want and only team up with friends or randoms when you run into something particularly difficult or to take on special foes designed for large teams. Like any multiplayer, you're bound to run into jackasses every now and then even though it's Co-Op, but so far all of my interactions have been really positive.
Warframe really isn't a p2p, or p2w. You can collect, research, and build what you need to succeed without spending a single penny. There are a few things you need Platinum for like slots, and certain customizations, but play enough and you're bound to come across something that someone else is willing to buy. There are already a bunch of great guides on how to earn Platinum instead of paying for it.
The graphics and voice acting are good, and the devs are always updating the game and designing new elements and content. Yet, it's still quite playable on my crummy laptop.
My only concern with Warframe is how difficult it can be to put down. It's one of those games that really soaks up your time if you're not careful.

L.A Noire delivers an exceptional story focusing on the exploits of a WWII officer turned detective in post-WWII L.A. The game efficiently blends story within story (past and present), via chapters that seamlessly blend together, efficiently creating a believable narration of one mans journey though a troubled time, and a troubled country. The game boasts amazing facial animation techniques, thus creating a greater range of viable facial contortions for the actors to express. The authenticity of the time is expressed in great detail as shown with the vehicle designs, the setting of the city, the music, and the people. The game boasts an extremely interactive environment in the form of interrogations, crime solving, clue searching (all being core aspects of gameplay), and in a most realistic way. Vehicular chases of any sort are exhilarating and finely executed (as well as the pedestrian chases), although general movement is a tad clunky, and unfortunately the combat mechanics are relatively mediocre, if fluent and stable. In conclusion: L.A Noire is well worth your time and your money, and is a must have for any fan of the mystery/thriller genre.

TL;DR at bottom
L.A. Noire is a cinematic, cut-scene-tastic game that is worth your money and time. Its not really a "fun" game, but its an entertaining experience that I wish more games would offer.
When most gamers say a story is good, they allude to the story that gives them purprose for their gameplay. In other words, the story is pushed onto the gameplay. This isn't a bad thing, it is just how most game are based off of. However, L.A. Noire does something remarkably different. The gameplay is pushed onto the story. The game is more about you enjoying a story instead of you playing a game.
This doesn't mean you're just sitting and watching videos. You have your good deal of driving, chasing, and shooting to take part of, but it honestly feels a bit clunky. But that's a good thing for this game. This is not GTA where you find your first assault rifle and go to town on a police force, or finding that really exotic Inferno. Sure, you still have your guns and cars, but they're more for atmosphere. You gun down enemies because you have to, not because you're inclined to. Finding cool cars and rare items is interesting to some, but not a thrilling experience honestly. Other little minigames (normally found in "Street Crimes") are relatively quick and unsatisfactory for the "game" aspect of this.
With those small game mechanics, your truly interactive part comes in with finding clues on the ground and using that information during interviews to gather information. You become the investigator (Cole Phelps), and you piece the parts together. You decide which places to visit first, and sometimes visiting certain locations first will end the case more quickly with and without any ill effect. You may have "intuition" points to you for your own benefit, but personal intuition is also useful when playing the game.
These game mechanics do well to keep you from becoming bored, but the interesting and entertaining aspect truly comes from deciphering the mysteries and uncovering the story. Certainly, there are some flaws. Cole Phelps is not necessarly a budding rose of a character, but it works. Some story ties seem to be lightly knitted together. But overall, the story is interesting, and you want to keep finding out more. You find out more about the backstory behind current events in the game, and it eventually ties together relatively well. I really did feel a sort of appreciation for the main characters at the end, and not many movies or games have been able to do that for me.
Also, as a small note, the setting of late 40's L.A. was remarkable and had me sold. Not just the environment, but the extensive historical knowledge of going-ons during the late 40's really had me immersed. Its not just things like "Oh, I'm sure glad the war is over!", but rather, for example, the more detailed mentioning of era-specific events, like HUAC hunting for "reds". If you're considering buying this game for someone who is a history buff, just stop reading the review right now and go buy the game.
Anyways, this is definitely not a kids game. Not because of the "Rated M" content, but because it takes an older audience to really appreciate the story, the history, and the different pace of the game. It certainly isn't perfect, but in my mind, it is one of my favorite games. Its not something that I would take off the shelf and waste 3 hours on a Friday night for, but it is something to be enjoyed, and thought about. I would like to see more games like this on the market, an actual story-driven game, and not a game with a neat story. BUt for now, L.A. Noire has a special place in my heart, and it should in your heart too.
TL;DR: Entertaining for an older audience and worth your time. Not a source of immense fun, but rather a source of interesting story and mind tingling details. Worth a buy at 20 at least.

I'm going to oversimplify the hell out of this game in this review because if I'm honest I never fully understood the game. I always had friends with thousands of hours walking me through things. This game is the ultimate grind fest. Now, I know that instantly sounds like a negative, but I'm always looking for games that have a large grind aspect to them and still stay fun because those games can hold your interest for a long time with the promise of infinite progression. So, what do I mean when I say Warframe is a grind fest? Well almost every time you choose a mission you're choosing it to get a specific loot drop. This means that you may end up playing the same mission or set of missions time after time. The reason I still had fun with the game while having to grind the same missions for weeks on end was that the gameplay is very fast paced and satisfying. If compare this to other games that have a similar grinding element, mostly RPGMMOs, those games will often have missions like "Travel from point A to point B" while Warframe keeps you constantly on the move and/or fighting enemies. The combat is simplistic, but because of the movement system and ability design it is highly satisfying.
TLDR: The game has a lot of grinding mechanics, but is supported by fun and satisfying combat. It's free, so check it out.

I purchased L.A. Noire back when Steam had one of their famous sales, and sat down to make it a point to play through it and beat it -- start to finish.
L.A. Noire is a very linear game, despite the open-world concept it got from it's thick Rockstar roots.  You play the role of Cole Phelps, an ex-war hero gone cop in L.A.  The story telling is fun and the crime scene investigation, questioning, and combat can be engaging and exciting...for a while.  That's when the player realizes:  Is that all L.A. Noire has to offer?
If you're into good noire style crime films, or old crime TV shows (or maybe even some newer ones, like CSI etc) you might still get a kick out of the game to play through the story for what it's worth:  A decent ex-war hero gone cop gone bad gone weird.
As far as the open world goes, the game tries to entice you in between cases to do things like fight "street crime" (which boosts your exp which you can use to solve crimes easier) or to go find hidden cars and vehicles.  Finally, it invites you to drive around L.A. looking at various landmarks.  The open world gets old fast, and as far as I can tell there are very little penalties for "losing your mind" and getting behind the wheel of a big rig and plowing through hundreds of people. The game does warn you about demerits, but we've already saved our game, right? ;)
All in all, L.A. Noire is a decent game, not the best that Rockstar put out, but still decent enough if you can get it on the cheap and find the time to stomach case after case of the same type of investigating, questioning, and interogation.

L.A. Noire is ultimate proof that a good concept does not make a good game. On the surface it seems like a breath of fresh air in the rapidly stagnating AAA game. Just a warning this review contains spoilers just so you can understand how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the premise of this game is
This game is basically jerk simulator 1946 where you play as Cole Phelps ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in chief "solving" LA's heinous crimes by wrongly jailing innocents and screaming at people. Each story case involves a search for clues followed by interrogations and occasionally the awful action sequences straight out of Grand Theft Auto 4 as well. There is little decision by you as to how the investigation will go as everything is on rails since it is, after all, a AAA title. Wouldn't want casuals to get confused or anything! You cannot even revisit crime scenes for crying out loud.
Now even if a game's streamlined it can be fun even if it's dumb fun, but this game manages to fail at that too! Clue hunting, the first part of investigations is flabbergastingly easy, with an intuition system that flat out reveals all the clues in a scene. Or, if you choose not to use it, it becomes greyed out with you find every relevant clue on the scene. Further the controller vibrates everytime you stumble across one. Talk about easy mode! But it's better than the other half.
The interrogation part is definitely the most interesting and unique part of the game... and also undeniably the WORST part of the game. It's quite obvious Rockstar worked very hard to get real, emotional faces on everyone while you're interviewing, but even with that the interrogations are mindblowingly illogical... you say one thing, they answer, you have to decide if it's true, whether you 'doubt its authenticity' or it's a flat out lie you have contradicting evidence to. There are so many horrible questions here it's unbelievable and it's made even worse by the fact that you can only ask once (totally realistic right). It's really pretty easy to tell if they're telling the truth or lying, however the stupid choices don't always necessarily mean what they say, and change from damn question to question. Truth/Doubt many times mean the EXACT same thing depending on the question: the witness is being honest but is leaving out details. Unfortunately you have NO way of telling which questions this is the case or not! And lie is plagued with a couple of cases where seemingly unrelated clues call the person out even though they don't prove jack. A great example of this is an empty film canister with someone else's name on it telling the player that the person was lying about the whereabouts of a completely different person than was on the canister. Further, if you care about your score (I'm not sure why the cases are even scored in the first place!!!!) if you answer a question incorrectly you can kiss goodbye to five stars on a case, and the only way to redo it is to end process on your game since hitting quit will still count the question wrong! Combined with only being able to ask once, Rockstar's message is clear. They did everything in their power to encourage you to use a guide to do the interrogations and I highly recommend doing so if you actually play it. HORRIBLE design.
It gets even better though. Oh yes. It seems clear that the way it was designed anything a witness says after answering a question correctly is mostly truth and that they won't try to lie again. So then you get to the Homicide desk cases and this fact still remains true. Except... it doesn't seem like the people you are jailing are doing it. Surprise! It's because they're not. And if you are actually intelligent enough to pick up on this not really subtle at all plot twist you have to finger them anyway. The best part is even when there's two of them and it's neither of them there's still a 'right' answer, something I was unfortunate enough to discover. This game just blows my mind at its stupidity...

This game man.  There is so much to like and it has come so far.  But speaking as someone who has gone to school for this industry, the devs of this game are doing EVERYTHING they can to screw you over.  They are some of themost Money hungry and incompetant devs ive ever personally watched.
They have a bug riddled game and they refuse to slow down on the new content and actually repair and cement their mechanical base.  They release dinosaur after dinosaur... with many that serve no or niche purpose and many more that are just basically power creep personified, again, never taking the time to actually iron out the finer points of balance and bug fix.  To top it all off, they declaire the game "Released" ... jack up the price almost double... and again... NOT FINISHED!  Still bug riddled and problematic.
Thats the problem at least with this group of Devs.  They got so used to being excused for their poor choices and game problems because it was in early access.   But now its been RELEASED,  and nobody did that to them but themselves.  So now the patience and understanding is gone and people expect a final copy grade game without the plethora of very game disrupting bugs and the devs dont get that.  They want to just keep putting out PAID content while not giving us what weve already paid for... a FINISHED game.
Now the funny thing is... I would have just swallowed down my opinions and shrugged.  I love this game... and I still retain hope that it might get better... not alot of hope these days.. .but a little.  I had/have every intention of even buying their next paid DLC even tho I hate myself for it.  I cant help but WANT these jerks to do better... and if that means I have to shell out ANOTHER 20 dollars for this "finished game" then so be it... but heres where I really get angry....
DELAYED!  Hyping this thing for weeks now, getting everyone excited and they wait until basically the last minute to tell their player base... sorry, but as you probly guessed ahead of time, we dont know how to keep a deadline... because we are not great at this.  We dont know how to keep a promise, or do our due dillegence before giving out a deadline.  Its par for the course, nothing weve ever promised or said has been entirely true or delivered within the deadline WE SET FOR OURSELVES!
In short... everything about this company screams incompetance.  I hate that I have to give them money to keep trying to get the game I was originally promised.  I have faithfully played this game for over 500 hours and bought all of the dlc they have put out and quietly let them keep lying to me long enough.  This is exactly what kind of Dev the early access system breeds.  The kind that cant finish anything, cant meet a deadline, and cant be bothered to hide its money grubbing true nature.

I do not recommend purchasing this game or any of its content unless you enjoy playing a partially finished game that will constantly try to take your money and give you the bare minimum.
