Okay, after coming around 1000 hours of gameplay time, I'll write this. So!
I love this game, man.
Seriously.
9999/10
But I'll keep this as relatively unbiased as possible.
This is a hard game. A really hard game. You will die over and over and over, because starting out, you don't know the mechanics very well. "But I played the tut-!" No. You have to practice a looooooot, which is what turns away many potential players. The learning curve isn't a curve. It's just a giant tower you have to climb by piling up the bodies of you and your enemies, and it -will- take time. But then the game starts to shine.
This is a game of skill.
"But Deytal, doesn't ever-" Noooo. I hate to bring the age-old comparison of Call of Duty, but whatever. You get shot in the back in CoD, you're done 95% of the time. In Chivalry, if someone gets the drop on you, you've got a very decent chance of coming around and smashing them. Sure, you'll be at a disadvantage, but you aren't just going to outright -die-. Unless you're an archer. Then, RIP you scumbag.
With plenty of variety in the classes, you can really choose how you want to play by what you enjoy most. Like incredibly fast, twitchy swordplay? Man-at-Arms.
Want a really big stick or sword and just cleave everything in sight? Vanguard!
Feel like tanking hits and relying almost exclusively on your weapon skill rather than mobility? Knight!
Feel like dying a lot? Archer.
But onto my opinion of actual game mechanics. You've likely read other reviews, explaining the use of the main three attacks: Slash, Stab, and Overhead. They do exactly as they say. However, you are able to speed up or slow down your attacks by moving your mouse, even letting you go around the side of a person if they aren't wary. There is the feint (faking an attack), which is insanely controversial, but it has uses in attacking and defense. (I personally don't use it offensively, due to the nature of blocking in this game). Damage is determined by where you hit them, with what attack, and with what weapon. -When- you hit them has no effect. In the DLC, Deadliest Warrior, timing matters. In the base game, it does not. This makes for some odd scenes, with a person swinging a sword as fast as a snail, then slicing off someone's head. This is a negative in terms of realism, but in terms of game mechanics, it adds HUGE depth to your timed blocking and attacking.
Okay, so I'll give a quick rundown of Pros and Cons.
If I had to give it a grade, I'd go with 80/100. Worth getting if you're into swordplay and the like, but it doesn't take long for you to have done everything there is to do. However, the skill ceiling pretty much never ends. There is always someone better than you, and someone worse. Besides, making a guy's head explode with your fist is always satisfying.

Warframe is a beautiful, fun game, based on grinding. It seems more grindy than it actually is, but the ultimate problem is that you are left with repeating what you've did for, say, 20 hours, again and again, until you are satisfied. The best advice I can give to new players is to not worry and enjoy, taking their time. The story is actually great, and the setting is pretty interesting. The gameplay is monotonous, but it it was almost never unfun, save for instances in which you had to repeat a run multiple times to get a particular part, that simply refused to drop. But oh well! There are numerous issues with this game, that need urgent fixes and those have stayed for a long time. The game is effectively still in beta, but updates are presented often and new content is added frequently to give completionists more things to do. I personally preffered just exploring. Overall, I deffinetely recomend Warframe. It is worth your time, but not all of it - this is the only negative I really have to give. Without even noticing, I had racked up 200 hours of this (during exams no less) and I expected something in the end. I expected an end! But the grind never, ever ends. And I was exhausted in looking for new things to do in the game, because it was extremely dissapointing to put this time into the game and to have only cool looking frames to show. I wasn't even that powerful. So my advice - don't worry, don't rush, beat the story and enjoy your time - this way it will be fun. Otherwise you will tire from the grind and just bash this game. Depends on the type of person you are. But if you like endless grinding... Oh, boy, is Warframe the pill you need. In either case, I recommend - just keep an eye on those hours. And feed your pet, before it dies on it's own because you didn't log in for a day.

Really incredible. The game play itself isn't anything spectacular, but the world that Rockstar has created in 1947 Los Angeles is really something to experience.

An interesting side note: Rockstar used over 180,000 aerial photographs in order to more accurately reproduce that noire feeling of 1940s Los Angeles. Actual radio broadcasts, commercials, and music (The Bickersons, The Jack Benny Program, Louis Armstrong, Ella Fitzgerald) were also used to further immerse the player.
A fun game, but if you're at all into 40s Americana it's worth buying just to cruise down Holywood Blvd in one of the 95 vintage cars listening to Bing Crosby.

This game is as hardcore of a game you're ever going to find so if you're reading reviews about people getting their bases raided or getting locked up as a prisoner for hours on end, then it's all true but they're the ones that don't have the intelligence to survive and/or they're just sore losers. YES, you are going to die and there will be times when it's smarter to die purposely just to keep being productive. The majority and I mean like 95% of the people that complain about getting knocked out and prisoned in a cage or their bases being raided out the first night they built it are people that are literally just doing what they see everyone else doing and that's building a base out on the beach where you spawn in at, somewhere where everybody can see it and basically saying hello! come raid me I'm right here!
Don't do that.
That's stupid.
If you're going to pick a PVP server to play on, then you're going to have to PVP. That's all there is to it. PVP stands for Player Vs. Player. If you're just starting out with the game, join a PVE server for a while and survive on your own against the wild dinosaurs and the heat/cold weather. You can also play this game one-player mode or even host your own server.
Once you do join a PvP server, here are the basics. 1.) Build hidden. 2.) Build small. 3.) Build near resources. 4.) HIDE your good loot. And if you really want to get technical, you don't even have to build a base!
1.) Hidden: Find a location in the thickest of trees and rocks. Look straight up in the air into the trees and if you don't see sky, then you're good. Players that fly over your base on birds will see your base through the trees and find your base. DONT DESTROY THE TREES AROUND YOUR BASE. If you need wood, then travel a little further away from your base  to knock trees down because the trees near your base will not re-grow back. I usually run away about 5-8 seconds from my base to get wood. If I have a really big rock next to my base blocking vision, I don't destroy it either. HIDDEN. STAY HIDDEN! DO NOT burn at night time! When it's getting dark out, then don't run a campfire or a forge or anything that gives off light. They can spot your base a mile away if you do!
2.) Small: I don't build any bigger than 3x3 when I'm solo and that's stretching it. There's no point in taming alot of dinos if you're a solo player also. You're just wasting your time and giving others something to kill when you're not online. Iguanadons are a really good choice of an easy dino to tame for a solo player starting out. They're fast, never run out of stamina and carry a decent amount of weight.
3.) Near Resources: Build multiple bases across the map. This depends on whatever map you're playing on of course. If you're building small, then the bases are going to be easy and fast to build.
4.) HIDE YOUR LOOT: Who cares if someone breaks into your house when you're offline if they didn't get your loot? Repair the door and/or whatever they destroyed and move on with your life! YES, you can hide your loot. There are alot of ways to hide your loot. You can put your stuff in a wooden box hidden in a bush under water. There are alot of ways to do it, just Youtube it.
5.) NO BASE: You don't even have to have a base if really don't want it. You can literally make yourself a wooden club and just go smack people on the beach until they pass out and take their loot.
Now, as far as getting into a tribe goes.. that' just depends on the tribe. Some tribes only recruit from applications being sent on websites because it's not smart to recruit players from the same server most of the time. DON'T TALK♥♥♥♥♥♥IN GLOBAL CHAT. A tribe will NOT recruit you if you bad mouth people in global chat because if they did, you would just be a lability to their tribe. They don't want trouble anymore than you do. They have more to lose than you!
As far as this game's quality goes, yes you will find a minor bug in the game here and there but it's nothing major. This game has came a long way and that's another reason why the ratings on steam are as low as it is. Don't pick a server that has a lot of players on it. It will be laggy. For some reason, the developers think that the game can handle as many people as it does. They're actually beta testing servers that will hold even more players than what it does now. I also would not suggest building a base on a raft either. There is a very annoying jittery feel when you walk across rafts that comes and goes.

L.A. Noire, by Rockstar and Team Bondi, is, without a doubt, a unique experience. The advanced facial technology which is by far the game's most famous feature really is incredible and for that alone everyone should try it out because there's nothing like it.
It's a slow-paced, methodical game. There are action sequences but these are an exception, not the rule, to this game. This game's main strength lies in its investigation and interrogation sequences, coupled with excellent acting and good plot. Note that I'm typing "acting" and not "voice acting". The technology in this game has finally reached the point where I can say that every character in this game is acting, and not just lending their voice to the game.
You can totally mess up in your cases, by the way. Like completely. But even if this happens to you, the main storyline will still keep progressing, albeit in dynamic and different ways. Your partners, peers, and superiors will comment on how you couldn't get that one case done, or if you did, praising you on your foresight. I found this really neat and a lot more investigation games should go for this dynamic direction as well instead of keeping you stuck until you find the perfect solution. (I'm looking at you, Phoenix Wright, and some point and click adventures as well)
As the title implies, it perfectly evokes that feeling of a 40's Los Angeles in a dark, depressing, noir setting. The vehicles, buildings, city, music, up to the radio commercials themselves are spot on. There is freeroam as you'd expect to find in your average GTA, and street crimes which are always action oriented as fun sidequests. The story of LAPD detective Cole Phelps is very interesting and involved, and while this game is about solving crimes, it's also about telling the story of this man, who isn't perfect, has its ups and downs, and is just amazing to go through. Fantastic protagonist.
I will say though that the ending felt kind of rushed, and there were a few loose ends. Closure where it was mainly needed was given though, so don't worry, this game didn't pull a Mass Effect 3.
More games like L.A. Noire need to exist. Even though I've had a LOT of cases to solve, I'm still yearning for more, and I'll definitely replay this after a few years at the very least so my memories won't be as clear and I can fumble about again, because it actually makes it enjoyable and realistic for me, that even the star detective such as Cole could get fooled and get it all wrong once or twice.
It's not all rainbows and sunshine though! This game is a bad PC port. Rockstar are known for being subpar when it comes to the PC, and L.A. Noire is no exception. I've had to open up a bunch of launch commands, even get a .dll file to get my game into a playable state. It doesn't help that its capped at 30 FPS either, because according to Team Bondi, the facial animations could get wonky were you to go any higher than that. 60 FPS fixes were applied and this wasn't seen though, so it's highly debatable.
If you can get this on the PS3 or Xbox 360, then do so as you won't have to deal with these issues. If you can't though, at least try to give it a go anyway because like I said, this is an awesome game if it happens to like your PC and everyone should play it. I'm all for a sequel or a game set in the same style as this one!

This game is a ton of fun. It doesnt necessarily look the best (Unreal 3 engine I believe), but it more than makes up for it with solid gameplay, ballsy attitude, and well populated servers (32 player matches). It's multi player only, although you can set up private servers and populate with bots if you prefer. Matches are your typical Deathmatch, Objectives (which are basically one team defending and the other attacking with objectives as you go along such as burning down or crashing gates, smashing towers, and so on on route to eventually trying to kill the King), Free For All (everybody vs everybody), etc..., but they are all quite fun. I've played through four different maps so far. I'm not sure how many more there are, but it's a little consequence. The gameplay is more important than the locations with this game.
The learning curve can be steep depending on the type of warrior you select as well as their loadout, (which is initially limited, but unlocks more stuff as you keep getting experience), but it is also pretty easy to get into the flow of the game. You WILL die a lot, and often in hilarious ways, such as getting set on fire just before having your head and an arm hacked off. You can also shout battlecries to your hearts content, lol.
You do get penalized for hitting your own teammates, which takes the form of longer respawn times, and if you are a repeat offender, everybody on your team gets to vote on whether or not to kick you. You can also switch sides if you like, mid game, and in fact, the game will sometimes rebalance and shift you automatically to even out the teams.  Speaking of respawns, while you are waiting, you basically are the ghost of your now dead warrior and can float around and/or above the battlefields checking out the battles while you wait.
All told, the game is a ton of fun to play, and I think it is pretty hilarious as well, with the graphic deaths, copious battle cries, and people running around like madmen.
Initially, I thought this was about 8/10, but the more I play, the more I lean closer to a full 10/10.

The multiplatform free-to-play game is an action shooter with some of the trappings of an MMO. It launched in 2013 and is available now on PC, PS4 and Xbox One, where it is regularly updated. As a recently-awoken space ninja called a Tenno, your job is to fly around the solar system doing space ninja stuff like assassinations, spying on people, stealing information, and performing sabotage. Each mission location and type remains the same, but the missions themselves are somewhat randomized. The game relies on a random tile system to keep things fresh. Your base of operations–and your main menu–is your ship.
When you log in, you’re sitting in front of your command console, which lets you select where you want to go in the solar system. To your right is the store. To your left is the codex. Behind you, deeper in the ship, are other stations, like the foundry that lets you build weapons or the armory that allows you to outfit and modify your frames.
Ah, right, frames. The eponymous warframes operate like character classes, except instead of being locked into one class per character, you can swap frames at will, with each frame having four unique powers. For one mission, you might feel like running the supportive frame Trinity, who can mass heal the entire team or provide energy vampire abilities to ensure quick regeneration. On the next mission, you might want to play as Ember, whose incredible World on Fire ability burns every enemy within a massive radius.
You obtain warframes by defeating bosses and getting their parts or by completing some of the game’s great quests. Warframes are not just some cool gimmick or branding idea, but a cool design choice. Two good ideas make them great: first, they’re all overpowered, and second, you have to hunt them down.
Warframe doesn’t care about balance. You’re a badass space ninja, after all! Rather than pushing players through a lengthy and meaningless grind, Warframe provides players tons of awesome and incredibly destructive powers. I love running Frost, a frame that launches a massive blast of ice, freezing everything around it, killing most low-level enemies. Playing like Frost feels like running around as a tactical nuke. The sheer destructive power being wielded is awe-inspiring, but that’s true of every frame. Valkyr’s power is invulnerability. It comes at the expense of ranged weapons, but that’s fine, because as a space ninja, your swords are just as cool, if not cooler, than your guns.
What’s great about being overpowered is that, since everyone is overpowered, no one is. The power you wield makes you feel like you’re actually a badass space ninja, because you’re killing lots of enemies quickly and efficiently. Other sci-fi games, like Mass Effect 2, force you into cover through a lack of health and a focus on small groups of enemies. There’s no sense of lethality or badassery going on when your character feels like they’re made of soggy toilet paper while enemies can last through an entire magazine of gunfire. Warframe understands this, so every frame feels fun to play, because every frame has powerful, over-the-top capabilities.

Though arguably a less serious and sincere, (though humorous) take on first-person historical combat, Chivalry is nonetheless an entertaining and somewhat addictive first person melee combat game, which does a decent job at standing it's own among a great variety of similar titles. In my view it is fairly comical, and really pushes to sell itself on an exaggerated take on medieval brutality on the battlefield, but it ultimately enjoyable if even in a tongue-in-cheek fashion.
Just play the tutorial (see how quickly you grit your teeth) or listen to some of the voice-overs to see where I think the game begins it's play on humor. Though I personally prefer an intuitive control scheme as featured in games like Warband, I find this is an enjoyable foray into the first-person competitive stylization of medieval combat.
The issues I have with it are somewhat minor. Projectiles seem to travel slowly and leave glaring streaks which arc behind them, presumably so the player can see where they're going similar in some respect to modern tracer rounds. The second issue is the clunkyness of some of the animations, and the very, very awkward running and moving animations. Take your character to third person, grab a shield, bear it up front, and crouch-walk forward to get a taste of what I mean.
Anyway, in conclusion. Enjoyable, silly and funny. I exploded a man's head with a sling bullet somehow.  I did the same with a mace. That's chivalry for you.

You can't love this game without hating it at the same time. I've played it a lot and will probably keep playing it for a while to come, but I won't recommend it to anyone .
The pro's and cons:
+ A survival game with 100+ dino's you can tame, breed and ride! What more do you want?
+ Endless customization options and mod support for running a single player game or a private server.
+ An active modding community that provides a steady stream of nice additions.
- The PVP mechanics are ruthless and heavily in favor of large, established player tribes. You can't beat those tribes so you have to join them. But then you don't have any enemies anymore, making the whole point of PVP rather useless.
- Shabby optimization, leading to regular performance issues.
- Bugs. Bugs everywhere. Bugs as far as the eye can see.
- A dev team that prefers introducing new content over fixing existing content, resulting in even more bugs.
- Dramatically poor communication from the devs towards the community. The official support forums are largely ignored. Game-breaking issues can exist for months without receiving any attention.
This game could be awesome if the dev team would spend about a year fixing what they have built so far. But right now, the game and community are in danger of collapsing in on itself due to the amount of bugs and performance issues becoming unbearable.

Every cop you encounter is intentionally incompitent, and you eventually get to shoot them all when your space marine firebat friend takes to the caves to fight Charlie. Origami plays a major role in the game, making it the only game to involve folding paper into little swans important.
Because it's California, drugs,♥♥♥♥♥♥on the railroad and arson by proxy cases usually lead to pedophillia and rifle stockpiles.
Overall, a solid and unforgettable game, mostly because the villian doesn't do anything evil and never kills anyone.

Pros :  Dinos. Dinosaurs make this game the bees ♥♥♥♥ing knees. Taming a giant rex and riding him around to just lay waste to everything around you fills you with a feeling I didn't know I had until I got my♥♥♥♥♥♥sucked.

Base-Building. Building your first base is trivial. You'll feel sort of off at first, but after getting into it, you swing your hips and voila~ your base is done. Gorgeous. Looks amazing, inside and out, and you're completely satisfied.

Progression. Progressing is by far one of the smoothest rides I've ever had, and I've been lubed and anally protruded before so I know what of which I speak. Bosses need to be beaten with dinos that have far surpassed the norm. Rexes need to be bred, and mutated, and painted nice colors. It's a joy-ride, and the only way to go is up.

Variety. All the variations of dinosaurs is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ic. You wanna go fly around? Sure. Wyvern, Bird, Gryphon, pterandon, bigger bird, small hover bird? You pick. Wanna kill things? Do it. Pick a dino. Have fun, easily burn 20 minutes mindlessly killing dinos.
I have to poo, so we'll do the cons now.
CONS :

Dinos. It happened again. Your bird got stuck (for whatever reason) in something somewhere and now it's dead. You, being literally powerless to certain dinos are now also dead. Fine. Let's go find where I dropped my stuff. It's gone.
To sum this up for new players: Sometimes your dinos get stuck in things and then they will most certainly die. Fun. Not to mention the ever buggy and glitchy world you play in. Can't stress this enough. I've played since alpha, and it's really never gotten better. Sure, some bugs are fixed. But the majority are the same. Can't tell you how many times I've gotten stuck in the map, or killed something for it also to get lost underground. Fun fun fun. Tons of fun. This game is buggy.

Base-building. Alrighty, so.. Earlier I had said your base was beautiful? It is, but it no longer exist because all your valuables aren't squished into a tiny room. Yeah, unless you're on PVE, you're literally never safe. Never. Not to mention that even if you surround your entire base in nothing but turrets. You're never safe. You can very Easily drop a random♥♥♥♥♥dino with C4 on it, around some players turrets, and if it has a good saddle it will take about 5-6 damage per shot. Progression. Progressing is a ton of fun. Unless you play on unoffical, progressing will take quite some time.. You have to watch your egg. All day. Better hope nobody steals it. Maybe you'll make headway? Not until about 400-500 hours of gameplay, which is also a variable considering if you're wiped.
Variety. Ooh! Whoa! I can take a total of three relevant dinos into boss arenas? huh.. Okay. So, everything that isn't a Giant tanky rex, a healing pig? As for everything else? PVP is simplified to this. This is one of the best free to play games ever. There is a wide variety of weapons; from guns to swords, to sonic weapons and rocket launchers, and tons of different fighting stances for each and every melee weapon type ( Which I find the most fun). As well as tons of different warframes (which are basically different classes with their own unique abilities and stats) and pets. There are also tons of modifications that you can use for your weapons; if you want a crit weapon you can modify one to be crit, or if you want an elemental weapon like blast or toxic or heat damage you can! There are honestly an insane amount of combinations of mods that you can put depending on your playstyle or your enemies. There are also tons of different missions that you can do, from stealth to elimination to boss missions as well as RAIDS! The graphics are good and you can customize your weapons and warframe. HOWEVER without putting in some dollars to this game it will be pretty hard to manage your weapons and pets. You have limited weapon, warframe and etc inventory so if you don't expand it using platinum you will end up selling a majority of your weapons. Another downside to the game is that you have to craft your weapons which take hours maybe days to finish which may turn some people off. You CAN definitely pay to win for the game but any content that you can buy you can also grind for and get.

A police investigation game from the makers of the Grand Theft Auto series, L.A. Noire is a unique title that has a lot to offer. The game's missions each focus on an individual criminal case, and require you to solve cases by means of scene investigation and interrogation of suspects, witnesses, and other persons of interest. The interrogations are the game's bread and butter. While you'll likely start out performing poorly at them, you'll find yourself growing better as time goes on. The dialogue is very good and the game's excellent face-capture adds to the immersion.
There's only one marked problem with this game, and it's a big one: the game is simply too short, and it has neither multiplayer nor any real replayability at all. Once you've solved every case, there's absolutely no reason to play through the game again. As such, this game does not justify purchase unless it is on sale.

I'm going to oversimplify the hell out of this game in this review because if I'm honest I never fully understood the game. I always had friends with thousands of hours walking me through things. This game is the ultimate grind fest. Now, I know that instantly sounds like a negative, but I'm always looking for games that have a large grind aspect to them and still stay fun because those games can hold your interest for a long time with the promise of infinite progression. So, what do I mean when I say Warframe is a grind fest? Well almost every time you choose a mission you're choosing it to get a specific loot drop. This means that you may end up playing the same mission or set of missions time after time. The reason I still had fun with the game while having to grind the same missions for weeks on end was that the gameplay is very fast paced and satisfying. If compare this to other games that have a similar grinding element, mostly RPGMMOs, those games will often have missions like "Travel from point A to point B" while Warframe keeps you constantly on the move and/or fighting enemies. The combat is simplistic, but because of the movement system and ability design it is highly satisfying.
TLDR: The game has a lot of grinding mechanics, but is supported by fun and satisfying combat. It's free, so check it out.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare brings adrenaline filled, honorable fighting back to gaming that has been lost from many modern AAA titles.
NO Noobtubes
NO long range sniping (archery requires some serious skill in this game if you want to hit anything smaller than a barn)
NO "I got 10 kills so now I repeatedly slaughter everyone on the map with a helicopter for 30 seconds"
This is not a game where rushing around swinging wildly will get you anywhere. You will need precision, grace and speedy reactions in order to block incoming attacks, evade large sweeps from 2 handed swords and duck beneath incoming arrows before you get the satisfaction of violently removing the head of your enemy...and that's assuming he forgets to block.

I have been playing this game for just about 5,000 hours now on steam so I should have a good idea how the game plays out. I personally would recommend this game to anyone that is interested in space/sci-fi shooters. Its core mechanics including shooting and parkour work so well together and makes the game feel so fluid and personally is what always has me coming back when a big update hits the game. The purchasable ingame items in the marketplace are not too overzealous with the majority of the items usually being the cosmetics for the warframes that are reasonably priced. Most of the equipment that can be purchased for real money in most cases are not worth it because most of the materials and wait times out weigh the negatives to be worth the investment. If you decide to buy something with money spend it on cosmetics, catalysts, reactors, or warframe and weapons slots. Those are the most valuable things to buy especially for a new players. Another thing to applaud the game for is its mysterous story that keeps you wanting more. There is something special for a free to play game to have story missions and quests that makes me appreciate what free to play games have never done before. Some things that do bother me quite often though is the lack of information that is in the game itself and the uneventful boss fights. These two things though can be eventually written off as the developers have started to address these issues with more feedback in the UI and some of the well done boss fights like the recently added and tweaked Kela De Thaym and The Raptors boss fights. In my opinion these two bring more to the table rather than some of the others that they have done that were more or less just a 2-3 shot meat bag.

Been playing since closed beta (game wasn't even on Steam at the time) and I loved it. Emphasis on "loved", and I'm writing this review after the fiasco with datamining and Defection game mode which remains unchanged (and just as buggy) as it was during the event a few months ago as of writing this (July 2017). The game Warframe may itself be fine, and the idea of it is great, but the people behind it aren't realizing its potential to be a great and fun for 4 friends to play.
Digital Extremes (DE) is continually making and breaking promises, and if they do follow through it's a disappointment. Relics (replaced Void Keys) are even more grinding and RNG than it was before because of the need for Void Traces (6 to 30 drop during missions), the need to farm those Relics they've shown the ability to buy Orokin Derelict Keys with in game currency, and the RNG on the actual mission (the possibility you'll have to run a mission you don't want to run). Focus is only used for the passive when they hyped it up before to be like another form outside the Warframe (which it was, but even that is so lame it might as well not be part of the game) and has still been ignored. Raids and Archwing might as well not exist since Raids are a buggy mess, there's only been 2 since they launched, and they're not going to be fixed any time soon. Archwing is just there for MR fodder, is terrible to control, and is just boring. They removed Draco, a very popular exp farming area, saying that they'll work to make other missions more exciting and rewarding to compensate. Still hasn't happened yet DE, and instead people are turning to Akkad (a new exp cave) which I expect you to nerf eventually too. Costs for the Hema and Ignis Wraith event being clan based is BS when previous research weapons were never like that (in fact the Hema is the only one like that at the moment) and you already knew people didn't like running the same mission over and over from previous events (100 runs of Gradivus Event is not fun) and the previous statement above about Draco. Mandatory mods are still a thing that you said you wanted to get rid of but continue to support through Primed mods. Power creep is more blatanly obvious in this game than any other with the Galatine Prime being a stat increase on the War which is a stat increase on the Scindo Prime.
I could go on and on, broken promise after broken promise, but what broke me and made me want to write this review is that they aren't just ignorant to the community. They want OTHER players to be ignorant to the community as well. Last week the Fomorian hit and could drop the Imperator Vandal (Archwing weapon, basically event locked MR fodder). One of the pieces of the Imperator Vandal (which has 2 pieces and the Blueprint drop only from that event) had a 2% drop chance. When people complained about it in the Region chat, you silenced them. Mods banned people or suspended them from the chat for daring to call out your abyssmal drop rates. Why? What was the point of this? I'd rather do 100 runs of Gradivus Event again because at least I KNOW I'll get there eventually for the Brakk/Detron.
DE is basically married to RNGesus, but they're the alpha in the relationship dogging RNGesus to screw us as much as possible. They'll stack RNG on RNG as much as they want, and put ridiculous costs to boot just because they can and they have. You're the abused child here who wants the relationship to get better so you can all be a happy family, and DE says they will and they PROMISE they will. But it won't. The game used to be so much, but I realize now that I was running more on the promise of something rather than the actual product. DE is hoping other players do the same.

See, your character isn't a criminal because he has a badge, similar in the way that a war hero isn't a mass murderer because he has a medal of honor. Investigation and interrogation are puzzle game mechanics reduced to pixel hunting, driving handles like a down's syndrome tank, and chasing and fighting makes you feel like a herp-derp robot. In fact, the last level of the game is spent burning fellow police officers alive with a flamethrower to catch an arsonist, and shoot him in the head. Because ♥♥♥♥ due process, that's why. They've culled together a huge cast of TV actors and extensively mocapped all their faces but it doesn't amount to much because as a film it's a stilted, convoluted mess and as a game it's a clunky GTA clone. L.A. Noire is an incredible interactive experience where you play the role of a detective in a wide variety of different police cases. The first noticeable thing is the amazing detail of the faces. And this is important because it is the player's job to determine whether people are telling the truth or lying based on their facial expressions during interviews.
The gameplay is essentially broken down into driving to different scenes, searching for clues, interviewing people, and occasionally chasing down suspects. It is really unlike any other game on the market and it does a great job at drawing you in. Musical chimes are used to let you know when you are next to something relevant so it is important to keep an open ear.
The story feels realistic and is broken into shorter chapters meaning it's easy to pick up again after not playing it for a while. The acting is superb. All the characters feel genuine and it is obvious they put their heart and soul into their roles adding to that sense of realism. The game also showcases some great music as well. With 30+ hours of enjoyment, this is a must play game in my book.

For those coming here for reviews to determine if you will buy this game, in order to set your expectations, you should know there are 3 games here:
1) Single Player: If you enjoy a sandbox world you will occupy in order to do your thing, this game absolutely ROCKS. Buy it... and buy the season pass. It is well worth the money. If there is a fear of needless grind, know that those elements can be configured at all levels. Each map is a brand new experience, and the game lets you move between maps with ease. My advise...start with the Island... then move to Scorched Earth. I rate the game 10 out of 10.
2) Multiplay Unofficial: If you yearn for company, I advise you seek it in unofficial servers. They tend to have policies in order to mitigate the griefing that will occur in the Official Servers. PvE or PvP, the unofficial servers tend to have a better community. The negative here is there can be Admin preferences and the server could disappear with the host gets tired of the game. A solution is to rent or build your own server, then cultivate a group of players to fill out your world. Multiplay is viable, but most players will want some systemic restriction in order to enjoy the many open world elements of the game that make it special. I rate this as 8 out of 10.
3) Multiplay Official: PvE is worth pursuing. PvP is not. There is little to no admin or moderation, and the game's player interactions are VERY open. In PvE, this leads to 'pillering' land in prder to prevent you from building in desirable locations, as well as the occational 'training' of wild dinos into your tames. In PvP, this the unrestricted nature of interactions, tribe size, and server to server transfers, leads to a constaint state of PvP raiding and wiping. If that is your hucleberry, you will enjoy it. Most of the other open world game elements will be subject to this PvP dynamic. Know that you are trading the single player open world game fo pursue PvP.
Another thing to consider with the Official Servers is that they are underpowered for the open gameplay elements. In either PvE or PvP, you will experience server lag on any mature server, regardless of how may people are on at any given time... and a full server will be worse. I rate this as 6 out of 10 for PvE and 3 out of 10 for PvP .
All this considered, I enthusiastically recommend this game. I played mostly singleplayer for most of my hours, then hosted my own multiplayer server for family and freinds. As of the release of the game, I am playing on Offical PvE Scorched Earth and am enjoying it, dispite the server load issues I expressed. As I am not interested in unstricted PvP, I can only go on what the community feedback on the lack of ruleset has wrought. That isn't for me. I give my total experience as 8 out of 10.

The multiplatform free-to-play game is an action shooter with some of the trappings of an MMO. It launched in 2013 and is available now on PC, PS4 and Xbox One, where it is regularly updated. As a recently-awoken space ninja called a Tenno, your job is to fly around the solar system doing space ninja stuff like assassinations, spying on people, stealing information, and performing sabotage. Each mission location and type remains the same, but the missions themselves are somewhat randomized. The game relies on a random tile system to keep things fresh. Your base of operations–and your main menu–is your ship.
When you log in, you’re sitting in front of your command console, which lets you select where you want to go in the solar system. To your right is the store. To your left is the codex. Behind you, deeper in the ship, are other stations, like the foundry that lets you build weapons or the armory that allows you to outfit and modify your frames.
Ah, right, frames. The eponymous warframes operate like character classes, except instead of being locked into one class per character, you can swap frames at will, with each frame having four unique powers. For one mission, you might feel like running the supportive frame Trinity, who can mass heal the entire team or provide energy vampire abilities to ensure quick regeneration. On the next mission, you might want to play as Ember, whose incredible World on Fire ability burns every enemy within a massive radius.
You obtain warframes by defeating bosses and getting their parts or by completing some of the game’s great quests. Warframes are not just some cool gimmick or branding idea, but a cool design choice. Two good ideas make them great: first, they’re all overpowered, and second, you have to hunt them down.
Warframe doesn’t care about balance. You’re a badass space ninja, after all! Rather than pushing players through a lengthy and meaningless grind, Warframe provides players tons of awesome and incredibly destructive powers. I love running Frost, a frame that launches a massive blast of ice, freezing everything around it, killing most low-level enemies. Playing like Frost feels like running around as a tactical nuke. The sheer destructive power being wielded is awe-inspiring, but that’s true of every frame. Valkyr’s power is invulnerability. It comes at the expense of ranged weapons, but that’s fine, because as a space ninja, your swords are just as cool, if not cooler, than your guns.
What’s great about being overpowered is that, since everyone is overpowered, no one is. The power you wield makes you feel like you’re actually a badass space ninja, because you’re killing lots of enemies quickly and efficiently. Other sci-fi games, like Mass Effect 2, force you into cover through a lack of health and a focus on small groups of enemies. There’s no sense of lethality or badassery going on when your character feels like they’re made of soggy toilet paper while enemies can last through an entire magazine of gunfire. Warframe understands this, so every frame feels fun to play, because every frame has powerful, over-the-top capabilities.

L.A. Noire is not the typical open-world Rockstar extravaganza of violence and free-roaming action, but rather a serious take on a detective drama set in the years after WWII. Although the open world is available to the player and it's possible to drive around in freedom, there is no real fun to be had in it. The action revolves mostly around investigating crime scenes, following up on leads and interviewing witnesses and/or suspects. The latter part is where the game really shines: all the faces in L.A. Noire are real actors, captured with great detail by a special camera tech. The result is an uncanny reproduction of their facial features, facial movements and emotions. Although the PC version is oddly inferior to the Xbox360 version due to some (very minor) technical/graphical glitches, it is still a brilliant showcase of the technology. This is a game which really depends on the technology behind it, but even when stripped down to its core it is still a worthwhile experience. Just don't expect GTA set in the 40/50's!

Running up a snowy mountain firing a machine gun at a woolly mammoth from the back of a tyrannosaurus is a fantastic example of the reason many video games exist: living out ridiculous childhood fantasies. ARK: Survival Evolved has plenty of that to go around across its multiple sprawling maps - which it calls ARKs - which can be explored solo or crowded with up to 100 players. Some lingering technical issues, bad dino AI, and an extreme amount of grinding to reach endgame are the main factors keeping it from being as sharp in the tooth as it could be.
Like many of the survival/crafting games of the genre it partially helped popularize, ARK dumps you on the beaches of a massive, foreboding island with just enough clothing to stay modest and your own two fists. From there, the challenge is to stay fed and hydrated while avoiding a huge variety of terrifyingly detailed dinosaurs and other beasts long enough to progress up the tech tree. Early in the life of a character, you might be taking out dilophosaurs with throwing spears and hoping a triceratops doesn’t come and knock your thatch hut over in the middle of the night.On public PvP servers, other players are both your greatest opportunity and greatest danger. As I learned the hard way more than once, making sure your shelters are hidden from potential looters is far more important than making sure they are strong, and I often returned from less than 12 hours offline to find my barricades wrecked and hours worth of resource harvesting hauled off. Things get much better if you can work your way into a strong tribe of players that can protect your stuff 24/7.But the excitement is dulled as the amount of menial grinding required to reach the higher tiers of technology goes up exponentially, to the point where it could take an entire day of playtime just to stock up on ammunition for certain weapons. This can cause things to really start to drag when you’re just getting access to some of the most interesting tech - especially if you don’t have a large tribe of other players to help you divide the labor. It’s one of those games that can be played solo, but at least on PvP servers, I wouldn’t recommend it.

Running up a snowy mountain firing a machine gun at a woolly mammoth from the back of a tyrannosaurus is a fantastic example of the reason many video games exist: living out ridiculous childhood fantasies. ARK: Survival Evolved has plenty of that to go around across its multiple sprawling maps - which it calls ARKs - which can be explored solo or crowded with up to 100 players. Some lingering technical issues, bad dino AI, and an extreme amount of grinding to reach endgame are the main factors keeping it from being as sharp in the tooth as it could be.
Like many of the survival/crafting games of the genre it partially helped popularize, ARK dumps you on the beaches of a massive, foreboding island with just enough clothing to stay modest and your own two fists. From there, the challenge is to stay fed and hydrated while avoiding a huge variety of terrifyingly detailed dinosaurs and other beasts long enough to progress up the tech tree. Early in the life of a character, you might be taking out dilophosaurs with throwing spears and hoping a triceratops doesn’t come and knock your thatch hut over in the middle of the night.On public PvP servers, other players are both your greatest opportunity and greatest danger. As I learned the hard way more than once, making sure your shelters are hidden from potential looters is far more important than making sure they are strong, and I often returned from less than 12 hours offline to find my barricades wrecked and hours worth of resource harvesting hauled off. Things get much better if you can work your way into a strong tribe of players that can protect your stuff 24/7.But the excitement is dulled as the amount of menial grinding required to reach the higher tiers of technology goes up exponentially, to the point where it could take an entire day of playtime just to stock up on ammunition for certain weapons. This can cause things to really start to drag when you’re just getting access to some of the most interesting tech - especially if you don’t have a large tribe of other players to help you divide the labor. It’s one of those games that can be played solo, but at least on PvP servers, I wouldn’t recommend it.

My first impression was this game wasn't as bad as other people's review. I saw a lot of complaints about bugs exploitation,glitches,etc. But I experience none of that when I play the game. The game is really fun even though it's hard to learn. Yes, it requires a lot of time to master this game. But that doesn't make this game bad. Serious players will find learning this game gives them a hell lot of fun due to the challenging gameplay.
But for players that are just curious about the unique FPS sword fighting gameplay, I'm sure most of them will find the game quite difficult. That goes to the conclusion that people who's complaining about hit delays, block failure bugs, etc. are just angry that they're being cut to pieces every time they try to play by experienced players. I saw a lot of 1,000 hours + gameplay players in this game. It's not peculiar that noobs won't survive during early games. Most of the angry reviewers only has <100 hours of gameplay.
Does that mean you have to be a serious to play this game ? Absolutely not. Me myself isn't a serious player. I only buy this game because of the unique gameplay and I got no intention at all to master this game. I had a lot of fun playing this game due to the unique gameplay. There're no other game that has this kind of high-quality graphics with FPS-TPS medieval sword fighting. Even the DLC is also not bad at all. The classes are really interesting and you can feel like you're in a real war during that era.
The only downside of this game was the server. The Chivalry : Medieval Warfare server is really crowded but it has no asian server. I'm from Indonesia and the best country that offers me good ping is Singapore and of course, Indonesia (duh). It's rather rare to find southeast asian server in the game and I had to play with >200 ping. That led to immature players mocking me for my bad ping. Indonesia's maximum internet speed bandwith is only 5 MBps with the government's Telkom Speedy ISP. That made me impossible to get good pings if I join servers outside Southeast Asia. So if you're from Indonesia, you should think twice before buying this game. The DLC also got the same problem. There's only 1-5 crowded server everyday and all of them has >200 ping. But I get the amount of fun I paid for. For me, it's worth  the money.

Easily one of the worst games available on steam. I was surprised when I found out it wasn't a beta test, but an actual game that they claim is finished.
The interface menu is clunky, and the configuration options make little sense. (The ability to toggle sprint, but not crouch?) The default keybindings are poorly done, and it may take some time to fix all of them as there is no real documentation of what the different commands do.
The combat is the real problem however. It is pretty much a slower, clunkier version of Skyrim's melee combat with worse hit detection. You may be expecting something like this:
What you get is this:
The majority of the gameplay is flailing about, trying to hit someone with their back turned. Even if you can get past the slow and clunky gameplay, the hitboxes, combinded with the lag, make it completely unpredictable as to whether you will actually, hit, be hit, or do nothing.
If you are looking for any sort of realism, this is not the game for you either. Archers will frequently cut down knights in plate armor with a dagger, while unarmored soldiers will shrug off crossbow bolt to the chest with ease. The primary difference between the classes is their weaponry, as armor is simply a health modifier which means very little and lighter armor equates to an almost indistinquishable change in speed.
The variety in the game is sorely lacking. Each class has two and a half appearances without buying the cosmetic DLCs. One appearance for the red team, one for the blue team, and you can pick from either the red or blue team appearance with custom colors for the Free For All mode. There is no performance customization past the weapon selection, where each class gets four primary weapons with unlockable upgrades for each. There seems to only be about 8 maps, with each of the game modes played on those same maps. The team objective game mode has horrible balance issues on almost every map, as there is no way to push to the offensive team backwards, making defeat almost certain for the defenders.
The one good thing I can say for the game is that the visuals would be pretty good for a game from 2009.

Yes, there are honest to goodness boss battles!  But some of them are quite hard, so you'll really have to rally your heroes to progress to the next stage!
Some of your heroes won't approve of some of the choices you make, though.  Ultimately it is up to you to decide what to do, but don't be surprised when Amenhotep scolds you.  He really does seem quite crotchety for an immortal hero being paid for his services!  Although, once you hire a hero you don't have to actively click anymore because they'll do the work for you, thus all the gold you're collecting is really the heroes' to begin with and... well, maybe Amenhotep isn't completely unjustified in calling you a foolish mortal and waiting impatiently for you to make decisions after all.  But be wary of the path you tread, for there are foul creatures that would promise you much for the price of your heroes' souls.  Again, it is up to you to decide what to do, but things are not always as they seem.  In the end, you'll have to decide if the end justifies the means.

Before reading this review, please note that I am recommending this on my personal experience with the game (I play on an unofficial PVE server with my friends), so please keep this in mind as you read. I will also try to touch on both pro's and con's of the game (Scroll to the bottom for a small recap of the review).
My Opinion of the game:
Ark: Survival Evolved has been one of my most played games for 2017. The adventures I've had with my friends and journeys across "The Island" and other maps have been loads of fun. The amount of replayability this game has to offer is amazing, with almost always something to do whether it be exploring a cave or obtaining more dino's for your army. Although a lot can be done for optimization for gameplay and game stability, I still find this game to be a lot of fun. I can see why so many people dislike the game/developers and their reasons are justified, but the game (in my humble opinion) offers a lot in terms of exploration and adventure than other games of a similar genre.
Pros:
- Large maps with lots to do, but not too large that you find yourself bored traversing the terrain.
- Lots of different creatures to tame, many of which have unique taming styles.
- Graphics are good.
- Great Co-op game with friends if you favour PVE style gameplay.
- Lots of challanges to overcome stronger wild creatures.
- A survival game that is not terrible or was dropped in development.
- Workshop support.
- Developers still releasing content and updating the game.
Neutral:
- Unofficial servers are really the only way to have a good multiplayer experience.
- Only join trusted or highly rated Unofficial servers, to avoid server wipes, abusive admins, etc...
- Difficult to play other games while invested into ARK, as the game needs plenty of time.
- Increased tame speeds and other multipliers are needed, or the game takes too much time to do anything.
- Boss fights are okay, but have minimal strategy (Most can be beaten just by swarming them with high leveled Rex's).
- Limited gameplay when alone.
- On maps other than "The Island", there are lots of terrain peices which you can walk through.
- DLC's are fun, but bug fixes should have been prioritized.
- Alpha creatures early game can be very frustrating, but rewarding late game to kill for their EXP.
- Crafting system is okay.
Cons:
- Optimization is poor, and the game runs different for everyone (more information later on in the review).
- The recommended PC specs don't mean much, as people with recommened can still have a hard time running the game.
- Plenty of bugs, which can make for frustrating situations.
- Official servers are terrible.
- Admins of both unofficial and official servers tend to abuse their power.
- PVP is unbalanced and boring.
- Singleplayer is boring, and harder to run on your PC than joining a server.
- Lack of dev support for bugs and server complaints.
- No official seller for private servers in North America.
- Renting a server can be quite expensive (Expect to pay $20CAD+).
- Not worth its full release price of $66.49CAD (I'd say it's worth $35CAD at most).
- The game demands lots of RAM.
- Breeding is needed to defeat higher difficulty bosses (breeding takes lots of time).
- Deaths on spawn can happen, before you're even able to run away from the threat.
- F****** Troodons.
Summary:
The game is good, but has lots of room for improvment. Official servers are terrible and should be avoided. Unoffical servers are the way to go, but finding a trusting server can be difficult to find. The game is only fun with friends, and is very frustrating to play alone. Optimization is okay, but changing graphics settings doesn't tend to make much of a difference in how the game runs, and the game runs much differently for everyone it seems, as I can run it on high with a 1050Ti, and a friend of mine can only run it on medium with a 1070 (with other better parts in his PC). The game has many clear issues, which need to be addressed by the devs. All in all the game is fun, but has many issues and feels like the game is still in a beta state. I can only recommend buying this game if it goes on sale for at least half off. If I had to rate the game out of 10, I would give it a score of 6/10.
Recommendations before purchase:
- Torrent or download the game off a friend first, make sure it will actually run well on your PC.
- Make sure you have friends who are willing to play and devote some time to help progress in game.
- If you have the funds or the ability to do so, running/renting your own server is a good way to ensure fair gameplay.
- Only purchase the game if you're okay with there being bugs, the game is far from perfect.

I'll recommend this game because it's free, so you can give it a shot and see for yourself if it is worth your time.
As the name suggest, Clickers Heroes is a clicker game, such as the (in)famous browser game named Cookie Clicker. It consist basically of clicking like crazy to reach an objective, all the while purchasing upgrades and units to help you with that. It's strangely addictive and compelling.
Clicker Heroes gave me a few hours of fun for free, so I cannot complain. The main problems I have with the game are balance issues. It becomes harder and harder to beat the stages (as it should be), but not in a natural/gradual way. After the first hours your upgrades become almost meaningless, and you become too dependant on powers (which have long cooldowns) to progress. At that point you're bound to either purchase gems with real money, or wait an eternity for each stage.
Some of the game mechanics are not very well explained as well (in a clicker game, really...). I didn't get to use a lot of things simply because I did not fully understand how they would impact my game. More variety on the upgrades would be nice as well.
Anyway, it's a free game, so go ahead and get it and see for yourself.

LA Noire is a grown up game. Grown up themes, grown up language, a unique period set grown up game through and through with only Mafia II getting even slightly close.

Interesting plots (cases) and the whole conversation-reading peoples faces-clue finding aspect is executed very well. I highly recommend this game to the thinkers out there. Players that like a mental challenge but on an entirely different scale.

Been playing since closed beta (game wasn't even on Steam at the time) and I loved it. Emphasis on "loved", and I'm writing this review after the fiasco with datamining and Defection game mode which remains unchanged (and just as buggy) as it was during the event a few months ago as of writing this (July 2017). The game Warframe may itself be fine, and the idea of it is great, but the people behind it aren't realizing its potential to be a great and fun for 4 friends to play.
Digital Extremes (DE) is continually making and breaking promises, and if they do follow through it's a disappointment. Relics (replaced Void Keys) are even more grinding and RNG than it was before because of the need for Void Traces (6 to 30 drop during missions), the need to farm those Relics they've shown the ability to buy Orokin Derelict Keys with in game currency, and the RNG on the actual mission (the possibility you'll have to run a mission you don't want to run). Focus is only used for the passive when they hyped it up before to be like another form outside the Warframe (which it was, but even that is so lame it might as well not be part of the game) and has still been ignored. Raids and Archwing might as well not exist since Raids are a buggy mess, there's only been 2 since they launched, and they're not going to be fixed any time soon. Archwing is just there for MR fodder, is terrible to control, and is just boring. They removed Draco, a very popular exp farming area, saying that they'll work to make other missions more exciting and rewarding to compensate. Still hasn't happened yet DE, and instead people are turning to Akkad (a new exp cave) which I expect you to nerf eventually too. Costs for the Hema and Ignis Wraith event being clan based is BS when previous research weapons were never like that (in fact the Hema is the only one like that at the moment) and you already knew people didn't like running the same mission over and over from previous events (100 runs of Gradivus Event is not fun) and the previous statement above about Draco. Mandatory mods are still a thing that you said you wanted to get rid of but continue to support through Primed mods. Power creep is more blatanly obvious in this game than any other with the Galatine Prime being a stat increase on the War which is a stat increase on the Scindo Prime.
I could go on and on, broken promise after broken promise, but what broke me and made me want to write this review is that they aren't just ignorant to the community. They want OTHER players to be ignorant to the community as well. Last week the Fomorian hit and could drop the Imperator Vandal (Archwing weapon, basically event locked MR fodder). One of the pieces of the Imperator Vandal (which has 2 pieces and the Blueprint drop only from that event) had a 2% drop chance. When people complained about it in the Region chat, you silenced them. Mods banned people or suspended them from the chat for daring to call out your abyssmal drop rates. Why? What was the point of this? I'd rather do 100 runs of Gradivus Event again because at least I KNOW I'll get there eventually for the Brakk/Detron.
DE is basically married to RNGesus, but they're the alpha in the relationship dogging RNGesus to screw us as much as possible. They'll stack RNG on RNG as much as they want, and put ridiculous costs to boot just because they can and they have. You're the abused child here who wants the relationship to get better so you can all be a happy family, and DE says they will and they PROMISE they will. But it won't. The game used to be so much, but I realize now that I was running more on the promise of something rather than the actual product. DE is hoping other players do the same.

This Game Is ♥♥♥♥ing Awesome.
Rockstar has came through again with a great title, and it's nice to see them do a change from the formula of GTA. You play Cole Phelps, a Marine in WW2 turned Cop when he comes home, and you rise quickly through the ranks.
The graphics are awesome, detailed and smooth, although I found even on my beasty rig, it chugged in busy driving areas. The facial graphics on the people during questioning, is the best I have seen, bar none, each person is different, and some will completely throw you off the scent with their poker faces.
The story is engrosing, and as you go through you unlock more of Cole's past, and the various Marines he was with, and it all wraps up into a well thought out, and surprising ending.
If you like games that make you think, and throw you curveballs, that have some action on the side, then i'd highly recommend you try L.A Noire.

Police procedural. It's a word you hear a lot when descriibing TV cop dramas. Despite how exciting those shows can be, the word itself sounds like something incredibly boring. Probably in real life it most often is. Great music and montages can do a lot to make a detective's life look enviable. The problem with LA Noire is that there are no montages. There's this huge world to explore, yet there's no reason or pull to. Each chapter, or 'case' is so short and contained that it never feels like the right time to go exploring. Why then make the game appear so much like a sandbox? Being 'on mission' all the time, having such a focus on realism, being rated constantly: it all amounts to nurturing a fear of experimenting and going off track. Yet these are the things which evoke fun times. I enjoyed the experience of LA Noire for the unique one that it was, but I probably won't be heading back.

This game is amazing. In its entirety it’s intriguing and different.
I like the detail put into it. In most games simple unimportant characters don’t really have a face of their own, they just use the same few models. (E.g. the citizens in Half-Life 2) but in this, every character has their own face and therefore their own identity, and I really liked that. They were all built around their voice actors and it was really amazing to see 3 or 4 actors that I knew of, appear in a video game. That was something that really did impress me.
It’s mainly a detective type game, and there is a lot more action to it than your average detective game. You get to drive around an open world city responding to street crime, be involved in car chases, find clues for your investigation and interrogate your subjects making sure you judge them right.
I only have one problem with this game and that’s the storyline. It isn’t exactly a “game breaker” for me, I just found it a little disappointing. At first I was extremely intrigued with the plot and it felt like it was going to go somewhere great and be really good, but it just wasn’t. I found it very up and down, it leads up to one thing then completely changes the subject.
At the end of every mission you are given a score as to how well you did, and there are some points where you can’t avoid doing the wrong thing, which I thought was really stupid. There’s even one part you get told off for doing the right thing! I just thought that it was all over the place when it came to plotline.
Apart from that I think this game is great, it’s a lot of fun and it’s not something you see all that often.

Now that this game has gone into full realease I would like to review it I have over 1,500 hours In this game and think I have a good grasp on it. First let me say this although it can provide okay immersion in some areas you will most likely never get an immersive experience out of it, at least from my experience. But what it does do is give you a sandbox to ride dinosaurs and build giant bases that intimate the entire server. I like this game but with its 60$ price(at least at the time of this review) is a it of a stretch but it does do something kinda unique. By this I mean it is the only "well" executed game were you can ride and coexist with dinosaurs while introducing a survival aspect. So I'll split the review into three parts: Survival, immersion, and social experience.
SURVIVAL:
The survival aspect is quite satisfying in my opinion you get to see your character grow up learn new things and gain the ability to tame larger better beasts. On the subject of beasts the Dino's progression is a bit lackluster as you learn to tame more creatures, older Dino's even if a high level become semi useless although it allows for the more advanced dino's to be more desirable, it means that the Dino's you've become attached to for so long must be forgotten to progress. So if you can give up old stuff and like to see yourself get stronger(absurdly stronger) while risking losing it all to a giant turkey the survival aspect might fit you.
IMMERSION:
As I said before the immersion of this game is not very good although you might get that one scene that looks amazing it'll be ruined by a wired UI feature or a dino headrusing you. Beacuse of the very pop-y UI at times you'll find that it pops you back into reality causing you to remember your in PJs and drinking coke while playing a video game. And beacuse most of the Dino's follow one of five templates everything seems like ai they don't feel like real creatures that could bite your head off. But one thing I remember from playing the game was when I was a wee little survivor and there I was in my little Thatch house in the middle of the night then out of nowhere a GIANT TREX EATS MY HOUSE AND EVERYTHING I OWN CAUSING ME TO HAVE TO RUN FOR MY LIFE SEVERAL TIMES. This made me so scared I stayed on the beach for several days :D.
SOCIAL EXPERIENCE:
Official servers are a bit tuff they follow mostly the base rates which cause for much grinding not to mention the players who will eventually raid your base... Unless your on a PvE server, but then you miss out on a lot of things, hey no PvP or base explosion just people surrounding metal spawns with big walls... But the social experience is the biggest part of this game enjoying hanging out with your friends on private servers with rates up to avoid all the grinding. That is one of the most enjoyable parts of this game this section right here.
So in conclusion this review was highly incognitive but let me get my points across:
Pros:
Okay survival experience
Fun social experience on servers with friends and rates turned up
Tons of cool Dino's
RIDING DINOSAURS
And building cool big bases
Cons;
High system requirements
Bad dino ai
Official servers suck...In my opinion
Super not great immersion
Dino's progression kinda lackluster( having to leave behind Dino's that you've become attached to)
I recommend this game to a certain breed of gamer someone who will enjoy seeing there character level up even very little at a time, someone who has some time to sink and someone who can enjoy socializing. Not to mention someone who won't  get too salty if they lose a lot of progress every one and a while.

If you like playing games to escape, this one will take you far away. We hear a lot of talk about atmosphere in games, but nothing comes close to LA Noire. Lots of games give you a feeling of being in another place, but LA Noire sends you to a different *time.*
The sets and models are meticulously designed and highly detailed, and the story + acting are authentic AFAICT. You won't being crashing cars all over the place (although you could) and you won't spend each mission shooting things (although there are shootouts). What you will do is solve crimes, look for secrets, collect cars and marvel at this incredible piece of software.
There are some issues, such as the problems with interrogating witnesses (I played it twice and the 2nd time used a guide for the answers), but you won't mind if you're the type of gamer that likes a good story and top-notch worldbuilding. Rockstar really tried to do something with this game, and although not everyone agrees it's great, I personally think it's their finest moment (except for RDR and Bully).

Had a great time on the free weekend. If you're on the fence about this game here's what you can expect:
-Fast paced large scale medieval battles with an upwards of 32 players at a time, (Sometimes more)
-A wide assortment of weapons with different power, reach, and statistics
-Melee combat is awesome, You have 4 different swings, some are faster or stronger, all of them are useful. There is also a feint you can use with any swing to fake out opponents.
-In Large scale battles you'd be surprised how many small scale localized fights break out, the winner of a duel will survive to assist his allies. You really need to see it for yourself.

I can't hide how much fun this game is! The combat is fast, visceral and deep. Much deeper than many people realize, and glance over it saying it pales in comparison to M&B or WotR. Combining the 3 basic slashes, combos, a directional parry, kicks, ducks and jumps, feints, footwork and coordination give even the most dedicated melee enthusiasts such a various move set at their disposal. Finding a weapon and class combination, whether you want to be a tower shield wielding Defender or an offensive, jumpy Man at Arms give loads of experimentation. The game modes range from simple Team Deathmatch and King of the Hill to a multi-tiered Team Objective mode taking place in beautiful maps, where teams will raid villages, push siege weapons, sink enemy ships, and (in my personal favorite segment) the player on the top of the leaderboard will become the King, and their team must defend him with their lives while the enemy charge in waves through the throne room. The immersion in the game is top notch, as your army lets the enemy hear their battlecries as they charge, blades clash together, you hear screaming from the distance, siege weapons wreck the battlefield and you truly feel the scope of your actions. I can recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun medieval game that, in my humble opinion, has the best melee system in any game to date.

L.A. Noire is made by the studio that made every Grand Theft Auto game, Red Dead Redemption, and so forth.  It uses a very nifty facial rendering technology which really gives the characters a lifelike look - as they are all based off real actors.  The game itself handles much like a Grand Theft Auto game, you play as Cole Phelps a LAPD detective who solves various overarching cases.  You'll drive to crime scenes, look at evidence, interview witnesses, chase suspects, get into shootouts, you name it...  It's very polished and cool, all the dialogue is voice-acted by real actors.  This is not a typical Grand Theft Auto game about shooting people and causing mayhem though, you are really there to look through evidence and solve crimes - shooting bad guys is somewhat secondary to that.  I would definitely recommend this game if you're a fan of hip crime novels and big-budget Rockstar games.

The Good - The Maps in this game are amazing. The game sounds and looks great. Never had this much fun running into battle screaming alongside my friends. The game leaves me feeling immersed in the world as I bask in the realism of the combat system/world created. That is until you play against "high level players".
The Bad - Servers. I have only played during free week but there were never enough "new player" servers with open slots to allow me and my group of friends to play. This meant we had to play in servers with no level restriction and we ran into people who exploit the ♥♥♥♥ out of this game and they tend to be "high level" players.
You will notice that all "high level" players do the same thing. They grab a heavy 2h weapon and through some use of video settings/exploits/scripts they are able to effectively become a whirlwinding machine of death, they kill they are not even looking at, and if you pay attention to these players you can watch as their character model actually contorts into crazy positions showing just why they are "high level" players. THey dont play the game better, they simply play a different game where they are able to kill people in front of them, on both sides of them and even behind them, with one fell swoop as their spine/hips rotate in ways/speeds that are not humanly possible. Not only are they still able to block every attack, while swinging away recklessly, they also never miss.
This game would be a solid 10/10, even a 20/10 when you consider the price and other things the game does well. But once you experience the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t "mechanics" that "high level" players employ to win matches, you will realize that the game has some major flaws.
My message to the devs, add some sort of speed limit to the rate at which classes can spin, dont make it dependent on the mouse. The basis for the game is super realistic, but this realism is♥♥♥♥♥♥on once you play against someone abusing these whirlwind mechanics and it completely ruins the game for anyone who cant get into a noob server.

L.A. Noire is one of the most interesting games I've ever played. You play as a police offier/detective and try to solve (random) cases. The faces are just brilliantly done. Having to guess if a person is lying or telling the truth is awesome to watch. Combine that with the realistic graphics and you've got one hell of a game (though it does outstay its welcome near the end).
But unfortunately the game has a 30FPS cap, and it's noticeable; there's some tearing every now and then. Now, I have to tell you that the game doesn't ever dip below 30FPS so it's absolutely playable. I heard it's because of the animation of the faces that 60FPS just isn't an option. I can live with it. The game definitely makes up for it. Recommended !

Oddball mix of police procedural and GTA. The highlight is incredible facial-capture tech that makes it hard to go back to mask-face mannquins in other games. You can recognize actors so that it's like being a player in a movie. In more ways than one, since you watch this cutscene-happy game more than play it. The clue-searching and interrogation gameplay is also fun, easy to use yet a bit challenging to master. Historic L.A. is cool to see, but oversize GTA map feels out of place and free-roaming has no real purpose or thrill, much like "Mafia." More interesting than good, this is still well worth a look as a new high point in the convergence of game tech and movies. One mystery your detective won't solve: why they put an "e" on the end of "noir."

A console ported facial expression simulator. You can skip social club registry. "backspace" can skip some cut scenes but not all. For the most part this is 50% gameplay 50% cutscenes. Interrogation mechanic has 3 options - do not pick "3: Lie" unless you have evidence to back it up. You can ask your partner for hints. The main story is mediocre.
Pros: has real L.A. landmarks, cases inspired by real crimes, setting is believable, and unique concept.
Cons: fov sucks, inefficient and not optimized, vsync locked at 30fps in-game, clunky controls, combat is whack-a-mole shooting and button mash melee, contains right-wing pro-christian anti-atheist anti-communist messages, and suffers from several bugs/stability issues especially at the last half of the game. Wont let you skip the credits at the end.
Hit or miss, I wouldn't pay more than $5 for this.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing. I hope you enjoy.
