ARK has been the first game I have purchased, that was in "Early Access".  With that said, I purchased it with the understanding that there would not be perfection throughout.  Over the past two years, and now in "Full Release" of the game, I can say that my feelings for this game have not changed.  I LOVE IT!
It's a game.  I understand there will be hiccups, I understand S is going to happen that'll make me ask "What the F?!"  In the end, I believe the devs have developed an amazing game, with gorgeous graphics, a fun premise, and an overall challenging experience.  If ARK was easy, you'd get bored and look for something else.
I appreciate the challenges, and although there are still quite a few minor patches I see download when I login to Steam, I get it.  The devs are still trying to create a fun experience for us all, and to do that, there may need to be a tweak or fix that needs to happen as they learn about them.
Overall, if you enjoy a challenge, a bit of grinding to gain resources, and good times, buy the game.  Try watching videos of the game; they'll give you a visual experience of what someone else is going through.

A great game that's also a missed opportunity. L.A. Noire is a great period piece with cases ripped from the history books. You really feel like you're in 1940s Los Angeles. The investigations and interrogations make up the bulk of the gameplay with exposition tying it all together. However, the game has very little replay value once you solve the crimes. And for as much time and effort Team Bondi put into recreating Los Angeles, there's very little to do in the city. This doesn't have GTA IV's minigames or stores. There's no reason to explore beyond finding hidden items. It can break the immersion. There's also a lack of a free-roam between cases. The game takes a episodic format instead.
However, I play games for the story, and the story here is fantastic with great acting and and dark and gripping plot. Highly recommended.

Rockstar has made a magnificently atmospheric game in this one. Though famous for GTA, in LA NOIRE you actually fill the role as a proper straight man; an ex-marine turned cop which is moving his way through the ranks from street cop to gritty, turn of the century detective.
Most of the game play actually revolves around inspecting evidence, piecing together clues and interrogating witnesses, which is a far cry from other Rockstar games' reputation of shoot and drive free-roam fun sandbox games. There's still plenty of driving around a thoroughly recreated 1930s fake-LA, but waving your gun around wily-nily will cause your score to plummet or end your game.
As usual, Rockstar has done a magnificent job with their voice acting cast and setting, but one of the real draws is the state-of-the-art motion capture system they used for facial animations in LA NOIRE, making every in game cutscene worth watching.
I highly recommend this title. Pick it up!

Once upon a time I lived in town and had cable with unlimited data, Then I moved out in the styx where I can't get cable all I can get is Sattelite internet with limited bandwidth.
I get bonus data between the hours of 2 and 8 am so I set steam to automatically install updates between those hours.
How it worked out was that Ark would update while I was sleeping and then there would be another update available while I was at work and I couldn't play it untill the update was installed....not wanting to use all my data I would have to wait untill 2 am to install the update.
I get to play once in a while on weekends when I don't have to work, but I do get frustrated when I download an update only to find that I still can't play it because I'm too busy nursing my limited bandwidth. I would still recommend this game but I would urge you to think twice if you have limited bandwidth.

I had gotten to the point in my years-long Chivalry career where I could no longer stand the divergence from the classic Age of Chivalry gameplay. For those readers who don't know, Age of Chivalry is the Source Engine mod that is the origin of the Chivalry series. The developers have chosen to embrace certain mechanics in the new game that I always found annoying since its release, mechanics that in my opinion muddy the balance between classes and lower the overall realism of the experience. It was especially due to the unrealistic nature of these mechanics that I stopped playing this game for a long while.
I realize that some people will consider my *hated flaws* as their *favorite features*. I also realize that it would take a heavenly intervention from Jesus himself to perfectly balance the gameplay, so you can be sure that I don't have any unreasonable expectations of this game. However, I would argue that the developers would consider gritty realism to be a key selling point for the series. Case in point: the weapons categories and character classes each have their own unique utility, strengths, and weakness that allow them play in a realistic way. Polearms have the range; two-handed weapons have power; one-handed weapons have speed; blunt weapons have bonus against armor; archers are squishy; knights are tanks; etc, etc.... it all makes sense. So clearly a deep level of realism has been strived for here. This is where the game mechanics added to Chivalry that weren't in AoC subtract realism from the sequel, and really take a big step away from balance between the classes.
First issue-this is the on minor end of my criticisms-is the new character abilities: the main point here is the lack of balance between the new abilities. They give an unnecessarily large advantage to two classes, leaving the other two classes in the dust in terms of power and usefulness.
The AoC Vangaurd has been weaponized as an Intercontinental Ballistic Vangaurd that can fly great distances to one-hit kill archers and otherwise deal huge damage with absolutely no skill required (even after a nerf). In regard to the vangaurd special ability, one could argue that it was specifically added to help vangaurds deal with archers. In fairness, it can be hard to counter archers since vangaurds have a distinct lack of a shield. However, almost all the vangaurd weapons can one-hit kill an archer already, and the ones that can't will still easily dispatch archer in two hits if the he is caught with his bow out. So, in the end, did this ability really add balance in this situation? Or did it simply skew it by bringing an unreasonably high-damage, broken attack mechanic to the vangaurd arsenal? I'll let you decide, but know that it causes glitchy vangaurd animations and unpredictable movement (sometimes it's a short hop of a couple feet and other times it's a Dragon Ball Z-esque power level 9000 long distance dive bomb) while dealing a hell of a lot of damage for a LMB attack. Bottom line: it's over powered.
The Man-at-Arms from AoC has been replaced by Nightcrawler from X-men, a dodge-happy teleporting menace that can absolutely dominate beyond reason in the hands of the better players, even after a nerf to the ability. I only have this to say about the dodge ability: Man-at-Arms was already the most mobile and agile class, why does this ability have to be so powerful? Also, why does the Man-at-Arms as a light, shield-using class have a two-hit left mouse button kill on the archer? I'm sidetracking here, but this has to be said: a two-hit kill using overheads or stabs I understand because these attacks require accuracy and rightly should deal higher damage than a slash. But a two-slash kill? It boggles the sodding mind. This is the single biggest balance issue in the game. I stress I don't expect perfect balance in this game, but this "MAA LMB two slash kill on archers" garbage should be fixed. The speed, agility, and shielding of the MAA rightly represents the biggest threat to the archer class as it is, why sour this relationship with imbalance in the form of an overpowered slash?
Meanwhile, the knight gets no upgrades (except for access to better sword/shield combinations, but that's more of a sidegrade than an outright upgrade) and the archer upgrades are spotty and in some cases actual digressions. (Javileneers even had an attack -the jav slash- completely removed in the transition from AoC to Chivalry). To call the single-use deployable shield of the crossbowman an ability is a sad joke, as it's usefulness is VERY limited in scope (read: as cover from other archers while reloading). The archer backstab ability is also a joke. The Chivalry archer's role is long range support, a glass cannon of sorts who should avoid melee when possible. However, the nature of the backstab ability is that of a stealthy, infiltrating assassin. As such, the backstab rarely has an effective use in this game since the archer is more of a Legolas and less of a Sam Fisher. Worst of all, it doesn't one-hit kill any class, meaning a melee battle will usually ensue after the backstab hits (or misses). Isn't a melee battle the one thing that bowman should be avoiding? A little logic goes a long way in highlighting poorly implemented mechanics, doesn't it?
All that said, the abilities are something that can be tweaked towards balance. As they stand in their current format, they are a noble attempt at progressing the depth of gameplay of the series, but are by no means balanced.  It is foolish to consider them in a 'finished' state.
The second issue and the most severe of my complaints is the movement mechanics. First up, weapon dragging. Experienced players will swear by weapon dragging, and fair enough, I do think it has a place in Chivalry. But in the current format it is too powerful.  It makes sense that the mouse movements can "rotate the hips" and help an attack connect earlier in the swing.  However, the idea that a hit early in the swing should deal full damage is flawed. The weapon in reality does not not have full momentum during the early swing and by the laws of physics should deal less damage. Let's keep dragging in the game, but enhance the realism by adding an incremental damage system or something to that effect to nerf the power of this mechanic.
The second critism in movement mechanics is the lack of momentum displayed by characters. This is probably a challenging issue to tackle from a programming perspective, but it's not impossible to implement. After all, it flies in the face of logic that a character can turn on a dime without losing momentum and head in an opposing direction at full speed. It allows for the exsistence of "ballerina" knights and vangaurds who behave more like a man-at-arms than an armor clad juggernaut. They're still juggernauts, only they can move like Black Swan and they're just as crazy. Developers, at the very least remove a character's sprint if he makes more than a 90 degree turn.
These two *features* of movement combine to slaughter any sense of realism so carefully incubated in the game.
There is exciting hope though. A new mod called Black Knight levels the playing field between classes. It features dismemberment as a game mechanic. It forces all classes (especially the heavy ones) to avoid damage trading and be more tactical with feints and parries. It allows the lighter classes to utilize their speed to greater effect. In short, the tanks are a little less tanky, the ballerinas can be slowed with tactical leg removal, and the speed of man-at-arms and archers plays a bigger role than in vanilla Chivarly. Taking hits is more costly, and this makes combat feel more real. After all, IRL who would let themselves get stabbed by a short sword just so they can draw an enemy in for a killing blow from a war hammer? The ballerinas can keep their vanilla Chiv, I'll take my Black Knight mod any day.
The game's combat is very fluent and it's fun to play with your friends. Glad the devs have updated for full controller support after release for Xbox 360.

ARK: Survival Evolved is one of the single most under(?)rated games on this platform. underrated? yes! and i will tell you why, starting with the least obvious point: the criticism;
People say that this game isn't worth the prize you now pay for it.
I have to tell you: that is wrong! I had more fun with this than with COD, I had more fun with this than with skyrim; both of which i paid more for than i would have to pay for this game now, though i bought it a lot earlier and only payed half because i realised its potential early.
People say that it is outrageous that the developers released a DLC during early access.
Really? I actually like how the developers do things differently than everyone before them. Scorched Earth was fun to play and well worth the money. The mythical creatures worked well in the game even when people said they wouldn't. etc. etc.
not to mention they told us players a viable reason for releasing the DLC: they wanted to test how to even make one and include it.
People also say that this game doesn't have a story.
This is kind of ironic since it is a survival sandbox game with building mechanics. a lot of similar games out there dont have even a small semblance of story and nobody complains about them!
Also, the developers already told us they will include a story in this with the two DLCs, so this is kind of a mute point.
The last point, which is in my eyes the only halfway viable argument against it, it that it is poorly optimized and runs badly on low-end pcs and only mediocre on higher-end pcs.
However, my pc is a few years old now, only has a gtx 550 ti, i only have 32 gb of ram and an i3 and i am still able to play it fairly smoothly (now) and no, i dont play on the lowest possible settings, more like medium. no 60 fps of course, but still smooth enough to play without lags or it being slow enough to be irritating;
Now to the good points; and i have to say this in advance: i dont know about the servers; I only did singleplayer in this game.
1. This game has the single best building system in any rpg game; Ever! The building system in fallout 4 for example was kinda awkward and you often built things where you didnt want them, whereas in this game, it is incredibly easy to build bases that are both big, useful, and really strong as well as aesthetically pleasing.
The amount of structures and structure types is amazing. Could use a little more furniture but other than that...
2. the flora and fauna in this game is great. The amount of different wildlife is amazing and every animal has their use and most are really cool. I even love the supernatural animals even though people thought they wouldn't fit in at first.
3. even though it is a survival game, you aren't constantly stressed and being hounded by predators/enemies, like in the game "the forest" for example. you get time to explore and really revel in the great landscape of the map, to build, to keep a small farm etc. Yet it isn't neglecting the real survival fans at all; it happened often enough that i got killed relentlessly several times by Dilos shortly after starting on the map, of course also when meeting a rex or carno randomly, and one time i even got attacked by a seagull (pelagornis) on ragnarok when i got on a rock so that i wouldnt get eaten by dilos right at the start.
4. of course: the taming system; it is novel, it is understandable, it is balanced and just overall great; on the serverside the animal armies provide for entertainment in form of massive raids of course; though i had enough fun on singleplayer just with finding, taming and collecting all of them (Gotta catch 'em all!!!) and storing them away in bases scattered all over the map. AI opponents would have been great, so that i could also do raids to keep me entertained, though that is just food for thought and I personally dont need them.
There is plenty of entertainment to be had in this game even in singleplayer. don't let yourself be discouraged by the negative reviews and the average rating; This is a great game to have and will only get better over time the more the devs optimize it and include new stuff.

This is a great game. Unfortunately you need some kind of super PC in order to run it, and even if you have one, it won't stop the lag, bugs and ignorance of the developers, who hardly ever listens to the community or do anything to improve the game - both performance issues or unbalanced gameplay. The single player mode is alright, but boring and unless you use cheat codes it's almost impossible to reach any kind of end game content, since the game focuses more on interaction between players. And as mention earlier, the online servers are barely working and most of them are full all the time. Good luck getting anything done. Did I mention the file size of the game? So far (Oct 2017, the game is about 60 GB. If you want the two free fan made maps (that Studio Wildcard later introduced as official maps and takes most of the credit for), or maybe if you want the official DLCs (that will give you a huge advandage in PvP and that you have to pay for), the game will be about 110+ GB. Oh, and there are at least 2 more DLCs that will be released soon. So the final size of the official game will be about 150 GB, I believe. It's simply not worth it. I've played this game since early beta, summer 2015 and I know what I'm talking about. The game had a potential to be something great, but the only great thing about it is the size. I respect that Studio Wildcard didn't want this to be a simple survival game with dinosaurs, but they should've stopped adding new stuff just to please the people. The game was at it's peak, in my opinion, in September 2016. I won't say it hasn't been fun playing the last couple of years, but to me this is the end. In the future, Ark will just be remembered as the game that broke the trust for Early Access titles on Steam.

I was too afraid to play multiplayer, so I played everything on singleplayer.
It's a good game, but it could be better. The A.I. was assembled with little to no thought whatsoever. The Carnivores attack anything and gobble it up, even engaging in fights until they die instead of running away (although a mod Zoology should fix these, I haven't been able to make the damn engrams work). The carnivores also never get fed up, leading to "terraforming", where carnivores dominate the land living in peace with each other, but killing every herbivore that spawns. Given the size and beauty of the worlds, this is probably ok, since I can't imagine the extra machine power it would take to power such huge maps as well as a decent A.I on every living thing. But it is not realistic. Taming something is like going to the shop and buying a doll. They mean nothing, they understand nothing. They stay still forever if you tell them and won't defend themselves if you tell them. They don't know what fleeing is or even how to stay in a certain area. Thank god for fences, but i'd be fine with just a leash or equivalent mechanic. The crown for dumb A.I take the bats. They know nothing except how to aggro toward a player and stand in the air. Some cave exploring.
Some creatures are ridiculously overpowered and give almost nothing in return. Early on, when I met the Daeodon and the Wolf, I simply couldn't win (metal armor). The Wolves attack very fast with huge knockback and eat mammoths by the truckload. I certainly couldn't kill two of them on my own, before I used good tames. Oddly enough, they spawn in the desert with thick fur, but the desert is 40°C. Preposterous. The Daeodon has huge health, knockback and regeneration, but you'll only get about 10 each of meat/skin. Ridiculous. Carnos are much easier and give prime meat. I feel cheated. Butfrustrated, even.
There is something very off about some domesticated species and their wild counterparts. Parasaurs and stegos run much faster wild, but their speed is cut down significantly when you tame them (stegos especially). There are many examples of this, like the flying Tapejara, which sprints regally away but is half as fast when you tame it. Some get faster after taming. What were they thinking?
I have other minor complaints, like why can't I pick up a rock in one click anymore? Who the hell nerfs picking up rocks from 2 to 0.5 per click? are they insane? Why do baby dinos eat so much damn food, enough for a hundred dinos? Why are dinos such a statistic devoid of life? Why do wolves get a packleader aura and hunt in packs, but not Utahraptors? Where the hell is my pizza? Why am I such a failure? Why are there 4 T-Rexes outside my door ON A SNOWY MOUNTAIN?

Review based on current price and from the perspective of an average player who does not have access to a private server.
If you are thinking about buying the game at £50 or even the £30 on like cdkeys etc, to play public servers, don't do it.
Firstly the game is like a job, there are litrally "chores to do" feeding dinos, restocking generators, restocking torches and so on, if you don't do this regualrly you tames will all die, your food and resources will spoil  and people will attack your undefended base, so there is a mandatory sign in every 3 days really, although if you want to keep your stuff you would be made to ever leave it that long.
However the main problem with this game is it takes forever to acheve anything and others but a moment to extiguish it. After about the 3rd or 4th time of getting utterly wipped while offline I personally gave up (if you are of any reasonable standing at all, an I'm talking you have made a single shot gun kind of level) you will never ever ever get some PVP all PVP is on this game is someone C4's their way into you base, an destorys everything you have.
I don't know why the dev's continually pump out videos of the tech level gear (future weapons and mech suits for dino's) as this is litrally for the 0.1% you will never ever get the amount of element required to do what they show on a public server, ever.
My advice if you want to play this game, you have to have a private server, put gather up to at least x3, same for taming, maybe even x5 for that and breeding, an then actually have some fun and do some of the stuff you have seen mad pictures of.
In summary the best comparison I can give is the greek story of Sisyphus, who was forced o roll an immense boulder up a hill, only to watch it come back to hit him, repeating this action for eternity. This is what this game is, it's immense labour for hours and hours and hours, but there is a ticking clock to when someone will come and reset your work for you, as there is absolutly no way to prevent someone just C4 wiping you.
On private servers I'd probably give this 7/10, this loses points purely because the game is still grind, the devs idea of quality game play hours seems to be, just getting you to repeat the same non-fun action over and over again, but the problem is, if you just spawn in what you want, the game loses all meaning, it would have been far better if there were simple means for building quickly and you had to complete missions (which they already have, caves) to collect nessesary  materials for equipment. It just makes no sense to me that you would have a mechanism for colelcting resource, activly and purposefully be a bore, we are here to have fun no?

La Rockstar ci ha sempre regalato titoli validi e saghe apprezzabili (anche se un po' ripetitive). Solitamente ci si aspetterebbe di trovarsi nei panni del criminale ma non in questo caso. L.A. Noire è un bel poliziesco in stile hard-boiled, intrigante nella storia principale e nella costruzione del protagonista che ci viene presentato da subito come uno zelante poliziotto in rapida ascesa. Così tra rapine, omicidi e semplici reati da strada, verremo scarrozzati in giro per la grande Los Angeles con lo scopo di ripulire la città e tenerla al sicuro dal crimine, ma non sempre il crimine è tutto nelle strade, a volte si trova anche in posti in cui la polizia ha tutto l'interesse a non calpestare...e lo scopriremo giocando.
I punti forti di questo gioco sono una trama ben costruita, lo stile molto azzeccato per l'ambientazione post-bellica ed un protagonista ben caratterizzato a cui ci affezioneremo presto. Punti deboli? Un po': i personaggi di contorno sono meri stereotipi, le missioni secondarie sono ripetitive e ben presto stancano, risulta difficile dunque arrivare ad un 100% di completezza senza qualche sbuffo di noia, le dinamiche di gioco sembrano essere più quelle di GTA che di un poliziesco...nel senso, risulterà molto più facile fare danni e fallire nelle missioni che riuscire a fare tutto con ordine, in certe situazioni ci troveremo di fronte a dei veri e propri ostacoli impossibili da superare o messi lì ad arte per farci fallire miseramente. Posso capire il fatto di non rendere facile la soluzione di un caso, ma costruire un gioco che ti porta più al fallimento che al successo...mi lascia un po' confuso.
Nel complesso tuttavia, un gioco godibile e consigliato se lo vedete negli sconti fateci un bel pensiero non ve ne pentirete.

I was at first excited to play this game, I had seen videos on youtube and thought it would be fun. Well, its not.
Overall: 2/10
Pros first (short list):
-Fair Graphics for no visual lag.
-Fairly easy controls for all that you can do.
-Tons of servers to play on.
Cons (long list):
-The games physics as relates to bows is a joke, base-line bows of the time had much better distance and travel time on arrows.
-Lengths of weapons are not properly simulated, Classes with the heaviest armor seem to be the weakest (Note on history: anyone in that time period who wore that level of armor was raised to be a soldier from a really young age, they could realitively easily scale walls in full body armor and their weapons, this game fails to simulate that.)
-Mapping as for running and slashing is fine, but the Archer class is highly ignored in the designs with a massive lack of elevated areas to shoot from, as was the case in history in defence situations with Archers using walls, towers and rooftops.
-Armor ranking seems to mean next to nothing between the classes.
-While friendly damage is expected, the penalties for it I found rather stupid given archers always end up hitting friendlies (been on both ends of the bow.)
-Team killing/wounding is a common and idiotic happening in this game and commonly makes for failed team matches. Specially when 80% of your teams on FFA right outside the spawn.
There is a much longer list of things I found that makes this game undesirable to play, but I dont feel like its worth the time writing that much out.
In short: If you know anything about history and/or have held/used the real weapons, dont play this game. If you just love seeing tons of gore and blood and dont really care at all about a game being based on a historical time period being inaccurate as heck, then I would suggest this is a game for you.

Space Ninja Capitalism.
There's a weird niche in this game that brings me back to what I loved about Diablo 2. It's the scenario having a bunch of garbage you pawned off so you could trade up for that big thing and then splatter maps with it, then you decide to make other things and keep doing this. One day you get bored, but you come back and all that stuff is still there (until D2 started deleting accounts for w/e reason).
There's also a factor in this game that's insanely hard to explain to new and fresh players. You probably won't get immediatly sucked into the gameloop because you are at a huge disadvantage out of the box. The starting guns are awful, everything seemingly costs a billion resources that you can't get and I can't even argue that looking at a shop full of things for real money looks a bit filthy. The starting mission types aren't progressive enough. The tutorials are awful and I only recently learned how melee actually works. It's impossible to understand that the game gets insanely fast paced, but also slows back down for a more tactical style later for higher end stuff. There's a bunch of hidden areas and literally whole hidden game systems that aren't revealed at first. You can also turn into a freaking Gundam and blow up crap in space which is honestly hit and miss, but a very fun time when it's hitting. So yeah... if you do a few missions and count this game out, you either decided the game wasn't for you which is fair, but also you didn't really see "the game", which is ... hard to steer people into that really want instant gratification. Also plat is obtainable in many ways once you get rolling. No you won't have a huge plat roll very fast, but with some patience and ripping off seasoned/lazy players you can stack it up. (Hence the D2 trading thing I was goign on about)
That said, give it some time to rise above that and the grind may consume you as it has so many Tenno. There's "end game" stuff to do but really this game excels in being a giant sandbox that has bread crumbs to certain areas but is perfectly fine with you one shotting level 5 mobs for polymer bundles if that's your thing or do level 100 stuff with organized groups (your level is only 30 max so that's the power creep in a numbered example). You can endlessly tweak your playstyles and frames and yes, you'll exhaust options one day but DE is pretty regular with introducing new things to try and with 30+ frames and tons of weps already, there's a wealth of time dump for new players. It's just a blast to me to see a virtual economy that's completely player controlled and how insanely well balanced they made in-game purchases, yet also limited the situation of just buying the best thing in the game and instantly getting to use it at level 0, hour 1.
It's a niche game that's hard to explain. To some it's just mashing space+ctrl and gunning to the end of the levels, but for many the numbers aren't high enough and capitalism takes hold. You're gunna have to work to see the end of the Void and there's no sugar coating it. It's very flawed in some areas, but it's hard for me to play other games now because the action of Max Payne bullet jumping everywhere and throwing giant ice comets, etc at stuff is way too far up my alley. Add a slice of cyberpunk to your space opera shooter and we have an insanely cryptic delight of a game... that I can't stress enough isn't for everyone.

So i moved on to other games, but when i met with 2 others that played ark, i decided to come back, we went to 3 different servers, all unofficial, and settled on a quiet server, only one other tribe we knew of, and we had allied with them, we logged off, 2 days later i came back, and they had killed us, all our dinos, and took all our stuff, while allied. They then left the server with thier base fortified enough so we couldnt get anything back. eventually, we killed all of thier dinos and stole our gear back, and took some of thiers. and again we settled. 2 months later another tribe joins, a massive group of people who make a massive stone base in minutes, it was unofficial with 7x rates so stone wasnt suprising, but they had rexes, a huge stone base, like it was MASSIVE, in a few days, and they outnumbered us 3 to 1, in an effort to keep the peace, i gave them our ♥♥♥♥♥iest ascendant gear, that way we could still defend ourselves if they decided to attack, they didnt, and eventually we became good friends with thier tribe.
That was a long time ago, one of the origional members of my tribe went renegade, and caused chaos in the server, getting him a ban from the owner of it. I still play, most of my other friends dont, and the admin is always watching to make sure that no trolls join who raid just to see others rage, if you are raided once, and it was a legitimate pvp raid to take your stuff, no tricks, no alliances, no offline raiding, then they arent a troll and arent under fire from the admin, but if you raid, just to blow someone elses♥♥♥♥♥♥up, then the admin keeps on your tail for the rest of the time your on his server. Fast paced hard core medieval combat. Chivalry MW, has both team based game-play and a free for all mode.
Team base missions are separated into objectives that can be individually won or lost, culminating in a total score
at the end. Team based Death match is a bloody rush to destroy the other team, with front line attackers guards and ranged combat all worked into the attack plan.
The Free for All is... bloody terrifying and fast passed, trust no-one and watch your head.
Free for all offers the fast passed environment that people have come to know from Arena M.M.O.F.P.S.
The combat system is uniquely suited to this type game, You start out with a few weapons and as you use them you unlock more and better weapons. Combat is more then just swinging a sword around in C.M.W. each attack is based on timing and movement allowing for a flowing smooth combat with a real combatant feel. shields can be bashed and weapons parried as well as surprise attacks and feints. The combat system is easy to learn but takes time to master giving you ample hours of game play.
Chivalry Is one of the best game I have ever played, fulfilling a need for Medieval combat in a way no other game has been able to. Try it out have fun and watch your head.

While the theme is a little outlandish, this game is definetly worth the price tag. The only exception is that it requires a bit of a beefy computer to run smooth on higher settings. Every dinosaur is different in terms of color and statistics. This makes hunting for the higher level creatures much more enjoyable, as it is more of a challenging quest to delve into deeper parts of the island, which consequently are more dangerous. There is a tremendous sense of accomplishment once you have a fortress alongside a team of dinosaurs, each with unique abilities and uses. They are your construction equipment, security, friends and tools. Getting anything done without them is near impossible. And while PvP is just like every other game with killing on sight, base raiding, and the thrill of a vast yet limited space to hold battles in. This game is fun for a long time by yourself on single player, but really shines playing in a group of friends. I recommend getting this with a few people, as the land itself is harsh enough without strangers ripping your walls off with a Tyranosaurous. Slight bugs are very rare, and it's nice to see the developers working in some new material on a regular basis. 9/10

Now, my hours on this game is very minimal because I idle a lot on this game, as well as most of my playtime has been offline.
At first glance, Clicker Heroes looks like a game that doesn't have much depth. It's a game where you click monsters, kill them, and get gold to buy upgrades for heroes that give you more damage output. Simple, right? Well, not so much.
Within just a few hours of playing this game, I had already found that I actually had to look up guides to make this game more efficient. By using your Ascension power from unlocking Amenhotep, you'll soft restart the game and it will give you hero souls. Those are very important as they give you abilities such as purchasing Ancients, which will boost your DPS based on your playstyle (idle, active, or hybrid). These Ancients carry their abilities through Ascensions, which is incredibly useful for giving your next runthroughs a much-needed boost.
After just a few hours, I had already found that this game has much more depth than it seems, and the feeling of getting a lot of Hero Souls each run (which may last a few days for early runthroughs) is so incredibly satisfying, because you know it's really going to help.
There's a goal in this game. Yes, you can play through the levels as far as you'd like, but most people consider the game finished when you've gotten every possible achievement. And even then, people still keep playing.
Seriously, the first runthrough (you should aim for about level 140 then) will take 3 - 5 days, but once you've gone through this process many many times and have levelled up your Ancients several times, just imagine shortening that process of 3 - 5 days to get to level 140 to 10 minutes to get to level 2000. It's unreal.
I highly recommend this game as a way to casually pass the time, idle for a few days, or furiously click away and ruin your mice one by one.
It's completely free, so you have nothing to lose!

As a F2P game, the grind in this game is not as much as I expected it would be, most items could drop after a reasonable amount of attempts, though to be fair some aspect of the game need insane amount of grinding (like the rivens). After 2500 plus game hours, I almost own every frame/weapon in the game except founder items. Any game could keep one playing for this long is not a bad game by any standard. But I have to say it does have many issues, namely a rough new player experience (though they have been trying to make it better over the years), repetitive gameplay, lack of challenge (though it might be by design, in order to give you a space ninja power fantasy, which is a good thing). You will feel burnt out at some point depends on your tolerance of the grind and lacking new content between updates. But the core horde shooting mechanics is sound, which is the reason I keep coming back to play more of it, and if you could find some friends to play together, it would be even more of a blast and keep you interested longer. This game deserves more recognition.

You get one life. One chance to enjoy yourself as much as you can before it ends. There are, accessible to you right now, magical fantasy universes, cutthroat competitive experiences, and a huge library of games filled with everything imaginable. So, don't for a second consider wasting any of your singular chance at life playing this "game," because there is no real entertainment value here. There is no story, no characters, no intruiging gameplay, and there is no purpose to anything you do in this game. You just sit there and you click the screen infinitely.
The only factor that keeps this game relevant at all is that - although it is remarkably monotonous - it is insanely addictive. Many lucky people, like myself, will launch it, instantly realize how senseless it is, and uninstall it. But, many unlucky people will get addicted and become practically paralyzed in their chair, doomed to waste away hundreds of hours trapped in an endless blackhole of clicking. All these people are sitting there, not really even enjoying themselves, and wishing they could stop. You could easily end up as one of those people if you download this game. For that reason, I would recommend clicking away from this page immediately and not so much as giving it a try.
Remember, you get one life. This is not how you want to spend any of it.

Well, 2,300+ Hours on the PC version, I suppose that qualifies me to talk about the game and what I like and don't.
Detailed Review Ahead.
The Good:
- It's quite the beautiful game, very detailed and innovative with how it goes about upgrading its look and feel. It always tries to optimize its visuals in ways that don't damage people playing on less powerful computers. From art, to lighting, to music and sound it all gets upgraded over-time which is good on them for being mindful of presentation.
- I very much enjoy the game play of it, it feels fluid and natural and overall fun. It's a 3rd person shooter that has you participating in various missions to accomplish distinct goals and obtain items.
- Supports & endorses community made designs through its "TennoGen" program. Allowing artists to create skins for Warframes and Weapons that get voted on to be added to the game. TennoGen rounds are done multiple times in the year and offer very high quality skins to be created.
- Very active among its playerbase with community interaction on all its media outlets. Community Team works on weekly streams for PC (PrimeTime), Xbox1 @1 (Xbox), and PS4 @4 (PS4). It also hosts a bi-weekly devstream to see the heads of departments sit down for 1 hour and discuss current ideas floating around, concepts, answering community questions, hearing feedback, etc.
- Generous with its cash currency (platinum). It can be traded among players in-game, log-in rewards have a chance to provide the player with coupons good for 20%, 50%, or 75% off that allow for a player looking to buy platinum to obtain it at very affordable pricing. You even start with 50 platinum when you create an account.
- Not at all to be considered 'pay2win'. In reality, most of the core content (weapons/warframes) can be farmed in-game for any free to play player, you can even sell items you obtain on the marketplace for platinum of your own (which is a well-known and often endorsed activity). The only items that directly cost money would be TennoGen cosmetics (these deduct funds from your Steam wallet). The money is divided between the player who created the skin, Steam/Valve, and the developers (Digital Extremes). At worst you can consider it 'pay2getfaster'.
- Community is actually very active, very populated, and overall quite nice. Can't say I've encounter much negativity, in fact the opposite. Lots of players are very helpful and willing to lend a hand. That's not to say that everyone is sunshine and rainbows, but it's not a case of a bad apple ruining a bunch either. You'll encounter some bad-mannered players like you would in any game but you'll likely encounter more helpful players than not.
The Mixed:
Lore: Although it has a very interesting story-line and presentation to said storyline, it often relies heavily upon the players themselves to piece it all together from the various lore sources in the game. Oftentimes have plot-holes appeared that made us question certain things and some things seem to just contradict. It has recently started using cinematics for more important quests (The Second Dream & The War Within) which have gone a way in helping overall presentation of lore but it's still a bit shaky. This is more of a mixed impression on tying lore together as opposed to a mixed impression of the lore itself. The lore itself is fantastic, there are various lore sources in-game (Codex, Quests, Scannable fragments, Events, etc). It's just tying it all together and having all parts make sense is a bit shaky. It is improving though I will say that much.
Varied Gameplay: I know I praised the game-play above and it is still rather fun and the like but this one is aimed more towards diversity. There's the normal various gameplay modes available in the starchart, PvP elements (Conclave), and an alternative PvE mode called Archwing (Flying around in space). The various gameplay modes normally available around the clock are numerous but also somewhat redundant. I'm struggling to really emphasize what I wish to say, but it feels as if you find yourself doing the same thing a lot. The Conclave and Archwing are kind of a joke and most of us don't really bother with it. There's been improvements made recently toward diversifying gameplay by adding missions that have a bit more to them than normal ones such as "Fissure" missions, "Kuva" missions, or the "Sortie" missions which add another element of gameplay in an existing game-type. There's still some styles of missions that feel as if they have no purpose and are just kind of there. Recent events have brought new game modes which have been enjoyable. Operation: Pacifism Defect brought a very nice and fun mission type but it's "event-only" so it disappeared after the event ended which is kind of a bummer.
Rewards:
A point of contention perhaps, dependent on player. Some mission types or formats don't feel rewarding enough for the time involved. Rewards are set on a rotation basis and after you complete a rotation (AABC), it feels as if there's diminishing rewards because content gets harder and you go back to the beginning in terms of rewards. You intentionally make a mission harder as time goes on but the rewards don't get better. It doesn't scale in other words, there's no reason to stay longer if the rewards aren't getting better after you finish a rotation. The "Sortie" missions are a daily series of 3 missions that have randomized special conditions and tend to be more difficult than normal gameplay. Which would be great except the rewards you can get from the table shown after completing Sortie Mission #3 have been subject to debate and memes. There are good and even great rewards and then there are rewards that players feel are redundant, worthless, and unappealing and its those rewards that you tend to get the most which leads to a feeling of "why do I even do this" (but its a good feeling when you get the better rewards). Then there's the isolated mission nodes that have fantastic rewards and people play those lootcaves and feel good after a rotation. There's Fissure missions that offer you the usual rewards of the game mode, additional rewards because of its "Fissure" nature, and free multiplier boosters to offer an incentive to stay longer.  These in-mission boosters award extra Credits (in-game currency), Affinity (experience) and more Resources. So you feel good because you leave the mission well-rewarded and you leave with "prime" items.
On the subject of drops from enemies, there's the very common things you'll soon find 100's of and then the rare things you'll be lucky as heck to get. The model of the game tends to try to find the balance between gametime and platinum. Therefore (like in most games) grinding for the stuff you want can be a huge pain in the back or it can go smoothly. RNG amirite?
The Bad:
- Content "droughts". The game does update on a weekly basis with skins, a weapon or two, fixes, stuff like this but the game goes months without a lack of engaging content. There comes a point where you have most of the things you want and you end up asking yourself "what now?". I may have an extensive playtime but even I take regular interval "breaks" and await the juicy updates that bring new quests, warframes, gameplay elements. The game tends to have Big Update -> series of smaller updates -> Big Updates -> repeat. The series of smaller updates tend to last months while the content for the bigger updates is assembled. It just feels like there's nothing to do atm so you leave and then come back later (which is what I find myself doing on occasion). I don't quite want to call it burnout so to say. Don't misunderstand, there's TONS of content for new players.
There's some room to say that some of the stuff I have on "mixed" could go under bad but this is just how I would describe my experience with Warframe thus far.
Overall I'd give it a 9/10, you should try it! Enjoy and have fun Tenno

With nearly 1300 hours of ARK experience under my belt, I can still say I have a love-hate relationship with the game.  I have many hours where my gaming is down time, relaxation, meant to be chill.  In these times where I'm using my gaming energies to recharge my personal batteries, I'm likely to roam the map, maintain a base, add a room on to a building or make some useful supplies or ammo.
Then there are my more energetic hours, where I'm collaborating with tribe members, taming dinos, and working towards progressive content.
ARK can be, in a word - hard.  It can be unforgiving.  It's because of the game's diversity and range of activities that I keep coming back.
It's a classic in my mind, balancing build at the medium block level, with beautiful graphics, and on occasion, terror-filled events because some dino has jumped out from behind its proverbial rock.  I'll be playing ARK for a long time and enjoying its diversity, challenges and its low-key moments as much as the boss fights and advancment towards ascension. When I'm done there, I might even go PvP a little. :)
If you like hard survival games that have multiple layers of depth, you'll like ARK.

When i first played this game i really enjoyed it. It's something about surviving in the early stages of the game that's really fun, however after a while everything becomes repetitive and boring. It'll take up a lot of your time to ever reach to a level where you have a strong base and a great collection of dinosaurs. You'll have to play the game constantly! If you're not in a tribe, you won't be able to build a large base. It will just take to much time. Playing on official servers i constantly experienced a lot of lagg, which is also very annoying.
My solution was to go and host my own unofficial dedicated server, where i would beef up some of the experience gained and the amount of resources gathered. Sadly the server won't show up in the unofficial servers list in ARK. I work with servers and networks for a living, however i wasn't able to fix this problem. Tried multiple times to contact support of Studio Wildcard and survivetheark, they either gave me no reply or an automated can't help you reply. Customer support is terrible!! I would never recommend a game that costs 60 euros without any type of support when you need it.
I still like to play this game from time to time, however that will be on my own dedicated server. People are able to join through the steam servers list or from the website
. But without the server showing up in the unofficial list it's impossible to get a good gaming community going. When reading forums, it even seems rented gameservers won't show up in the servers list most of the time.
If you don't mind a bit of lagg, want to play on official servers with friends in a tribe, don't want to host a server for yourself and have a good computer which can handle unoptimized games. Then you could enjoy this game.
If you don't want lagg, want to host your own gameserver and expect atleast a notable response from customer support. Then you don't want this game.
Final verdict: Not recommended!

It's a good concept, but Studio Wildcard's handling of the production of this game is neutral at best. They continue to add content to a game that is suffering under bugs and systems that promote unhealthy and unrealistic expectations of gameplay. When the best fix that the community can offer is to subvert the official gameplay, perhaps the official gameplay has an inherent problem. I love the idea, and I feel that there is a huge amount of potential here. However, at this time, I can not recommend this game.

Ark is a game that depends a lot on if you can find a friendly server and people to play with, since being a solo person tribe can be really challenging for beginners and veterans alike. On official servers its impossible to play alone I feel, since levelling, farming and taming takes so long that it just isnt worth it. I think its the best to find an unofficial server with enhanced rates, but then you have the problem of unstable servers and uninvolved admins.
I was lucky to find a servercluster owned by someone who really cares. Yes, he takes donations but keep in mind that hosting a server costs real time money so i feel its only fair since he is online at least 3 hours every day, and he even added me on steam so we can approach him when people are breaking the rules. I've been on countless servers where unanounced server wipes wiped my max lvl imprinted rexes, or where the server uptime is less then 50 percent. Also the only time me and my friends joined a pvp server we got bullied by one of the alpha tribes because we were active on the server and they didnt like that we might overtake them if we kept going.
I think ARK is totally playable, but not very friendly to new players. My tip? buy the game together with a friend and start playing together on an unofficial server. Ask for help from the more experienced players. My tribe would give away our low lvl tames and bad hatches to new players on the server. Some people might call this cheating, but games are supposed to be fun, right? I think that the more experienced players on the servers should be a little bit more mindfull of noobies.
Off course there still is the problem with how the game runs but since I don't have a top notch pc I have learned to cope with my 20 frames a long time ago. I think the game is fun and playable, but I might be biased since I was initiated in a tribe that knew the game well, and I never played alone until I had over 200 hrs experience. Don't buy this game if you like to play survival games alone, you might be better off buying a game like subnautica.

TL;DR: Bite the bullet and pay for a private server with your buddies if you want to have any fun.
In the newest trailer for ARK, a naked man awakes on a beach with no idea what the hell is going on. Seconds later, he's killed by a woman riding a raptor and wielding an AK-47 simply for the crime of existing. While this was a wonderful cinematic that was meant to promote the game positively, it incidentally showed potential players the single WORST part of the game and the reason you should avoid it entirely.
Unless you're planning on playing on a private server with friends, which will cost you at least $15 a month, you're guaranteed to only enjoy playing ARK if you get incredibly lucky. And I mean -incredibly- lucky. You may even find better luck on public servers if you have a friend who's got 5,000+ hours in game and can supply you with everything to get started. I've tried no less than 24 times to start fresh on public servers, and here's just a sampling of the things that've happened to me:
- Chased down by a three men riding Tyrannosaurs because I tried harvesting fiber on "their beach"

All in all, it is the pinnacle of what survival games are and can be.

I have played this game for 1200+ hours.  I loved this game when I first started and it has (maybe had with Anthem on the horizon) potential.  DE (Digital Extremes) DOES NOT tell you in game where to find anything in game except buy it from ingame currency (platinum).  That means that you HAVE to use the wiki in order to figure out where to find the drop rates and locations of every item in game.  Now the big problem is that they have recently filled a lawsuit against the dataminer Void_Glitch.  Thanks to his work the wiki has any information and you can play the game and enjoy it.  If the wiki did not exist you COULD NOT play this game.  There would be no way to find out how to play certain missions to get a certain item or kill a certain enemy (there are more than a few items that only drop from one enemy) to get an item/mod.  If DE didn't make the users look for the information on how to play their game then there would be no need for datamining.  If you don't think this is a big deal then play the game from scratch and try to figure out how to start quests or get parts for more frames without haveing to spend hundreds of dollars to get ahead in the game.

When I first got this game it was very early in the Early Access process and to be honest, it sucked. Graphics were pretty but the game was buggy, ran terrible, and just simply was not fun. I shelved it.
So I came back a month or so ago as it was out of EA and I figured... it has to be better now right? Besides, I'm all down for Minecraft + dinos! Thankfully I was right, it is bettter... in almost every single way and the things I didn't especially like? I could adjust the config for most of them. Sweet!
That said, there's still some pros and cons I'll quickly go over:
Good:
- Tame dinos! Ride a t-rex! RAWR!
- You can get your build on
- Workshop support and heavily moddable / configurable
- Graphics are purdy
- Controller support if you're in to that sort of thing
- Supports Oculus Rift [haven't tried it personally yet]
Bad:
- Default settings can be extremely grindy. Thankfully this can be adjusted quite a bit.
- I'm running the game on a GF 1080 and it runs great with no stutter. Problem is, I'm on a 1080 to get that performance. If you don't have a beast rig you may have issues running the game. This is literally the new Crysis. Devs haven't done much in the way of optimization sadly. I ran it on a 770 when I played the first time and it was very bad.
- No terrain editing. Want to dig a hole? You can't. Terrain is completely unalterable other than trees and random boulders you can smash for resources.
- Suffers from same sandbox survival game issues as everything else in the genre, eventual boredom unless you really like building
- Official servers can be a mess, granted this is true of most any game
- Primitive Plus total conversion that ships with the game is a disaster which is a shame because it has a ton of potential if WC ever fixes it
- Devs can be... hit and miss
Ugly:
- The snap building system makes me want to take my own life
Weird:
- Devs seem to like picking up community-made items and bundling with the game. This is how Ragnarok came about as well as Primitive Plus. I hope they tossed some coin at those folks.
So do I recommend it? Yes with the caveats above. The free DLC added a great couple maps, especially Ragnarok, which vastly improves upon the first EA map, The Island. Future DLC promises to add even more things and there is a season pass you can get tho it is $$$ on top of a game being sold as a AAA title. I got it in EA when it was like $10 so I have no room to complain and will be getting the season pass most likely soon.  Like most survival games, you can play it single player but it is better with friends and fully supports both PvP and PvE so you can do what you like.

Rockstar have done it again. They've created another game with a richer story than you'd get from a modern Hollywood blockbuster.
They combined it with a new style of game. L.A. Noire tells the story of Cole Phelps, an LAPD detective in post-war Los-Angeles. While the game has the same look and feel of GTA IV and Red Dead Redemption.
L.A. Noire's gameplay is completely different. Gone is the ability to shoot up the average passer-by; as Cole Phelps, you're a good cop in a world of corruption. Instead of pumping lead into the criminals, you now have to coerce information and confessions out of them. Suspects must be interrogated in order to open up new avenues for you to investigate. This game takes a bit of brainpower and skill in order to read whether your suspect is telling the truth, or if they're trying to serve you a plate full of stinking lies. Revolutionary, refreshing and compelling. L.A. Noire will keep you hooked as long as you can appreciate it for what it is.

That said, it's linearity actually felt like a break from the daunting sandboxes of GTA IV and Red Dead Redemption, and its focus on investigation and dialogue evokes the feel of old-school adventure games. The combat felt tacked on, but the car chases were probably my favorite sections, and I found myself wishing there had been more of them. The game's touted facial animation technology is indeed impressive, and the dialogue mostly well-writen, giving the game a true cinematic quality. It has a few story elements I could have done without, but there's a few sequences- the trail of riddles left by the Black Dahlia murderer, the shootout at the movie set, the entire Nicholson Electroplating case- that made the tedium of the overall length of the game feel somewhat worthwile.

I've played it for over 400 hours and I still have so much left to do. The game is just absolutely gorgeous to look at and well made in my opinion. This game is essentially what you'd get when you cross a 3rd Person Action game like "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City" with a Point & Click Mystery game like "Art of Murder: FBI Confidential". The story is very character driven rather than plot. Lots of clue finding and enough shooting action to keep you awake.
The highlight of the game are the interrogation scenes. Usually game developers will create a 3D mesh of an actor's skull including mouth, teeth and eyeballs. In L.A Noire, I'm not 100% sure, but it looks like they've kept oldschool and recorded the actor's facial expressions into a moving texture, baked and then bumped mapped it on a 3D model of the original actor. Personally I found it misleading.

Not many games can capture the essence of a time period, but this game absolutely nails it. Its riveting dialogue sequences kept me on the edge of my seat hanging at the end of every superbly written piece of dialogue which the perfect voice acting simply enhances. The facial motion capture technology makes the characters feel genuinely real and would be half the game without it. You sincerely care for the characters with this beautiful combination of writing, voice acting, and motion capture.
In this day and age of copy cats and cash-ins, Team Bondi and Rockstar took quite the risk, and for that alone I seriously respect their glorious effort to produce this refreshingly original and fantastic game. If you're looking for a story-driven action adventure game with a deep and compelling crime drama story, or if you're just looking for something new, then this game will complete you.

First off, L.A. Noire is one of the most amazing games I've ever played.
The game starts off with renovating gameplay being shoved down your throat with great, well planned scenenarios to play through and very entertaining interviews. The dialog in this game is top notch. You will experience every emotion your character is experiencing with the extremely convincing voice acting and ground breaking camera technology utilizing 32 cameras to capture every angle on the actors face, directly porting it over ingame.
Story wise, you always have cases with big twists and the occasional rather droll mission, but it generally stays top notch with very deep character qualities which really gets you attatched to the characters in the game. Sure, the ending may not have been the best but it still manages to be a very amazing game and should be checked out by anyone seeking a mystery thriller game.

This is a dark and controversial detective story taking place in L.A. of 1947. Everyone's a sinner in this game. It's very good at visually, musically and sometimes psychologically resembling the real Los Angeles of that time. The city consists of a couple of connected districts, from Hollywood to the central one. That is enough to make the game world huge. There are 95 types of cars from the most famous manufacturers, like Ford, GMC, Buick and Chevrolet. As for the gameplay, it feels like Mafia II combined with a groundbreaking police detective simulator inspired by well known crimes, such as The Black Dahlia murder. Among the innovations are the amazing facial animations never seen in videogames before. Unlike Mafia II, the game is mainly focused on looking for evidence, interviewing and interrogating people rather than gunfights. At the same time, nobody stops you from entering the Free Roam mode just to drive the cars, look around and prevent street crimes filled with action.

Okay next, the combat. This game is ♥♥♥♥ing broken. High level players can take advantage of really obscure tricks, and I will list of a few I have seen being used in game. For example, I've seen experienced players hit people who are behind them, by aiming up as far as possible and swinging backwards, very much like the infamous Excorcist stair scene
. Another trick involves jumping in the air and kicking the player or kicking their shield out of the way, which stuns the player. This trick is unfair as it barely gives the player time to react when done correctly. Also, instead of the kick, someone can jump and stab a player's head, or jump around them and stab them in their unprotected side, still not giving them any time to react. Another trick (my personal favourite for its extreme ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ttery) involves aiming down as low as possible and crouching when someone swings horizontally at you. This trick will cause the trickster to become impossibly low to the ground and not get hit.
My point is, there isn't much skill involved in the combat unless you play an archer (you actually have to aim, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥, which is the weakest class and will get one shotted by heavier classes. This armour does not cause much of a hinderance to movement speed however, e.g. a Knight or Vanguard can easily chase the Man at Arms class down (who is supposed to be fast).
So, as you get to the higher levels, you better be using those obscure exploits I went through earlier, or you'll be in for a treat (I lied, you'll actually just get jump kicked by a man in full steel armour and then stabbed multiple times because you've been stunned).

I'd say 65 hours of gameplay is enough to write a review, right?
Let me tell you this, Steam, and don't you forget it: This game will ride you like a frickin' horse. You will die. Many, many times you will die. Even the players on the level 0-15 noob servers will kick your♥♥♥♥♥repeatedly. You will struggle to do good, and your first games will be spent trying to keep from sitting at the bottom of the scoreboard and looking like a no-skill idiot.
Aside from the grueling learning curve that makes games like Dark Souls or look like the next Call of Duty, there is heaps of fun to be had in Chivalry.
Let's start with the basics.
MAPS-
Pretty decent design overall. The simplier ones like arena3 or moor are the most fun, especially if you can find a 50-64 player server with decent ping.
GAME MODES-
Standard FPS game modes. Team deathmatch, free-for-all, capture the flag, last team standing (TDM with no respawns), and team objective. I find myself playing FFA more than other online games because, on lower population servers, it's arguably more fun than the team-based games. If you don't mind getting stabbed in the back by some gyroscoping knight♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this is where the lulz are obtained. I vividly remember wordlessly teaming up with some pink pole hammer-wielding stranger to take on the server in jolly co-operation. A couple of the people who saw us charging at their unprotected asses, our weapons poised to mess them up, ended up juming into the lake. We made first and second place.
CLASSES-
Hoo boy, here we go. The four character classes (Archer, Man at Arms, Vanguard, and Knight) are for the most part, fair and balanced in the right hands. Don't be too shocked to see that the vast majority of your team or the enemy's are playing Vanguard. Those ♥♥♥♥s are grossly overpowered by wielding the second most damaging weapons with the longest reach in the game. Unless you're also vanguard, avoid getting into 1v1 situations.
The other three classes are decent. MAA is fast, can dodge around like a friggin' gazelle. Archers can pull of headshots that pops their skulls like melons. Their daggers are OP. Knights are slow, but their weapons are crazy powerful. Expect VGs and Knights to make up the bulk of your team.
CUSTOMIZATION- Not extensive, but pretty cool. You can recolor your team based classes a little (i.e. one side can be colored with blue, white, and gold and the other can be red, black, and brown). FFA coloring is a bit more flamboyant. Don't expect a crazy color wheel full of options, but you can have some fun with it. Expect to find at least person on a FFA server to be strangely commited to the color black. You can also buy character reskins from Torn Banner, but the skins are ugly and cost too much money.
Over all, give Chivalry Eight oil pots out of ten.

L.A. Noire is a fantastic showcase of what technology has in stored for the games of the future. A point-and-click game under the guise of modern AAA titles, Rockstar's latest title is a breath of fresh air and its efforts to revive a dying genre has not gone unappreciated.
The problem with procedural games is that they are too often too narrow. What you may interpret as a piece of incriminating evidence may not be what the developers intend. It's frustrating to see what you would do become limited by what you can do.
The city of Los Angeles, despite being full of life, comes off as a bit... empty. While expansive, there isn't a lot to do. You're limited to collecting hidden goods and solving a handful of street crimes.
What you get out of L.A. Noire ultimately depends on your taste in games and whether or not you're a perfectionist. Obtaining maximum rank on all cases (without walkthroughs) will significantly prolong your play time.
Enjoyable and worth its price? Yes.

A prime example of storytelling done right in a game. With complicated and relatable characters this game immerses you in a fictional yet realistic depiction of the dirty-cop world of the Los Angeles of yesteryear.
The acting is superb, and the full-body motion capture coupled with tbe brilliant facial animation technology makes it feel real in a way no game previous has been able to pull off.
The action is paced and fun, the driving is solid and skippable (if you don't like it), the jokes are funny, the dialogue is well-written and well-executed, and the music and artistic design is spot-on.
The game has an open-world environment, akin to GTA, yet is structured well so that the player never feels lost, or bored, or just wandering around. The addition of well-made "partner" characters help to guide the player while adding depth to every scene, unlike so many "partners" of so many other games that simply get in the way, and contribute minimally to the storyline.

L.A. Noire is a fantastic showcase of what technology has in stored for the games of the future. A point-and-click game under the guise of modern AAA titles, Rockstar's latest title is a breath of fresh air and its efforts to revive a dying genre has not gone unappreciated.
The problem with procedural games is that they are too often too narrow. What you may interpret as a piece of incriminating evidence may not be what the developers intend. It's frustrating to see what you would do become limited by what you can do.
The city of Los Angeles, despite being full of life, comes off as a bit... empty. While expansive, there isn't a lot to do. You're limited to collecting hidden goods and solving a handful of street crimes.
What you get out of L.A. Noire ultimately depends on your taste in games and whether or not you're a perfectionist. Obtaining maximum rank on all cases (without walkthroughs) will significantly prolong your play time.
Enjoyable and worth its price? Yes.
Grade: B

A prime example of storytelling done right in a game. With complicated and relatable characters this game immerses you in a fictional yet realistic depiction of the dirty-cop world of the Los Angeles of yesteryear.
The acting is superb, and the full-body motion capture coupled with tbe brilliant facial animation technology makes it feel real in a way no game previous has been able to pull off.
The action is paced and fun, the driving is solid and skippable (if you don't like it), the jokes are funny, the dialogue is well-written and well-executed, and the music and artistic design is spot-on.
The game has an open-world environment, akin to GTA, yet is structured well so that the player never feels lost, or bored, or just wandering around. The addition of well-made "partner" characters help to guide the player while adding depth to every scene, unlike so many "partners" of so many other games that simply get in the way, and contribute minimally to the storyline.
I would rather drag my balls across a mile of salty sandpaper and dip them in lemon juice than play this game.

Only a few survival games that are worth recommendation in my book.  For me, I've learned that games worth playing are not necessarily perfect games but ones whose gameplay and content far outweigh the problems.  So as you'd guess I'm not going to say Ark is a perfect game by no means but what keeps me playing is the draw of the world.  Take my review as one from the perspective of a builder.
Granted, the building has it's downfalls and can be a bit glitchy at times, I'll be honest but it really is pretty open to your creativity.  There are a lot of different ways you can approach building in this game and so many mods that you can make the game fit your own needs and style.  I run with  S+  (a must for builders)   Extinction Core, and a few others myself.
The dinos you're able to find and tame are many.  You'd be hard pressed to find all of them and/or tame them.   So if you're a collector of sorts it should keep you busy a good while.  Something about being able to bring "pets"home to your base, is a really big draw also.
I highly recommend this game along with it's sister game, Dark and Light, although the latter one I would be less inclined to give it as much of a glowing review as ark because of it's early stage in development.
So after 352+ hours of game time I will add something to this review.  I won't change my opinion on this game, only add to it the amazing number of mods and customization included in this game is mind blowing.  Even if you don't find the vanilla version of the game outstanding, I'd be surprised if there wasn't a mod or two to spark the interest in the game well after you've spent many hours playing.  Mods including things from new dinos, game changing overhauls, maps and building parts.  There's literally something to cover just about every aspect of the game.

Team Bondi and Rockstar Leeds' debut game is one of the best 2011 games I have played.  This detective game makes fantastic use of revolutionary facial animation technology in order to find clues an information for a vast amount of cases.  The music works amazingly well with the game, giving suspense thrilling moments.  The music is done so well, that even while questioning suspects and witnesses the slight change in music and tone automatically lets you know you screwed up.  The story is very immersive as this "dark and violent crime thriller"'s story unfolds.
This PC port has some downsides though.  While the facial and other animations are great, the textures are noticablly low resolution.  Also, at times, the lips will get a little buggy and blurs will be seen in the lips.  However, it is to be expected with new technology.  Despite these hickups, this 20 hour game is definitly worth your $50.

Phew. What an engrossing game! I highly recommend it! The story, while not as good as Ellroy's novels, seems as it if was ripped straight off the pages of L.A. Confidential, Black Dahlia and  Big Nowhere. The police chief advocated violence and peppers his speeches to Phelps with 'boyo' -- the Elysian fields, Captain Donnelly's lingo paralleing the Irish lit of James Cromwell. There are even gratuitious references to Johnny Stompanato, the Black Dahlia and Veronica Lake. None of which are exclusive to Ellroy novels but come on, he built many of his stories around those characters and events. You also have the WWII flashback angle which strongly resembles Edmond Exley's backstory in the L.A. Confidential book. The short version: If you ever wanted to play out a James Ellroy novel, this game is a must!

Warframe is a bit of a mixed bag for me. I've had moments were I really loved it and there have been numerous moments where I've wanted to smash my desk with a sledgehammer.
I'll just write a short and simple review.
Combat - 8/10
Really satisfying and fast. But the late game can get stressful and too hectic.
Movement - 7/10
Mostly same as above, but what brings it down a bit is the numerous enemies that kill your momentum and the Co-op elements.
Multiplayer - 5/10
Great in the beginning but it really gets dragged down in the higher levels where all players just speed around the map to the objectives and it starts to feel more like a speedrun. I always found it annoying when people would just race past enemies and do all these exploits just to get through the level faster and I would struggle to keep up.
Story - ?/10
I don't have much to say since the story is unfinished, but the little that I've seen thus far is pretty interesting.
Visuals - 8,5/10
Absolutely stunning. The lighting really makes the game. It's so bright and vivid, and it runs great I might add. And I really like the designs for all the different warframes and cosmetics.
Missions and objectives- 5/10
This is sadly the weakest point of the game. The missions and levels get really repetetive and grindy. And trying to get new gear can sometimes take weeks. (Including build times) This is the part where you're really reminded that this is a F2P game. I would've prefered to pay for a full game with less of a grind since I've already spent way more than 60$ on rushing items and buying cosmetics. I'll add that I'm not a fan of grinding (which is why I've spent so much money on the game.), I know some people are and kudos to you if you're into that stuff but I'm not.
Keep in mind that these are my personal opinions and experiences. Correct me on anything that's wrong and feel free to share your thoughts with me.

There are constant updates, fixes, changes and new content is added regularly which adds a lot of dynamic to the community and the game itself. But above all, the very way you control your character, the very way you play the game, is what makes this a great game.

I really liked this game at the start which makes it hard to vote it down. It was fun, something new and a very interesting idea. 16v16 soldiers, running into the heat of battle screaming random things and then exchanging frantic hits with the enemy only to be smacked and killed by one of your own team is hilarious sometimes. On the other hand the imbalanced gameplay and glitch exploitation make it very easy to vote down. When you start out there are level 0-15 servers which only those levels are alowed to join. It makes a somewhat even playing field because all the new and newish players are all trying to figure out which end of the stick goes in the other guy and are all swinging like crazy just to land a hit and steal a kill. I had many a laugh at how funny the game can be, however after level 15 your only choice is to join the other severs where the new aim of the game is who can exploit the most glitchiest gliches and who can do it faster than the other person exploiting their glitchiest glitch. This exploitation of some stupid game mechanics where your character almost bends backwards while swinging, hitting everything around them while being virtually unhittable became very annoying very fast. This part of the gameplay quickly sucked all the fun out of it. There is also some problems with terrible hit markers which I overlooked at the start because the game was quite fun. You thrust into someone chest but completely miss them and then someone miles away somehow headshots you with a tiny sword. The game is supposed to be unrealistic (its a game, duh) but its also supposed to be fun and after being killed reapeatably by people exploiting these glitches in the game it became a not so fun experience. So if you are buying it with some friends and just want to have a bit of a laugh with them its a good game. If you are buying it to play on the servers i definitely would not recommend this glitch... i mean game :P
