is a game that can either be loved to the point you play hundreds to thousands of hours in a very short amount of time, or be remarkably disliked.
It can be understandable in terms of why someone would dislike playing Warframe when it comes to the
aspect of the game, sometimes it can be very frustrating how many times you have to repeat the same mission over and over to get that one part, that one item. However, there are also players like me whom do find satisfaction in grinding that much, hence Warframe is definitely not for those who have no patience nor pleasure in (excuse the term) working hard to get what you want.
Some might say that Warframe runs a pay-to-win model, looking at the shop, but when we take a deeper look at it there is no actual basis to definite it so. Everything you buy with real-life currency can be obtained without - except, of course, some cosmetic items. Most of what you can purchase with Platinum you can buy with in-game credits too, hence the advantage that Platinum provides is simply getting things done faster.
Warframe unleashes an incredibly high level of optimization! Sure, it requires a good machine in order to run it at high settings, but it is very light and is very, very well optimized. The graphics are stunning, the level of details is incredible. Overall it certainly is a masterpiece to whom, like me, loves playing games with this kind of graphics.
In terms of gameplay and mechanics, I do love the combat system - I'm not exaggerating when I say that it has one of the best movements and combat I've ever had the pleasure to play with. What makes the game very sustainable in a long-term stay is the amount of different 'characters', weapons, missions, bosses and modes Warframe has to offer.
I highly suggest you give
a try - it is free afterall.

Base game contains 4 classes which have all unique weapons and playstyle to keep the game interesting. Keep playing with certain class and a weapon type and kill enemies (other players) to rank up expirience points to unlock new different weapons with different stats. Such as weapon swing speed, reach and base damage. As I mentioned game requires skill and there is no ''overpowered'' weapons. You can dominate anyone with any weapon if you just know how to use it. So you do not have to worry that players that have played the game a long time would have weapon wise a advantage. What they do have, is expirience with the game.
Game has few game modes to choose from. Some are very familiar such as free for all, team deatmatch and capture the flag. Though I personally like team objective missions. These missions have unique objectives which keeps the game interesting and you feel like there is a real battle going on with a purpose behind it. For example you have to light a signal fire to let your fleet to know to move in and open fire on the walls while the other team tries to stop you from doing that. If your able to signal the battle ships they destroy the wall and a new objective is given, destroy the enemy catapults so they won't demolish your fleet that just moved in etc. It's interesting over any regular game modes.
There's plenty of maps to play and as I said team objectives are totally different in each map and they are very fun to play.
Gameplay itself is smooth and responsive, and as I mentioned fast paced so you better not be day dreaming. Keep your guard up and play smart. Remember that your weapon can damage and kill your friends so do not just mindlessly swing your weapon.
Game looks visually nice and has plenty of blood and gore in it. The sounds, death screams, swords colliding with other swords, flesh getting cut, arrows passing by your head sounds awesome and gives the game intense atmosphere when your running into the heat of battle.
Definitely worth the current 22,99 euro price tag.
My score for the game would be a solid 8/10, superb multiplayer expirience.

I have been playing Ark since the begining. I have, unlike most of the other reviewers, over 3100 hours played, and still play the game. It is fun, engauging, terrifying, and awe inspiring. Ark: Survival evolved to me, is in my top 5 games of all time now.
Ark, is more than a survival game, an RP game, or an Open World game. This game has just as much potential, if not more than Mindcraft to me. The graphics are great, but you must have a mid to high end PC to play it. The gameplay is perfect for PvE, and PR. PvP still needs some tweaking on the combat and animations, but that is to be expected with a newer IP. The Optimazations are there now as well.  There is crafting, building, level progression, boss battles, Tribes(guilds), Pets/tames, Dinosuars, Modern Weapons, and Futuristic weapons as well in Ark. In Ark, there is more to keep you going for a long time than most other survival games. Even at $60, it is still a bargan with all the hours of gameplay and fun you will get out of it.
And as the cherry on top, there are over 56k mods for this game right now on the Steam Workshop. And that is growing everyday. There are mods for every type of gameplay you can imagine, and if one is missing, you can create it. Also, there are still 100's of larger mods still in developement. IE Dragonpunk is one of them. Wild Card also has a Sponsored Mods program where they PAY the Modder for great content. Ragnorok was one and was then brought in as an official DLC, and ISO Crystal Isles, S+ and Castles, keeps and Forts, are others int he program now. Those 3 are in the top 40 downloaded mods of all time. Overall, you will never get bored with all the unique and crazy mods that will change your gameplay and challenge your survival instincts.
Wild Card is not "Money Hungry" or "Grabbing for Money". They are a company that makes games that are suppost to be profitable. And this one is. It still ranks in the top 10 most played games on Steam at any given day, and continues to sell well at the current $59.99 price. The game rocks! And it a very enjoyable experience. If you stay away from the Infested Official servers.
Oh, did I mention I am a server owner. I own 4, soon to be 5 Ark servers, and have been hosting Ark servers since it was an available option. And never looked back at the Official negative, grieving, infested Official servers. I can choose what type of gameplay I want on my server, and pick and choose which mods to use. So, hosting is the way to go with this game, or join a good high quality hosted server.
In the end, It is your choice to make. Do not let these negative whiners keep you from experiencing one of the most fun games since Skyrim and Witcher 3. And above all, respect your fellow gamer. You can kill them all you want, but at least respect him or her.

A great experiment with mixed results, the use of face capture technology is very impressive but probably won't age well. Tying the unique tech to an interrogation mechanic is a great idea, though sometimes the interrogations themselves can be frustrating and illogical, even to the point that I'd just restart the mission if it became a wash. Shooting and driving are both passable and functional, except for a frustrating sequence in the finale which involves way more shooting than the rest of the game.
What I love most about this game is its adherence to Noir style, complete with all the backstabbing intrigue that comes with it. Nearly every Noir trope is in full effect here, and there's some truly excellent acting to be found, on par with Hollywood productions, probably because there are a great deal of talented character actors involved that you'll probably recognize from this thing or that. The story is solid and kept me hooked, and its final scene is brilliantly delivered. As with others I've enjoyed, this is a game I recommend not for the strength of its mechanics, but for its "feel", and in terms of making you feel like a hard-boiled Noir detective, you won't find anything better on the market.

This is a unique piece of game. Love the 40-50's era. I have never seen a detective game before and this may be the first one. The gameplay is amazing, ranging from interrogations, car chases, suspect chases and more. Some of which are similar to GTA. Nothing wrong with that. Interrogating is incredible. The facial animation is top notch. You play the game the way you want, whether you think someone is lying, doubt someone or think they are telling the truth. There is only one correct answer for each interrogation though, but the experience you get when you get it wrong is amazing. You can doubt or you can think they are lying. Either way you will have a blast. The gameplay mechanic is just fascinating. You won't be able to stop playing. After you finish a case, you want to keep going. What keeps you going is finding clues and using those clues to help you with interrogation to find out the culprit and do it again for next case. I also love the back story of WW2. Get it!

This game is great.
Warframe is a Massive Multiplayer Online Shooter, with non Pvp elements. The game has a very intresting story. There is an advanced movement system which very well articulates what it feels like to be a ninja. There is enough content that kept me going for ~1000 hours until I had all I needed to do off my plate. This game is also very beautiful, and has very good optimization. The devs hold livestreams often for the community, showing off new content.
However, with these very numerous good things, there are a few bad things. As someone who as poured a lot of time into this game, it DOES get boring. There is not very much endgame. At a certain point, you mostly have nothing to do. At the moment the only thing I have to do is get the new prime weapons (which I don't really care that much about), and do the new octavia quest. If the devs could show some love to the players who have stuck with this game for a long time I would be very appreciative. Second, is power creep. New prime weapons being released every so often get more and more powerful, forcing me to grind for them to compete. This also makes weapons I enjoyed using feel invaild due to all of the better choices (e.g Dex Sybaris). The last (and not really effecting you if you don't care about Pvp), is conclave. When you're a super agile ninja versus other super agile flying ninjas, you can see why conclave would not be that fun (at least for me). For me usually consists of spamming control and space to bullet jump constantly all over the place, while one person with a snipetron vandal gets muiltitudes more kills than anyone else.
^ Now while that paragraph of things I find wrong with this game may be much bigger than the things I love, I definitely like this game much more than hate it. I can remember all the good times I had in my early times playing this.
Would recommend.

So you heard about Warframe, it’s got lot of positive feedback and you want to know if it’s really good and worth your time?
Well it’s free, why wouldn’t you give it a shot? If you snag 100+ hours game time of good gameplay then it was well worth it right?
Well it’s kind of a mixed bag with this game.
In the start it can look and feel really good but longer the time you are wasting playing and thinking you are building your character for something big, getting better in the game, got all this different gear, you don’t even mind the grind because you think it will pay off in the end.Then all of a sudden it hits you like a brick, THERE IS NO ENDGAME, NO CHALLENGE, NO PURPOSE, NO REWARD, NO PAT IN THE BACK FOR PLAYING GOOD, FOR THE IMMENSE GRIND.
When I first started playing few years ago there were no tutorials, not even a line of text to tell me what is the purpose of anything in the game.I heard people talking about lore and story but I couldn’t find it in the game.The few quests you had were roughly 3 hours of gameplay and they explained nothing.
Later they added few, hour long quests which should have been in the game from the start, but even now after they added some more it’s too little too late.
I don’t know what were the devs drinking but you don’t go building a game from the middle or the end and after 3 years you make a tutorial and character creator.
OK, so after some 20 hours you understand the game is not about soloing and story experience, it’s really about mindless hack and slashing and grinding for gear, so you can grind for more gear.
Also there is something like 6 different maps all together.
I have no problem with procedural map generation, it works great in some games but not here.
There’s something really uninspired about the level design.I noticed this from the start; the same corridor, same rooms I’ve been in thousand of times, the same waypoint, the ugly earthly color palettes on everything, rough textures all over the place… it just repeats itself.
There isn’t even a random detail here and there, every map tile is 90% the same, just the corridors are messed up.It’s lazy programming and bad design.
But maps are the least of Warframes problems, the main problem is the lack of endgame challenge and reward for putting in many hours.
For a noob at first there is a lot to do, but when you get to the level when you have the best gear and frames and now you want to do something else besides grind you hit a wall.
Where are the raids, dungeons, challenges, leaderboards for the best to compete?
Well there are something like raids, but they are too few and they are really not worth the time because the rewards are laughable.

If you ask in the chat they will say you have other modes, that there is a lot more to do!
Like you have a PVP arena style deathmatch and team DM..sounds cool at first but sadly the PVP is broken, poor server and connection issues make it impossible to have a decent experience.The game was primarily made as a PVE, so the hitboxes, server response and the physics don’t translate here at all.
Then you have some stupid sport game no one cares about, you can even play idiotic retro 2D minigames if you are getting bored from grinding.
The devs have tried to shove as many of unnecessary additions instead on working on the main game content that could lift this stale gameplay which almost has the game in a Beta state after so many years it has been released.
The plans for upcoming features state they plan to add Archwing racing as a core feature… racing… yeah it’s not even funny anymore.
But yeah DE has given up long time ago, they get enough money from new players to cover running costs.Making some grand changes in a game that is already kind of old is probably not a good financial idea, and since they are already shifting their crew to work on a new game Warframe is now like the Titanic after a kiss with the iceberg.
That is why nobody should invest their time on a game that is going nowhere creatively.
Maybe if you don’t mind the grinding, don’t mind the missing endgame content, you like hoarding items and having inventory full of unused trash, or you’re a big fan of hats in TF2 you will surely like the awesome gameplay of changing different color palettes of your frames and selling your hard grinded drops for in game currency so you can buy more cosmetic items.
Also as a side note I have to add something about the way the updates and reworks work in this game.
Usually a normal online multiplayer game has a test server, or some kind of site where there can be community dialogue and where you can exchange ideas for future plans and major updates.
Well screw that DE likes to take all the decisions themselves, they just roll with an update, barely testing any bugs or disbalance issues.
So we, the PC players test those things for them for free, and then later console players get updates after DE fixes bugs or nerfs stuff into oblivion.
And yeah the nerfs, there is no - lets tweak this weapon a little bit so it’s not picked over the others.
They just ram it so nobody touches it ever again, which is strange since this is a PVE game so you can’t have an advantage over other players and kills mean nothing.
Overall it’s sad because the game could have been so much more, the foundations were all here.
I think the free game marketing and development, investing too much time and programming in microtransactions and stuff to make it profitable took away from what it could have become.
It can kill time and your mouse.

Absolutely recommend this game and I'll tell ya why.
The combat is obviously the first piece of this game that deserves some attention. If you enjoy Dark Souls or Oblivion style sword fighting, then you'll absolutely love this. There are so many different ways to attack people, example: scrolling up to jab, scrolling down to overhead swing, and different buttons to swing your sword/flail/mace/axe left or right -- this game makes sword fights memorably epic. You can totally kick people off ledges, dodge them, block them....everything! You can also throw axes/knives ... and just yesterday I killed a dude with an axe to the nuts. Did I mention you can sever limbs and heads?
The maps are beautiful and diverse. From textures, to lighting, to the design of the landscape itself, you're always super immersed. The weather really changes your visibility in battle and there are even civilians running around to confuse you. My favourite part of the maps is that they are so dynamic in their elevations. The map designers really didn't think of maps as having a few different heights; you can literally jump off anything and land on anything, and it very well may give you the advantage in battle.
There are a ton of weapons to choose from and a ton to unlock. Each weapon is super unique, and really feels different from the last. You can really find the weapon you do best with, and it may be just a bit shorter or faster than your last. There are crazy weapons too - polearms, quarterstaffs, halberds, slings for throwing rocks, throwing spears, maces, flails, crossbows, daggers....you name it.
Customization is bang on. They focus mainly on colour and pattern choices, which there are plenty of. The people who do care about customization stand out; and it's super easy to spot your favourite allies or nemesis. There's also a green marker above your friend's heads to make them even easier to spot.
Absolute favourite part of this game is the skill level. If you can focus, breathe slowly, and time your blocks; you actually can take on hordes of people at a time. Especially if you're smart enough to funnel them onto a bridge :)
If you have a slow connection, beware. With every inch counting with a swing of a sword; you just really can't lag or it's pointless.
This game has a super steep learning curve. Even once you learn all the buttons, it's really hard to control yourself in the middle of combat. It's super immersive and exhilerating so it's easy to press the wrong button in the heat of the moment. With super realistic health levels, you can easily die in 1 hit.
Seems to work fine for a couple weeks then freaks out and bugs like crazy. Should go back to early access.

is a game that can either be loved to the point you play hundreds to thousands of hours in a very short amount of time, or be remarkably disliked.
It can be understandable in terms of why someone would dislike playing Warframe when it comes to the
aspect of the game, sometimes it can be very frustrating how many times you have to repeat the same mission over and over to get that one part, that one item. However, there are also players like me whom do find satisfaction in grinding that much, hence Warframe is definitely not for those who have no patience nor pleasure in (excuse the term) working hard to get what you want.
Some might say that Warframe runs a pay-to-win model, looking at the shop, but when we take a deeper look at it there is no actual basis to definite it so. Everything you buy with real-life currency can be obtained without - except, of course, some cosmetic items. Most of what you can purchase with Platinum you can buy with in-game credits too, hence the advantage that Platinum provides is simply getting things done faster.
Warframe unleashes an incredibly high level of optimization! Sure, it requires a good machine in order to run it at high settings, but it is very light and is very, very well optimized. The graphics are stunning, the level of details is incredible. Overall it certainly is a masterpiece to whom, like me, loves playing games with this kind of graphics.
In terms of gameplay and mechanics, I do love the combat system - I'm not exaggerating when I say that it has one of the best movements and combat I've ever had the pleasure to play with. What makes the game very sustainable in a long-term stay is the amount of different 'characters', weapons, missions, bosses and modes Warframe has to offer.
I highly suggest you give
a try - it is free afterall.

I think this is one of the better free to play games out there and I'm going to list the pros and cons of it from my perspective.
Also, I like how they have an array of AA options although I just use FXAA because....750 Ti. (No seriously, MSAA x2 is sometimes too much on my card in games, I don't need the quality AA, I'm fine with FXAA)
Pros:
Fun, fast paced action.
You have the ability to sprint and dodge roll, double jump, etc during fights, you can also scope to aim more accurately and use combat abilities to dispatch opponents.
There's a lot of options which are all unique in usage, you wont be able to say "I don't like attacking" since the options all feel remarkably different, like firing bolts of lightning at your foe which is essentially cheating due to the massive damage and that it's impossible to miss, although this is balanced by the fact it requires energy to use these abilities and you can't just go burning through it all.
Gunplay is pretty good too, I never felt like I missed a shot because of the game screwing me over, only my own incompetence at aiming.
There's also a level of customizability with the weapon and your armour, the game seems to take great pride in this as well, although I find it slightly unfriendly so I imagine new gamers will get rather confused, any old gamer could figure out how to upgrade and install weapon/armour mods.
PS: The mods are exclusive to the weapon, you can't take your rifle mods and put them on the pistol.
I know that may sound obvious but not all games have this level of seperation, if it's a weapon then it's a weapon, like in Skyrim, you can equip literally any enchantment to anything but not in this game, it's exclusive to that weapon type.
As I said previously, it's slightly unfriendly but nothing you couldn't figure out from playing around, after all, I did and I'm a moron.
Graphics: It looks great and even my 750 Ti can run the game maxed out, although I prefer to put games on minimum and 720p so my fan doesn't become a jet turbine, you can most definitely play at higher settings on a weaker PC, if you got a 1060 or RX 480, you could probably push the 1440p mark easily.
Cons:

Ark: Survival Evolved is a great game to play but with a lot of headaches that come with it. The game clearly needs to be optimized further even after it has exited Early Access. The game has beautiful graphics and the dinosaurs look amazing. As a player I focus more on Single player or PVE servers than PVP. The game has plenty of room for ideas on building great bases, ranches, and fortresses among other things. The gameplay can be hard at first and frustrating like everything is out to get you but then with a little experience it can be one of the most fascinating games to play. The idea of the whole world at your fingertips to build on, explore, and tame creatures makes it exciting. Taking down or taming a T-Rex can feel like such an accomplishment. Building your own base no matter how good or bad you are at it really makes the game feel like it fits to you, and doing so with others makes the game even more fun. I know there is a lot of problems with the game. It takes a high end Graphics card to actually enjoy the game without laggy pauses in both Single player and Multiplayer even at low settings. In PVP and sometimes PVE bases get destroyed and everything you worked for is gone either looted by others or eaten by the Gigantosaurus chewing at the last of your stone fence, but it is a game where you can rebuild, learn new ways to survive, and explore the farthest reaches of many places with hopes of doing everything a little better than last time.

A prime (ehhehe) example of free to play done right. With a constant stream of content, intimate developer and community relations, and a player driven economy based on a tradable and therefore entirely unnecessary to purchase premium currency, as far as free to play games go, it really doesn't get better than Warframe.

You'll be constantly doing missions to get drops, often the same ones over and over again, with a secondary goal generally being to do it as fast as possible, all so that you can get various item drops to make other weapons and frames to do it all over again. It doesn't really sound great spelled out like that, but it really is.
If you like action oriented games, loot driven games, third person shooters, going real fast, the art style or any combination of those things, you'll probably like Warframe.

Chivalry is a one of a kind experience. When you take a first-person shooter and an action adventure game set in medieval times and cross them you get Chivalry. In essence it's a first-person shooter type game with the exception of using swords, maces, bows and other old weapons instead of firearms. What's really good about that, is that you can't just point and click to hit someone. You have to take into account your weapon reach, weapon speed, the movement and turning of your body and that of your opponent. And timing. Especially timing. A split-second could mean the difference between your demise or triumphant victory.
The use of weapons is deceptively simple. After playing the tutorial you can probably use every kind of an attack there is. But getting good at using them is going to take time. The learning curve is rather steep in that sense, but fortunately there are servers now which have a level limit so you can relax and practice your skills there.
Despite the learning curve, playing the game is fun. And intense. There is no downtime or planning phase. You'll be in the middle of the action almost immediately. So whether you want to invest a lot of time to the game and become the ruler of the battlefields or just drop by for some action and a laugh, Chivalry has a lot to offer you.

This is a game that demands your time, literally. Most of your gear must go through a mobile-game style timer in order to be made. But this is a sacrifice that opens up the rest of the game to free players without needing to pay.
This is not a pay to win game, it's a pay to win faster game, paying only shortens the time it takes to get warframe, weapons, etc. But the great part about this is that you can trade in-game items for premium currency, so you can very easily access premium content without paying a dime.
As far as gameplay goes, the shooting is responsive. The melee is fluid and satisfying. And the movement is quick and require some skill to use to it's fullest potential. The wide variety of unique warframes and weapons makes this game endless fun. It's a grind, but it's a somewhat enjoyable one. It's all worth it when you finally make your next warframe.
There is a very steep learning curve that must be bypassed in order to understand the game though, which is a big turn off for new players.

Lag fix for the n00bs
1. Go to:
C:\Program Files\Steam\SteamApps\common\chivalrymedievalwarfare\Engine\Config
OR on a 64-bit system:
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\SteamApps\common\chivalrymedievalwarfare\Engine\Config
2. Open BaseEngine.ini with Notepad. Note: You may want to create a backup
of this file if you're worried you'll mess things up.
3. Push Ctrl+F (The Find window should pop up).
4. Type bSmoothFrameRate into the box.
5. Click Find Next.
6. Change TRUE to FALSE. The line should now look thike this:
bSmoothFrameRate=FALSE.
7. Exit the Find window.
8. Exit Notepad and click Save when promted.

First of all, I love the concept of this game. It's not that I played this for 15mins and decided this wasn't for me. I usually play for between 30-40hrs per week. That's how good it is...
But...
I am sick of constantly losing all my good gear due to bugs. If you fall from a high place, you usually glitch through the world underneath the map. If you die to certain animals/dinos they will eat your corpse and no matter if you kill them immediately after you respawn you will not get your stuff back. It is foggy every 10mins ingame. Wildcard recently patched it so it's more foggy. It's unrealistic for it to be raining 10 times and it being foggy for 5 separate occasions in the course of one day. Plants literally do not have to be irrigated due to the amount of rain ingame. Building in Ark has been known to give people cancer. Even weeks after being added into the game baby otters are still bugged and spontaneously stop eating. This issue has happened in the past when new creatures were added so I don't understand how it hasn't been fixed yet. When trying to tranq animals they tend to run into the water just before becoming unconscious. Ark cannot handle anywhere near 100 people on their servers, despite this being the max. Anything over 80 makes the game almost unplayable. Collusion seems to be an alien concept to Wildcard. Dinos constantly get stuck within one another & even some of the biggest dinos get stuck on rocks smaller than their feet.
All of this would seem like minor issues, but the point is after 2yrs if people are still complaining about the same thing, what are the developers doing?
I would recommend this game if Wildcard ever fix the many continuing bugs even after 'full release'.
fyi 'full release' should be a complete game, not open beta on an incomplete game expecting people to pay full price.

If you are willing to get annihiled by people who have played this game far more than you, this may still be worth picking up on sale. The melee combat is excellent, albeit difficult to master. There is an archer class as well, but only pansies play archer (KILL THE ARCHERS!). Blocking does not necessarily negate all damage, so you must be very careful to aim your blocks in the direction of the enemy's weapon to take effect. Weapon swings have multiple different styles, each with an alternate attack to swing from the opposite direction. The weapon attacks move with the direction that the player turns, allowing for advanced tecniques to swing around shields and parries or delay attacks to throw your opponent off. Each fight is a mind game that tests the combatant's wits and skill, although unless you play on specific servers, others can run in to steal your kills or in some other way ruin your fight. Intense and skillful most of time, there are still plenty of random moments you can expect to see out on the battlefield to lighten the tension. Pick this up when it is 50%-75% off or just wait until the next sale.

(TL;DR at bottom)
So, I'm beginning this review to help potential buyers decide whether they want this game. This review will track my progress as I log more and more hours into the game as it stands (as per this edit) I'm at
, that's just under one full day of gaming. At the end of this review, I'll try to break down pro's and con's of the game and look a little more in-depth at what the game has to offer.
Starting the game, you'll notice the lack of single-player options - and right you are. This game is based around purely multiplayer midieval combat. So lets start our first game. Picking a server is easy at a lower level, those highlighted in green are
servers, that means players level 0 to 15. These servers generally have a high population, and cycle through the game modes.
When you (or I, in this case) pick a server, you'll be able to see the current gamemode as well as current/limit players. I started with a low-pop Team Deathmatch game with 16 total players. When I hopped into the game, it was about halfway through, and as the teams were even, I got to pick a side (Agatha Knights or Mason Order). Now, these teams don't really matter all that much later on, no one will shun you for picking one over the other, but in my case I chose the Mason Order (Favorite color is Red). From there, there are four different classes.
So I hopped in as an archer, and immediately regretted my decision. Team deathmatch is almost squadbased, with groups of 3 or 4 charging at once, and everyone seems to have a general hatred towards archers. So, I died. A lot. Eventually I switched to a Man at Arms with the beginner shortsword. The speed was amazing, and I managed my first kill before dying. The game appeared ruthless to me, with wave after wave of enemies ready to stab me in the back - or throw something into my lower♥♥♥♥♥♥area. But it was fun, decapitating the few I could. By the end game, I had 5 kills and 13 deaths - but the five I killed were well worth it.
Game after game, I was killed. Repetitavely. But, I got better. Learned how to be more aware of my situation. Learned the different swings, and when to block/kick. By the time I was level ten, I could hold my own - and had even won a few 1v4 fights. My friends then got the game on sale - and let me tell you, when your friends are playing, the fun increases exponentially. Between level ten and fifteen I had my best games, including my very best being 43 kills and 3 deaths (Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥. And the best part, I was progressing. I unlocked equipment, weapons. I learned when to use specific classes. I memorized the maps and knew my strategy. I went from absolutely terrible to a force to be reckoned with.
I just reached level 16. But it's far from over. I have many more weapons I want to unlock, and many more kills I wish to obtain. I do like this game, a lot. Even the deadliest warrior portion - though it is significantly more buggy.

I have no idea how I feel about this game. 107 hours suggests I like playing it, and with friends I definitely do. Though I'm sure I'd enjoy playing most games with friends. Realistically though, the building in the game is awful which is odd since it's such a core aspect. You almost NEED to install like 4/5 different mods just to be able to build. Considering how many games out there do this easily, there's no excuse for this especially in a game with such a high price tag.
There are incredible amounts of clipping issues to the point where it's the norm, not a jarring rarity. This is kind of a big problem in a game where a dinosaur's mouth clipping through a wall literally makes the difference between you living or dying. Or your entire collection of dinos living or dying.
Online play brings problems too. Searching for lobbies literally crashes my entire internet connection to the point I have to reset my router. Sometimes two or three times before the game decides not to cut my internet. Joining lobbies can be hit or miss, finding lobbies can be hit or miss, it adds a significant amount of stress to an experience that is supposed to be enjoyable. I should add that I own 85 games on Steam, and 20-30 on other platforms, ARK is the only game that causes such a throttling issue with my internet connection.
Yet, besides all of the above (which to be honest, ignoring can be difficult), the game is brilliant. The scenery is beautiful, the dinosaurs are incredible in their variation and scale. Their unique traits and personalities. There is so much to do, so much to build, so much to explore. So many dinosaurs to learn how to tame, and try tame. So many moments of utter fear when you crest a hill to find a pack of Allosaurus. However, building is one of the main aspects and I consistently find it to be an absolute nightmare, at least without mods.
At the price I paid for the game, which was around 15 quid on sale while it was in early access, I got far more than my money's worth. Super, super happy I didn't have to pay £50 for it. Releasing DLC while in early access is unethical in my opinion. Doubling the price of the game on release is unethical in my opinion. Personally my advice would be to wait for a sale, get it cheap. Then the horrific clipping, bugs, and incredibly frustrating building mechanics will sting a little less.

Releasing DLC while in early access is unethical in my opinion. Doubling the price of the game on release is unethical in my opinion. Personally my advice would be to wait for a sale, get it cheap. Then the horrific clipping, bugs, and incredibly frustrating building mechanics will sting a little less.

Going to go tame something useful?  You'll need to stock up on tranq arrows, bolas can be useful to slow down smaller quick dinosaurus, with many other tips learned over time.  The feeling of taming a monster like the Spino or Rex on harder difficulty is not matched by many other games...
Overall I say this game is a good buy, family friendly to a point, many can enjoy it for years to come.  I give it 9/10, or 10/10 since it's replay value is quite high.

TLDR; Decent core game, scummy dev practices (like siccing lawyers on an innocent 17 year old) and hidden extreme grind, adding new superfluous reasources to grind for new frames and poor communication overall.
You can read more by visiting the warframe subreddit - I wouldn't trust the official forums as far as I could throw the server rack- which is nowhere (because is is overseen by the devs.)
Pros:
-Great movement system and core gameplay. It feels like you're a cybernetic ninja mowing down mobs in a hail of bullets, or cutting them down, setting them alight... which brings me to my next point.
-Great variety in weapon types/frames.
There's a different tool/playstyle for just about any mission type / faction type (corpus, grineer and infested). Mods further increase this variability in build variety and strength.
Wanna go around stealthily shivving people? Check. Or would you rather be an unstoppable force facechecking bullets without care and just mass slaughter with no care for stealth. Absolutely.
-New weapons and gear
Something to look forward to building, if you like gear treadmills.
-Beautiful, beautiful game
Wonderful cohesive artstyle and map tiles.
-Pretty good optimisation
Unless you're using intergrated graphics, this game can run pretty well on any rig. Can't speak for consoles
Cons:
-Developer Behaviour
I'm putting this at the top because frankly what DE recently pulled was nothing short of shady and outright antagonistic to the free flow of data regarding ACTUAL DROP RATES in this game. They recently sent a legal letter to a dataminer by the name of VoiD_Glitch to stop his efforts of revealing drop rates due to the actions of another hacker, which VoiD_Glitch was not responsible for.
It is not illegal to datamine from local files stored on your computer, and his work was transformative, as he had to decrypt and assemble the drop tables in a readable format for players, thereby being fair use and not infringing on copyright law. But even knowing he is in the right, doesn't mean he has the financial means to contest a lawsuit from a larger entity such as a game company. So he is silenced regardless of the truth of the matter. He is being bullied into compliance by DE.
Even if DE did produce drop tables- who's to say they are accurate? They've been innacurate before in reporting where parts drop, or just quietly removing them.
-Obfusicated drop rates
Relics are an essential part of this game if you wish to grind prime weapons and frames without buying prime access packs/ plat to trade. You can improve your chances of getting rarer drops from relics by upfrading them with void traces. Looking at the UI, you would assume you would have about 10% chance to get a rare after fully upgrading a relic.
It's actually much lower than that at 2%. But you don't know that, as DE NEVER releases the odds of drop rates willingly. Either it's found out by players grinding it, or datamined. But in some cases, DE has had made it outright impossible to obtain certain items that were advertised at obtainable through normal gameplay without paying, and only changed it when it was caught by dataminers who found out that the part/ item didn't drop at the mission node it was supposed to, or wasn't part of an rng table (A certain type of kubrow- a compainion could not be obtained without spending money to get the gene blueprint, while all other kubrows could be randomly obtained through an egg hatching.)
There are mods which prior to datamining, no one knew had a 0.17% drop chance. I'm not kidding. Brings me to my next point.
-MODS MODS MODS
In order to get the best from your warframe weapons, you need mods. For some weapons, especially melee weapons, the difference between a godlike and eh build is a single stance mod. And often, the superior stance mod drops very rarely from a very rare enemy or from caches.
For other mods, they may be from a unique event long gone, and thus limited in its circulation making it very expensive.
So it's either pay up, or hope that you get that 0.17% chance drop. Hope you like grinding.
-Grind (warframes and weapons)
Certain warframes require several layers of grind beyond the normal "kill boss for bp/parts, grind resources for said parts"
Vauban for example is only obtainable when alerts are on for his parts. You have no other way of obtaining them at this present moment.
Mesa can only be obtained by grinding 3 nave beacons to get a CHANCE at getting a part from a boss. At least with vauban alerts you know what you're getting at the end of the mission, even if you have to wait weeks of months between alerts.
The Hema, which can only be obtained through clan research, requires a rare resource called mutagen mass, and a LOT of it. For larger clans, this was around 20k for something that has a very poor drop chance and you usually get 1-3 from playing invasions (which require you to do the same mission 3-5 times), and mutagen masses aren't usually required in any great amount for anything else. So it's very unlikely someone has ran invasions for kicks and giggles and happens to have 20k they can donate to their clan.
-Limited mission types
Currently, there are 19 types of mission in Warframe. But generally you are going to be doing (if you only do PvE).
-Survival
-Defence
-Interception
-Mobile defence
-Extermination
-Excavation
-Sabotage
-Spy
Most of these mission types are "defend point/object, kill hordes of enemies" with little variation. The only real different type would be spy or sabotage, as you have multiple ways to achieve your objective. For example, I could take a stealth frame, learn the layout of a spy vault and seamlessly slip in and steal the data. Or I could brute for through alarms and take it by force, if I did it in time.
The real variablilty come with weapons/ frames, but some weapons and frames are more equal than others.
-Balance, augments and rivens.
Some frames are better than others for different job types. That's fair enough- but some warframes are absolutely outclassed in their role by another warframe.
-Nyx's chaos is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ version of Lokis radial disarm with the irradiating disarm augment.
-Rhino gets stomped by Inaros and Nidus in terms of early and late-game tanking.
Augments are mods which add additional utility to a warframes abilities for the cost of a mod slot that could be taken up by something else. Why not just add the utility to the warframe outright, or give more slots? It would still cost mod capacity to put it in.
Rivens - A band-aid solution to bring up old, outdated weapons to spec with newer weapons. It's RNG what weapon you get after unvieling, and they can only be gotten by CHANCE from sorties. And some riven types ae rarer than others - ie shotgun rivens are super rare due to there being few shotguns in the game.
They then require addtional grind to roll decent stats unless you get super lucky on a riven for a weapon that's useful.
-Kuva and Nitain
Added new resources that new frames/ weapons seem to always need. I guess this is them trying to push veterans into grinding more, thus more playtime = greater chance of spending money to get past the wait.
CONCLUSION
It's an enjoyable game at first, but unless you like not knowing the odds of your grinding, doing the same stuff every day and dealing with shady devs I wouldn't recommend getting into this game. The gear treadmill will suck you in, then you'll leave until next patch. Or at least, that's what I do. ALSO NEVER SPEND PLAT ON FRAME OR WEAPONS - IT IS A WASTE.
Like I said, you can find far more in-depth reports on DE's shady ways and the dynamics of Rivens/Balance/Grind elsewhere, but after the VoiD_Glitch incident I wanted to write to alert people of what they're signing up for, and who you are giving your time and possibly money.

Void is Seventeen and had stated he would gladly take down any part of the github repository on request. DE has contacted Void precicely Twice since datamining. I could point to other examples of antagonism between developers and players such as Oberon's Rework, Behavior on Dev-Streams being condescending if not outright mocking, having a community that needs to scream as a collective voice to get 'compromise' measures, and more. Instead they do not go after the actual hackers and go after the prominant largely benign dataminer who has repetedly expressed a willingness to work with Digital Extremes.
I cannot condone this behavior nor will I advise anyone give them business until this matter has resolved as a show of support.

Chivalry. This game is awesome. Here's why:
The Combat
It's glorious. It's fun, simple, yet dynamic, the basics are easy to grasp, but the longer you play, the better you get, even if you still die in hilariously simple and stupid ways ALL THE TIME. An arrow to the head. A wild stone. A teammate who's not playing with a full deck. All sorts of things, and this adds to the experience. Chivalry isn't an accurate game, it doesn't try to be. It's meant to be a cluster♥♥♥♥ of idiots, roleplayers (there are some, believe me), cheaters (there's always some), tryhards, casuals, all in one server, fighting agaisnt one another.
I can only put a few cons in this game:
There's no matchmaking. Depending on your internet and location, it might be hard to find a server for what you want to play. When you do find it though, it's worth it.
If the server you pick has ping, you're going to have a bad time.
The Hit Reg isn't exactly..the best thing ever. It works surprisingly well most times, even with a bit of lag, but can also suddenly break down and allow a swing in the air to lop your head off. So there's that.
All in all, it's not perfect, if you like medieval , skill based games, you should buy it. You might hate it, you might love it, and you'll play it for ages.
9/10. Cheers!
Edit: I forgot to mention, there's quite a few people who enjoy ducking/rotating 360 while swinging. I don't really get it, so I won't pretend to. It's cheap, it works extremely well, and you'll have an awfull time trying to fight them if you can't do the same. Just..avoid them. Or scream at them over the mic. You'll figure something out.

Holy sh*t! Where do I even begin...
Alright, let me do a small TL;DR : If you like grindfesty-RNG games with an emphasis on freedom of movement, you're probably gonna like this game. If not... try it, it's free ;)
So with that out of the way, let me get through my
opinions of the game.
Pros:
- as mentioned before, a lot of emphasis on freedom of movement
- a buttload of weapons to play around with
- space dogs (and cats, yes) as pets that are actually useful and can help you during missions
- aescetically speaking... it's definitely up there.
- good sound design
- free2play
- not a pay2win game... because:
- PvE focused (PvP specific mode is available)
- one of the single best communities I've ever been part of
- easy to find clans
Cons:
- long waiting times for the foundry (crafting station)
- mostly RNG-based loot
- a lot of "speedrunners"
- borderline impossible to get on a "raidbus" (more on this later)
- people get more greedy as more players join
- some warframes are "unbalanced"
I think most of my points speak for themselves, but there are a few that I think I should explain why I feel the way that I do.
- as mentioned before, a lot of emphasis on freedom of movement:
When it comes to the whole "emphasis on freedom of movement", what I mean is that there are a lot more movement options than in most other games, whether we're talking about this genre or otherwise, but don't interpret this in the sense that you can do a 1080° quadruple sideflip with full 360° spin control... but seeing as this game was advertised as you playing as "space ninjas", you can expect the obvious; running along walls, against walls, flips, barrel rolls, etc.
- aescetically speaking... it's definitely up there.
About the whole aesthetic thing... I mean, it's a subjective thing, but I like it :P but then again, I'm pretty biased towards both space stuff and ninjas, sooo... you be the judge xD
- one of the single best communities I've ever been part of
I swear to the big G, I don't think I've ever been a part of a more hospitable and helpful community as this one, if you need help or an answer to some question, just ask the in-game chat, you're bound to get an answer in five minutes, tops.
- easy to find clans
Just google "warframe clans recruiting" or something like that, and you're sure to find some clan that you can join and get access to some of the sweeter gear ;)
- long waiting times for the foundry (crafting station)
Weapon: 6 - 24 h (generally speaking)
Warframe part: 12 h
Warframe (when all parts are done): 72 h (!!!)
- mostly RNG-based loot
F*CKIG RELICS PIECES OF SH*TS !!!!
- borderline impossible to get on a "raidbus" (more on this later)
I'm guessing that most of you reading this are familiar with the term "raid" from either WoW or some other game, so I'll skip over the definition of what a raid is, and "raidbus" is a term for a bunch of veterans of that specific raid are taking a bunch of greenhorns with them to teach them how to do the raid (and maybe eventually speedrun it). However, there are never anyone willing to "take you aboard", as it were. In one way I do understand that, but the thing is that if someone hosts the raid (uses the necessary item in order to run the raid) and the group fails, no worries, someone else can host the next time or something. but maybe this is a Europe thing only and overseas things are better, who knows, not me atleast xP
- a lot of "speedrunners"
I know I mentioned it above, but if we're talking about certain things, such as raids, I understand the speedrunner mentality, but when you're playing in a casual public game... there's really no reason to speedrun certain missions especially if you have some beginners with you.
, there are a lot of people who seemingly have a gigantic need for speed and outrun beginners who are still getting used to the control scheme (in order to show of their skills and then b*tch about why the others are so slow once they get to the end of the mission), I mean... don't be a d*ck, dude...
- people get more greedy as more players join
There are two different type of currencies in the game; credits (non-premium) which are earned by completing missions and other regular stuff, and platinum (premium) which can be bought with real money, OR, you can farm prime parts and blueprints (almost every weapon and warframe have a prime version that have some advantage or another over the regular variant) from relics and then sell those to the other players for platinum. Here's the thing, let's say the average price of something is 30 platinum, then people won't sell it for anything under 60 and won't buy it for anything more than 5. I know it sucks to pay for some virtual part, but if you can't keep up, don't step up.
- some warframes are "unbalanced"
WAIT, HOLD ON!! Let me explain. Since this is a PvE focused game, then this statement might seem really, really f*cking stupid... and I get that, so I'm guessing most of you reading this are gonna take it the wrong way. Obviously, you're gonna have your DPS characters, your tanks, healers, buffers, debuffers, so on and so forth, I understand... but then you look at warframes like Loki, who can cheese just about any mission (solo even, if you know what you're doing)! Or how about Ivara, the stealth warframe that can outlast just about any other beefy warframe in survival missions. Not saying this is a huge detraction of the overall enjoyment of the game (which is why I put it so low), but it's one of those things that I feel like DE could and should address.
With all this being said, I've had a blast with this game ever since 2013, even if I've taken several breaks from it, and I can't wait to see what ideas DE has in store :3 the reason why it took me so long to write this is because I've wanted to get a good idea of what potential this game has to offer and where it seems to be heading.
So all in all, as an overall game, I'd give it a 7/10
but as a free2play game, it's easily a 8,5/10 or 9/10

This game has been changing a lot rather quickly. First, you had the Dread Knight, which was the point where lots of players just gave up and stopped trying, like I did. Back then, you had to ascend (Pretty much like prestige, wiping your progress just to get a tiny bonus that keeps stacking the more you keep doing it) over and over again a few times before you were able to get past zone 140 or so, because the price of the Dread Knight was astronomically insane. Lots of us, who hate doing the equivalent of rolling heavy rocks up a hill just to watch them roll down again, just stopped playing here.
After that, they decided to add mercenaries, and my god, this change was amazing. Now, you didn't had to ascend anymore, you could simply send your mercenaries to farm Hero Souls and money, and getting through the zones was pretty much a breeze now. You could also farm those random fish drops in hopes of getting rubies, and you could also send your mercenaries for rubies, too. So, you could skip ascending altogether, just gather enough rubies for a quick ascension, and there you go! I got through zone 200-1800 that way, and it seems like the game was getting a bit too easy, but still, you could finally feel some kind of ♥♥♥♥ing progress.
Then, update 1.0 came. They nerfed lots of ancients, for example, it was quite easy to get Chronos stupidly OP, giving you like an extra 300 seconds for your boss timer if you were an idler like me. They nerfed it so it only gives you around 16 extra seconds or so. But hey! You can level Chronos up now! It's just going to cost you 5 quadrillion souls! For a whooping .22 seconds. So, idling now like in the old days was out of the question. But hey, you could still gather rubies to get another quick ascension, right? Well, yes, but now, there's super ancients basically, that look like Lovecraftian old ones. What's the catch? You HAVE to trASScend to get these, which means  you have to wipe your progress. Just ♥♥♥♥ you, you have to wipe your progress if you wanna get far now. And nope, there's nothing you can do to avoid said wipe. So, unless you've got an awful lot of time to spend in this game, getting far is now pretty much a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ Going from zone 1950 or so all the way back to zone 1 makes me feel like killing myself. And I didn't even got that far compared to other players out there.
This is where I call quits, they just nerfed everything that exists to give you an excuse to grind harder. I know lots of you will love it, and I  know I might get lots of hate for my point of view, but that's how I feel at the moment.

ARK is an excellent project, but, unfortunately, is being developed by a very incompetent company. The adventure and concept of ARK is most entertaining and provides hours, if not, days of entertainment. However, if you are using GNU/Linux (SteamOS), or MacOS, this game is so very ill supported and seems to be receiving more problems with every update, even after ARK leaving early access.
The bugs (briefly Google it) that are in ARK for the GNU/Linux and MacOS platforms have been around prior to ARK leaving early access and continue to grow, without a word of any fix.  There is no communication to the users of ARK on these platforms and if any information that is directed to the developers on the official forums, then you are surveilled and false flagged.
Other problems that have occurred are numerous and can be read throughout the web, particularly for the MacOS and GNU/Linux users. Some are just opinion regarding sales of DLC's during early access, but this was not an issue for me. In fact, as long as ARK was being proactively fixed I was happy to support them. Sadly this is not the case.
It really saddens me to write such a negative review, but the surveillance on the official forum by Jerryn was the last straw.
Perhaps if you use M$ then this maybe a positive experience, but if you are using GNU/Linux (SteamOS), or Mac OS, then you really should not purchase the game.
Studio Wildcard does not understand customer relations and customer support. The best that could be done with ARK is to sell the project to a more competent company.

Pros:
Interesting concept (open world survival centered around taiming, breeding, and fighting dinosaurs, as well as some mythical creatures).
Pretty solid modular building system.
Large player base in both PvP and PvE.
Large amount of servers to choose from, both official and unofficial.
Large modding community.
New content added often (though this is a double-edged sword that I'll touch on later).
Massive list of creatures in the game.
Amazing looking maps and visuals.
A lot of replayability and many hours to be invested.
Whenever they release new DLC, all the new content with the exception of the map can be obtained by players who don't own the DLC, so that the playerbase isn't split. This is also a double-edged sword.
Cons:
Devs are very bad about communicating with the playerbase and make terrible decisions (This is probably the worst thing about the game. They just don't seem to listen to feedback. They released paid DLC before the game was even fully released which is about as scummy as a dev can get imo. There are many other examples that you can find without digging very far that I'm not going to go into at the moment)
Price of game is $60 (now I know what you're probably thinking that this is the general price of a vanilla AAA game these days. As far as content and time spent on this game goes, yes it is probably worth $60. HOWEVER, the general quality of the game that has not changed much since they released this on early access so long ago would be similar to that of a $20 game at the most. The shear amount of bugs and stutter still in this game is staggering. This game should've been no more than $40 to compromise.
Massive DDOSing has occured, and will most likely continue to happen on many servers. There isn't really anything that the devs of this game (or the devs of ANY game to be honest) can do about it, so it's not really their fault. It still needs mentioning, though.
New content released often. So here's the issue with that: Every time they release a new creature that adds something new to the game, they neglect to balance it beforehand. So what you usually end up with is a creature that is either incredibly overpowered, or terribly useless. We saw this quite a bit with the release of Wyverns in Scorched Earth, and will no doubt see it with the new Abberation DLC.
Back to the new maps added, while players without the DLC can technically obtain the new creatures and items, it is incredibly difficult for them to do so. They typically have to get them from the players who DO have the DLC. This problem was somewhat mitigated with the free Ragnarok map that contains content from both Scorched Earth and the vanilla game, but this wasn't released until about a year after Scorched Earth and I'm worried that Abberation is going to bring it full circle all over again. I suspect that each new DLC is like a premium Pay-2-Win period, as the players who purchase it will have easy access to all the new creatures and items right away, whereas the players who do not buy it are at a distinct disadvantage.
Offline base-raiding. (Only really a problem on PvP servers) I'll be honest when I say that this is always going to be a problem in open-world multiplayer survival games. It's not a good experience when you've spent many hours building a base only to have it all gone when you relog the next day. Alpha tribes that can have players online 24/7 rule this game. Solo players/small groups are going to have a difficult time, but it's not impossible.
You are probably going to need a PC beyond the recommended specs to play this game the way it's meant to be played. The game still isn't as optimized as it should be. The minimum settings are painful to look at imo, and the game crashes every now and then. There are some fixes you can google to improve your framerate a bit.
All in all, I've got to give this game a negative review, because I simply CANNOT recommend people buy it for the $60 pricetag + however much for all the DLC that is going to be released. I may update this when the price goes down, however.

The Good:
- It's a fun game, especially to play with friends.

- Everything is customizable
- Mods are always a plus.

- CHALLENGING
The Bad:
- Many tasks are quite boring, like maturing baby dinos.

Overall:
I love the game, though some peices are clearly still being developed.  It needs to be more optimized - my computer can run almost anything on ultra - but with THIS game it has to run at almost minimum, even when I downgrade it to use DX9.

I recommend this game to anyone who has the ultimate gaming PC, enjoys survival games and FPS, as well as anyone who has unlimited downloading from their internet provider.

Good day fellow soon to be space ninjas! I come from the stars bearing some useful information!
I am a long term player who has seen this game change and to be fair in mostly good ways. This isnt your average garden variety MMOFPS, its a well designed game that takes tactical play to a desired level. That said there are issues and I will get into those more deeply soon. I believe that this game has over the years Ive known and played it become something unique and better then other FPS types and in some cases better then alot of SP FPS franchises out there. That is due to the nature of combat and more recently since the storys were beginning to evolve.
Now to the fun stuff!
Word of warning this review will be quite in-depth and lengthy so I will put in here that it is worth a shot for veteran and new FPS players alike. Massive customisation options through the Mods system as well as various playstyles on offer through the design of the Warframes themselves.
Pros of being a space ninja!
Combat.
Excluding the Archwing system which has been and is still undergoing changes combat in this game is visceral violent and FAST. You have your standard Primary and Secondary slots with the ability to have melee weapons of various designs that can bring a big difference in the way you play. Most Primary and Secondary weapons are the standard bows and guns though there are several including the Quanta and Optiocor which are energy weapons with various added effects. The ease of use straight off from a fresh install is pretty standard with the sad exception of the Archwing weapons and flight controls which I will cover later down in the cons.
Customisation and Loadouts.
This is a pretty intense subject as there are always going to be sub par par and optimal builds for w/e your goals are and various loadouts will be available to you later on as you progress. There are always discussions on the subreddit and ingame as well as on DE forums about whats best at any given time but while they can be handy if your going for long endgame runs the game is yours to do with as you please. The Mod system is easy to understand and your given some information as part of the initial tutorial on how to use it. Loadout slots are there as well and as you progress through the Mastery Rank system more become available. This pair of systems combines into a quite intense at first look but very VERY handy tool for your progression.
Warframes.
The type of playstyles each warframe has would take forever and be a guides worth of information alone but I will try and summarise best I can. There are multiple roles the 4 big ones for me being Support (Currently filled by 3 frames at this point to varying degrees.) Tanks Offensive and Stealth. There are hybrids within each role an example being Nidus who is Offensive/Support. He can deal significant damage to enemies while providing soft crowd control and area healing. Stealth would be exemplified by Loki who has the ability to distract and disarm enemies for extended periods when modded appropriately. I could go on but I think you get the idea.
Progression System.
This is where it gets intensely interesting for me. I was playing before the release of the Map 2.0 overhaul which changed the layout of the map for the game. This in turn changed the process of gaining Mastery Rank which is required for benefits like access to more powerful weapons Loadout slots and the like. The new player experience as it stands with this in mind is a bit awkward but once you get the idea of it you will find it flows fairly easily. The map has you start on Earth when you begin the tutorial and when you finish youll be able to then unlock each node on Earth. Once this process is complete you will see Junction nodes to other planets. Hover over them complete the tasks and you will have a chance to fight a Solar Rail guardian. If you succeed in killing that guardian you then access the planet the rail links to with quite a cool animation scene too. That is the basic situation with Progression but it also ties into my next positive point.
Story Missions
This is a big big one that has recently become prevalent over the last few major updates. Once you get to a certain point youll get a junction reward that lets you start on a quest called Natah. This questline is really cool and has multiple cinematics as well as a choice system. As you progress you will get further questlines related to that story with further lore and choices to make. These additions have greatly added to Warframe adding some sorely needed backstory and expanding what is a great universe.
Cons of being a space ninja!
Archwing flight system and combat.
Currently the archwing flight system when used with KB+M is very difficult to handle for me and is fine when using a controller. This affects combat and another issue is in combat when your melee swinging you charge at nearby enemies which in some cases can cause disorentation and nausea. This can be mitigated to a degree with lower display quality.
Particle visuals.
These can in some cases be quite nausea inducing and I would advise lowering settings if this happens as it can take some getting used to. There are options to disable entirely but that is a personal choice based on your experience.
Community issues with ingame chat channels.
This one is kinda personal but worth mentioning. I believe that DE is working on more permanent solutions but sadly at present for the Oceanic/Asia servers which I play on Region Chat can be quite toxic. The perfect game to play while you cook this:
Ingredients
4 tablespoons soft unsalted butter
150g dark brown sugar
225ml cream
2 tablespoons cornflour
½ teaspoon salt
375ml milk
3 large egg yolks
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
2 tablespoons hazelnut vodka
Honeycomb, crushed, to serve
Method
1. Melt the butter in a medium heavy-based saucepan. Add the brown sugar and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved. Add the cream and bring to a simmer, stirring until you have a nice thick butterscotch sauce.
2. Meanwhile, place the cornflour in a bowl with the salt and slate with a couple of tablespoons of the milk until smooth, then whisk into the rest of the milk in a large bowl. Whisk in the egg yolks with the vanilla extract and then gradually add the hot butterscotch sauce, whisking constantly.
3. Wipe out the saucepan. Strain the mixture back through a fine-mesh sieve back into the saucepan and cook over a medium heat for 5-6 minutes, stirring regularly, until the butterscotch custard starts to thicken.
4. Remove from the heat and stir in the vodka. Pour into pretty glasses or ramekins and chill for at least an hour or up to 3 days.
5. For a lighter result, allow the custard to cool in a bowl with the surface covered with cling film to prevent a skin forming. To serve, whip lightly with a whisk or use the paddle of a kitchen aid before spooning into the glasses or ramekins. Garnish with crushed honeycomb.

Paranoid schizophrenia, or schizophrenia with paranoia as doctors now call it, is the most common example of this mental illness.
Schizophrenia is a kind of psychosis, which means your mind doesn't agree with reality. It affects how you think and behave. This can show up in different ways and at different times, even in the same person. The illness usually starts in late adolescence or young adulthood.
People with paranoid delusions are unreasonably suspicious of others. This can make it hard for them to hold a job, run errands, have friendships, and even go to the doctor.
Although it's a lifelong illness, you can take medicines and find help to stop symptoms or make them easier to live with.
Paranoid Symptoms
Delusions are beliefs that seem real to you, even when there's strong evidence they aren't. Paranoid delusions, also called delusions of persecution, are rooted in fear and anxiety. They might make you feel like:
A co-worker is trying to hurt you, like poison your food.
Your spouse or partner is cheating on you.
The government is spying on you.
People in your neighborhood are plotting to harass you.
These beliefs can cause trouble in your relationships. And if you think that strangers are going to hurt you, you may feel like staying inside or being alone.
People with schizophrenia aren't usually violent. But sometimes, paranoid delusions can make them feel threatened and angry. If someone is pushed over the edge, their actions usually focus on family members, not the public, and it happens at home.
You could also have related hallucinations, in which your senses aren’t working right. For example, you may hear voices that make fun of you or insult you. They might also tell you to do harmful things. Or you might see things that aren’t really there.

My opinion on this game has flopped several times due to various reasons. The reason I didn't recommend this game, at one time, was because they changed an endless mission system that I felt was the only true challenge left in the game. The reason I can recommend it now, is because that change actually made me experiment with the other parts of the game. I truly came to enjoy the creativity in the mods, weapons, and warframes that they've added in the past few years.
If you're a new player, take your time and enjoy the game and mechanics. I recommend playing with friends as that's the most fun, but if you are a lone wolf then a clan is really nice way to play with people your level. Making friends with the community, where you can, is a rewarding experience that I can vouch for. Don't go for the meta weapons or anything like that right away. Go for the weapons that look cool or are just plain fun to use. Set small goals and you'll get absorbed into the gameplay right away.
If you're a veteran player then remember that you can actually become a barrier to entry for newer players of warframe. By "power leveling" or "boosting" them you can strip away the experience that made you enjoy the game in the first place. Be an asset, not a crutch.
If you haven't played this game, well you're missing out on something pretty special.

Realistic review: The combat is satisfying as f***. Possibly one of the best FPS games I've played. The archery is a bit underpowered, but it's made up for by making archery fairly deadly at a distance. The feeling you get when you get a kill on this game is unlike any other. When you stand toe-to-toe with an opponent and parry back and forth until you finally swing your sword and behead him and warcry, you feel like a damned champion.
If you enjoy FPS games and games like Elder Scrolls, this game is definitely for you. It's PVP Elder Scrolls combat with siege weapons and different classes and the combat is far more active than the standard hack-n-slash that ES gives you. The combat is a bit wonky at first but as you get used to the controls and better at playing the game, you will become so immersed that you will lose yourself within the game for hours.
As for the CONS: my largest gripe is that you hit your teammates quite often and they quite often hit you sometimes causing one of you to kill the other. The melee radius is extended to your left and right (in an unreasonable and unrealistic manner) as you swing your weapons causing teammates and yourself to hit each other but also, sometimes allowing you to score extra hits or kills, so it's a bit of a hit-and-miss.
Second, the archery is SEVERELY underpowered. You will sometimes find yourself hitting opponents with 3-4 arrows before they die, which would be fine, but if you get hit ONE TIME by an armored class like Vanguard, you are dead, which happens more often then naught. So archery is extremely slow, low damage and already very hard to control in close quarters. However, this would be a bit more bearable but it seems like the servers have such a low polling rate or tick rate such at 10hz or possibly even lower, that you can hardly ever score a hit at long range unless the target is standing still. Far too many times have I found myself shooting an arrow at an opponent and watched the arrow go through his body or hit his body in a place the arrow didn't go or catch on his shield even though I shot directly at a different spot. The hit detection for archery is very bad and I hardly play as an archer because of it.
All in all, reccomended. The game has some small flaws but the entirety of this title is incredible and the longevity of it is even better. As you profress through the game, you unlock more weapons and gear such as throwable firebombs and such and better primary weaponry. It's a fantastic game that gets even better the more friends you play with. It's an incredible game that you will have fun with until you either can't play it anymore or the servers get shut down.
I can't stress it enough. The game is fantastic. Reccomended, reccomended, reccomended.

I have played over 1,200 hours so I feel I can write a truthful, and hopefully, helpful review for this game.
Let me start with the conclusion for those that find this TLDR:  Buy and play this game if you only want the PvE experience.  Do not buy this game with PvP intentions *unless* you can be part of a mega tribe, or with a group of friends that can ALL play 8+ hours every single day.
The long version, or "explanation":
So, there I was 18 months ago playing PvE on The Island riding my Barbie bike around thinking I was Johnny Bada$$.  For a year afterwards, I tamed most every dino, built huge bases, recruiting ~6 friends into my Tribe, got deep into breeding and mutations, etc...basically I experienced almost everything the PvE game had to offer land, air & sea on The Island, Sorched Earth and Ragnarok, albeit not completing all the end boss events.  And then, one night ~6 months ago during a 2x weekend, we decided to try one evening of PvP on The Island and my life changed forever...
We went "Lord of the Flies" circumventing the entire island on a raft raiding and destroying almost every other raft and structure we saw.  Although we didn't kill most tamed dinos, we♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pillaged and destroyed; it was the single most fun night of gaming I have ever had.  In 2 days, we were in our 70s, built a metal base and thought we were on our way.  Then we experienced what we had heard about...the resident Alpha Tribe rightfully wipe us and our tames.  We rebuild, they did it again.  We rebuilt, they did it again.  We hid in the NW icebergs rebuilding, again we were wiped.  There was no way we could go back to PvE, the real game had been revealed to us.  Being the far superior humans we know ourselves to be, we decided another server and/or map was the place for us.  At this time, the Server Kill list was published and the announcement of new servers and Legacy servers occurred.  I'll let you research it all, but in a nutshell, Legacy servers will slowly die (actually happening much quicker than we thought), so it only made since to restart completely on the "new" servers.
I cannot express strongly enough how utterly defeating from this point on the game is unless you can be part of a mega tribe, or with a group of friends that can ALL play 8+ hours every single day...don't miss a day or you'll be toast.  We tried almost all PvP maps across Asian, EU and NA servers, and within 1 to 3 days were fully wiped time, after time, after time, after time, after time, after time, after time, after time, after time, after time again (much more than that actually).  Simply put, within the current constructs of the game, there is absolutely, unequivocally, ZERO hope for you in PvP w/o the exception noted above.  NONE...TURN AWAY and run from this game if PvP is your desire.
I have gone back to my Barbie bike in PvE pretending to be the badda$$ I know I am...
P.S. The sad part of all this is the game really WANTS to be great...it screams for it.  Wildcard made a monumental mistake upon official release by only trickling out a few servers at a time; Alpha tribes have been able to establish footholds within each push out of a few servers and then on to the next batch, etc.  Truly, a colossal error.
