I'm dissapointed to have to post a negative review for this game as I was really excited to play it and have wanted to play a game like this for quite some time.
Now going into this review I'll state I have a good gaming laptop which can run most games on high or highest settings smoothly enough to play as well as or better than my console sometimes. Can't remember the exact model but its an MSI I'm not a hardcore gamer but I wanted to spend a bit of cash when I was moving on to this laptop so I could play the odd game on it and I've never had a problem with any.
Short Review:
Good Idea, Poor exicution. Feels unfinished. Looks bad. Mainly Dissapoined but very glad I never payed full price.
Longer Review:
The First problem I encountered was a crash on the initial load of the game... Not a good omen
Afte that I thought "I'll try training as its a gametime I've never played before" 3 times I had to go through it as it crashed and bugged out twice.
Then I tried to go onto multiplayer and there were no servers showing up so I thought "maybe I have to go through training and go to the multiplayer gate there first time to access it" NOPE! there was a bug which I had to then go online and find out how to fix.
After all that nonsense I managed to get into a game... where I had to drop my graphics to low to even be able to connect my sword to an enemy.
Let it be known this isn't a rage quit review I realise this game probably has a steep learning curve. I just personally felt the whole time I was playing the game I was saying in my head "This game is a finished game?" It looks pretty bad, some of the viewing controls feel like playing the old school Duke Nukem games with wierd warped vision looking up and down at objects close by.
The controls feel so loose and sloppy and "Partial conntroller support" is as it says PARTIAL. you still need a mouse to navigate menus and choose a team/character type.
I had to stop playing after the first game becaue it just felt like a badly made game. I am SO glad all I payed was £4 odds on sale as I would be extremly annoyed to pay full price for this game.
Its a shame because this looked really in trailers but they do not compare to gameplay.
Personally I feel unless it has some major fixes and a lot of work done on it I wouldn't even bother playing it again.
I was hoping to put 100+ hours into this game, come here and write a positive review... I never even made it to an hour before I just gave up.
I never got annoyed at it. got 3 kills in the first game (though I don't know how or who) and just played it feeling nothing. No excitment no joy but not angry or upset... Just dissapointed.
I know a lot of people love this game and play it with 1,000+ hours and lots of good reviews. I wish I could say the same but I just can't.

This game starts humble enough. I won't spoil anything, but I will give the gist of it. It starts off where there is a monster on the right of the screen with a health bar. It seems like your average clicker game. For example, as in all clicker games, the first upgrade or "hero" as the game calls it upgrades your click damage which trust me, becomes nearly non-essential later in the game, but none the less important. Soon once you start dropping monsters, you end up having to wait a bit. Or click until your hand goes numb. If that happens, which there is a 99.9% chance it will, you are addicted. Just like milllions of other players, you have fallen into the trap. It seems simple at first glance, but once you get past say, level 30 it gets much, MUCH more complicated, causing for different types of upgrades which reduces the amount of monsters to fight, how much money you make when you're away, etc. Then, once you get to about 75 - 80, you can do something called "ascending", but I won't spoil it. I will just tell you that it sounds like a bum deal, but litterally essential for the later game. This game can be picked up by anybody of any gamer type of any age. It's cute, and each character is diverse and unique with a surprisingly deep lore behind them (deep story in a clicker game, who knew?) Any way, if I were to rate this game, from the unexpected variable gameplay to the amazing animations, this game gets my 8.5 out of 10. It is definly a game you should pick up and try, and now is the perfect time with the 1.0 patch here for the taking.

And then my 2.5GHz Lenovo with NVidia GeForce 720M GPU came. Doesnt seem like it should run the game too on medium-high settings, but on high it would run it like my asus, on medium it runs it in 60FPS EVERYWHERE except PoE and earth [which gave 20 and 10 FPS on asus, respectively]
The game is optimized so well, that even my old laptop that was inferior to... not even my Lenovo, it was inferior to freaking Commodore 128, have run it... and now my new laptop goes beyond what i ever expected to see in games.
The game has been created by developers known to world of gaming as DE, which is short for Digital Extremes, they have literally made a game with great gameplay, that is able to run even on the worst PC's of all time, and with a PC able to run it in 60 FPS on lowest settings it still looks great and plays even better...

...ALSO...did i mentioned i did run this game on DirectX, and not something like Vulkan that could explain why the game runs so well?
shortly, Digital Extremes truelly can optimize their games to the absolute Extremes
The good, the bad, and the neutral.
Pros:
-Great gameplay, filled with guns, swords, and parkour. Also, each Warframe has its own abilities which can slash, crush, and send enemies flying.
-Beautiful graphics, even on lowest settings. Burns eyes of people like me who see good graphics once a year when using highest ones.
-Insanely good optimization. Game looks amazing even on lowest settings, AND manages to run on lowest-spec laptops with basically no graphics card!
-Mods are what you will have to use throught the entirety of the game. They can double, triple, or somethin-ple the damage of your weapon and power of your Warframe, this also makes amazing weapons be bad enought when used by a noob, but allows bad weapons to be used far into the game, too.
Neutral:
-Extremely long crafting times, in this game you craft stuff with what basically is a 3D printer on steroids... But on the other hand, you instead of 3D objects filled from inside, create extremely complex things that normally would take weeks, or even months, or will just be impossible to make...
-Platinum the premium currency, is a PAIN to get, but you dont need real money, making it a neutral. I will never forgive this game for having me wait a whole hour for someone to trade few Prime parts for some platinum...
Cons:
-Can be very confusing at start, i have had problems with learning what am i supposed to do to get stronger and ended up running with unmodded Lex for 30% of the time i spent without knowledge that mods can make even worst weapon usable far into the game.
-I can not recommend the game for some people, more precisely - people that like to talk on global chats.
The kick bot in this game is absolutely SAVAGE, if you say something it doesnt like you will get chat banned right away anywhere from 24 hours, and a week.
And the worst part about it, is fact, is when you will try to get help on the forums - you most probably will get your account banned for several days, for something you have not even did.
I myself have been banned for 4 days for saying a "particularly insultive homosexual slur", which not only isnt true, as i never was a pervert and never talked about such things, not only in Warframe, but anywhere.
You dont even get a warning in this game, just straight off a savage, several day ban. And they also say they do that because they want me to become better. Seriously? I mean, anyone normal would get ♥♥♥♥ING MAD if he got banned and didnt even know for what, GIVE SOME DAMN WARNINGS FIRST GOD DAMMIT.
Conclusion: Get the game, its free, but dont you dare to use that damn chat to anything more than item previewing and trading, otherwise - you will most probably end with a ban.

After so long I've decided to finally review this game. I bought this game shortly after it was up for sale in 2015, and the game has come a long time since then.
Looking through these reviews talking about performance issues, I can honestly say that I haven't had any performance issues since maybe early 2016 when the game was in its infancy still. My pc is 5 years old and it runs this on a mix of high/ultra at 60fps+.
That's not to say the game doesn't have its issues, bugs, dupers and other botters, but what game doesn't? It seems people are too lazy to google "improve performance ark" or something like that since there is a few easy things anyone can do to improve performance by a bit.
I've played on both official and unofficial servers, ill talk briefly about my experience.
I've put in the bulk of my hours(1600 in fact) into one official server, and while I love this game, the official servers are brutal. Playing on these is a MASSIVE time investment, and I mean MASSIVE. It takes a long time to do anything, and starting on an official is brutal, much more so if it's a pvp server.
As far as unofficial servers go, if you can find one with higher rates and a decent friendly community then you're all set, get in there and enjoy the game.
The bottom line is that yes, the game has its issues as any other game does. There is a steady stream of content being added continuously, and the game is ultimately fun.
If you're on the fence about it, don't take all the negative reviews for fact, if you want to try it then jump in and try it. And unless you have alot of time or are a masochist then try find yourself a nice unofficial server to begin with.

Clicker Heroes is an incremental idle game with a higher than average depth within its genre. You click on sprites, you get money to become better at clicking on sprites, and the cycle goes on.
The game unlocks several systems the further you get in (random item drops, random powerups, timed quests) and requires a decent amount of optimization in order to achieve significant progress. The core of the game is "ascending", or starting the game again with buffs from the previous playthrough, in order to advance further and faster.
Although the game does what it says on the tin, I have two major problems with it.
First: Steam achievements. A slew of new achievements were recently added to the game and brought the bar of completion from a far yet reasonable level to months if not a year or two of constant grinding. Premium currency related achievements are ridiculous (you can get rubies ingame, but you know how f2p games are).
Second: The "Rate us on Steam, but please don't if you didn't like the game" button. Customers' interest comes before dev's feelings.
Apart from that, it's an idle game, you know what you are getting into. The "idle" part, though, is undermined by the need of upgrading heroes every time you ascend, then ascend, then reset again and level up again. The "efficient" route of ascending every hour or every few hours means I need to pay a lot more attention to the game than I should for an incremental game. You barely make any progress if you leave it running overnight or while you are at work.

That's not to say the game doesn't have its issues, bugs, dupers and other botters, but what game doesn't? It seems people are too lazy to google "improve performance ark" or something like that since there is a few easy things anyone can do to improve performance by a bit.
I've played on both official and unofficial servers, ill talk briefly about my experience.
I've put in the bulk of my hours(1600 in fact) into one official server, and while I love this game, the official servers are brutal. Playing on these is a MASSIVE time investment, and I mean MASSIVE. It takes a long time to do anything, and starting on an official is brutal, much more so if it's a pvp server.
As far as unofficial servers go, if you can find one with higher rates and a decent friendly community then you're all set, get in there and enjoy the game.
The bottom line is that yes, the game has its issues as any other game does. There is a steady stream of content being added continuously, and the game is ultimately fun.
If you're on the fence about it, don't take all the negative reviews for fact, if you want to try it then jump in and try it. And unless you have alot of time or are a masochist then try find yourself a nice unofficial server to begin with.

I played this during the EA phase back in 2015; it was a fun concept but horribly buggy and unoptimzed, so I decided to shelf it until release... Well two years later the fun concept is still there, certainly two years worth of content was added, but the game is still horribly buggy and unoptimzed. Clipping and rubberbanding are absolutely insane - you can get stuck (yes STUCK) on a rock half your size just if you get too close to it. You can have your tamed dinosaurs following you (a common procedure), only to have them rubberband into your position and now you are both stuck on each other (yes you can get unstuck without much trouble, but when it happens in a fight those few seconds of immobility can easily get you killed). The final straw for me was trying to tame a sabertooth - I shot him 12 times in a row only to watch him rubberband 15 feet away and have the shot not count as a hit. Then he'd just glitch right up to my face and take a cheat shot at me. There's just no gameplay possible with that much lag, you just stand there and shoot and desperately hope the server counts the shot that so obvisously hit on your own computer.
All these issues just stack up and completely drain any enjoyment this game has (which would actually be quite a lot, the base concept of this game continues to be very fun). Here's hoping that WC spends some time actually fixing bugs and improving server performance. Until then though, I just can't recommed this game.

I use the warframe launcher without steam, i have over 5000 hours in missions (aka the time you actually spend playing, do not confuse with the ammount of time the application is open) and i can safely recomend the game.
So do not pay attention to the time displayed here on steam as that was the time i used to buy a steam skin.
It starts by providing a glimpse of the gameplay and how everything works, since it's a sandbox game that is used to develop the engine and to provide an enviroment for artists to dump content into the game, it's really up to the player to define an objective.
Since Digital extremes doesn't know where you will go after getting your starter warframe and weapons, all paths have some grind to it, so one of the most common issues is when the player tries an objective that is impossible to achieve and that is to collect everything, while it's true you can get most things by playing (warframe, weapons, mods), expect to play alot, if you really are a completionist then not only is that very expensive (tennocon exclusives, workshop items at 6€ each in some cases and prime access) but it's also impossible to actually get everything.
Past events may have released sigils and emblems for you to use and those are not returning, founder exclusives are also out of your reach, cool looking sigils may also require you to be a guides of the lotus or the admin of the warframe wiki
The theme of the game is to play the way you want, you are a space ninja and you use all kinds of weapons, abilities and methods to kill enemies, you gain credits, resources, endo and many other things from kills and missions and those are used to mod the gameplay in the way you like.
You can add firerate, elementals to weapons, you can add more range to your abilities and you can have different abilities if you grind or buy other warframes, but the more content you skip, the more you will need to play, you see if you buy a completed warframe and you buy a booster to lvl up quickly you will likely have less experience in the game overall and less resources, credits and endo than other players, this means you will feel that you need to buy endo, credits and mods in order to compensate, leading to more costs.
If you bypass that initial difficulty then the game gets easier and easier and the game heavily rewards effort, effort in trying again, in killing enemies, in doing things multiple times.
Gameplay is a nice mix between Mass effect combat (3rd person shooter with abilities) and Phantasy star online (companions, lobby system, killing enemies 1 room at a time altough here you can easily skip rooms)
Developers do try to pace things out, so that boss missions do not end up being 10 minutes long for new players and 1 minute long for powerfull players, invulnerability stages and timers exist so that super efficient players can be rewarded but not by a degree of duzzens of times.
Even so, some players can easily achieve possibly 100x more kills in a mission than you (you killed 10 enemies, someone kills over 1k), be glad that here the goal is teamplay, so everything is shared, performance made by others can be used by you.
Players that do more effort and use all of the tools to kill and do the mission will essentially fail less, get more kills (so more resources, endo, exp,...) and will eventually get more in less time. This means that if you play poorly and rely heavily on the end mission reward instead of doing stuff in the actual missions, you will need to grind more, so the less effort the more punished you will be, this is a common issue that leads to complaining and it's usually the player's fault.
The players get more wacky and random as you progress as each player has his/her own definition of efficiency, initially you might be paired with players that have the same warframe and weapons as you, but later on a team is just as creative and cool to play with as the next 1000 missions that follow, so the game tries to keep things fresh, enviroments different and the gameplay fun.
It really all comes down to what you want to do in the game, but do not expect no grind if you want to collect 20 frames and all the weapons, many users complain when in reality it's their fault.
The game is really hard to balance, digital extremes does make an effort to try and keep the grind reasonable, for someone playing once a week this is an issue, but for someone playing daily, it doesn't take much time to get the new desired content and so the developers either introduce new grinding mechanics (that puts everyone on the same playing field for some time) or they introduce new resources, if they simply release something and use old resources or old mechanics, there will always be someone who can do that weapon instantly, no grinding required because it has been done in the past.
However, they have introduced many systems already and the game is becoming a bit overwelming on that aspect, to many currencies (ducats, credits, platinum,void traces,...), things to lvl up (focus, sindicates, warframe, weapons, mods) can also be a problem.
At some point they will need to stop and need to polish what they currently have without making the playerbase wait months.
So the game becomes super simple and easy for heavy and hardcore players, but super grindy for someone playing 1 mission a week, if that's the case then it is recomended that you lower your expectations on the time required to get a single warframe and that you create a more reasonable objective, do not aim to collect everything and then complain about lack of time to do it.
Music is superb, graphics are great and the game compatible with legacy hardware and OS (like direct x9 graphic cards, windows xp,....) and the gameplay is super enjoyable.
The downsides?
- for starters, prime access cost is the price of a tripple A game and this happens every 3 months for some discounted platinum, warframe, weapon and cosmetics.
The game offers exceptional value for it's cost (free) but then has these unique cosmetics that are in a bundle that costs 60$, a single cosmetic and a few boosters for that price is a terrible value.
- tennogen item costs are absurd, 6€ for a single skin? no platinum cost, if it was a platinum cost then those trading would be rewarded for it, but by having it tied to steam things get problematic.
- Many bugs, especially client and host related bugs, it happens in pretty much every update, where colors, mechanics and features work greatly as the host, but quickly fall appart when you are the client, yes the game is p2p.
Things that worked well before end up breaking in the most insane ways possible, this happens in every game with updates, but in warframe it's just silly the ammount of things that stop working after a single big update.
Some updates are clearly rushed and the end result is atrocious sometimes.
- Regrind aspect, sometimes you will be regrinding for the same content, DE certainly doesn't like you to upgrade existing content, they prefer making you play again to lvl up something new that makes the old obsolete, for example you get the dera weapon but there is a different weapon called dera vandal, making the regular dera rather obsolete if your goal isn't mastery.
Overall a great game, a great free to play game, very friendly aproach on the f2p genre, DE is a bit on the greedy side of things but considering i can do anything in the game and the most i have payed in the game ends up being a 6€ skin, i believe the value beats any other game that i have played.
The income for digital extremes comes mainly from the players that purchase plat and they often make bundles (like prime access) so that players feel inclided into buying the cosmetics, but if you only care about player quality, your own gameplay, then the game can offer that and charges nothing.
You can essentially be the best warframe player outthere, do any mission you like, play the way you like and in the end not pay for anything.

I started playing as a founder way back, and I still play today. The game is always changing, what we play today is so different than what I played back 4+ years ago, and I'm sure it will keep evolving. I love the devs and how they have kept up with players with twitter, livestreams, and forums. Personally, I like co-op grinding games and shy away from PVP, so really enjoy this one. Co-op is where the game really shines, and you can solo a lot of it as well. If you are looking for PVP it does exist, but it was added on much later. The game was created with co-op in mind and it is still mostly a co-op game.
Certainly worth a download and test, if you are even a little curious. I would also recommend checking out some of their dev streams on Youtube/Twitch, to get an idea of how the devs think and their direction.
-graphics: great, and improving. They add new shaders and update graphics as the game goes on.
-gameplay: I love it, especially since the last overhaul, making the mechs feel more "ninja-like" in how they move. I like the 3rd person gunplay and the melee is also a blast for me.

PROS:
-Lots of content

CONS:

OVERALL THOUGHTS:
If you have a system that can run it then go for it. Playing with friends definitely yields the best experience. Running it with an R9 390X and a I7 4690K I got about 50 fps on medium settings. The games still beautiful don't get me wrong, but it's still rough around the edges.

The game is optimized so well, that even my old laptop that was inferior to... not even my Lenovo, it was inferior to freaking Commodore 128, have run it... and now my new laptop goes beyond what i ever expected to see in games.
The game has been created by developers known to world of gaming as DE, which is short for Digital Extremes, they have literally made a game with great gameplay, that is able to run even on the worst PC's of all time, and with a PC able to run it in 60 FPS on lowest settings it still looks great and plays even better...
And the gameplay... the first video you see of the game doesnt lie, this game does look and play like this.
...ALSO...did i mentioned i did run this game on DirectX, and not something like Vulkan that could explain why the game runs so well?
shortly, Digital Extremes truelly can optimize their games to the absolute Extremes
The good, the bad, and the neutral.
Pros:
-Great gameplay, filled with guns, swords, and parkour. Also, each Warframe has its own abilities which can slash, crush, and send enemies flying.
-Beautiful graphics, even on lowest settings. Burns eyes of people like me who see good graphics once a year when using highest ones.
-Insanely good optimization. Game looks amazing even on lowest settings, AND manages to run on lowest-spec laptops with basically no graphics card!
-Mods are what you will have to use throught the entirety of the game. They can double, triple, or somethin-ple the damage of your weapon and power of your Warframe, this also makes amazing weapons be bad enought when used by a noob, but allows bad weapons to be used far into the game, too.
Neutral:
-Extremely long crafting times, in this game you craft stuff with what basically is a 3D printer on steroids... But on the other hand, you instead of 3D objects filled from inside, create extremely complex things that normally would take weeks, or even months, or will just be impossible to make...
-Platinum the premium currency, is a PAIN to get, but you dont need real money, making it a neutral. I will never forgive this game for having me wait a whole hour for someone to trade few Prime parts for some platinum...
Cons:
-Can be very confusing at start, i have had problems with learning what am i supposed to do to get stronger and ended up running with unmodded Lex for 30% of the time i spent without knowledge that mods can make even worst weapon usable far into the game.
-I can not recommend the game for some people, more precisely - people that like to talk on global chats.
The kick bot in this game is absolutely SAVAGE, if you say something it doesnt like you will get chat banned right away anywhere from 24 hours, and a week.
And the worst part about it, is fact, is when you will try to get help on the forums - you most probably will get your account banned for several days, for something you have not even did.
I myself have been banned for 4 days for saying a "particularly insultive homosexual slur", which not only isnt true, as i never was a pervert and never talked about such things, not only in Warframe, but anywhere.
You dont even get a warning in this game, just straight off a savage, several day ban. And they also say they do that because they want me to become better. Seriously? I mean, anyone normal would get ♥♥♥♥ING MAD if he got banned and didnt even know for what, GIVE SOME DAMN WARNINGS FIRST GOD DAMMIT.
Conclusion: Get the game, its free, but dont you dare to use that damn chat to anything more than item previewing and trading, otherwise - you will most probably end with a ban.

Chivalry Medieval Warfare is a very fast-paced online sword fighting game that focuses on multiplayer battle. There are  modes such as free for all, team deathmatch, lastman standing, and many team objective battles. It actually takes great teamwork to push past objectives and win the battle. When you first start playing this game, you have the option of playing in a low rank lobby that lasts from ranks 0-15. This will help you get use to this game and prepare you to play with the big boys. The fighting in Chivalry is spectacular. You get such satisfaction chopping off enemies limbs or getting double kills. There are many ways of swinging your weapon by using mouse wheels or you can customize your controls. You can also block or dodge depending on your class. There are four different classes: Archer, Man at Arms, Vanguard, and the Knight. Each class has a diffent speeds, weapons, and armor. There are many maps you can play on in Chivalry as well. A big problem with this game is that there are many bugs that make your game randomly freeze and you'll have to exit out of it. Also, you randomly lose connection from your game. All in all, Chivalry is a great medieval multiplayer fighting game that you should pick up when it goes on sale.

Diving into melee combat, your skill against another person, and the uncertainty of what can happen on the battlefield at any time...it gets intense. Previously, I would have recommended this game, however, after taking a break for a while and coming back after the "Battle for Balance" Update, I can no longer say that this game is any fun...  The new update totally breaks the game's class system and removes all need for skill.  The entire combat system has been somewhat dumbed down, making it more of a class vs class battle.  For example, a knight will one-hit and MOH and two-hit and vangaurd.  Vangaurds kill knights in three hits and other vangaurds in two hits.  Essentially, because of the health/damage rework, the MOH class is unviable...  Same goes for archers, sadly.  Now the game is just a battle between knights and vangaurds as the other classes do not stand a chance in combat.  It's funny, because prior to this update, all of the classes were perfectly balanced.  A MOH could take down a vanguard and a knight, had the player enough skill.  Vanguards might have found it difficult to take down MOH due to the vanguard's lengthy weapons.  Basically, every class had an enemy in which they were strong against and an enemy in which  they were weak against.  After the new update, MOH and archers are weak against all, and knights and vanguards are balanced foes for each other.
If the old combat system comes back, maybe I'll reinstall Chiv...  But for now, it shall sit in my steam library and not on my hard drive.

Warframe has come a long way from when i first started playing, but i can honestly say the majority of it was great! Let me start by describing what warframe is. Its an over the shoulder third-person shooter where you play the role of a ninja warrior in space. The solar system is in chaos, and it's up to you to maintain the balance. With many weapon types to choose from, and different frames to use to suit your playstyle, the possibilities are endless. However there are certain strategies in higher level missions that even veteran players will tell you work. It's pretty much an MMO at this point, so certain "classes" of warframes work better at farming resources on certain missions. The developers also release new content as operations to introduce the new features, for example, the newest addition was corpus dropships that drop squads of enemies into battle. It was introduced as Operation: Ambulas Reborn, which featured a reworked boss that dropped in from the ship with a squad of regular enemies. There were a few bugs at first, but the incredibly awesome support team was very quick to respond to reports and get back within 24-48 hours. All in all, this has become one of the best free to play games i have ever played, and the graphics do an excellent job of immersing you in a living, breathing world that is constantly changing. I have to say that there are certain aspects of the game which require you to pay for features. Such as certain weapons, cosmetic packs, etc. Other than that, if you work hard and spend a decent amount of time on it, everything important is attainable without paying money for it. I do encourage you to support the developers by buying things that you may like, but only at your own discretion. Speaking of which, there is also a thriving market for the ingame currency, platinum, where you can spend platinum to buy parts, weapon mods, and other hard to obtain aspects from other players, as well as selling your own parts and mods to other players to obtain platinum. The prices will indeed vary on the rarity of what you are trying to get, but there is also sites and a wiki for any questions you may have about said things. All in all i have had a great experience with this game, rather than reading my long-winded review about the game, why not try it yourself? It's free! Also feel free to add me ingame and i will do my best to be as helpful as possible, my name is Mix_Masterson. See you on the battlefield, and have fun!

TL,DR: This game is fun. Still, I think it is completely destroyed by jerky character movement and some bad combat mechanics.
The fighting mechanics in general are pretty good. I love the mayhem when several knights with two-handed swords swing furiously and blindly around themselves. That's awesome. One particular feature I dislike is blocking. It's very weird when you can block a 20kg hammer with a dagger... isn't it? The most feature I hate most is the ability to spin around vertical axis without speed constraints. If you set high enough mouse sensitivity, you can swing the sword/axe and then quickly turn around, instantly hitting everybody. That's not much realistic, but it gets worse with overhead swings and thrusts. You can wind up your overhead or thrust facing one direction, and then, *in the middle of the swing*, easily turn 180 degrees and hit someone behind you. I don't object arcade style fighting, but this is too much. Experienced players use this often and the game becomes more about learning the timings of moves than about actually fighting simulation. Not enjoyable. I'd love if they made it the same way as in e.g. Witcher 2 - you can't spin around like a dancer mid-swing with a heavy sword, that's just BS; everything has its own weight, even you do.
The objective modes are also great. Castle sieges, protecting carts and vagons, killing kings, burning ships, simply great.
Music is very much lacking, in my opinion. There's only one good song that I heard, the rest is almost non-existent.
My additional pet peeves include a complete lack of damage information, which is a power motivator in other games. You won't know who killed you and from where. You won't know how much damage have you caused to other people before they killed you. You will be asking yourself whether you have actually hit somebody or not. You will see some summary once the game ends, but just basics, and not sooner. It would be so easy to add that information (e.g. to chat area), but it's not there. Such a pity.
What kills this game, is jerky movement. My experience is that player movement and weapon movement is far from fluent - it's like seeing 15 fps game (when I actually run with stable 60 fps). Especially the long weapons like swords - the blade is teleporting from one place to a different place. Of course this is connected to player's ability to spin around freely, like having no weight at all. That makes the blade movement even more unpredictable. And that's not something you would expect from a two-handed sword. I don't think the jerky movement is caused by lag, rather it seems like graphics engine deficiency. When I compare player and weapon movement to e.g. War of the Roses, the difference is clear - jerky vs fluent (of course, War of the Roses' combat speed is slower, that also influences that, but that's not what I'm talking about).
So yeah, game is fun, but... it is far from what I expected and wished for. It's for people mindlesly killing people arcade style, or for people who wish to learn the game deficiencies and flaws in detail and then base their skills on that. It's not the enjoyable medieval combat simulator I hoped for.

shortly, Digital Extremes truelly can optimize their games to the absolute Extremes
The good, the bad, and the neutral.
Pros:
-Great gameplay, filled with guns, swords, and parkour. Also, each Warframe has its own abilities which can slash, crush, and send enemies flying.
-Beautiful graphics, even on lowest settings. Burns eyes of people like me who see good graphics once a year when using highest ones.
-Insanely good optimization. Game looks amazing even on lowest settings, AND manages to run on lowest-spec laptops with basically no graphics card!
-Mods are what you will have to use throught the entirety of the game. They can double, triple, or somethin-ple the damage of your weapon and power of your Warframe, this also makes amazing weapons be bad enought when used by a noob, but allows bad weapons to be used far into the game, too.
Neutral:
-Extremely long crafting times, in this game you craft stuff with what basically is a 3D printer on steroids... But on the other hand, you instead of 3D objects filled from inside, create extremely complex things that normally would take weeks, or even months, or will just be impossible to make...
-Platinum the premium currency, is a PAIN to get, but you dont need real money, making it a neutral. I will never forgive this game for having me wait a whole hour for someone to trade few Prime parts for some platinum...
Cons:
-Can be very confusing at start, i have had problems with learning what am i supposed to do to get stronger and ended up running with unmodded Lex for 30% of the time i spent without knowledge that mods can make even worst weapon usable far into the game.

You dont even get a warning in this game, just straight off a savage, several day ban. And they also say they do that because they want me to become better. Seriously? Conclusion: Get the game, its free, but dont you dare to use that damn chat to anything more than item previewing and trading, otherwise - you will most probably end with a ban.

Sept 2014: Yet another game that holds so much promise that fails misserably due to client side hit detection. If everyone in the server is running low pings, the battles can be intense and rewarding. However once pings begin to climb, your sword will pass through your enemies like spectres and your blocks will mean nothing against the enemys delayed hits. I really enjoy the idea of this game, and when it works, I have a blast. But because of the spotty hit detection. I'm left wishing I had saved my money.
July 2015: A year Later nothing has changed... It has only gotten worse. US servers are bombarded by people across the globe with pings in the 300's taking advantage of the garbage hit detection. Try to take advantage of this yourself and join a server half way across the world, and you're instantly kicked. Aparrently we're just too kind and allow anyone to walk into our servers... Interesting.
Besides the game breaking Client side hit detection, the game has become nothing more than a metagame of even more ridiculous exploits that have never been fixed by the devs. Why? You may ask. It's simple... The devs care more about piggy backing DLC content into the game to make more money, and have completely abandoned the actual game and gameplay mechanics.
So, a year later do I recommend this game? Have I changed my mind? Absolutley not. My initial thumbs down stands ten fold.

Fantastic game. Literally nothing else like it.
Dinos. And wow at all the Dinos. A lot of thought has been put into the AI of each and every single species, and some will surprise (& terrorize) you with their behavior.
Oh boy, here we go....
No seriously. Unless you REALLY like PVP, and can handle being a victim of the truly nasty behavior that is, by design, part of the game....don't do it. The mechanics of the game encourage players in PVP to drug, imprison and blood♥♥♥♥♥♥other players. It's ridiculous, but it is part of the game, so I'm not knocking it. I just don't do PVP in this game, simply bc I have to be a victim until I get strong enough to protect myself, and that takes a VERY, very, very long time. PVE has it's own issues, and those are enough for me w/o the hassle of PVP. If it's not fun, why do it?
in PVP is an exercise in futility. At least for early-mid game. Theoretically, if you have a very large, powerful, active Tribe, you can police your server to keep griefing down to a minimum. But the truth is, there is almost always someone stronger than you, and at some point you will have your base destroyed. Again, not knocking it, this is part of the game. It may be your thing. If so, go for it.
- You pretty much have to build your base near the water. You will eventually need plumbing in your base, and will absolutely need to be near the water.
Guess what, this is true for EVERYONE. So, everyone builds on the water, and everyone expands their territory markers way out in order to claim land and keep anyone else from building anything near them. These Land Grabs can severely limit your ability to build, and IMO, this game mechanic should be changed to limit the size of your territory to a reasonable area. You want more land? Build multiple bases somewhere else on the map. As it is now, nearly every scrap of quality waterfront land on every original server is taken, and (as far as I know) there is nothing you can do to reclaim an ancient base someone deserted when they moved to a new server months ago. If it's abandoned, it should (ultimately) be reclaimable. Reclaimed as in taking over ownership, not as in destroying it all. It would be reasonable to allow people to take ownership of an existing base if it has been abandoned for a set period of time, without having to completely destroy said base.
My idea is to just make it like the Taming process. Make it so you have to use a certain device, Engram or level of tech in order to plant a crafted object in said base that takes time to take over ownership of structures in a limited abandoned area. Just an idea, but I think a sound one. If this already exists, I would love to hear about it.
That's really the only serious negatives. There are a few usability complaints I wish they would change, but nothing major.
However, be warned: The patience level required to play Ark is extremely high.
- You will die. Often.
- You will get camped, either in PVP or by a Carnosaur, who incidentally seems to have the largest aggro range of any creature in the game.
- In early-mid game, your base will be destroyed many times. Again, in PVP or in PVE by predators.
- You will have your consumables stolen by a large bird that you have no apparent defense against. Said bird will camp your base, your bed, and generally ruin your life. This bird is actually satan.
- You will lose all your stuff. Either thru dying and not being able to reclaim your gear, or by the total destruction of your base by something meaner & more powerful than you.
- Then you will lose it all again.
- You will have to start completely from scratch. More than once.
- You will be tempted to completely quit the game and go play Candy Crush.
Yes it's hard. But it is rewarding when you do finally start to progress. Once you tame your first Dino you will be hooked. Once you finally get a feel for what you need to do to build a better and more easily defensible base, you start feeling much more comfortable in the game.
If all this is something you think you can manage without throwing things at your monitor, then give Ark a try. If not, then just go play something else, bc otherwise, the frustration you will experience as part of this game is just not going to be worth it to you.

I have played over 1300+ hours on Ark Survival Evolved.
After experiencing in full what the game has to offer.
I am very happy to see that the VAST MAJORITY who's played Ark are united on the same page and feel the same way about this game.
That general consensus being that this game had great potential but the developers has done nothing to help it's community in achieving what it's player base wanted.
Ark is fun in some ways. However, it is THE MOST TIME CONSUMING game you will ever play. This is due to the system of the game which offers no balance to new players or fresh players that have just come to a new server. The aim of the game has become to oppress the newcomers and to never trust a single outsider, sometimes even the members of your own tribe who may seek to overthrow you.
As the leader of an official server, despite having achieved all I needed to achieve to be at the top, I soon realised it was taking me 3-4 hours of daily maintenance in order to ensure my base was up to date and secure. To spend that much time just to be on a game NOT TO PLAY, but to complete "Chores" in order to survive in a game before being able to play in it is much too ridiculous if I may say so.
The bugs and glitches are many and yet the devs continue to implement and add new things and creatures to the game without improving the gameplay or optimization one bit.
EXAMPLES INDLUDE: You can easily get stuck in rocks and die of a glitch anytime. You can sit down on a chair you made and try to fish and suddenly you die due to some completely unexpected glitch is just fkn unacceptable.
With all of this being said, there are still quite a few things that aren't quite right with Ark. Whilst many of us have supported Ark's Developers and invested much of our hard earned money in hopes of seeing this game come to fruition. None of this has come true for us. To add a final bitter aftertaste for all of us loyal supporters who helped support this game for years, we are then forced to an Ultimatum to either purchase the game for the full price or not be able to play this game even after paying $30 USD for a poor Early Access which required financial aid from a then non-existent player base.
Having given a piece of mind, I bid this game farewell. AND I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME TO ANYONE.
JUST PLAY A BETTER GAME AND SUPPORT BETTER DEVELOPERS.
Have a good one. Thanks for reading.
P.S - Thank you to the Ark Developers who created something that had some great features in it and for enabling me to make some great moments and memories through the game. Sorry I am unable to support you any longer. Good bye.

For all those interested in buying this game, I can sum it up in one word - "satisfying".
Learning this game takes a good few hundred hours but every second is worth it.
TIME FOR PROS AND CONS
PROs
. Excellent combat system - there are so many aspects of this which you will pick up in time. No two players will have the same fighting style, and a lot of it boils down to body language and seeing patterns in your oppents' attacks.
. Variety of weapons - personally, i <3 using the heavy crossbow and my fists, but if you want to go sword and board, that's cool.
. Variety of game modes - Free For All, Team Deathmatch, Last Team Standing (a "battle royale" mode; if you find yourself being the last man standing on a team, prepare to have the biggest adrenaline rush in your gaming life), Duel, Team Objective.
. Balanced weapons - a lot of people will disagree with me here, but I think the weapons in this game are balanced and fighting comes down to skill and not zweihanders
. This game will keep you hooked and coming back for more
CONs
. Lag - ALWAYS check the "ping" column on the server list before joining a server and lag won't be a problem.
. Empty servers! WTB more Last Team Standing servers with low ping
. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t - Sometimes you will die, and you will literally say "WHAT THE HELL JUST HAPPENED", perhaps an enemy dragged you, or stabbed around your shield, or you got feinted or shot in the head or someone magically attacked faster than you despite you winding up waaaaay before him or someone simply hit through your block. These sorts of things drive a lot of new players away, but personally I love the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
. Rage - "♥♥♥♥♥♥ ARCHER/FEINTER/DRAGGER/LAGGER/BACKSTABBER" immediately springs to mind.
TIPS
. Be wary of anyone rank 40 or higher, these are the best players the game has to offer. However, always remember that THEY CAN BE KILL JUST LIKE EVERYONE ELSE. So many times I have seen a 1 hp rank 40+ beat a rank 30 because the rank 30 fearfully tried to block his oppenent to death.
. Unlock weapons through official servers, just to be sure it registers each kill for your next weapon.
. Knights aren't as tough as they look, 4 quick stabs with the thrusting dagger, 3 stabs with a spear, 1 body hit with the maul, are all you need to kill a knight.
. Rush the enemy archers!
. Bow to challenge someone to a duel, i love this player made mechanic, challenging someone to a duel may result in an epic 1 on 1 for the ages, or a quick backstab from an enemy teammate

The bugs and glitches are many and yet the devs continue to implement and add new things and creatures to the game without improving the gameplay or optimization one bit.
EXAMPLES INDLUDE: You can easily get stuck in rocks and die of a glitch anytime. You can sit down on a chair you made and try to fish and suddenly you die due to some completely unexpected glitch is just fkn unacceptable.
With all of this being said, there are still quite a few things that aren't quite right with Ark. Whilst many of us have supported Ark's Developers and invested much of our hard earned money in hopes of seeing this game come to fruition. None of this has come true for us. To add a final bitter aftertaste for all of us loyal supporters who helped support this game for years, we are then forced to an Ultimatum to either purchase the game for the full price or not be able to play this game even after paying $30 USD for a poor Early Access which required financial aid from a then non-existent player base.
Having given a piece of mind, I bid this game farewell. AND I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME TO ANYONE.
JUST PLAY A BETTER GAME AND SUPPORT BETTER DEVELOPERS.
Have a good one. Thanks for reading.
P.S - Thank you to the Ark Developers who created something that had some great features in it and for enabling me to make some great moments and memories through the game. Sorry I am unable to support you any longer. Good bye.

Storming into a valley with ten of your teammates, all shouting 'FOR THE GLORY OF AGATHAAA'. All with their swords at the ready aiming to dismember the Mason Order ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s on the other side. While trebuchets are flinging rocks overhead at the enemy citadel and enemy archer's arrows barely missing their targets you find yourself suddenly surrounded by three enemy knights. You manage to pierce the left guy's adomen, making him staggering back in pain. In that moment the others succesfully slice your head clean off in response.
In your final moments you'll see your body succumb to gravity while your separated skull makes the most of it's new-found freedom, aimlessly rolling into a shallow puddle of blood-stained water. The world slowly fades to black while you say goodbye to the corporeal vessel that lays before you.
You briefly witnessed glory in it's true nature: both a beauty and horrific. And you loved every second of it. Let's try that again.

First and foremost, it's a click spam "adventure" based around big numbers, idling, and getting the feeling of progression at all times. It's a clicker through and through, so if those aren't your cup of tea, give it a pass.
That said, the animations in the game are smooth, and it has lots of mechanics that give you different things to look forward to. Hiring mercs to go on quests for bonus stuff (to enhance your not playing the game, of course!), optimizing ancient beings to buff your stats, and even a clan system with daily raids on a special monster that rewards players for their contribution.
Between the plethora of mechanics and the smooth, neatness of the game, the text is witty and fun, making references to other brands and pop culture at times, while still having its own personality. Finally, the game offers a cash shop that you can choose to use. Naturally it's faster to acquire the special currency the cash shop offers by purchasing it, but you can also acquire it through gameplay as well, so you don't need to feel pressured to buy any.
At the end of the day, the game is free and a fairly small download. If you're even a little curious, give it a download and see for yourself. Just remember that certain things in the game are locked until you progress a ways in, so don't be surprised when your options for the first hour are "click" and "don't click"

I wish there was a different developer on this game, becuase from what I have seen, these ones are a little slackish and don't really listen to the community. While it's still a fun and good-looking game, you need to have a monster pc to run it at above 40 fps. They kept adding to the end-game when the start and mid-game weren't done yet. They released the game when it wasn't NEARLY finished. They needed to optimise the water, the foliage (have you looked at the trees?), the shadows, particles, and the A.I. is still terrible. I honestly hope the devs give full modding compatability so people can fix it like with Skyrim, make it better. There is already a awesome mod that is constantly being developed that completely revamps the way you tame and the way dinos think, and it's doing great (the mod is Zoology). They didn't put enough time into making better for the community, they just made it better for those that were dominating the servers, then they wiped everything and destroyed their playerbase. By all means it's a very fun game, I will continue to play it often, but I would only recommend it if they pull a "No Man's Sky" and continue the expansion of the early and mid-game. And generally optimise it better. What is says in the minimum is playing with literally everything turned down, even the resolution, so you can't tell the difference between a rex and a dilo from across a river. Get this if you have a beast pc and enjoy the passive-ish grind with occasional half-hour bits of action. Otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it, it isn't finished yet, despite it being "fully released".

So im still a little bit of a noob to this game (137 hours when writting this) and am far from knowing all the ins and outs of the game. But the reason I wrote a review was because something truely special happened today.
I finally finished building my first prime warframe, at mastery rank 6 after many weeks of hard grind and dedication. Not only during missions but also trading at Maroos bizaar. It was trinity prime. After only having played excalibur (the starter warframe) i didnt know what to expect. What I experienced was something i cannot fully describe. All i can tell you is that at the moment I equipped trinity Prime, I realised that this game was more than just a game. I spent about 2 hours customising her looks and my weapons looks to find the perfect balance of colours. Im still in shock as to how amazing it is getting a prime warframe, beautiful things they are. I was so proud when i started playing in Pub games with her (although I clearly had no clue as to how to play her).
After playing her for an hour or two, I truely grasped what it was to be God-like. Jumping to one of (if not the most) powerful Frames in the game from an excalibur is mind opening.
Now to the actual review... This game has scarse few tutorials and requires constant 3rd party research for you to understand how to do something. You may spend dozens of hours grinding to just get enough loot to build 1 weapon. The in game currency (plat) is overpriced AF. Sometimes you may fall through the map or get stuck.
But. This game has some of the cleanest animations and details that I have ever seen on a game (my i3 and GTX 750Ti get around 140fps without V-sync @1080P max settings incl. anti ailising ect). The "grind" is actually such fun that it doesnt feel like grinding. You can get plat and every item (maybe not skins) in the game without paying a cent (through trading). This game is NOT a PaytoWin but the first 100 hours sure do feel like it. After a while you will see that you dont need to pay to get the best loot in the game. The movement engine is designed so exquisitely. The gameplay is always fun (except for PvP, that just sucks). it has RPG elements but doesnt feel anything like one.
In short, I urge every PC gamer out there that doesnt have a wooden PC to try out this game.

I don't really play this game as much anymore, but I still log in on occasion to see what's new and kill some trash mobs.
As you can tell by my hours, I was once incredibly addicted to this game, though I should point out that a lot of my time logged in was me being afk and leaving the launcher running while I'd go to school and stuff. Still, even if half my hours are a result of afk, I still played this a LOT.
The grind is real and it's easy to get hooked trying to upgrade all your crap. Ninja-parkour-robot-hack&slash-3rdpersonshooter with many playable warframes, weapons, and customizations for your loadout. It allows for many types of gameplay and levels that ease the monotony of the grind a bit and let you zone out and kill stuff in pretty neat ways.
The AI is pretty dumb and end-game becomes more about calculations and maximizing your DPS to kill the mobs that don't really increase in difficulty other than how long it takes to kill each one, and how much damage they do. Creating teams of warframes that work well together is pretty much essential late game to make sure you don't die too quickly, and that you can kill mobs before they kill you.
Overall, for a free-to-play game, it's pretty solid and can be incredibly addicting. It's not really pay2win either, it's more of paying for convenience, timers, and skins. If you do spend money, it just allows you to get items/mods for your weapons/warframes faster with less hassle, but since this game isn't very focused on PvP (although there is some) it really isn't a pay2win model and you can have fun with or without spending a dime.

Ark is a survival game set on an island inhabited by dinosaurs and other prehistoric creatures. And dodos.
To survive on this Island you have to eat, drink and build a shelter to withstand the cold of the night. Of course you also need weapons to defend yourself from the creatures of the Island and maybe even from other players.
With nearly everything you do you get experience and levelups. With each level up you get a certain amount of skill points and engram points. With skill point you are able to increase your stats. With the engram points you are able to unlock new
engrams (blueprints) to craft new items or objects.
Another rather important thing is the possibility to tame the creatures. Therefore you need to get them unconscious and then feed them until the taming bar is filled. Depending on the type of food the bar feels faster but nevertheless it takes very long until it is completely filled. To ride the animal you also need a suitable saddle.
Even though the may be fun to play there are way to many things that lower or even destroy the fun you could have with the game.
The first thing are many bugs that occure and since the game is now released from Early Access im most certain those things wont be fixed.
The next thing, and probably the most important one, is the performance. Since the beginning of the game in its Early Access phase the game suffered from a very poor performance. The developers promised ever since to improve it. Not only that, they also promised to release a patch to support DirecX 12 which also should improve the performance. But till the present day the performance is still terrible and it seems like the plans for the DirecX 12 patch are comletely gone.
The last thing I want to point out are the developers. Even though they knew of those problems they just made promises. They released a few patches which increased the performance. But not enough. They made patches which fixed some bugs. But not enough. They decided that it was more important to release content like new creatures or new objects to craft. And then they decided that it was more impoertant to use the money they got for finishing their game to make an expansion. An expansion which is not more than a new map with little changes to the gameplay.
Ark: Survival Evolved was a promising game at the beginning of its Early Access Phase. But as it went on the developers carried on to destroy it. And with the release of the expansion it was clear that the developers gave up on the game and just wanted to make money with it. And then they even decided to release it in its current state. I can't recommend this game and I honestly can't understand people who recommend it.

At the time of this review, My playing time was 6.2 hours.
Introduction
Okay, my review will be bad because I'm six hours into the game, I'm only earning quintillion, and doing 1,000T damage. I have no hero souls and I have never ascended, I'll update this when I have got a bit futher, but as of now, here is my opinion
First Hour (explaining features)
It starts off with you, no gold, no DPS, 1 click damage and a monster. (dps stands for damage per second) you kill the monster and earn gold. Enough to upgrade Cid the Helpful Adventurer who gives you more click damage. Then there is Treebeast who gives you dps. As you progress, you unlock more hero's. You can then advance stages, and like the golden cookies in cookie clicker, there are rubies and this weird orange octopus who gives you rubies. Rubies are used to buy cool things like instant ascension with 7 hero souls (I'll get to that later) Rubies are easier to get when, yes, purchased. After you kill a few monsters and get to stage five, a boss appears who has a 30 second timer. You can get hero upgrades which upgrade your hero. Hero souls are used for upgrading cool little guys that give you bonuses (e.g you get 80 more seconds to kill a boss) . You also use hero souls to summon them. There are achievements which when earned grant you a gift (e.g 0.3x your dps).
Pros And Cons (+= pros -= cons)
+Always entertaining
+Cool Features
+Original Clicker Game
+Free
-Addictive
-Numbers dont make sense (E.G 1,000T dmg per second)
Rating
7.4/10
Summary (TL;DR)
A great game with tons of features but with very little issues, and its addicting.

Ark is a survival game set on an island inhabited by dinosaurs and other prehistoric creatures. And dodos.
To survive on this Island you have to eat, drink and build a shelter to withstand the cold of the night. Of course you also need weapons to defend yourself from the creatures of the Island and maybe even from other players.
With nearly everything you do you get experience and levelups. With each level up you get a certain amount of skill points and engram points. With skill point you are able to increase your stats. With the engram points you are able to unlock new
engrams (blueprints) to craft new items or objects.
Another rather important thing is the possibility to tame the creatures. Therefore you need to get them unconscious and then feed them until the taming bar is filled. Depending on the type of food the bar feels faster but nevertheless it takes very long until it is completely filled. To ride the animal you also need a suitable saddle.
Even though the may be fun to play there are way to many things that lower or even destroy the fun you could have with the game.
The first thing are many bugs that occure and since the game is now released from Early Access im most certain those things wont be fixed.
The next thing, and probably the most important one, is the performance. Since the beginning of the game in its Early Access phase the game suffered from a very poor performance. The developers promised ever since to improve it. Not only that, they also promised to release a patch to support DirecX 12 which also should improve the performance. But till the present day the performance is still terrible and it seems like the plans for the DirecX 12 patch are comletely gone.
The last thing I want to point out are the developers. Even though they knew of those problems they just made promises. They released a few patches which increased the performance. But not enough. They made patches which fixed some bugs. But not enough. They decided that it was more important to release content like new creatures or new objects to craft. And then they decided that it was more impoertant to use the money they got for finishing their game to make an expansion. An expansion which is not more than a new map with little changes to the gameplay.
Ark: Survival Evolved was a promising game at the beginning of its Early Access Phase. But as it went on the developers carried on to destroy it. And with the release of the expansion it was clear that the developers gave up on the game and just wanted to make money with it. And then they even decided to release it in its current state. I can't recommend this game and I honestly can't understand people who recommend it.

I've been burned out on MMOs for a few years now, even after trying WoW for the first time only a few months back. And so, for years, I've been stipulating the kinda things MMOs need to change the formulae and come back on top. After a sudden surge of the ARPG I thought this was the way forward. Combat is fundamental in maintaining gamer's attention and overal meat of the game. ARPGs have a knack for making enemies a physical construct (that you don't just tab target to) and so the feeling of attacking NPCs becomes more real. But little did I know this could still be done in 3rd person.
Warframe contains within it at least most of the things I want MMOs changed to. It encorportes two essential games into one, IMO, which are Borderlands and Prototype; both of which were games known for their fun gameplay. To encorporate high level design, for parkour, loot scavanging and creative exploration is not an easy feat especially fitting it into a sub MMO. I say sub because it's two multiplayer varients; 4 player co op for all missions and actual mass multiplayer for Hub areas; for trade. It's easy to see why they did this, we all know how belittling it is to be part of vast groups online where you hardly feel any impact coming from your own actions. Warframe counters this pathetically ancient trend, the holy trinity, by making all classes self sufficent by allowing you to change how they work through mods (roughly translated as armour upgrades and skills all in one).
The only drawback I've found is, as mentioned earlier, a distinct lack of mass multiplayer due to 4 player co op system. There are emotes put into the game your character performs in a familiar mmo archetype but this is evidently inconsequential given the lack of social mechanics beyond trade and guild hub interactions. Arguably this applies to most MMOs as well, as we expect to bump into other players during escapades and come together naturally, achieving common goals. The lack of a holy trinity system, limited players per match and lack of interactable non-combat related mechanics beyond trade is the only reason a Warframe player will seek additional content in other MMOs. However this is certainly not something that can easily draw players away. When I think about the social interaction, yes it is vitial to the genre but, it's being away from the rest of what Warframe does right that ultimately negates bothering with another MMO again. I will miss being self sufficient, powerful from the start, high & layered level design, solid phyiscal models for NPCS and simplicity of crafting and progression. All of which is offered at no cost to the player to play. I can only hope ARPG MMOs will lean towards these single-player influences mechanics as it still remains the fate of MMO genres depend on their success.

The game is amazing with beautiful landscapes and quite pleasant crafting and building system. The best part is definetly to explore the world and tame the many, gorgeous dinosaurs out there. You level up, become stronger, learn more recipes and then further expand your base. It is fun.
Now, why a negative review? Because I can't recommend it and I will list a number of reasons.
1. The developers released a paid DLC during Early Access. The game was full of bugs and poorly optimized and yet, they released a DLC for an unfinished game.
2. Said bugs persist even today. I have been playing for roughly 30 hours and the number of bugs I found were ridiculous. While trying to solve some of them I found out there are bugs from 2015 that are gamebreaking and have not been fixed yet. To mention one, randomly everyone on the server started to get negative skill points, blocking our advancement. Isn't that nice?
3. Very, very poorly optimized. I have a great machine, but I can't run ark on ultra. Sure, it is gorgeous, but they need to polish this, otherwise randomly you may face FPS drops.
4. Multiplayer is a bloody mess. If you plan to have your own small server well, tough luck. You are tethered to the host. You can not move more than 760meters away from him. Their excuse is that it is made to optimize how the game works and not lag, but the same would happen if I were to open a dedicated server. It is a notable lie... Which brings me to another painful point...
5. Scam Server? I am not 100% sure, it is just a feel on this one, but you can check it yourself. Creating a dedicated server for Ark is HELL! I made servers for KF2, for Counter Strike, 7 days to die and heck, many Minecraft server, but none was as difficult as ARK. It bugged, I had to restart the server. Lost everything at least twice until finnally it SEEMS to work. Why do I call it a scam? Because they promote a company that rents EU Servers. That to me is absolutely fishy...
tl.dr: Good and possibly fun game, definetly not worth the investment, shady devs, avoid until you get at least a 90% discount.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is a team based hack & slash game. It takes place in a fictional world that is reminiscent of Europe during the crusades.
The kingdom of Agatha has had a time of military victories and expansion. However, the series of victories ends when the Agathian king decides to attack the nation of Tenosia. Being unprepared for Tenosia's desert climate the Agathian Army fails horribly and the king dies in battle. A big portion of the Agathian army, led by Malric Terrowin, pulls back while others refuse to give up yet. Eventually the Agathian Knights, led by Feydrid Kearn also leave Tenosia since there is no chance of victory left. After arriving at home they find that Malric already has begun to unite the Agathian kingdom under his rule. He claims that since he was one of the highest-ranked figures in Agatha's military he is the one who should be in charge of preparing Agatha for the inevitable Tenosian counter-attack. He does not recognize the authority of the Agatha Knights since they have been fighting a lost war instead of returning home to prepare for Tenosia's revenge. The Agatha Knights however claim that the former king's nephew Danum Argon should be crowned king to preserve the bloodline. Because Danum has no military experience whatsoever Feydrid Kearn would in that case be in charge of the armies.
None of the two factions wanting to back down quickly leads to a brutal civil war.
The player chooses between either Feydrid Kearn's Agatha Knights or Malric Terrowin's Mason Order. Both factions have access to the same classes and equipment. There are four classes:
Man-at-Arms are the fastest class altogether as well as the most fragile melee class. They rely on their speed and their dodge ability. Double-tapping a directional button makes them perform a very fast dodge move. They mostly use one-handed weapons and small shields.
Vanguards offer a balanced mix of speed and sturdiness. They use polearms or two-handed swords and deal heavy damage. They have the ability to execute a sprint attack if they build up the proper speed beforehand.
Knights are the slowest and tankiest of the classes. They also need less stamina for parrying and blocking. They are either equipped with one-handed weapons and shields or two-handed weapons. Some of their weapons can be either wielded one-handed or two-handed.
Archers are the most fragile of all classes but also nearly as fast as Man-at-Arms. They can be equipped with bows, crossbows, throwing spears or slings. Archers also deal bonus damage when they hit enemies in the back with a melee weapon.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare features an extremely in-depth combat system while still being accessable and playing fast. It is quite easy to pick up but difficult to master since there is much room for skill. In the beginning you will most likely get horribly murdered but you will find yourself getting better and better and occasionally being able to make plays of a lifetime.
Every character can be equipped with a primary weapon, a secondary weapon and a piece of special equipment. Special equipment can be shields, throwing weapons, or class based equipment like fire pots, smoke pots, pavises or special ammunition.
Every melee weapon has three types of attacks: slashes, stabs and overheads. Also there is an alternate version of each attack. You can also kick or shield bash your opponents. Attacks can be manipulated by moving the mouse during the attack release. This makes it possible to speed up or slow down your attack or make it go around the enemy's parry. It is also possible to chain different attacks together with proper timing. You can also feint an attack and immediately follow up with a real attack. You can even perform a riposte - chain a parry into an attack the will be most likely faster than the enemy's parry. Parrying actually involves quite a bit of skill. The parry must be properly timed as well as aimed at the enemy's weapon's tip. Blocking with a shield is considerably easier since the shield can be held up for a longer time - although not indefinitely - and covers a much larger area. However it should be noted that while wielding a shield you can not riposte and kicks against your shield will stun you. So having a shield is not simply better than having none but rather a tactical choice. There are however other ways of evading attacks besides parrying and blocking. It is also possible to jump over or duck under attacks as well as lean back to avoid the attack by a hair's breadth. You also have to manage your stamina during fights since you cannot attack or block indefinitely. Also, it is clearly noticeable when you run out of stamina, so your opponent may use that opportunity to retaliate.
The various weapons in Chivalry: Medieval Warfare are separated into weapon classes. By accumulating a certain amount of kills with a weapon you unlock the next weapon within that class. Unlockable weapons are not straight up better though. Every weapon has benefits and drawbacks to it and most of them are used frequently.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare offers a variety of game modes. Some of those like Free-for-all, Team Death Match or Last Team Standing are pretty basic. But there is also a duel mode in which the winner is determined by a series of one on one battles as well as Objective Mode. In Objective Mode one of the teams has to completing a series of tasks within a certain time while the other team has keep them from completing those tasks within the given time. For example there is one map on which one team has to destroy a village outside of the castle, then move a ram to the castle gate, crush the gate and kill the enemy leader. One player on the defending team will then become the leader, having improved hit points and regeneration as well a changing appearance to be easily distinguishable.
There is also an expansion pack called Chivalry: Deadliest Warrior. While I don't have room to discuss it in depth I will give a short description. Deadliest warrior runs seperately from the base game, so there is no play between Medieval Warfare and Deadliest Warrior. The expansion has slightly different mechanics and focuses on faster gameplay. Also the expansion does not try to have an authentic feel to it but rather portrays a what-if scenario. What if some of the most known warriors or human history would meet and battle each other? You can play as Knight, Ninja, Pirate, Samurai, Spartan or Viking. Each of those have different abilities and equipment. Sadly the expansion does not feature Duel or Objective Modes. It is still a lot of fun though.
If I would name any weaknesses of Chivalry: Medieval Warfare I would say that it is not as polished as it could be. However, the developer's are showing real efforts in improving the game further. I think the game would also really benefit from some sort of single-player campaign but that is probably out of the developer's scope at the moment. Lastly, DLC seems really overpriced to me. Luckily the DLC only consists of cosmetic items for visual character customization and has no effect on the gameplay.
If you like slashers or medieval themed games I definitely recommend Chivalry: Medieval Warfare. It has the best combat mechanics I have ever seen in a game of that type.
Also:
It has a dedicated button for screaming like a madman.
It has a tavern map on which you can only fight using your fists and get stronger when you get drunk.

Ninja-parkour-robot-hack&slash-3rdpersonshooter with many playable warframes, weapons, and customizations for your loadout. The AI is pretty dumb and end-game becomes more about calculations and maximizing your DPS to kill the mobs that don't really increase in difficulty other than how long it takes to kill each one, and how much damage they do. Creating teams of warframes that work well together is pretty much essential late game to make sure you don't die too quickly, and that you can kill mobs before they kill you.
Overall, for a free-to-play game, it's pretty solid and can be incredibly addicting. It's not really pay2win either, it's more of paying for convenience, timers, and skins. If you do spend money, it just allows you to get items/mods for your weapons/warframes faster with less hassle, but since this game isn't very focused on PvP (although there is some) it really isn't a pay2win model and you can have fun with or without spending a dime.

This game used to be fun.
I harrassed friends into playing it, I talked about it non-stop and played it for hours every day.
Now I would recommend Daikatana over this.
All of the fun and skillful melee combat, that was hectic, terrifying and exhilirating, has been patched out. Leaving only a few somewhat spammy-feeling and exploitative methods of dominating the battlefield.
Want to see a guy with a two handed sword run away from you then proceed to swing his massive sword - in completely the wrong direction only to spin 180 degrees and decapitate you with it?  Well you will. Over and over and over.
Want to experience the joy of really only being able to play as one or two classes with one or two weapon combos lest you get stomped into the dirt? You'll be experiencing ONLY this.
It makes me so sad that the vocal whiners on the forums who constantly berated the inclusion or the viability of archers, javelineers, man at arms who could dodge in and out of combat as being unrealistic or unfair, have had their voices heard - resulting in a watered-down husk of what the game used to be.
Variety now only comes in the form of different helmets.  That you buy for real cash.
All the original maps are in there, with very little new having been added by the devs over the years- leaving one to either play the same 4-5 maps, or play on half-baked and amateurish community maps.
I think a couple of new weapons have been added, but who really cares at this point? They have all been patched into pretty much the same thing now.
At least the sounds are still hilarious.
